papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Network Analysis Identifies Diagnostic and Immune-Associated Hub Genes in Urothelial Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Alkhatib SN, Binsaleh AY, Al-Hoshani N, Bakhsh T, Alqahtani HA, Aziz T.
papers.abstract: Background: Urothelial carcinoma exhibits molecular heterogeneity, high recurrence, and progression rates, and is poorly diagnosed and treated. Transcriptomic and systems-biology analyses can detect dysregulated genes, signaling pathways, and interactions of immune cells. Proposed biomarkers, however, have not been validated, evaluated, and confirmed to be cell-type specific, limiting their potential for clinical translation. Methods: The transcriptomic data in GSE13507 were used to identify features of differential expression, functional enrichment, protein interaction network, and hub genes. Findings were assessed by using external validation, ROC and machine learning models, immune-infiltration analysis, single-cell expression profiling, and survival analysis. Results: In total, 7459 differentially expressed probes were detected, and pathways involved in immunity and cytokines were noted to be enriched. The best diagnostic performance was observed with IL6ST (AUC 0.927), LIFR (AUC 0.921), and JAK1 (AUC 0.843). We found a correlation between hub genes and infiltration of immune cells, and a difference in single-cell distribution; however, none of them was shown to have a significant association with overall survival. Conclusions: The IL-6/JAK/STAT hub gene network was highly diagnostic and immune-relevant in urothelial carcinoma and had limited prognostic significance. The three most promising candidates were IL6ST, LIFR, and JAK1. The genes identified in this study could be validated in tumor-normal pairs and in prospective clinical samples of future studies, accompanied by protein levels and functional studies.

papers.title: HPV16 E7-Containing Exosomes May Contribute to PD-L1 Expression in Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes of Cervical Cancer.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Shen G, Luo L, Feng Y, Wang S.
papers.abstract: Background Human papillomavirus 16 (HPV16) plays a major role in the development of cervical cancer (CC). Programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression in tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) is an important feature of the tumor immune microenvironment and may affect responses to immune checkpoint blockade. However, the relationship between the HPV16 E7 oncoprotein and PD-L1 expression in TILs remains unclear. Aim To investigate the presence of HPV16 E7 protein in exosomes from CC tissues and plasma, determine the association between exosomal E7 and PD-L1 expression in TILs, and explore whether E7-rich tumor-derived exosomes contribute to increased PD-L1 expression in TILs. Study design This study combined clinical observational analyses and in vitro experiments. Three CC single-cell RNA sequencing datasets, a 30-patient HPV16-positive cohort, and a 104-patient tissue microarray cohort were analyzed. In vitro experiments were conducted to further examine the potential relationship between exosomal E7 and PD-L1 expression in TILs. Methods Blood and pathological samples from 30 patients with HPV16-positive CC, as well as culture fluid from the C33A and SiHa CC cell lines, were collected. Exosomes were isolated, and E7 protein expression was assessed. Bioinformatics analyses of CC single-cell RNA sequencing datasets were performed to evaluate CD274 mRNA expression in TILs. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) was used to assess PD-L1 protein expression in TILs in the 30-patient cohort, while multiplex immunofluorescence was used to evaluate E7 and PD-L1 expression in TILs in a 104-patient tissue microarray. Exosome uptake by TILs was assessed using confocal microscopy. TILs were co-cultured with exosomes, and HPV16 E7 and PD-L1 expression was evaluated by quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) and western blotting in the TIL blank control, co-culture blank control, co-culture empty vector, and co-culture E7-overexpression groups. Results E7 protein was detected in exosomes from the peripheral blood of 28 of 30 patients (93.3%) and in exosomes from SiHa cell culture. PD-L1 was expressed in TILs, with a positive rate of 43.3% (13/30). In the tissue microarray cohort (n = 103; 28 events), higher CD3 + PD-L1 + /CD3 + expression was associated with poorer survival (HR = 2.97, p = 0.009). CD3 + E7 + /CD3 + expression showed a borderline association with poorer survival in the dichotomized analysis (HR = 2.15, p = 0.052) but was significantly associated with survival when modeled as a continuous variable (per 10%: HR = 1.28, p = 0.002). In the 30-patient cohort, exosomal E7 protein content was significantly associated with PD-L1 expression in TILs (Cramér's V = 0.728, p = 0.0001). qRT-PCR and western blotting demonstrated increased PD-L1 mRNA and protein expression in TILs exposed to exosomes from E7-overexpressing cells. Conclusion HPV16 E7 protein is present in exosomes from patients with CC and HPV16-positive CC cells. Higher exosomal E7 levels are associated with increased PD-L1 expression in TILs, and exposure to E7-rich exosomes is associated with upregulated PD-L1 expression in TILs. These findings suggest that exosomal E7 may contribute to PD-L1 regulation in TILs and may be associated with poorer prognosis in patients with CC. Further studies are needed to determine whether E7 directly mediates this effect and to clarify its functional and clinical significance.

papers.title: B cell response to HCMV gH/UL116 elicits neutralizing and FcγR-activating antibodies
papers.authors: Ashurov, A.; Hoffmann, K.; Ramamohan, A. R.; Karthigeyan, K. P.; Ashurov, A.; Rotzler, M.; Kohl, A.-K.; Torres, G. M.; Binuya, C.; Williams, C.; Crooks, C. M.; Schlachter, L.; Shestopal, D.; Ullrich, L.; Hornung, C.; Lotfi, R.; Kolb, P.; Kreer, C.; Koch, M.; Permar, S. R.; Hengel, H.; McLellan, J. S.; Klein, F.; Zehner, M.
papers.abstract: Humoral immune mechanisms that can contribute to limiting HCMV disease include neutralizing antibodies that block viral entry and Fc-mediated effector functions that promote elimination of infected cells. Here, we identify the gH/UL116 envelope complex as a naturally immunogenic target that elicits antibodies capable of mediating both of these immune mechanisms. Using single-cell sorting of antigen-specific memory B cells, we isolated gH/UL116-reactive monoclonal antibodies from HCMV-seropositive donors. Epitope mapping showed that gH binding was required for virus neutralization, whereas UL116 targeting was associated with potent and broad Fc{gamma} receptor (Fc{gamma}R) activation. Furthermore, cryo-electron microscopy provided high-resolution structures revealing how UL116-specific antibodies bind gH/UL116. In mice, gH/UL116 immunization elicited serum IgG responses whose binding titers strongly correlated with both neutralization and mouse Fc{gamma}R activation. Together, these findings provide an epitope-level map linking antibody specificity to neutralization and Fc{gamma}R activation across HCMV gH-associated complexes and position gH/UL116 as a promising HCMV vaccine candidate.

papers.title: Prenatal immune priming to Plasmodium falciparum is characterized by multi-lineage T-cell responses that are influenced by maternal microchimerism and predict malaria outcomes
papers.authors: Jiang, Y.; Bach, F.; Houck, J.; Carlson, M.; Mahamar, A.; Gaoussou, S.; Attaher, O.; Morrison, R.; Kumar, S.; Armistead, B.; Zaidi, I.; Kappe, S.; Dicko, A.; Duffy, P.; Fried, M.; Pepper, M.; Harrington, W. E.
papers.abstract: In malaria endemic settings, the fetus may be exposed to Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) antigens leading to prenatal immune primming (PIP). The fetus also acquires a graft of maternal cells in utero, a phenomenon known as maternal microchimerism (MMc). We have previously identified that MMc at birth predicts altered malaria susceptibility in early childhood, and we hypothesized that this association may be mediated via two potential mechanisms. First, the fetus may acquire Pf-specific MMc T-cells that directly respond to postnatal parasitemia. Alternatively, MMc may indirectly influence the quantity or quality of PIP. To investigate this hypothesis, infant cord bloods from 97 Malian primigravidae were screened for MMc using qPCR. A subset of ten cord blood mononuclear cells with variable MMc levels were stimulated with purified Pf merozoite extract and activated T-cells were sorted by flow cytometry for scRNAseq analysis. Transcriptional profile was used to differentiate Pf-responsive versus bystander activated T-cells, and MMc cells were identified using the Cellector algorithm. Among Pf-responsive cells, we identified four key populations: activated CD4 T-cells, ZBTB16+ CD4 T-cells, activated V{delta}1+ {gamma}{delta} T-cells, and cytotoxic V{gamma}9V{delta}2+ {gamma}{delta} T-cells. The minority of sorted cells were of MMc origin; however, there was a strong association between the presence of MMc and the quantity and quality of PIP. MMc+ infants had significantly fewer Pf-responsive T-cells, as well as a shifted distribution of these cells with fewer ZBTB16+ CD4 and cytotoxic V{gamma}9V{delta}2+ {gamma}{delta} T-cells. Clinically, MMc was protective from incident parasitemia and febrile malaria, whereas the frequencies of ZBTB16+ CD4 and activated CD4 T-cells were associated with increased risk. Together, these data demonstrate that MMc influences malaria outcomes through regulation of offspring inflammatory responses to Pf.

papers.title: Innate Immune Dysregulation Precedes Clinical Onset in Neuromyelitis Optica
papers.authors: Muller-Jensen, L.; Chakravarty, D.; Bellucci, G.; Ding, Y.; Hughes, M.; Garcia, A. M.; Moseley, C. E.; Dandekar, R.; Rose, J. W.; Peterson, L. K.; Wong, K.-H.; Demarest, B. L.; Carlson, N.; Horvat, D. E.; Groshans, K.; Tagg, N.; Osbourn, S. R.; Mabila, S. L.; Bou-Chahine, R.; Wang, V.; Paz Soldan, M. M.; Pittock, S. J.; Cree, B. A. C.; Zamvil, S. S.; Green, A. J.; Harroud, A.; Baranzini, S. E.; Wilson, M. R.; Clardy, S. L.; Abdelhak, A.; Smith, T. L.
papers.abstract: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) is a disabling inflammatory central nervous system (CNS) disease characterized by pathogenic aquaporin 4 (AQP4) autoantibodies. The biological events that precede clinical onset remain unknown. In a unique longitudinal NMOSD cohort from the U.S. Department of Defense Serum Repository, with samples collected up to 24 years before onset, we applied discovery proteomics (~5,400 proteins), pan-viral antibody profiling (VirScan), and in silico analyses to characterize preclinical NMOSD versus matched healthy controls. Innate immune activation, particularly CXCL1 elevation, was the dominant immunological feature of preclinical NMOSD, preceding onset by ~12.7 years. AQP4-IgG was detectable more than 3 years before onset, while CNS injury markers increased only after disease manifestation. VirScan identified enhanced CMV-specific antibody reactivity following AQP4- IgG seroconversion, and network analyses revealed interactions between NMOSD-associated and CMV-derived proteins. Together, these findings establish a novel multi-hit model of NMOSD, with implications for understanding antibody-mediated autoimmunity more broadly.

papers.title: MMP14-mediated proteolytic cleavage of LAMC2 domain III fragment drives osimertinib resistance in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.authors: Lu CH, Bi WD, Gao ZY, Huang DJ, Lin CY, Wu D, Yu HY, He Y, Li L.
papers.abstract: Acquired resistance to osimertinib remains a critical clinical challenge in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), with 40%-60% of progressing patients lacking an identifiable genetic resistance driver. Through quantitative secretomic profiling of paired osimertinib-sensitive and -resistant NSCLC cell lines, we identified laminin subunit γ2 (LAMC2) as markedly enriched in resistant cell secretomes. Single-cell RNA sequencing reanalysis revealed a LAMC2-high drug-tolerant persister subpopulation that expanded under osimertinib pressure, with pseudotime analysis suggesting progressive co-upregulation of LAMC2 and matrix metalloproteinase 14 (MMP14) along the treatment-to-resistance trajectory. Across four independent cohorts, MMP14 exhibited the strongest co-expression with LAMC2 among all metalloproteinases; the two proteins also physically interacted, and their concurrent high expression predicted the worst overall survival. Mechanistically, MMP14 cleaved LAMC2 to release a bioactive Domain III (DIII) fragment harboring EGF-like repeats, which reactivated EGFR/AKT/ERK signaling despite continued osimertinib exposure. Exogenous DIII conferred resistance in sensitive cells, whereas an anti-DIII blocking antibody reversed MMP14-driven resistance in cell lines and patient-derived organoids. The selective MMP14 inhibitor NSC405020 restored osimertinib sensitivity in vitro and suppressed xenograft growth. In residual tumor tissues from neoadjuvant osimertinib-treated patients, non-responders exhibited higher LAMC2/MMP14 co-expression and more prominent spatial exclusion of CD8⁺ T-cells from the tumor core compared with major pathological responders. These findings identify the MMP14-LAMC2-DIII proteolytic axis as a non-genetic resistance mechanism and suggest that MMP14 inhibition or DIII neutralization may represent a rational strategy to overcome acquired osimertinib resistance.

papers.title: Molecular HLA matching in kidney transplantation: the emerging role of eplet mismatch analysis.
papers.authors: Mehra S, Chauhan R, Tiwari AK, Shingatgeri VM, Bhardwaj G, Gupta S, Kahlon S, Kumar P.
papers.abstract: Introduction Kidney transplantation is the preferred treatment for end-stage kidney disease, but long-term graft survival remains limited by alloimmune injury, particularly donor-specific antibody-mediated rejection. This review evaluates molecular HLA matching as an approach to improve donor-recipient compatibility assessment beyond conventional antigen-level matching. Areas covered The biological basis of HLA epitopes and eplets is described, with emphasis on HLAMatchmaker, HLA-EMMA, PIRCHE-II, and related computational approaches. Evidence linking molecular mismatch with de novo donor-specific antibodies, antibody-mediated rejection, chronic allograft injury, and graft survival is reviewed. Qualitative eplet immunogenicity, structural accessibility, amino-acid properties, antibody verification, and HLA-DQ-associated risk are also examined. A literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus, focusing on studies published during the preceding 10 years, employing terms related to kidney transplantation, HLA eplet mismatch, molecular HLA matching, donor-specific antibodies, rejection, and graft outcomes. Expert opinion HLA eplet-based matching may improve immunological risk stratification and individualized surveillance. However, algorithmic variability, incomplete antibody verification, differences in HLA typing resolution, population limitations, and lack of standardized thresholds restrict implementation. Prospective multi-center studies are needed to establish clinical utility, cost-effectiveness, and whether molecularly informed donor selection or monitoring improves patient and graft outcomes.

papers.title: In silico approach to Helicobacter pylori vaccine design.
papers.authors: Mariño-Perea S, Canal-Alonso Á, Chamoso P, Mezquita Y, Góngora S.
papers.abstract: Helicobacter pylori , a Gram-negative microorganism, infects over half of the human population worldwide. Its extensive genetic variability and capacity to bypass host immune defences continue to impede the creation of an effective vaccine. Nonetheless, contemporary progress in computational biology and immunoinformatics has introduced innovative methodologies that can substantially support and accelerate vaccine design against this pathogen. In the present work, an in silico strategy was employed to develop a multi-epitope vaccine targeting H. pylori . The FlaA, UreB and PSA D15 proteins were chosen as primary antigens due to their strong immunogenic potential, critical roles in bacterial physiology, and comparatively low sequence variability among strains. Using advanced bioinformatics and immunoinformatics pipelines, potential epitopes for both B-cell and T-cell were identified and assembled through rational protein engineering approaches to generate the final vaccine construct. Before computational validation, the safety of the selected epitopes was predicted through toxicity, allergenticity, and non-homology to human analyses, which resulted on positive results. Furthermore, the construct's physicochemical parameters were under acceptable values, as for the population coverage. This construct was subsequently analysed through molecular docking simulations to evaluate its interaction with host immune receptors. The obtained results demonstrated that the designed molecule could accomplish stable interactions with high affinity with the immune components, supporting its potential as a viable candidate for experimental validation and subsequent development.

papers.title: PMEPA1 in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma: Prognostic value, immune associations, and predicted drug sensitivity.
papers.authors: Zhang P, Wu H, He J, Zhang D, Yi J.
papers.abstract: Reliable prognostic biomarkers for laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) remain limited. This study evaluated prostate transmembrane protein androgen induced 1 (PMEPA1) expression, prognostic significance, functional effects, and immune and drug sensitivity associations. Transcriptomic and clinical data from The Cancer Genome Atlas and Gene Expression Omnibus were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier analysis, Cox regression, functional enrichment, immune deconvolution, and drug sensitivity prediction. Expression and knockdown effects were assessed using quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, western blotting, cell viability assays, and Transwell assays. PMEPA1 was upregulated in tumors and cancer cell lines. Higher expression was associated with poorer overall survival in two cohorts and remained significant after multivariable adjustment in the discovery cohort. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) for tumor-normal discrimination ranged from 0.835 to 0.944; nomogram AUCs were 0.766, 0.772, and 0.809 at 1, 3, and 5 years. Enrichment analyses highlighted extracellular matrix organization. PMEPA1 knockdown reduced viability, migration, and invasion in one LSCC cell line. Computational analyses linked higher expression to greater proportions of unpolarized (M0) and alternatively activated (M2) macrophages, lower cluster of differentiation 8-positive (CD8+) T-cell proportions, and higher stromal and immune exclusion scores. Expression correlated positively with predicted half-maximal inhibitory concentrations (IC₅₀) of entinostat and vorinostat and negatively with those of dasatinib and AZD1332. PMEPA1 is a candidate prognostic biomarker with functional relevance in LSCC; its immune and drug sensitivity associations require experimental and clinical validation.

papers.title: Peptidomics and Computational Docking Prioritize Candidate Peptide-Protein Associations Relevant to Upper-Gastrointestinal Biology in a Fermented Soy-Derived Postbiotic.
papers.authors: Tremblay A, Harms C, Nankar A, Gupta R, Buko A, Tompkins TA.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives : Gastro-AD ® (GAD) is a fermented soy-derived postbiotic supported by clinical and preclinical evidence related to gastric comfort and mucosal injury. Although fermentation-derived metabolites have been characterized, the peptide fraction remains poorly defined. This study characterized GAD peptides and explored their potential biological contexts. Methods : Untargeted peptidomics was used to identify soy-derived peptides in GAD and map them to source proteins. A diversity-sampling panel of ten peptides was selected using sequence, physicochemical, and predicted structural features. These peptides were screened against a human protein-structure library by computational docking, followed by GO enrichment and context-based prioritization of candidate interactors. Results: A total of 219 peptides, originating predominantly from soybean storage proteins, were identified. The GAD peptide fraction contained extensive overlapping sequence families and truncation ladders, consistent with extensive proteolytic processing. Three literature-reported antioxidant peptide sequences were identified as exact contiguous regions within longer GAD peptides. Large-scale docking against the screened human protein-structure library combined with GO-enrichment recurrence analysis and an independent review of top-ranked docking-derived candidates identified 180 candidate protein targets spanning innate immune and inflammatory defense, protease activity and peptide processing, extracellular-matrix remodeling, tissue repair and wound healing, and apoptotic signaling and epithelial turnover. Repeated randomized-affinity controls yielded substantially fewer FDR-significant GO terms than the observed docking-derived rankings, supporting non-random functional structure in the docking-derived protein rankings without establishing the accuracy of individual peptide-protein interactions. Context-based prioritization identified 43 unique Tier 1 and Tier 2 candidates with direct or context-dependent extracellular accessibility. The prioritized biological contexts included mucosal immune regulation, extracellular-matrix remodeling, epithelial turnover, and tissue restitution. Conclusions : The GAD peptide fraction described herein comprises multiple overlapping peptide families whose prioritized biological contexts center on mucosal defense, remodeling, and tissue restitution. These findings support further investigation of peptides as potential contributors to the multi-component biological properties of GAD.

papers.title: StainAI-Web: An Interactive Platform for Whole-Slide Microglial Morphology Analysis
papers.authors: Liu, D.-Y.; Chuang, H.-J.; Hsu, C.-H.; Chang, B.-M.; Ette, E.; Shih, M.; Liao, Y.-A.; Zehra, H.; Ali, S.; Tu, T.-R.; Lin, S.; Wang, P. C.; Shoykhet, M.; Tu, T.-W.
papers.abstract: Microglial morphology analysis has emerged as a critical approach in neuroinflammation research. The increasing availability of high-resolution and whole-slide histology images has created strong demand for robust, scalable analytical methods capable of efficiently processing these datasets. Existing approaches may require code-based local computation or prolonged processing times for whole-slide images, while manual morphology quantification remains labor-intensive. To address these limitations, we introduce StainAI-Web, a server that performs rapid, automated microglial morphology detection across whole-slide immunohistochemistry images in the cloud. The system provides interactive grayscale preprocessing and supports ROI-based regional quantification, allowing users to define specific tissue regions and systematically compare microglial populations across regions. An interactive visualization module dynamically updates quantitative summaries of morphological distributions as ROIs are selected or modified. Analysis results, including structured JSON files and morphology-annotated overlays, are downloadable for downstream analysis or integration into external computational pipelines. These integrated features provide an accessible framework for efficient and reproducible whole-slide microglial morphology analysis. The StainAI-Web is available at https://stainaiviewer.azurewebsites.net/.

papers.title: Rethinking Pathogenesis of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.
papers.authors: Demir M, Weglage J, Sigal M.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease characterized by progressive fibroinflammatory injury of intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts that may lead to cirrhosis, hepatobiliary malignancy, and death, with liver transplantation representing the only effective intervention in end-stage disease. Rather than a single dominant pathomechanism, the data support a model in which four axes - bile acid metabolism, the intestinal microbiome and gut barrier, biliary epithelial dysfunction, and Th17-skewed immune dysregulation - are reciprocally coupled and converge on a shared periductal fibrogenic output dominated by TGF-beta signaling. This review summarizes key mechanistic advances from genetic, epigenomic, single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, and microbiome studies. These investigations implicate antigen presentation pathways, Th17-skewed immune responses, cholangiocyte senescence and profibrotic signaling, and disrupted gut-liver communication as central drivers of chronic biliary injury. Emerging spatial and multi-omics approaches further reveal complex cellular crosstalk among cholangiocytes, immune cells, macrophages, and mesenchymal populations within portal inflammatory niches. We discuss evolving biomarkers and recent clinical trial data targeting bile acid metabolism, fibrosis, the microbiome, and immune pathways. In conclusion, research data suggests viewing PSC as a network disease, which provides a unifying framework for disease pathogenesis and may enable biomarker-guided patient stratification and mechanism-based therapy development targeting distinct pathogenic pathways.

papers.title: CytoRipple: Mapping Tissue Polarization through Subcellular Cytoskeleton Dynamics
papers.authors: Chen, D. G.; Yee, T.; Saco, J.; Patten, J. J.; Lackner, A. I.; Angelo, M.; Heath, J. R.; Ribas, A.; Campbell, K. M.
papers.abstract: Spatial multi-omic technologies entail simultaneous measurement of tens-to-thousands of molecular features (e.g. RNA, protein). While cell type and state profiling is the major focus of spatial multi-omic analyses, cytoskeletal proteins are often solely utilized for cell segmentation and quality control. Here, we introduce a new computational framework, CytoRipple, that leverages these concomitant spatially-resolved single-cell measurements of cytoskeleton proteins to identify tissue-level vector fields. Polarization vectors are known to associate with cell movement and phenotype, inferring their physical orientation. We validate these associations across biological contexts and reveal how polarization vector fields can be harnessed to discover multi-cellular structures (e.g. "streams" of cells with similar polarizations). These multi-cellular cytoskeleton dynamics associate with distinct phenomena, such as vector "divergence" with CD8+ T cell activation and "streams" with spatially segmented stages of the anti-tumor immune response. Together, these data support a role for CytoRipple in revealing a dynamic layer across spatial multi-omic platforms.

papers.title: Spatial proteomic profiling of cardiac stromal populations and microenvironments in systemic sclerosis-associated primary myocardial involvement
papers.authors: Stuetz, A. N.; De Luca, G.; Matei, A.-E.; Li, Y.-N.; Filla, T.; Batani, V.; Tuemerdem, B. S.; Rigau, A. R.; Bruno, C.; Merkt, W.; Zweck, E.; Buettner-Herold, M.; Rizzo, S.; Peretto, G.; De Gaspari, M.; Eckstein, M.; Schett, G.; Basso, C.; Matucci-Cerinic, M.; Distler, J.; Gyoerfi, A.-H.
papers.abstract: Objectives: To define cardiac stromal heterogeneity and spatial stromal-immune organization in systemic sclerosis-associated virus-negative myocarditis (SSc-VNM), a manifestation of primary SSc heart involvement. Methods: Imaging mass cytometry, a single-cell multiplexed spatial proteomic technology, was applied to endomyocardial biopsies from ten patients with SSc-VNM, seven with VNM associated with other systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (a-VNM) and nine with isolated VNM (i-VNM). Single-cell phenotyping, cellular-neighborhood and spatial-interaction analyses, and correlations with histological fibrosis were performed at patient level. Results: Among 82,673 segmented cells, we identified seven fibroblast phenotypes and one CD34+ stromal-cell population. The overall fibroblast/stromal compartment was expanded in SSc-VNM compared with i-VNM (adjusted p = 0.00973). The composition of fibroblasts/stromal cells differed profoundly in SSc-VNM compared with a-VNM and i-VNM, with numerical increases in CD34+ stromal cells and SOX9+ and PI16high/POSTNhigh fibroblasts and de-enrichment of FAPhigh/POSTNhigh fibroblasts and myofibroblasts. Spatial analysis identified ten cellular neighborhoods and revealed distinct SSc-VNM-associated patterns, including altered stromal-immune interaction networks. These included enriched interactions of CD34+ stromal cells and PI16high/POSTNhigh fibroblasts with CD163high/HLA-DR+ macrophages and CD68+ mast cells. PI16high/POSTNhigh and PI16-/POSTNhigh fibroblasts demonstrated the highest collagen type 1 expression among all stromal cell subsets across all VNM entities and PI16high/POSTNhigh fibroblasts were numerically increased in biopsies with [≥]10% fibrotic remodeling and were spatially associated with collagen-rich areas. Conclusions: Our findings refine current concepts of human fibrotic myocardial remodeling and support therapeutic targeting of specific stromal players such as POSTNhigh fibroblast subpopulations. Keywords: Systemic Sclerosis; Myocarditis; Myocardial Fibrosis; Fibroblasts; Imaging Mass Cytometry.

papers.title: Nanobody-Based Lateral Flow Assays: Applications, Innovations, Challenges, and Future Directions.
papers.authors: Peng Y, Gómez-Castillo M, Hoehndorf R, Kiessling F, Renn D, Rueping M.
papers.abstract: Nanobody-based lateral flow assays (LFAs) are an emerging class of point-of-care diagnostics that combine enhanced thermal stability, target affinity comparable to or in some cases exceeding that of conventional antibodies, and low-cost recombinant production of nanobodies with the versatility of conventional antibody-based detection formats. This review examines recent progress in nanobody engineering, assay architecture, and signal amplification strategies that improve analytical sensitivity, specificity, and multiplexing potential. Despite these advances, several technical and translational challenges persist, including broad analyte compatibility, difficulties in optimal nanobody pair selection, scalability of expression systems, and the need for robust and reproducible conjugation chemistries. The growing integration of computational modeling and AI-driven nanobody design has accelerated the discovery and optimization pipelines, yet standardized frameworks for validation and benchmarking remain scarce. Addressing these limitations will be important for the further clinical translation and commercial deployment of nanobody-based LFAs across diverse applications in infectious disease diagnostics, food safety testing, and environmental monitoring.

papers.title: Evidence for Reduced Somatic T-Cell Receptor Sequence Diversity Profiles Among Midwestern Amish in an Aging Cohort Study.
papers.authors: Cruz LA, Liu S, Miskimen KL, Cooke Bailey JN, Kinzy T, Song YE, Laux RA, Miron P, Ogrocki PK, Lerner AJ, Lynn A, Fuzzell SL, Hochstetler SD, Konidari I, McCauley JL, Scott WK, Pericak-Vance MA, Haines JL, Crawford DC.
papers.abstract: Background The causes of late onset Alzheimer disease (LOAD) are not known but several recent lines of evidence implicate the adaptive immune system. Objective To characterize the adaptive immune system among Midwestern Amish participating in longitudinal studies of aging. Methods We immunosequenced the T-cell receptor (TCR) beta chain from genomic DNA of 72 participants, including those with clinically diagnosed LOAD (n = 6), mild cognitive impairment (MCI; n = 16), cognitive impairment but not AD (n = 3), and 35 cognitively unaffected. For a subset of participants, LOAD pathogenesis plasma biomarkers were available. Results TCR sequence diversity measured as Simpson's clonality was lower among LOAD+MCI compared with non-LOAD, but these differences were not independent of age. Relatively few clonotypes (exact nucleotide sequences) were shared across participants; of those few shared include the Epstein Barr virus associated clonotype. HLA-A*03:01 and several HLA-DRB1 alleles were under-represented among LOAD+MCI participants compared with cognitively unaffected participants, but these associations were no longer significant in adjusted analyses. Among LOAD+MCI participants, increased p-tau181 was nominally associated with decreased TCR sequence diversity, and the nominal association was independent of age; however, this association did not remain statistically significant after strict correction for multiple testing and the limited sample size precluded formal tests of heterogeneity. Results In this limited Midwestern Amish sample, the preliminary TCR diversity trends are consistent with the involvement of the adaptive immune system in LOAD.

papers.title: Hypothesis-Generating Single-Cell Analysis of the Endometrial Cancer Immune Microenvironment With Complementary Multiomics Evidence.
papers.authors: Ouyang X, Guo X, Yang X, Wen J.
papers.abstract: Background Endometrial cancer (EC) has a heterogeneous immune microenvironment, and response-associated biology remains incompletely characterized. We used the retained EC single-cell dataset to describe immune-cell states and complemented it with TCGA-UCEC, independent gut microbiome cohorts, and RL95-2 proof-of-concept experiments. All responder versus nonresponder scRNA-seq comparisons are descriptive and hypothesis generating because only one sample was available per clinical response group. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from EC patients undergoing anti-PD-1 immunotherapy (GEO: GSE251923; one responder, GSM7990051, and one nonresponder, GSM7990052; 17,546 cells retained after quality control) were analyzed using Scanpy, Leiden clustering, and over-representation analysis with GO biological process, KEGG, and MSigDB Hallmark gene sets using Enrichr with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Bulk RNA-seq from TCGA-UCEC (554 tumor and 35 normal samples) was used for complementary transcriptomic analysis. Gut microbiome 16S rRNA datasets (SRA: PRJNA897842 and PRJNA833670) were analyzed as independent cohorts, and RL95-2 qRT-PCR experiments were interpreted as proof-of-concept. Results Ten major cell populations were identified in the EC immune microenvironment. In this single responder/nonresponder sample pair, the nonresponder sample showed patterns consistent with higher M2-associated macrophage marker expression, increased T-cell checkpoint/exhaustion marker expression, and lower cytotoxic activity scores. These observations are descriptive and cannot establish patient-level significance. TCGA-UCEC analyses and the independent microbiome and RL95-2 experiments provide complementary, hypothesis-generating evidence; no unverified classifier-performance estimate is reported. Conclusions This study provides a hypothesis-generating description of immune patterns in one EC responder and one nonresponder sample, complemented by TCGA-UCEC, independent microbiome datasets, and RL95-2 proof-of-concept experiments. The findings nominate candidate immune, hormonal, and microbiome-associated pathways for further investigation but do not establish patient-level response differences, causality, or clinically validated biomarkers.

figure.label: Figure 1
figure.caption: Single‐cell transcriptomic landscape and cellular composition of the endometrial cancer microenvironment. (A) UMAP visualization of single cells, colored by annotated cell population. (B) Distributions of quality‐control metrics by condition. (C) Polar plot summarizing the distribution of cells across annotated cell populations. (D) Comparison of cell type proportions between the nonresponder and responder samples. Each line connects the proportions of the same cell population across the two conditions; the vertical axis indicates the percentage of cells. (E) Dot plot of marker gene expression across annotated cell populations. Dot size represents the percentage of cells expressing each gene, and color intensity indicates the mean expression level. (F) UMAP density contours showing the distributions of cells from the responder and nonresponder samples. The scRNA‐seq dataset comprises one biological sample per condition; therefore, between‐condition comparisons are descriptive and exploratory, and no patient‐level statistical inference is made.

papers.title: Sustained antigenic engagement programs multidimensional CTL states with distinct cytotoxic capacities
papers.authors: Rodriguez-Gutierrez, H. F.; Jainarayanan, A.; Tosolini, M.; Aslani, F.; Iscache, A.-L.; Müller, S.; Corre, B.; Vanazzi, A.; Elanchezhian, M.; Laurent, C.; Valitutti, S.; Khazen, R.
papers.abstract: Cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) eliminate infected or malignant cells through repeated target-cell encounters, yet how they sustain cytotoxic activity during extended antigenic stimulation remains poorly understood. In particular, it remains unclear whether preserved population-level killing reflects maintenance of a uniform effector phenotype or diversification into functionally distinct CTL populations. Here, we combined live-cell imaging, high-dimensional cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, phenotypic trajectory analysis, population sorting, and rechallenge killing assays to define how human clonal CTLs remodel during sustained antigenic engagement. Prior antigen encounter altered the kinetics and pattern of target-cell membrane permeabilization but did not compromise overall subsequent killing upon rechallenge. Single-cell transcriptomic profiling after prolonged engagement revealed broad remodeling of antigen-experienced CTLs and heterogeneous cytotoxic transcriptional programs. Time-resolved scRNA-seq further showed that these functional dimensions remodeled with distinct kinetics, with rapid induction of activation- and cytotoxicity-associated programs, later remodeling of vesicular-trafficking programs, and progressive reduction of adhesion/ contact interaction -associated programs. High-dimensional cytometry showed that this temporal remodeling was accompanied by progressive redistribution of CTLs across a multidimensional protein-expression landscape defined by distinct combinations of cytotoxic, vesicular/degranulation, activation, cytokine, adhesion, and regulatory features. Phenotypic trajectory analysis organized this protein landscape along a temporal remodeling axis, with early lytic-granule-rich profiles giving way to multiple late-engaged phenotypes with distinct combinations of functional protein features. Surface-marker-defined late CTL populations displayed distinct killing capacities upon rechallenge, demonstrating that preserved population-level cytotoxicity can coexist with substantial functional heterogeneity. Finally, CAR T cells exposed to CD19+ targets retained cytotoxic activity upon rechallenge and acquired multidimensional phenotypic features that partially overlapped with the remodeling framework identified in clonal CTLs. Reanalysis of longitudinal patient-derived CAR T-cell transcriptomes further showed that related functional programs were dynamically organized after infusion, with the features distinguishing responder and non-responder tisa-cel samples changing between the infusion product and day 7. Together, these findings indicate that sustained CTL killing is accompanied by progressive multidimensional remodeling and diversification rather than maintenance of a fixed effector phenotype. Our findings support a model in which population-level cytotoxic activity can be maintained while the CTLs composing that population progressively diversify into functionally distinct states during sustained antigenic engagement.

papers.title: Deep Learning and Engineered Biomaterials-Enhanced Imaging-Guided Cancer Immunotherapy.
papers.authors: Lv K, Li B, Xiao B, Zhou F, Zhao H, Sun J, Liang JL.
papers.abstract: The clinical success of immunotherapies is hindered by the absence of robust methodologies for the early and accurate assessment of antitumor immune responses. Integrating engineered biomaterials with artificial intelligence (AI)-driven molecular imaging technology offers a powerful approach for predicting immune efficacy. However, its clinical translation is significantly hindered by several critical limitations, including the complex and costly synthesis of multifunctional imaging probes, insufficient deep-tissue penetration, suboptimal in vivo signal-to-noise ratios, potential immunogenicity and off-target toxicity, and the limited generalizability of deep learning models across heterogeneous patient populations. In view of these pressing scientific challenges, this review focuses on the application of chemical and biomolecular strategies-enhanced engineered biomaterials in promoting the sensitivity and specificity of advanced imaging modalities for visualizing signaling molecules and immune cells in the tumor microenvironment (TME). Meanwhile, recent progress in deep learning-driven image analysis has enabled strong predictive capabilities and automated the understanding of complex immune system dynamics. Together, these technologies provide a transformative platform for non-invasive monitoring, personalized treatment, and response prediction, with the potential to advance precision immuno-oncology and significantly impact both basic research and clinical translation.

papers.title: A novel framework for identifying cellular signature LncRNAs and their functional coregulatory networks with prognostic implications at single-cell resolution.
papers.authors: Bai J, Li X, Hu C, Peng C, Chen J, Liang W, Li X, Zhang Y.
papers.abstract: Introduction Long non-coding RNAs have been implicated in crucial roles in developing malignant tumors. However, comprehensive analyses of lncRNA within the tumor microenvironment, particularly at the single-cell level across various tumor types, remain limited. Objectives This study aimed to establish a comprehensive methodological framework for prioritizing and identifying novel cancer-associated lncRNA biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets at the single-cell level, and to integrate these findings into a unified platform. Methods We developed SIGLNCOS, a computational framework for analyzing single-cell lncRNA regulation via: i) Constructing the lncRNA visualization landscape. ii) Identifying cellular signature lncRNA. iii) Functional enrichment of clncRNAs. iv) Identifying co-lncRNA pairs based on shared functional annotations and weighted functional association scores. Cell-composition-adjusted prognostic analysis evaluated the prognostic relevance of individual lncRNAs and co-lncRNA pairs. Results Applying SIGLNCOS, we identified 667 cellular-signature lncRNAs (clncRNAs) from over half a million single cells across 31 cancers, revealing their roles in immune modulation, tumor progression, and differentiation. NEAT1 was associated with distinct macrophage states and functional changes along pseudotime. SIGLNCOS identified 3,381 co-lncRNA pairs involved in key cancer-related pathways, revealing a complex landscape of lncRNA co-regulation. Notably, we uncovered distinct co-lncRNA networks associated with different thyroid cancer states, particularly between papillary thyroid carcinoma and anaplastic thyroid carcinoma. These networks exhibit functionally concordant regulatory effects that individual lncRNAs cannot, underscoring the importance of co-regulation in tumor evolution. The prognostic analysis demonstrated that co-lncRNA networks outperform individual lncRNAs in predicting patient outcomes, emphasizing their potential as biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Conclusion This study constructs pan-cancer lncRNA landscapes and develops SIGLNCOS, a comprehensive framework for uncovering lncRNA at single-cell resolution, offering new insights into cancer biology and potential avenues for targeted therapies and novel biomarker discovery. We further developed sCo-Lnc (https://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/scolnc), a web-based platform for visualizing novel lncRNA biomarkers across cancers.

papers.title: Glioblastoma immune landscape remodeling following treatment with CD70-targeted CAR-T cells.
papers.authors: Kourtesakis A, Agardy DA, Tejido Dierssen C, Hai L, Hoffmann DCF, Mussnig N, Sinn R, Fischer M, Schacht A, Breckwoldt M, Bunse L, Sauer T, Platten M, Wick W, Kessler T.
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has shown limited efficacy in glioblastoma (GB), largely because of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). We have previously demonstrated that the ligand-based mCD70-directed construct mCAR27 specifically eliminates CD70⁺ GB cells in vitro , and induces durable tumor remission with prolonged survival in a syngeneic model of orthotopic GB. Despite the therapeutic promise of CD70 as a GB CAR-T cell target, the impact of CD70-directed CAR-T cells on the brain tumor immune landscape after target interception remains unexplored. Here, we independently confirmed a tumorigenic role for CD70 in murine GB by performing bulk RNA sequencing and in vivo experiments. Next, we applied single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) to decipher the transcriptome of GB-infiltrating immune cells in immunocompetent mice bearing CD70 + GB after intratumoral mCAR27 therapy. CAR-T cell treatment expanded adoptively transferred cells and was associated with increased endogenous Cd8⁺ T-cell infiltration, alongside a reduction in immunosuppressive populations, including T regs and anti-inflammatory M2-like macrophages, but also subsets of dendritic and natural-killer cells. CD70 expression was detected on multiple GB-infiltrating immune subsets, notably T regs and M2-like macrophages. Transcriptionally, mCAR27-mediated GB remission led to a coordinated downregulation of type-I interferon-stimulated genes and immunosuppressive mediators such as Arg1 , Tgfbi , Cd274 , Pdcd1lg2 and Lag3 , coupled with upregulation of genes involved in inflammatory resolution, findings consistent with attenuation of GB-derived inflammatory stress and immunosuppression. Collectively, we showcase that CD70-directed CAR-T cell therapy remodels the post-treatment immune landscape towards resolution of inflammation and reduced immunosuppression, supporting sustained immune surveillance.

papers.title: Neuro-Immune Interactions in the Tumour Microenvironment: Implications for Cancer Progression and Treatment.
papers.authors: T Ardah M, Ali Bakr R, Malathi H, Arora V, Priyadarshini Nayak P, Urazbaeva D, Djumaniyazova M, Moxinur S.
papers.abstract: The nervous and immune systems, once viewed as distinct biological networks, are now understood to be closely linked in regulating cancer development, progression, and responses to therapy. Neural structures infiltrate the tumour microenvironment and communicate with immune cells, influencing key processes such as tumour growth, invasion, and metastatic spread. Through neurotransmitters, neuropeptides, and continuous signalling between peripheral tissues and the brain, nerves affect immune cell recruitment, activity, and overall immune balance. Factors including psychological stress, circadian rhythm disturbances, and gut-brain communication further shape antitumour immune responses, highlighting the complexity of these interactions. Research suggests that neuronal signalling not only contributes to cancer-associated symptoms, such as pain, but also affects the efficacy of chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immunotherapy. Neural biomarkers may provide prognostic value, while interventions targeting neural pathways could strengthen anticancer immunity. Nevertheless, major challenges remain, including cellular heterogeneity, dynamic spatial and temporal interactions, and the limitations of existing experimental models. Continued progress in molecular techniques, bioinformatics, and cross-disciplinary research will be crucial for clarifying these mechanisms. Investigating the neuro-immune-cancer interface offers significant potential for developing innovative treatment approaches that combine neuroscience, immunology, and oncology to enhance patient survival and quality of life.

papers.title: CXCL9-Dependent Immune Networks of Spontaneous Tertiary Lymphoid Structures in a Murine Subcutaneous Tumor Model
papers.authors: Qin, R. Z.; Abberger, H.; Man, G.; Broomfield, B. J.; Williams, B. E.; Tan, C. W.; Duckworth, B. C.; Jenkins, M. R.; Geoghegan, N. D.; Rogers, K. L.; Tuong, Z. K.; Groom, J. R.
papers.abstract: Recent discoveries have identified human tumor tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) as organized clusters of innate and adaptive immune cells and stromal cells. Cancer-associated TLS can promote tumor clearance and enhance responses to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) immunotherapy. However, the absence of TLS in conventional mouse tumor models, particularly subcutaneous transplant models, limits experimental manipulation and study of TLS development. By tuning tumor antigen expression, we have generated a subcutaneous tumor model that naturally forms TLS within the immune-hot, vasculature-rich peritumoral adipose tissue. These TLS were identified as clusters of B and T cells in close proximity to high endothelial venules. TLS organization was underpinned by spatially compartmentalized chemokine expression, with CCL21 produced in the T cell zone of perivascular TLS and CXCL13 present in the B cell region. Single cell transcriptomic sequencing showed that the immune composition in the TLS forming peritumoral tissue resembled human cancer TLS signatures. Upon anti-PD-L1 ICB treatment, TLS underwent expansion, which was associated with increased interferon responses in macrophages and coincided with tumor clearance. We further identified the interferon-inducible chemokine CXCL9 as a key regulator of the TLS microenvironment. CXCL9-expressing macrophages populated TLS, interacting with B cells following ICB treatment. CXCL9 deficiency reduced B cell recruitment to peritumoral tissue and TLS formation. Further T and B cell receptor sequencing indicated a CXCL9-dependent promotion of antigen-specific responses within the tumor and TLS niche. Combined, these findings establish a tractable subcutaneous model of naturally arising tumor TLS and define the cellular and molecular networks that regulate their formation and function. This provides a platform to dissect how TLS develop and test strategies that promote TLS formation to enhance cancer therapy.

papers.title: Programmable bacterial vaccine vectors: A Design-Build-Control framework for precision immune engineering.
papers.authors: Bakhsh M, Kwon J, Haq IU, Riaz J, Kim CM, Lee JH.
papers.abstract: Live bacterial vectors combine intrinsic adjuvanticity, mucosal targeting, and programmable antigen delivery within a single engineerable chassis, yet their development has historically relied on empirical attenuation rather than systematic design. We present a Design-Build-Control framework, adapted from synthetic biology paradigms, that reframes bacterial vector engineering as a unified biotechnological problem. Design principles govern trade-offs among safety, immunogenicity, tissue tropism, and route of administration. Build-stage strategies translate these principles into genetically stable vector platforms through attenuation, balanced-lethal systems, and antibiotic-free plasmid maintenance. Control-stage tools, including inducible promoters, quorum-sensing circuits, and kill switches, enable dynamic regulation of vector behavior within the host. We apply this framework across major platform classes, including live attenuated Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, probiotic chassis, and non-replicating systems such as outer membrane vesicles, bacterial ghosts, and spores, and examine how biomaterial-based formulation, including encapsulation and mucoadhesive coatings, extends engineering control into manufacturing and delivery. We evaluate translational determinants, including genetic stability, environmental containment, and regulatory compliance, alongside applications spanning infectious disease, oncology, and veterinary medicine. We further assess the emerging role of artificial intelligence in bacterial-vector design, distinguishing established computational applications, experimentally validated approaches, and prospective uses that still require experimental validation. By integrating advances in synthetic biology, biomaterials, and computational design, this review presents programmable bacterial vectors as an emerging biotechnology platform and proposes a Design-Build-Control (DBC) framework for systematically evaluating biosafety, manufacturability, and clinical translation.

papers.title: MRI-Based Radiomics Predicts FAP Expression and Immunosuppressive Tumor Microenvironment in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Gao R, Han G, Wang Q, Zhang M, Yin F.
papers.abstract: Purpose To develop a Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) -based radiomics-clinical model for noninvasive prediction of fibroblast activation protein (FAP) expression in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and to explore its association with tumor microenvironment (TME) characteristics and potential immunotherapy response. Patients and methods This retrospective study included 104 patients with HCC from the Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University, 31 external MRI cases from The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA), and 363 transcriptomic profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Immunohistochemistry (IHC) assessed FAP expression. Tumor regions were manually segmented, and radiomics features were extracted using PyRadiomics. Multiple machine learning classifiers were used to construct and validate models for predicting FAP expression. Logistic regression was selected for its balanced performance between the training and validation cohorts, with the smallest area under the curve (AUC) difference among the five machine-learning algorithms. A radiomics-clinical combined model was further developed by integrating the radscore with clinical indicators. Radiogenomic analysis explored radscore-related transcriptomic features and immune infiltration characteristics. Results In the validation cohort, the AUC values of the intratumoral, peritumoral, and intratumoral + peritumoral radiomics models were 0.757, 0.502, and 0.784, respectively. The intratumoral + peritumoral model also achieved a sensitivity of 0.692 and a specificity of 0.788, indicating the best overall discriminatory performance among the three models. The radiomics-clinical combined model integrating the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), prognostic nutritional index (PNI), and radscore achieved an AUC of 0.816 in the validation cohort. Radscore-related transcriptomic modules identified 10 hub genes for risk stratification. Patients in the high-risk group exhibited a more pronounced immunosuppressive TME and poorer predicted benefit from immunotherapy. Conclusion The MRI-based radiomics-clinical model effectively predicted FAP expression in HCC. Radscore reflected FAP-related immunosuppressive TME remodeling and may provide insights into potential immunotherapy response stratification, which requires further validation in independent immunotherapy-treated cohorts.

papers.title: Human Organoids in Infectious Disease Research: From Host-Pathogen Interactions to Vaccine Development.
papers.authors: Zielinska D, Fol M, Druszczynska M.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Human organoids have emerged as physiologically relevant models bridging conventional two-dimensional cultures and animal models. This review summarizes advances in their application to infectious disease modeling and vaccine research, with emphasis on host-pathogen interactions, immune responses, and translational potential. Methods : A narrative review was conducted using targeted searches of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and ScienceDirect. Publications from January 2000 to June 2026 were considered, and relevant evidence was qualitatively synthesized according to established applications, proof-of-concept studies, and prospective uses. Results: Human organoids have advanced the study of viral, bacterial, parasitic, and fungal infections by enabling investigation of pathogen entry, tissue tropism, barrier integrity, and immune responses in human-relevant systems. Immune and tonsil-derived organoids have also demonstrated applications in evaluating vaccine-induced immunity, comparing vaccine formulations, investigating mechanisms of immunogenicity, and identifying potential correlates of protection. Integration with single-cell and spatial omics, advanced imaging, and computational approaches is further expanding their utility. However, incomplete immune and vascular complexity, inter-model variability, limited standardization, scalability constraints, and insufficient validation against in vivo and clinical outcomes remain important challenges. Conclusions: Human organoids represent complementary human-relevant platforms with substantial potential for mechanistic and translational vaccinology. Further standardization and prospective validation are required to establish their predictive value for vaccine development.

papers.title: Longitudinal BCR repertoire dynamics reveal the evolution of broadly binding antibodies following heterologous SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and breakthrough infection: a single-donor case study.
papers.authors: Qiao R, Chen X, Zhang X, Shao Y, Zhang L, Yang L, Mi Y, Lu Y, Li J, Chen Y, Yu H, Wang Y, Zhao X, Wang P.
papers.abstract: Continued SARS-CoV-2 antigenic drift and the persistent risk of zoonotic sarbecovirus spillover highlight the need for broadly protective countermeasures. Here, we longitudinally profiled the B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire of a single volunteer who received heterologous booster vaccination followed by Omicron BF.7 breakthrough infection, integrating bulk BCR sequencing with single B-cell culture and antibody binding analysis. Breakthrough infection was associated with broadened serum neutralization across SARS-CoV-2 variants and related sarbecoviruses, consistent with recall of antibodies targeting conserved epitopes. Repertoire analysis revealed stage-specific remodeling, with high-affinity binding antibodies shifting from an IGHV1-46-enriched profile after vaccination to preferential representation of IGHV3-30-3 after infection. Isolated monoclonal antibodies exhibited nanomolar-to-picomolar binding affinities to diverse animal-derived sarbecovirus spikes, with broad binding commonly, but not universally, associated with CDRH3 lengths of 14-16 amino acids. Phylogenetic and sequence analyses defined divergent evolutionary trajectories for IGHV1-46 and IGHV3-30-3 lineages, highlighting candidate genetic features that warrant validation in larger cohorts. Together, these findings describe how sequential heterologous antigen exposures can reshape the humoral repertoire in one individual and generate hypotheses for future pan-sarbecovirus antibody and vaccine studies.

papers.title: Addressing complex autofluorescence signatures in solid tissue samples to enhance full spectrum flow cytometry of non-immune cells.
papers.authors: Gkantsinikoudi C, Terranova-Barberio M, Dufton N.
papers.abstract: FSFC is an emerging technology that can greatly enhance our understanding of the single-cell proteomic landscape. We demonstrate that this application is applicable to cells derived from solid tissues which have traditionally been hampered by their complex autofluorescence signatures and lack of optimized tools for non-immune cells. We present a protocol and discuss key controls that minimize the impact of unmixing errors, enabling us to resolve multiple EC subpopulations isolated from different tissues in models of chronic tissue injury. Research topics vascular biology, cell heterogeneity, full spectrum flow cytometry.

papers.title: NECTIN-4 orchestrates macrophage-mediated tumor plasticity in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Acharya SS, Paul S, Viswanathan S, Bajoria AA, Patnaik S.
papers.abstract: Tumor associated macrophages (TAM) are key regulator of the tumor microenvironment (TME), however, the upstream factors that contribute to the polarization and functional reprogramming in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remain largely unclear. This study evaluates the role of Nectin-4 in modulating tumor-immune interactions and its impact on OSCC progression. Detailed transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-OSCC dataset revealed that high NECTIN-4 expression was associated with enrichment of pathways involved in epithelial mesenchymal transition (EMT), angiogenesis, and stemness, and was inversely correlated with inflammatory signaling and immune infiltration.Additionally, single-cell transcriptomic analyses demonstrated an increase in macrophages, solely focused on the stroma, in Nectin-4 high tumors. Consistently, SCC-9 cells exhibited high levels of Nectin-4 and Nectin-4 enriched conditioned media (CM) derived from SCC-9 cells induced polarization of THP-1 monocytes toward a TAMs-like phenotype, characterized by increased CD163 expression and elevated secretion of immunomodulatory cytokines such as CCL-2. Co-culture of TAMs with SCC-9 cells promoted tumor aggressiveness, as evidenced by increased expression of EMT markers (E-cadherin, N-cadherin, vimentin) and stem cell markers (CD133, OCT4), invasion and cytoskeletal remodeling. These TAMs also enhanced angiogenesis in cancer cells by increasing the expression of VEGF-A, angiopoietin-1 (Ang-1), and TGF-β, along with in ovo neovascularization and promoting endothelial tube formation. Overall, the study identifies Nectin-4 as a key mediator of tumor-immune crosstalk in OSCC, driving macrophage enrichment, immune suppression and pro-tumorigenic signaling. Therefore, targeting Nectin-4 signaling could be a new approach to restore anti-tumor immunity and inhibit OSCC progression.

papers.title: A Clickable Phospholipid Platform for Ultra-Fast and Preferential Azide Labeling of Cancer Cells and Antibody Recruitment.
papers.authors: Gonzales L, Antoine-Brunet T, Beauvais B, Flon V, Carty M, Mamputu S, Schlichter A, Vertueux S, Haefele A, Bailly L, Petit E, Besson T, Renard PY, Berthet N, Balieu S.
papers.abstract: In this study, we present an innovative synthetic strategy to form clickable glycerophospholipidic species such as phosphatidylcholine, phosphatidylethanolamine, phosphatidylserine or phosphatidylglycerol from the corresponding clickable phosphatidic acids based on microwave irradiation to functionalize the phosphoester polar headgroup into phosphodiester, while the modification of the glycerol core allows the preservation of the main biological properties compared to the native biomolecules. This new phosphatidylethanolamine probe enabled ultra-fast and selective targeting of cancer cells while sparing healthy cells, establishing a novel strategy for tumor-specific targeting. The relevance of our method is robustly demonstrated through comparative analyses across various cancer and normal cell lines, revealing consistent and significant differences in glycerophospholipid uptake and efficacy. Quantitative validation was achieved using flow cytometry, providing high-throughput, single-cell-resolution data. Notably, we show that our strategy enabled in cellulo click-chemistry with antigens recognized by antibodies from patient-derived sera, underscoring their immunological relevance and potential for clinical translation. Importantly, cytotoxicity assays confirmed the absence of adverse effects on healthy cells within the operational range of the probes, highlighting their potential for therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Accelerating Molecular Dynamics with Hydrogen Mass Repartitioning to Prioritize Immunogenic Neoantigens for Cancer Vaccines through Peptide HLA Binding Free Energy Calculations
papers.authors: Amaya-Ramirez, D. A.; Florez-Suarez, J. B.; Mora-Fonseca, J. D.; Parra-Lopez, C. A.
papers.abstract: Personalized neoantigen based vaccines have progressed from concept to clinical evidence for some of the most aggressive human tumors, yet a key challenge remains: determining which candidates should be prioritized for vaccine inclusion. Public neoantigens, shared across tumor subtypes and patient populations, offer potential as off the shelf candidates for broad spectrum immunotherapy. Candidate selection relies on in silico pipelines that estimate binding; however, binding affinity alone is an imperfect marker of immunogenicity. Molecular dynamics (MD) combined with endpoint free energy methods estimates binding free energy directly from simulated trajectories, and hydrogen mass repartitioning (HMR) mitigates the computational cost of hydrogen involving bond vibrations. This study assessed whether HMR accelerated MD can prioritize immunogenic neoantigens through peptide HLA binding free energy calculations and quantified the trade off between accuracy and computational cost. Ten immunogenic public neoantigens (seven paired with their wild type counterparts and three frameshift neoantigens analyzed as unpaired references) were modeled in complex with their HLA I alleles, built de novo using AlphaFold3 and propagated with a 4 fs HMR time step. Mean binding free energy was computed across ten replicas per complex, and each SNV pair was scored concordant with experimental data when the neoantigen formed a more favorable complex than its wild type. Free energies were recomputed at 100 to 500 ns to identify the shortest trajectory preserving reliable ranking. Free energy calculations reproduced experimental concordance for six of seven SNV pairs and were inconclusive for TP53 R8H. Frameshift neoantigens yielded comparable values. Most complexes retained both peptide termini anchored to the HLA groove throughout, and RMSD and RMSF metrics agreed with one another and with the free energy rankings. The PIK3CA E545K (E11K) pair showed the most distinctive signature: the peptides engaged the groove almost identically over P1 to P8, with the entire difference confined to the C terminal pocket, where loss of the wild type's anchor also disrupted its backbone anchor. This pair showed the largest free energy separation in the panel, and restricting analysis to bound frames confirmed a substantial electrostatic and van der Waals advantage favoring the neoantigen. These findings support HMR accelerated binding free energy MD as a practical refinement step for neoantigen prioritization and its application to assessing public neoantigens for cancer vaccine design.

papers.title: Verbascoside inhibits ovarian cancer proliferation via IRAK4-CXCL5 axis-mediated suppression of neutrophil infiltration and neutrophil extracellular trap formation.
papers.authors: Ren Y, Yu T, Wang Z, Ma Y, He J.
papers.abstract: The specific mechanisms of verbascoside (VB) in ovarian cancer (OC) remain insufficient. This study aimed to explore the anti-tumor mechanisms of VB in OC, focusing on its ability to modulate the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), particularly through targeting neutrophil infiltration and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs). The anti-tumor and anti-NETosis efficacy of VB was evaluated in vivo using subcutaneous, orthotopic, and pulmonary metastasis mouse models of OC. Microproteomics and bioinformatics analysis identified the direct molecular target of VB and the key neutrophil chemoattractant. The underlying mechanisms were validated in vitro and in vivo (using SKOV3, ID8, and neutrophils), alongside loss-of-function approaches. The combination of VB with anti-PD-1 immunotherapy was also assessed. VB inhibited OC proliferation/metastasis, promoted anti-tumor immunity, and suppressed neutrophil infiltration and NETosis. Neutrophil depletion attenuated VB's anti-metastatic effect. Microproteomics and bioinformatics screening identified IRAK4 as a direct molecular target of VB and CXCL5 as a key neutrophil chemoattractant. SPR confirmed the direct binding between VB and IRAK4, and molecular docking revealed specific hydrogen bond interactions. Mechanistically, VB treatment or IRAK4 knockdown suppressed CXCL5 expression, and consequently reduced neutrophil infiltration and NETosis. Consistently, CXCL5 overexpression abrogated the inhibitory effects of VB on neutrophil NETosis and recruitment. Furthermore, VB synergized with anti-PD-1 therapy, thereby achieving superior tumor growth inhibition, reduced Ki67 expression, and enhanced CD8 + T cell infiltration. In conclusion, VB exerts potent anti-tumor effects in OC by targeting the IRAK4/CXCL5 axis, thereby inhibiting neutrophil infiltration and NETosis, reshaping the immunosuppressive TME, and restoring anti-tumor immunity.

papers.title: Diverse patterns of transcriptional regulation and epigenetic reprogramming within PMDs contribute to ESCC progression by regulating EMT and immunosuppression.
papers.authors: Huang Y, Xue J, Luan X, Zhang H, Ding J, Xu J, Zhao Z, Li Q, Tu K, Wang X, Ge W.
papers.abstract: Partially methylated domains (PMDs) represent extensive genome-wide hypomethylated regions that drive genomic instability and proto-oncogene activation. However, their complex regulatory influence on tumor-specific transcriptional networks remains largely elusive. In this study, we developed a robust computational pipeline to characterize aberrant PMD landscapes across pan-cancer. We specifically focused on the epigenetic features associated with transcriptional dysregulation in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). By analyzing gene expression patterns, we classified PMDs into four distinct classes and revealed that several immunosuppressive genes were recurrently activated within Tumor-PMDs across various cancers. While these PMDs were generally marked by elevated repressive H3K27me3 and diminished active histone modifications, the activated genes within them paradoxically exhibited a precise, localized enrichment of H3K9ac and H3K27ac near their transcription start sites (TSSs). This localized epigenetic rewiring suggests a potential correlation where collaborative histone modification landscapes may shape oncogenic chromatin remodeling to license transcriptional dysregulation. Furthermore, we identified a robust co-expression axis between the prognostic gene ATP6V0D2 and established immune checkpoints ( HAVCR2 , TDO2 ). Elevated ATP6V0D2 expression was found to potentially contribute to ESCC progression and poor prognosis by activating the complement system and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) pathways. Capitalizing on these findings, virtual screening and in vitro validation suggested that caffeic acid could act as a potential ATP6V0D2-binding compound, effectively suppressing the migration and viability of ESCC cells. This study further nominates caffeic acid as a candidate compound for further mechanistic and therapeutic investigation in ESCC.

papers.title: Interferon-Associated Inflammatory Remodeling and Oxidative Metabolic Repression Define the Skeletal Muscle Transcriptomic Landscape of δ-Sarcoglycan Deficiency.
papers.authors: Cancino-Bello A, Hernández-Somilleda M, Bahena-Culhuac E, García-González EG, Hernández-Hernández O, Coral-Vázquez RM, Hernández-Hernández JM.
papers.abstract: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy R6, formerly LGMD2F, is caused by mutations in the δ-sarcoglycan ( Sgcd ) gene and is characterized by progressive skeletal muscle degeneration. Although loss of δ-SG protein compromises sarcolemma stability, how δ-sarcoglycan deficiency reshapes inflammatory and metabolic gene programs across distinct skeletal muscles remains incompletely defined. Here, we profiled soleus and extensor digitorum longus (EDL) muscles from wild-type and Sgcd -/- mice treated with vehicle or (-)-epicatechin, a dietary flavanol with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, using bulk RNA sequencing, pathway analysis, immune-cell deconvolution, and RT-qPCR validation. δ-sarcoglycan deficiency produced broad transcriptional remodeling while preserving baseline muscle-type identity. Across soleus and EDL, the dystrophic transcriptome was marked by interferon-associated inflammatory remodeling together with repression of oxidative and mitochondrial metabolic programs. Within this shared disease state, soleus displayed a stronger induced inflammatory component, including innate-sensing and macrophage-linked features. Computational deconvolution, which estimates immune-cell proportions from bulk transcriptomes (quanTIseq and mMCP-counter), supported genotype-dependent shifts in immune-cell signatures, with concordant monocyte/macrophage signals. Finally, (-)-epicatechin produced context-dependent transcriptional effects and attenuated a defined interferon/innate-sensing module in dystrophic soleus, as supported by RNA-seq and RT-qPCR. Together, these findings establish inflammatory remodeling with a prominent interferon component and oxidative metabolic repression as central transcriptional features of δ-sarcoglycan-deficient skeletal muscle, while revealing an amplified innate-sensing and immune-enriched module in dystrophic soleus that remains transcriptionally responsive to (-)-epicatechin treatment.

papers.title: Patients with cyclops syndrome exhibit elevated synovial fluid interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α) levels and disorganized collagen remodelling within the lesion: A histological and molecular study.
papers.authors: Morici L, Tscholl PM, Skau EL, Eyer K, Clerc L, Gauthier M, Nikolic I.
papers.abstract: Purpose Cyclops syndrome is a clinically relevant complication of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction characterized by the formation of a fibrotic nodule (cyclops lesion) that causes extension loss and often requires a revision surgery. Biological mechanisms underlying lesion formation remain poorly understood. The purpose of this study is to characterize the tissue architecture, cellular composition, inflammatory profile and single-cell cytokine secretion patterns of patient-derived biopsies to gain mechanistic insight into disease pathogenesis. Methods This prospective observational comparative study included three patient groups: patients undergoing revision surgery for cyclops syndrome ( n = 10), patients undergoing primary ACL reconstruction with subsequent successful recovery ( n = 10) and patients undergoing revision surgery for ACL graft re-rupture ( n = 2). Tissue biopsies and synovial fluid samples were collected intraoperatively and used for histological, cellular and cytokine analyses. Results Histological analyses demonstrated that cyclops lesions exhibited disorganized collagen architecture, neovascularization and infiltration of immune cells. Flow cytometry identified activated FAP + CD54 + fibroblasts as the predominant cell population (~80%), accompanied by CD206 + pro-fibrotic macrophages. Synovial fluid from cyclops patients contained significantly elevated IL-6 and TNF-α concentrations, whereas IL-1β levels did not differ among the groups. Looking at the cells, single-cell cytokine secretion profiles revealed detectable IL-6 secretion in up to 11% of cells, while IL-1β, TNF-α and TGF-β secretion were not detected, indicating that at least the source of TNF-α has to be found elsewhere. Conclusions Our preliminary data from a small patient cohort show that cyclops syndrome may be observed as an active fibro-inflammatory process rather than a purely mechanical post-operative complication. Patient-derived samples revealed persistent inflammatory activity characterized by immune cell infiltration, elevated levels of pro-inflammatory mediators, and sustained activation of fibroblasts. The absence of detectable TGF-β secretion despite established fibrosis suggests that lesion persistence may be maintained through alternative fibrotic pathways (non-TGF-β/non-canonical pathways), which requires further investigation. Level of evidence N/A.

papers.title: From MAPK Reactivation to Response: Clinical Approaches Targeting BRAF/MEK Resistance in Melanoma.
papers.authors: Topcu TO, Dinçkal Ç, Eroglu Z.
papers.abstract: Resistance to BRAF/MEK inhibition remains the central therapeutic challenge in BRAF mutant melanoma. Although combined MAPK-targeted therapy induces rapid and often dramatic tumor responses, most patients ultimately develop progressive disease. Over the past decade, translational studies have fundamentally changed our understanding of this process. Resistance is now recognized not as a single genomic event, but as a biologically heterogeneous and adaptive phenomenon involving tumor cell plasticity, microenvironmental remodeling, and immune evolution. This evolving framework has important clinical implications. Recent randomized sequencing clinical trials have shifted treatment paradigms toward a front-line immune checkpoint blockade for many patients. Similarly, triplet approaches combining MAPK inhibition with immunotherapy have shown heterogenous results on progression-free survival benefit and durable overall survival benefits remain uncertain. At the same time, therapeutic options after progression are rapidly expanding and include ERK inhibitors, next-generation pan-RAF inhibitors, vertical pathway targeting strategies, and emerging approaches directed against persister-cell biology and adaptive resistance states. In this review, we integrate current insights from genomic, transcriptomic, single-cell, and spatial studies with the most relevant clinical trial data to provide a contemporary framework for understanding resistance to MAPK-targeted therapy in melanoma.
