papers.title: Wnt10b is required for the increase in cancellous bone caused by oxidized phospholipids blockade.
papers.authors: Palmieri M, Nookaew I, Thostenson JD, Joseph T, Bustamante-Gomez C, Delgado-Calle J, Goellner JJ, O'Brien CA, Almeida M, Ambrogini E.
papers.abstract: Oxidized phospholipids containing phosphatidylcholine (PC-OxPLs), present on oxidized low-density lipoproteins (OxLDL) and apoptotic cells, are pathogenic in osteoporosis. PC-OxPLs are bound by the IgM E06 antibody, which blocks their deleterious effects. Overexpression of the antigen-binding domain of E06 (E06-scFv) increases bone mass in 6-month-old mice and attenuates high fat diet- and age-induced bone loss by increasing osteoblast number and function. The mechanisms mediating the anabolic effect of oxidized phospholipids blockade are unclear. In previous work, we showed that E06-scFv upregulates the expression of Wnt10b and Wnt signaling in vivo. We report herein that the bulk of Wnt10b in the bone microenvironment originates from osteoblast lineage cells. OxLDL decreases the expression of Wnt10b and Wnt target genes in osteoblastic cells, and single cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) of mesenchymal cells reveals an increase in Wnt10b and Wnt target genes in pre-osteoblasts and osteoblasts of E06-scFv transgenic mice compared to WT. Loss of Wnt10b prevents the increases in BMD by DXA and in vertebral and femoral cancellous bone in 6-month-old E06-scFv transgenic male mice, and attenuates these increases in female mice. Collectively, these findings indicate that oxidized phospholipids decrease bone mass, at least in part, by suppressing Wnt10b.

papers.title: Site-Specific Cutaneous Inflammation: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications.
papers.authors: Marella S, Shao S, Tsoi LC, Naik S, Andersen B, Kong HH, Plikus MV, Haniffa M, Gudjonsson JE.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory skin diseases exhibit prominent anatomical distribution patterns that have long guided clinical diagnosis, yet the biological mechanisms underlying site specificity remain incompletely defined. These regional predilections arise from structural, immunological, and microbial heterogeneity across human skin. Epidermal barrier architecture, which varies substantially between body sites, including 10- to 100-fold differences in stratum corneum thickness, and prevalence and types of hair follicles and glands, creates distinct microenvironments that shape resident immune populations, microbial communities and host antimicrobial defenses. The skin harbors an estimated 20 billion tissue-resident memory T cells that persist within anatomically restricted niches, providing a mechanistic basis for disease recurrence at the same sites. In parallel, the skin microbiome contributes to regional specialization by forming distinct communities in oily, moist, and dry regions, which are disrupted in disease-specific ways, while environmental exposures such as ultraviolet radiation, mechanical stress, and humidity further reinforce regional variation. Recent advances in single-cell and spatial transcriptomic technologies have enabled inflammatory responses to be mapped with high precision, allowing detailed interrogation of site-specific cellular interactions and signaling pathways across the skin. Collectively, these findings support a unifying model in which regional tissue properties and local immune ecosystems shape disease-specific inflammatory circuits, accounting for the anatomical predilection of inflammatory diseases and underscoring the importance of tissue context for precision therapeutics.
papers.venue: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology

papers.title: Ethmoid bone marrow region modulates lymphoid activation and differentiation with distinct myeloid profile in neuroinflammation
papers.authors: Laaker, C. J.; Kovacs, K. G.; Madrid, A.; Herbath, M.; Vi, K.; Port, J.; Vrba, S. M.; Limkar, A. R.; Ordonez, S. F. W.; Coogan, S.; Priyathilaka, T. T.; Hsu, M.; Sandor, M.; Fabry, Z.
papers.abstract: The skull bone marrow axis has recently emerged as an important source of immune cells during neuroinflammation, including in the experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) , the mouse model of multiple sclerosis. The cribriform plate bone marrow (cpBM), is a portion of the ethmoid bone of the skull of mice, and is positioned next to nasal regions. At the cribriform plate olfactory nerves pass through the skull and recent evidence supports that it represents an important immune niche with links to CSF outflow and connections to cpBM. Previous data supports cellular composition of the ethmoid bone marrow in mice is altered in neuroinflammation suggesting it senses inflammatory cues, but the exact nature of these changes is still unclear. Here using scRNAseq and flow cytometry of the ethmoid bone marrow region we test how the region responds to EAE. In addition we also compare the cpBM region with systemic bone marrow in the femur to understand region specific differences. We report that neuroinflammation creates a regulatory response at these sites and implicates the cpBM in controlling these effects. A better understanding of the cribriform niche may offer new treatments for neuroinflammatory disease

papers.title: Nanomedicine strategies for overcoming cellular and microenvironmental barriers to cuproptosis-based cancer therapy.
papers.authors: Ge L, Wang D, Tang BZ.
papers.abstract: Cuproptosis, a copper-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by mitochondrial proteotoxic stress, has emerged as a promising vulnerability for cancer therapy. However, its therapeutic translation is limited by cellular and microenvironmental barriers that restrict effective copper delivery, intracellular copper accumulation, mitochondrial engagement, and antitumor immune activation. This review summarizes the molecular basis of cuproptosis, including copper homeostasis, mitochondrial copper trafficking, lipoylated protein aggregation, and iron‑sulfur cluster disruption. We then examine how dysregulated copper transport, glutathione-mediated buffering, metabolic reprogramming, hypoxia, and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments attenuate cuproptosis-based treatment. Focusing on these barriers, we discuss nanomedicine strategies designed to modulate copper homeostasis, deplete glutathione, reprogram tumor metabolism, alleviate hypoxia, and enhance antitumor immunity. These multifunctional platforms can enable tumor-selective copper delivery and spatiotemporally controlled activation while integrating complementary therapeutic modalities. Finally, we highlight unresolved challenges, including incomplete mechanistic understanding, tumor heterogeneity, insufficient real-time monitoring of cuproptosis, and the need to balance therapeutic efficacy with systemic copper toxicity. A systems-level integration of nanomedicine, mechanistic biology, and computational design may support the development of safer, more precise, and clinically actionable cuproptosis-based cancer therapies.

papers.title: Single-cell dissection of self-derived versus donor-derived T cell exhaustion niches in patients with acute myeloid leukemia.
papers.authors: Yu CZ, Chen YL, Zhang XH, Xu LP, Wang Y, Chen H, Chen YH, Wang FR, Sun YQ, Zhang YY, Lv M, Mo XD, Cheng YF, Liu KY, Zhao XS, Sun XQ, Zhao XY, Huang XJ, Chang YJ.
papers.abstract: Relapse remains the main cause of death in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and T cell exhaustion is related to relapse in both non-allografting and allografting settings. However, differences in exhausted T cells (T ex ) across different disease contexts remain incompletely understood. We performed single-cell RNA and T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing to systematically characterize T ex in AML. Both self-derived T ex in non-transplantation and donor-derived T ex in post-transplant settings express similar surface markers, but NFATC1/NFATC3 with downstream TOX and EOMES are enriched in self-derived T ex , while NFATC2 with downstream NR4A2 predominates in donor-derived T ex . Both self-derived and donor-derived bone marrow environments are enriched with immunosuppressive monocytes, dendritic cells, and regulatory T cells. Cell-cell interaction analysis reveals strong direct and indirect interactions between T ex and AML cells, primarily mediated by galectin-9, MIF, and TGF-β1. These findings highlight differences and commonalities between self-derived and donor-derived T ex and identify potential therapeutic targets for reversing T ex in AML.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomic and immune microenvironment analyses reveal a TIMP1-associated OLFM4⁺ tumor epithelial program linked to colorectal cancer progression and immune evasion.
papers.authors: Leng R, Cui X, Wu X, Zhao Y, Sun L, Jin H, Li W, Lin J.
papers.abstract: Background Colorectal cancer (CRC) is characterized by marked epithelial heterogeneity and dynamic tumor-microenvironment interactions. However, epithelial states associated with progression across the normal-adenoma-carcinoma sequence remain incompletely defined. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing data from normal colorectal mucosa, adenoma, and tumor tissues were analyzed using inferCNV, Monocle, Slingshot, CytoTRACE, CellChat, and SCENIC. An OLFM4⁺ tumor cell risk score (OTRS) was constructed using Cox and LASSO regression, and TIMP1 function was evaluated in vitro. Results Eight major cell types and nine tumor epithelial subtypes were identified. C3 OLFM4⁺ cells showed elevated transcriptional activity, stemness, metabolic activity, and greater representation in carcinoma than adenoma tissues. Trajectory analyses positioned these cells in an early-to-intermediate transitional state. CellChat predicted prominent fibroblast-C3 OLFM4⁺ interactions, including a putative WNT2B-FZD/LRP axis, while SCENIC identified XBP1, NFIA, PPARG, HDAC2, and UBE2K as subtype-associated regulators. The C3 OLFM4⁺-derived OTRS stratified prognosis; high OTRS was associated with poorer survival, macrophage-enriched infiltration, higher stromal, immune, and TIDE scores, and differential predicted drug sensitivity. TIMP1 knockdown suppressed malignant behaviors in CRC cells. Conclusion C3 OLFM4⁺ cells represent a stem-like, metabolically active tumor epithelial state associated with CRC progression, fibroblast-derived WNT signaling, immune-evasion-related features, and unfavorable prognosis. The OTRS model may support prognostic and therapeutic assessment, while TIMP1 contributes to malignant CRC cell behavior.

papers.title: Clonotype specificity distinguishes epitope-tailored and permissive somatic hypermutation
papers.authors: Rao, V. N.; Bonnettaz, B.; Civljak, A.; Abbad, A.; Krammer, F.; Coelho, C. H.; Bajic, G.
papers.abstract: Identifying antibody features that reliably encode epitope specificity poses a major barrier towards modeling antigen-antibody interactions. Affinity maturation offers a unique opportunity to probe the molecular basis of antigen-antibody interactions by revealing how individual somatic hypermutations (SHM) refine antibody binding. Using SARS-CoV-2 spike-specific germinal center B-cell repertoires, we show that antibodies harboring multiple SHMs that are restricted to their respective clonotypes (clonotype-restricted SHMs) preferentially recognize cryptic epitopes. We structurally characterized three such antibodies: two recognized a cryptic epitope on the receptor-binding domain whereas a third bound an N-terminal domain epitope that is almost entirely occluded in prefusion spike. In contrast, SHMs shared across multiple clonotypes using the same V gene recur across antibodies targeting diverse antigens but generally fail to enhance affinity when introduced into diverse antibody backgrounds. Together, these findings define a spectrum of SHM behavior, distinguishing epitope-tailored mutations from broadly recurrent but largely permissive substitutions.

papers.title: Antigen-aware TCR embeddings reveal conserved immune patterns for personalized immune monitoring
papers.authors: Pan, M.; Hu, J.; Wang, Y. T.; Tan, Y.; Hu, H.; Yang, Z.; Fleming, J.; Pang, Y.; Li, B.
papers.abstract: T cell receptor (TCR) repertoires are highly individualized, while technical variation further complicates comparisons across individuals and cohorts. Here, we present TCRmeta, an antigen-aware framework that integrates population-scale repertoire relationships with experimentally defined antigen specificity to establish a shared space for repertoire analysis. TCRmeta predicted mutation-induced changes and captured antigen-related relationships in TCR specificity. Despite extensive sequence diversity, TCRmeta revealed a conserved repertoire landscape, enabling construction of a healthy reference for quantifying repertoire dispersal. Across cohorts, aging was associated with conserved V gene changes and progressive dispersal, with greater dispersal in CMV-positive individuals. Longitudinal analysis showed that repertoires progressively shifted toward the healthy reference following bone marrow transplantation or antiretroviral therapy. To directly compare repertoires in TCRmeta space, we developed Energy Shift, a pairwise measure robust to technical variation and HLA background while remaining sensitive to biological differences. Together, TCRmeta enables quantitative cross-individual and longitudinal immune monitoring.

papers.title: Heterogeneity of HCMV-Specific CD8+ T Cells is Established Early in Infection, Clonally Encoded, and Stable Over Time
papers.authors: Klebanoff, S. D.; Lawrance, M.; O'Brien, K.; Smithmyer, M. E.; Speak, C.; Codd, A. S.; Ford, E. S.; Koelle, D. M.; Buckner, J. H.; Newell, E. W.; Campbell, D. J.
papers.abstract: Human cytomegalovirus (CMV) elicits lifelong memory T cell responses of striking size and phenotypic diversity, but how these diverse responses are established during acute infection and evolve over decades of chronic stimulation is poorly understood. We tracked CD8+ T cells specific for the viral antigens pp65 and IE1 by single-cell RNAseq, TCRseq, and CITEseq over a period of 16 months in a newly seroconverted donor, and in five latently infected donors over intervals ranging from 4.5 to 12.5 years. We found that individual T cell clones exhibited distinct, specificity-dependent transcriptional profiles, with pp65-specific cells skewed toward central memory phenotypes and IE1-specific cells enriched for effector and chronically activated states. Among pp65-specific T cells we identified a CMC1-expressing state not previously described in virus-specific T cells that shares transcriptional features with exhausted T cells in human tumors yet remains phenotypically stable and clonally intact for over a decade of viral latency. Distinct clonal phenotypes arose during acute infection and were remarkably stable during viral latency, and these phenotypes tracked with relative TCR avidity and TCR sequence. Our findings reveal that the phenotypic diversity of the human CMV-specific CD8+ T cell response is organized at the level of individual clones, with distinct functional identities established during acute infection and preserved with striking fidelity across decades of viral latency and chronic antigen exposure.

papers.title: Single-cell profiling of physically interacting immune cells using image-guided sorting
papers.authors: Kang, N.; Kim, C.; Scriba, T. J.; Peters, B.; Burel, J. G.
papers.abstract: Single-cell transcriptomics of cell-cell complexes offers key insights into in vivo immune interactions, yet distinguishing true physical contacts from artifacts remains challenging. Here, we integrated spectral imaging cell sorting with physical cell deconvolution to separate circulating T cell-monocyte doublets from tuberculosis patients into physically interacting (in-contact) and non-interacting (coincidental) populations. Single-cell sequencing of individual cell partners revealed that physical contact is associated with robust signatures distinct from singlets, including unidirectional monocyte-to-T cell RNA transfer, heightened metabolic activity and T cell cytotoxicity, and a trend toward antigen-specific enrichment. These signatures spanned all T cell and monocyte subpopulations, reflecting a global program of T cell-monocyte engagement. Coincidental doublets displayed intermediate transcriptional profiles between singlet and in-contact states, suggesting the presence of recently disrupted or forming physical pairs. This framework provides high-fidelity deconvolution of cellular interactions, uncovering signatures governing T cell-monocyte communication in human disease.

papers.title: Single-Cell Multiomics Integration Reveals Cell Trajectories and Regulatory Networks in Breast Cancer Progression.
papers.authors: Jin X, Ma C, Xin H, Liu Y, Sun C.
papers.abstract: Background Breast cancer is a molecularly heterogeneous disease encompassing distinct subtypes with divergent prognoses and therapeutic responses. Despite extensive bulk genomic characterization, the single-cell transcriptional trajectories, chromatin regulatory landscapes, and intercellular communication networks that drive breast cancer progression from luminal to mesenchymal states remain incompletely understood. Emerging evidence implicates gut microbiome dysbiosis as a systemic modulator of breast cancer risk, immune regulation, and treatment response; however, its coordinated characterization alongside high-resolution single-cell profiling has not been undertaken. Integrating single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with chromatin accessibility profiling (scATAC-seq), cell-cell communication inference, and gut microbiome 16S rRNA analysis offers a comprehensive multilayered approach to dissecting both the intratumoral regulatory logic and the systemic microbial landscape of breast cancer progression. Methods We performed integrated multiomics analysis of 42,037 high-quality single cells from breast cancer patient samples obtained from the GEO database (GSE161529), encompassing tumor and adjacent normal tissue. scRNA-seq data were processed using Seurat v4.3.0 and Scanpy v1.9.1. Dimensionality reduction, Leiden clustering, differential expression analysis, pseudotime trajectory inference (Monocle3, scVelo, Slingshot), SCENIC regulon analysis, chromatin accessibility profiling, cell-cell communication inference (CellChat), and functional enrichment analysis were applied. Key marker genes were validated by quantitative RT-PCR in MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 cell lines. In parallel, gut microbiome 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing data from 599 matched breast cancer-healthy control pairs (266 genera, four BioProjects) were analyzed for alpha/beta diversity, differential genus abundance (Mann-Whitney U with Benjamini-Hochberg correction), genus co-occurrence networks, and random forest breast cancer classification. Results Unbiased clustering identified 12 observed cell populations spanning luminal (Luminal A, Luminal B), basal, HER2+, cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF), tumor-associated macrophage (TAM), CD8 T cell, regulatory T cell (Treg), NK cell, B cell, endothelial, and pericyte compartments. Quality control confirmed robust data quality with median 2400-3100 genes per cell and mitochondrial content below 20%. Pseudotime trajectory analysis revealed a continuous epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) spectrum with three divergent lineages: EMT, senescence, and immune activation branches. SCENIC identified SNAI1(+), ZEB1(+), and FOXM1(+) as the most differentially activated regulons in basal/mesenchymal cells. ATAC-seq chromatin accessibility profiling confirmed EMT transcription factor access through distal enhancers. CellChat identified TGF- β 1-TGFBR1 (CAF → tumor) and PD-L1-PD-1 (tumor → CD8 T cell) as dominant intercellular communication axes. Multiomics integration enhanced cell-type classification AUC from 0.76 (scRNA-seq alone) to 0.91 (full multiomics). EMT-high tumor status was associated with significantly inferior overall survival (HR = 2.14, p = 0.001). qRT-PCR validation confirmed ERBB2 enrichment in HER2+ lines and KRT5/VIM enrichment in basal/TNBC lines (all p p = 6.1 × 10 -4 ), significant community-level separation (Bray-Curtis PERMANOVA F = 30.2, p = 0.001), and nine differentially abundant genera including enriched Faecalitalea (log 2 F C = 1.44), Parasutterella (log 2 F C = 1.21), and Bacteroides (log 2 F C = 1.19). A random forest microbiome classifier achieved a cross-validated AUC of 0.79 (95% CI: 0.74-0.82), supporting the gut-breast axis as a systemic codeterminant of cancer state. Conclusions This integrated single-cell multiomics and gut microbiome atlas of breast cancer progression characterizes the transcriptional regulatory architecture driving cellular trajectory diversification, highlights SNAI1-ZEB1-FOXM1 coregulatory networks as candidate therapeutic targets, suggests that multiomics integration can enhance molecular stratification of breast cancer subtypes with clinical prognostic relevance, and identifies gut microbiome dysbiosis as a potential systemic dimension-characterized by loss of microbial diversity and enrichment of specific genera-as a systemic dimension of breast cancer pathobiology that warrants integration with intratumoral molecular profiling.

papers.title: Cell-free DNA fragmentomics and epigenomic profiling in hematologic malignancies: current evidence, translational limitations, and future directions.
papers.authors: El-Sehrawy AAMA, Abdullah SS, Mamedova G, Rizaev J, Abdelrahim IM, Srivastav SK, Khaleel ZT, Jabir MS, Bainsal N, Smerat A.
papers.abstract: Mutation-based liquid biopsy supports diagnosis and disease monitoring in hematologic malignancies, but interpretation of plasma variants may be complicated by clonal hematopoiesis, treatment-related changes, and nonmalignant blood-cell turnover. This structured narrative review evaluates whether cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentomics, DNA methylation, and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) provide complementary information beyond mutation detection. Direct plasma evidence is most developed for selected fragmentomic and 5hmC applications, although most studies remain retrospective, internally validated, or proof of concept. Fragmentomic studies have reported associations with lymphoma classification, outcome assessment, and longitudinal tumor-effector profiling during chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy, but routine clinical utility and decision thresholds are not established. Plasma 5hmC studies have reported associations with lymphoma classification, treatment response, prognosis, and measurable residual disease in acute myeloid leukemia, whereas pharmacodynamic monitoring during Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibition remains hypothesis-generating. DNA methylation may support source-cell or lineage inference, but lineage assignment does not establish malignant fraction, and key disease-assessment studies remain largely tissue-based, cellular-DNA-based, cross-cancer, or methodological. The novelty of this review is a structured evidence map that distinguishes direct plasma evidence from indirect support and compares the three modalities by biological information, assay compatibility, and validation maturity. We also propose a hypothesis-generating framework for sample-level integration using separate assay-specific aliquots and computational combination of outputs. No universal analytical order or clinically validated integrated workflow has been established. Fragmentomic and epigenomic profiling should therefore be regarded as investigational complements to mutation-based testing, requiring independent prospective validation against established genomic, cellular, imaging, and tissue-based methods.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning analysis of immune-inflammatory biomarkers for predicting no-reflow in patients with acute myocardial infarction after percutaneous coronary intervention.
papers.authors: Liu R, Peng Y, Qin H, Zhou Y, Li X, Wang H, Li Y, Zhang H, Hu X, Zhang Z, Ren W, Shu X, Zhang J, Nie L, Zou X, Jing T.
papers.abstract: Objective To evaluate whether routine immune-inflammatory biomarkers predict no-reflow (NR) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients, quantify their incremental predictive value over clinical variables, and build an interpretable peri-procedural prediction model. Methods This prospective cohort recruited 382 AMI patients undergoing PCI. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified independent correlates; confounder-adjusted restricted cubic splines (RCS) assessed nonlinear associations. LASSO regression selected core predictors with variance inflation factor (VIF) assessing multicollinearity. Four machine-learning models underwent 1000-iteration bootstrap internal validation and SHAP interpretation. Incremental value was tested via ΔAUC (DeLong test), continuous NRI, and IDI. Stratified regression and interaction tests evaluated AMI-subtype effect modification. Results NR occurred in 91 patients (23.8%). Multiple neutrophil-centred indices independently correlated with NR after adjustment. Seven predictors constituted the final model (all VIF Conclusion Pre-procedural neutrophil-centred inflammatory biomarkers are independent correlates of post-PCI NR and offer incremental predictive value over conventional clinical variables. The interpretable LightGBM model supports peri-procedural NR risk stratification, though external validation and recalibration are mandatory before clinical application.

papers.title: Identification of Macrophage Polarization-Related Biomarkers in Multiple Myeloma Using Integrated Bioinformatics.
papers.authors: Wang R, Zhang J, Qi J, Jiang Y, Wang N, Huang J, Tang S, Wei Y, Xiang Y, He H, Huang L, Wei Z.
papers.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) is an incurable hematologic neoplasm with heterogeneous prognosis. Within the bone marrow microenvironment, macrophage polarization (MP) contributes to immune remodeling and may influence disease progression, yet MP-related prognostic biomarkers remain insufficiently characterized. In this study, we integrated transcriptomic data from UCSC Xena (n = 844) and GSE4581 (n = 414) to identify differentially expressed genes between immune-hot and immune-cold MM samples stratified by single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA)-derived immune scores. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and intersection with published MP-related genes yielded candidate genes, which were further refined using univariate Cox regression combined with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), eXtreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and support vector machine recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE) machine learning algorithms to construct a prognostic model. An eight-gene signature (LGALS3, IL2RG, ADAM8, MERTK, ACSS1, ARSK, CBX6 and SOCS3) was established, demonstrating acceptable discriminatory ability for 1-, 2-, and 3-year overall survival (AUC 0.666-0.736 in training cohort). Risk groups differed significantly in immune infiltration patterns, predicted drug sensitivity, and survival outcomes. A predicted competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network centered on MERTK and SOCS3 was also constructed. These findings identify eight MP-related hub genes as candidate prognostic biomarkers and provide a risk model with acceptable predictive performance, offering insights into the immune-metabolic interplay in MM and suggesting potential avenues for personalized therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: In Silico Design and Comprehensive Evaluation of a Novel Multi-Epitope Vaccine Candidate Against Chandipura Virus
papers.authors: Yella, S.; singh, h.
papers.abstract: Chandipura virus (CHPV), an emerging arthropod-borne member of the Rhabdovirdae family, is an acute neurotropic pathogen responsible for explosive outbreak of acute encephalitis syndrome (AES) predominantly in pediatric cohorts. with mortality rates exceeding 70%, seizures, and death within 24 to 48 hours. the complete lack of approved antiviral therapies or preventive vaccine makes this a severe global health threat. to address this ,our study utilized a computational reverse vaccinology approach to design and structurally evaluate a novel epitope-based vaccine construct. and computationally validate a 104-amino-acid chimeric peptide vaccine candidate targeting immunoinformatics screening confirmed that the construct possesses strong predicted protective antigencity (VaxiJen >0.40) complete absence of allergenicity across multiple machine-learning models (AllerTopv2.0 and AllergenFP v1.0),and zero cellular or hemolytic toxicity (ToxinPred SVM regression score < 0.0). physicochemical characterization via EXPASY ProtParam established an 11.76 kDa construct comprising 1,653 atoms, with a theoretical isoelectric point of 7.78 an instability index of 39.92 (classifying the protein as physically stable), an aliphatic index of 81.73, and a grand average of Hydropathicity (GRAVY) of -0.350. These values confirm the construct is highly soluble in aqueous environments, which is necessary for physiological delivery. to prepare for expression, the sequence was reverse translated by codon-optimized for escherichia coli strain K12. JCat analysis returned a codonasaptation index (CAI) of 0.956 alongside of GC content of 61.48%. Subsequent in silico cloning successfully placed the 315 bp expression cassette into the pET-28a(+) vector, directly downstream of the T7 promoter. next, we evaluated receptor interaction by docking the construct against human Toll-Like Receptor 4 (TLR4;PDB ID: 4G8A). Using Hawkrank score of -5845.39 We validated this affinity with MM/GBSA calculations, which revealed a strong net binding free energy ({Delta}Gbind) of -29.12 kcal/mol, because static dicking cannot account for molecular flexibility, we then performed normal mode analysis (NMA) via the iMODS server. this dynamic simulation demonstrated structural stability throughout the construct was analyzed. The analysis found a fundamental eigenvalue of 4.62422*10-. the covariance matrix and elastic network showed highly correlated residue motions. to predict the vaccine's effectiveness we ran a 70-day simulation with C-Immsim. the data showed antigen clearance along with a strong primary IgM response successfully changed into IgG1 and IgG2 antibodies levels. The model also predicted an increase in active helper T cells. it also showed production of Th1 cytokines (inf-{gamma} and IL-2). this computer result prove the immune health of the chandipura virus construct. they give a reason to move this candidate forward for recombinants expression and in vivo preclinical testing.

papers.title: From HPV infection to cervical precancer: Molecular mechanisms, immune microenvironment and emerging technologies.
papers.authors: Zhou Y, Ge Y, Liu K, Liu H, Dong Z.
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women globally, with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection as the primary etiological factor. Cervical precancerous lesions, including high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions and adenocarcinoma in situ, represent the critical window for intervention prior to invasive cancer development. However, additional factors such as immunosuppression, smoking, and microbiome composition also play crucial roles in the development of cervical precancerous lesions. While HPV vaccination, screening, and treatment have reduced cancer incidence, these must be complemented by personalized approaches that target the molecular mechanisms driving carcinogenesis. Key dysregulated tumor suppressors (e.g., p16) and signaling pathways (PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Wnt/β-catenin) highlight the need for advanced therapeutic strategies. The immune microenvironment also plays a critical role in cancer progression, suggesting potential for immunotherapy. Promising biomarkers like p16, Ki67, and microRNAs require integration with technologies such as single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics for deeper insights into tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment dynamics. Additionally, while deep learning models hold promise in improving diagnostic accuracy for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), challenges such as data variability and interpretability need addressing. In conclusion, incorporating genomics, transcriptomics, immunotherapy, and artificial intelligence will enable more personalized and effective interventions, ultimately reducing the global burden of cervical cancer.
papers.venue: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS

papers.title: HSP70-Mediated Macrophage-Stromal Crosstalk is an Immunopathogenic Driver of Recurrent Implantation Failure.
papers.authors: Tang M, Lu Y, Huang X, Wu Q, Fu Y, Zhang T, Hao W, Zhang S, Xu J, Wan S, Jing Q, Xu J, Zhu Y, Xiao P.
papers.abstract: Background Recurrent implantation failure (RIF) remains a major challenge in assisted reproductive technology (ART), affecting a considerable proportion of patients despite multiple transfers of high-quality embryos. Although impaired endometrial receptivity is recognized as a critical contributor to RIF, the molecular mechanisms responsible for establishing a non-receptive endometrial microenvironment remain incompletely understood. The proliferative phase precedes decidualization and subsequent embryo implantation, representing a critical period for endometrial preparation. The endometrium is a highly dynamic tissue composed of diverse epithelial, stromal, vascular, and immune cell populations that undergo coordinated remodeling throughout the menstrual cycle; however, the cell type-specific alterations and pathogenic immune-stromal interactions during this phase have not been comprehensively characterized. Objective This study aimed to dissect the transcriptional landscape of the proliferative-phase endometrium in RIF patients, and validate the key pathways through experimental approaches. Study design We for the first time performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of proliferative-phase endometrial tissues from RIF patients and control subjects to characterize cell-type-specific transcriptional alterations and intercellular communication patterns. Peripheral blood scRNA-seq was additionally performed to determine whether immune alterations were tissue-specific or systemic. The impact of HSP70 on the transcriptome of endometrial stromal cells was investigated using RNA sequencing. The production of HSP70 and CCL7 in RIF patients was measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). The HSP70/CCL7 axis-mediated functional crosstalk between macrophages and endometrial stromal cells was investigated using Transwell assay, QPCR, and SA-β-Gal staining. HSP70-induced activation of PI3K signaling was predicted using RNA sequencing data, then validated through Western blot, ELISA, and Transwell assay. Results We identified excessive inflammatory immune infiltration as a microenvironmental hallmark of RIF endometrium, as reflected by increased percentages of T cells, monocytes, and NK cells. This alteration is associated with pathogenic macrophage - stromal crosstalk. Mechanistically, an inflammatory milieu promotes the expression of 70-kDa heat shock protein (HSP70) in macrophages, which stimulates CCL7 production in endometrial stromal cells via PI3K signaling. CCL7 drives the recruitment of multiple types of immune cells that further amplify the inflammation. Neutralization of CCL7 or inhibition of PI3K signaling prevented this pro-inflammatory infiltration. The HSP70-CCL7 axis facilitates endometrial stromal cell senescence and leads to impaired decidualization. Conclusion This study provides the first single-cell transcriptomic atlas of proliferative-phase endometrium in RIF and identifies a pathogenic macrophage-stromal communication network associated with HSP70/CCL7 axis. Our findings reveal that inflammatory microenvironmental remodeling occurs before the window of implantation and contributes to subsequent endometrial dysfunction. Targeting HSP70/CCL7-mediated immune-stromal crosstalk may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for early intervention and prevention of RIF.
papers.venue: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology

papers.title: Omega-3 fatty acids reprogram tumor-associated macrophage cytokine signaling and suppress pancreatic cancer growth.
papers.authors: Sakuma S, Zhao S, Hildreth A, Liu G, Shah V, Sun M, Tan S, Jacobs E, LaPorta MA, Furguiele J, Avina-Ochoa N, Globig AM, Tripple V, ImmgenT Consortium, Maier G, Panda S, Reyzer ML, Kang JX, Ma DWL, Rodeheffer M, Shaikh SR, Kaech SM.
papers.abstract: Dietary polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) shape inflammatory signaling within the pancreatic tumor microenvironment (TME), but the cellular mechanisms underlying their effects on tumor progression remain unclear. Using orthotopic models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), we show that omega-3 (n-3) and omega-6 (n-6) PUFAs are differentially incorporated into tumor lipid pools, generating spatially heterogeneous lipid microenvironments. While an n-6-enriched diet accelerated PDAC growth, an n-3-enriched diet suppressed tumor growth in a T cell-independent manner. Examining inflammatory effects in PDAC tumors, the n-3 PUFA-enriched diet reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines, including IL-6 family members, and single-cell and spatial analyses identified tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as the primary diet-responsive population. Indeed, selective conversion of n-6 to n-3 fatty acids within myeloid cells using an inducible fat-1 transgene, which encodes an n-3 desaturase that converts n-6 to n-3 PUFAs in vivo, was sufficient to suppress tumor growth, whereas fibroblast-restricted conversion had no effect. This finding is the first to formally establish that cellular origin of PUFA metabolism within the TME is a key determinant of tumor progression and identifies TAMs as critical mediators of n-3-dependent tumor suppression. Furthermore, the n-3 PUFA-enriched diet reduced Arg1 + immunosuppressive TAMs and promoted C1q + and MHC-II + antigen-presenting TAM populations enriched for antigen processing machinery and T cell-recruiting chemokines, alongside reduced IL-6 family cytokine production. Together, these findings establish macrophages as key mediators of n-3-driven tumor control and define a mechanism by which dietary lipids remodel cytokine signaling in the PDAC microenvironment.

papers.title: Deciphering the Molecular and Cellular Landscape of Early Diabetic Nephropathy through Single-Cell RNA Sequencing and Protein-Protein Interaction Networks.
papers.authors: Qin L, Liang Y, Xuan L, He R, Pang S, Ding T, Xie W, Yuan J.
papers.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) arises through complex pathological mechanisms that remain incompletely understood. This study employs transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) approaches to systematically characterize gene expression patterns, cellular composition changes, and intercellular communication networks in early DN. Analysis of the GSE111154 transcriptome dataset identified 259 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including 118 protein-coding genes (70 downregulated and 189 upregulated) in DN samples. Functional enrichment analysis revealed significant involvement of these DEGs in immune response pathways and extracellular matrix (ECM) organization. Single-cell analysis of the GSE131882 dataset resolved 12 distinct renal cell populations, demonstrating significant shifts in cellular proportions in DN, with notable expansions of endothelial cells (ENDO), fibroblasts (FIB), principal cells (PC), and parietal epithelial cells (PEC). Protein-protein interaction network analysis identified COL1A2, FLNA, A2M, and PLG as central hub genes in DN pathogenesis. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed enhanced interaction frequency and intensity in DN, particularly involving FIB cells through specific signaling pathways including CDH5, KIT, THBS, EGF, and FN1. In DN originated FIBs, the differential genes enriched transcription factor was NR2F2. Through immunohistochemical staining, NR2F2 was up-expressed in DN samples while CD31 was down-regulated. These findings collectively demonstrate profound dysregulation of immune responses, ECM remodeling, and cellular crosstalk during DN progression, highlighting key molecular and cellular drivers of disease pathogenesis.

papers.title: Evolution of SARS-CoV-2 reshapes upper airway immunity in children
papers.authors: McEwen, S.; Roehmel, J.; Wisniewski, S.; Loske, J.; Messingschlager, M.; Liebig, J.; Chua, R. L.; Seegebarth, A.; Ten, F. W.; Sawitzki, B.; Sander, L. E.; Conrad, C.; Eils, R.; Mall, M. A.; Lehmann, I.; Trump, S.
papers.abstract: Children were relatively protected from severe COVID-19 during the early pandemic a phenomenon linked to rapid and heightened innate immune responses in the upper-airways. Although adult upper-airway antiviral responses varied across successive SARS-CoV-2 waves, whether viral evolution similarly reshaped pediatric mucosal immunity remains unclear. Here we used single-cell transcriptomics to profile 229,533 upper-airway cells from 68 unvaccinated children including 17 uninfected controls, spanning the wild-type SARS-CoV-2, Alpha, Delta and Omicron waves. Epithelial interferon responses were primarily determined by time since symptom onset but were, unlike in adults, independent of disease severity. During early infection, anti-viral responses differed across variants without following a progressive pattern of attenuation. Alpha and Delta elicited the strongest interferon programs across epithelial and immune cell populations, whereas Omicron exhibited a shift towards macrophage cytokine signaling and T-cell cytotoxicity. These findings reveal variant-specific remodeling of pediatric upper-airway immunity that fundamentally differs from that described in adults.

papers.title: FLNA Expression in Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts Is Associated with Immunosuppression and Tumor Progression in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.authors: Yao Q, Liu N, Li S, Liu B, Ding G, Zhao H, Fu W.
papers.abstract: Background The role of Filamin A (FLNA) in colorectal cancer (CRC), particularly within the stromal compartment, remains poorly defined. This study investigates its expression, function, and clinical relevance in CRC. Methods We integrated transcriptomic data from the GSE39582 training cohort and TCGA/GSE75316 validation cohorts. Analyses included functional enrichment, tumor microenvironment (TME) assessment (ESTIMATE, TIDE), immune correlation, and survival analysis. FLNA's cellular expression was delineated using single-cell RNA-seq data from 27,414 cells. Results FLNA was upregulated in advanced-stage CRC and exhibited diagnostic potential in microsatellite instability (MSI) samples. Pathway analysis revealed a significant enrichment of FLNA in biological processes implicated in cell adhesion and remodeling of the extracellular matrix. High FLNA expression correlated with an immunosuppressive microenvironment, characterized by elevated stromal/immune scores, increased cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) and macrophage infiltration, and exclusion of CD8⁺ T cells. It also showed strong associations with multiple immune checkpoints. Single-cell transcriptomics confirmed specific, high FLNA expression in CAFs, fibroblasts, and endothelial cells, where it was associated with pro-tumorigenic functions, including actin cytoskeleton organization. Furthermore, FLNA emerged as an independent predictor of adverse outcomes and was independently associated with reduced overall survival (OS). Conclusion In summary, our findings suggest that FLNA expression is associated with tumor progression and an immunosuppressive microenvironment in CRC, and that FLNA warrants further investigation as a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target.
