papers.title: Niches in cancer: from primary tumors to metastatic disease.
papers.authors: Chao Z, Wang X, Wang Z, Wu K, Li L.
papers.abstract: Cancer progression does not occur in isolation: malignant-cell states and fates are shaped by specialized microenvironments, or cancer niches. Within primary tumors, vascular, stromal, immune and neural interactions create local hypoxic, metabolic and mechanical conditions that together influence malignant-cell behavior. These local environments sustain stem-like states, regulate immune surveillance and vascular remodeling, and influence dissemination and treatment response. Tumor-derived extracellular vesicles and other systemic signals connect primary tumors to distant organs, conditioning tissues before tumor-cell arrival and subsequently modulating disseminated tumor-cell seeding, dormancy, reactivation and outgrowth. Cancer niches therefore operate across spatial scales and disease stages, shaping tumor behavior in ways that cannot be explained by tumor-cell-intrinsic properties alone. Advances in single-cell and spatial profiling, organoid systems and intravital imaging are revealing their cellular composition, local architecture and evolution. In this review, we integrate primary, pre-metastatic and metastatic niche biology, examine how local environments evolve and influence one another during cancer progression, compare organ-specific metastatic niches and assess emerging therapeutic strategies. Effective niche-directed therapy will require identifying the interactions that sustain disease, showing that treatment disrupts them and determining which patients are most likely to benefit. Greater spatial, temporal and functional resolution may reveal new therapeutic vulnerabilities and create opportunities to prevent relapse and achieve more durable disease control.

papers.title: Integrated Multiomics Profiling Reveals Membrane-Associated Signaling Alterations Associated With Disease Activity in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
papers.authors: Zhang Q, Chen F, Dai Y, Zhang W.
papers.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex autoimmune disease characterized by pervasive immune dysregulation, yet membrane-associated molecular alterations in immune cells remain incompletely defined. Here, we performed integrated proteomic and phosphoproteomic profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from a self-established cohort of 130 SLE patients across disease stages and 90 healthy controls, with individual samples pooled into 36 samples for LC-MS/MS analysis, complemented by publicly available transcriptomic data from 1461 SLE patients. Focusing on membrane-associated proteins, we identified alterations in protein abundance and phosphorylation involving cytoskeletal organization, cell adhesion, and membrane trafficking, with the RHO GTPase cycle consistently enriched in both omic layers. Dynamic multisite phosphorylation of FLNA and increased abundance of FLNB and FNBP1 were observed. Clustering revealed distinct disease-stage-associated patterns involving integrin proteins in SLE in remission (SLE_R) and cytoskeletal and mechanotransduction components in active SLE (SLE_A). OAS3 and IFIT5 showed concordant transcript-protein changes, while interferon- and NF-κB-related transcriptional programs were implicated. Computational kinase analysis identified disease-stage-associated predicted activity patterns involving PKC, MAPKs, CDKs, and CaM-Ks. Together, these findings provide a multiomics view of membrane-associated molecular alterations associated with disease activity in SLE.

papers.title: Incorporating visceral adipose tissue into dual-region deep learning radiomics on CT improves preoperative lymph node metastasis prediction in gastric cancer: A multicenter study.
papers.authors: Miao S, Xiong Z, Yang H, Zhang L, Qi H, Liu Z, Wang Q, Ding X, Wang R, Lu P.
papers.abstract: Background Visceral adipose tissue (VAT) is associated with tumor progression in gastric cancer (GC), but its added value for predicting lymph node metastasis (LNM) remains unclear. Purpose This study aimed to construct a DR-DLR model that incorporates CT-based features from both VAT and tumor, with the goal of predicting LNM in GC patients, while investigating its biological relevance. Methods 855 GC patients were retrospectively collected across three clinical centers, divided into a primary cohort, one internal test cohort, and two independent external validation cohorts. An Attention Residual Transformation Network (ARTNet) extracted imaging representations from CT images. Feature representations and clinical variables were integrated using a multilayer perceptron (MLP) to build the DR-DLR model. Model performance, generalizability, prognostic value, and biological relevance were evaluated using internal/external testing, radiologist comparison, survival analysis, and radiogenomics analysis. Results Incorporation of VAT-derived features improved predictive performance compared with tumor-only models. The DR-DLR model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.898 (95 % CI: 0.817-0.946), 0.834 (95 % CI: 0.743-0.897), and 0.848 (95 % CI: 0.775-0.901) in the internal and two external test cohorts, respectively. It outperformed junior and senior radiologists in LNM assessment. Overall survival was shorter in high-risk patients than in low-risk. Radiogenomics analysis revealed that the high-risk phenotype was associated with activation of immune-related pathways and increased infiltration of CD4 + T cells, plasma cells, dendritic cells, and mast cells. Conclusion The DR-DLR model improved LNM prediction, with its high-risk phenotype linked to immune-related molecular alterations, supporting its value for preoperative risk stratification.

papers.title: Role of pyroptosis-related hub genes in necrotizing enterocolitis: a study based on bioinformatics analysis and clinical cohort validation.
papers.authors: Li Y, Sun W, Liu X, Hu Z, Li Y, Jin X, Zhu X.
papers.abstract: Objective To characterize the expression patterns and clinical significance of pyroptosis-related key genes in necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), and to identify potential biomarkers with adjunctive diagnostic value. Methods Pyroptosis-related candidate genes associated with NEC were screened through transcriptomic differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and immune infiltration analysis, followed by validation in an NEC mouse model and an LPS-induced IEC-6 cell model. Furthermore, a clinical cohort study was conducted to compare serum ADIPOQ (adiponectin) levels and related laboratory parameters, and logistic regression together with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to assess its diagnostic performance. Results Transcriptomic analysis identified 1,693 differentially expressed genes, which were predominantly enriched in metabolism- and immunity-related pathways. By integrating WGCNA and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, four NEC-associated pyroptosis candidate genes were identified: Ccr5, Tlr9, Lcn2, and Adipoq. Both in vivo and in vitro experiments confirmed that Adipoq and Tlr9 were significantly downregulated in NEC in a time-dependent manner (P Conclusion Adipoq and Tlr9 participate in immune and inflammatory dysregulation in NEC and may be involved in pyroptosis-related pathological processes, representing promising novel targets for the prevention and treatment of NEC.

papers.title: Targeting myeloid cell plasticity and metabolic reprogramming to alleviate T cell dysfunction and exhaustion-associated states and enhance immune checkpoint blockade therapy.
papers.authors: Wang M, Chen J, Wu Z, Wang Z, Zhong Z, Zhong Y.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy has achieved clinical progress in various malignancies, yet primary and acquired resistance limits its efficacy in solid tumors. Myeloid cells in the tumor microenvironment (TME), including tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs), and myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), undergo metabolic reprogramming under hypoxia and nutrient stress. They impair effector T cell function and may contribute to exhaustion-associated states via nutrient competition, release of toxic metabolites, and formation of physical barriers, representing a critical resistance mechanism. This review summarizes the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of myeloid cells and the metabolic networks underlying their immunosuppressive phenotypes, focusing on dysregulated lipid and cholesterol metabolism, amino acid remodeling, the glycolytic switch, and subcellular stress responses. We analyze how metabolic dysregulation causes T cell dysfunction and, in defined contexts, contributes to exhaustion-associated transcriptional programs through nutrient competition, toxic metabolite accumulation, and upregulation of inhibitory receptor ligands, and summarize intervention strategies targeting myeloid recruitment, phenotypic remodeling, metabolic reprogramming, and pathological structures combined with ICB. We discuss challenges of efficacy heterogeneity and safety in clinical translation, and highlight the prospects of multi-omics and computational biology in guiding next-generation combination immunotherapy. Understanding myeloid metabolic plasticity may provide a basis for overcoming immunotherapy resistance and establishing precise synergistic strategies.

papers.title: Immunoinformatics-Based Design of a Chimeric Vaccine Against Necator americanus Targeting the Na-APR-1, Na-GST-1, and Na-ASP-2 Vaccine Candidates
papers.authors: TANGAN, Y. A. S.; Nchanji, G. T.; Nkineh, K. P.; Efeti, T. M.; Chick, J. A.; Ndumu, E.; Shinyuy, L. M.; Moyeh, M. N.; Ghogomu, S. M.; Shey, R. A.
papers.abstract: Hookworm infection, caused predominantly by Necator americanus, is a soil-transmitted helminthiasis that disproportionately affects impoverished communities across tropical and subtropical regions, with an estimated 406-480 million people infected globally. Control continues to rely largely on mass drug administration, an approach challenged by rapid reinfection, the absence of durable protective immunity, and growing concern over reduced drug efficacy. While the leading recombinant protein antigens Na-APR-1, Na-GST-1, and Na-ASP-2 have demonstrated clinical safety and immunogenicity, the withdrawal of Na-ASP-2 after triggering allergic reactions in individuals with prior natural exposure revealed both the promise and the risk of single-antigen approaches, underscoring the need for a rationally designed multi-antigen vaccine. We used an immunoinformatics approach to design a novel chimeric vaccine candidate by combining carefully selected B-cell and T-cell epitopes from the major clinical-stage hookworm protein antigens with an immunostimulatory adjuvant sequence. The candidate's 3D structure was predicted, refined, and validated using established bioinformatics approaches, and its interaction with the innate immune receptor TLR4 was assessed through molecular docking and normal-mode analyses. The selected antigens showed conservation across related hookworm species, suggesting the potential for broader cross-protection. The designed candidate was predicted to be antigenic, non-allergenic, and non-toxic, and immune simulation analyses indicated its capacity to elicit coordinated humoral and cellular immune responses. HLA coverage analysis indicated broad population applicability. Docking and normal-mode analyses of its interaction with TLR4 indicated stable and favourable binding. This study offers a rational, safety-driven approach to multi-epitope vaccine design against hookworm infection, integrating the strengths of clinically evaluated protein antigens while addressing the safety concerns raised by prior single-antigen candidates. Further experimental validation is required to confirm the safety and efficacy of the vaccine construct in vitro and in vivo. These findings lay the groundwork for future efforts toward an effective immunoprophylactic strategy against this neglected disease.

papers.title: NeoOmni Atlas: an integrated database for pan-cancer neoantigen derived from proteogenomics analysis
papers.authors: Zheng, T.; Ran, Z.; Zeng, J.; Wang, T.; Fu, S.; Cai, L.; Wu, D.; Ding, J.; Liu, T.; Li, Z.; Yuan, K.; Lin, S.; xu, h.
papers.abstract: Tumor neoantigens derived from diverse molecular aberrations are important targets for personalized cancer immunotherapy, but existing resources incompletely integrate mass-spectrometry-supported canonical and non-canonical antigen evidence across cancer types. NeoOmni Atlas is an interactive pan-cancer T-cell epitope resource, built via proteogenomic reanalysis of 7,561 immunopeptidomics datasets comprising 511 million raw spectra from 2,341 samples across 26 cancer types. The analysis yielded 872,414 eluted canonical peptides and 198,961 non-canonical peptides spanning 18 molecular alteration classes, along with 759,386 unique ligands presented by 322 human leukocyte antigen (HLA) alleles. Relative to existing repositories, NeoOmni Atlas covers a broader range of cancer types, includes 60 additional HLA alleles, and catalogs 369,781 novel ligands. A computational tumor-specific filtering framework identified 316,126 tumor-associated epitopes and 61,231 tumor-specific epitopes. Tumor-specific epitopes showed stronger predicted binding affinity than tumor-associated epitopes for HLA class I A and B alleles, and 65 conserved tumor-specific epitopes recurrent across more than 10 tumor types represent potential shared antigen candidates. NeoOmni Atlas also prioritizes candidate tumor-associated antigens including PMEL (gp100:209-217) and CSPG4, and supports browsing, searching, and downloading by cancer type, human leukocyte antigen allele, peptide sequence, and source event. NeoOmni Atlas is freely accessible at http://modinfor.com/NeoOmni-Atlas/.

papers.title: Pharmacological targeting of FKBPL with rapamycin sensitizes triple-negative breast cancer to ferroptosis.
papers.authors: Li R, Ke H, Chen Z, Xu J, Qian D, Luo B, Jamshidi S, Zhang Z, Xu H, Sun J, Xiong H.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains a clinically formidable subtype, while resistant to conventional apoptotic cell death pathways, it exhibits a unique and exploitable vulnerability to ferroptosis. Here, we identify the FK506-binding protein-like (FKBPL) as a novel scaffold that dictates ferroptosis sensitivity and promotes TNBC progression. Bioinformatic and clinical analyses revealed that FKBPL was significantly overexpressed in TNBC and correlated with inferior patient prognosis. Functional characterization demonstrated that FKBPL knockdown markedly impaired TNBC cell proliferation and migration in vitro and suppressed tumor growth in vivo. Mechanistically, FKBPL modulated the kelch-like ECH associated protein 1 (KEAP1)-associated ubiquitination and increased nuclear factor erythroid-related factor 2 (NRF2) protein abundance, reinforcing cellular antioxidant defenses and reducing ferroptosis sensitivity. Notably, the clinically approved agent rapamycin was found to directly bind to FKBPL, inducing its proteasomal degradation and significantly sensitizing TNBC cells to ferroptosis. Given the emerging links between ferroptosis and immunogenicity, single-cell transcriptomic analysis further illustrated that FKBPL + malignant cells are predicted to interact with neighboring immune compartments, suggesting a potential association with microenvironmental remodeling within the TNBC microenvironment. Collectively, this study identifies FKBPL as a pivotal regulatory node connecting protein homeostasis with ferroptosis and provides a mechanistic rationale for repurposing rapamycin to therapeutically target the inherent ferroptotic vulnerability of TNBC.

papers.title: Neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease: From glial cell states and molecular networks to biomarkers and precision therapeutics.
papers.authors: Samantaray P, Verma P.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is now recognized as a biologically heterogeneous syndrome in which amyloid-β pathology, Tau-related alterations, and neuroinflammation are key interconnected processes. Microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, complement, inflammasomes, neurovascular cells, and peripheral immunity are implicated as both adaptive and disease-promoting contributors to the pathophysiology of AD. Here, we highlight mechanisms by which innate immunity and peripheral immune cells influence amyloid β-peptide metabolism, Tau pathophysiology, excitatory synaptic function, oxidative stress response, blood-brain barrier integrity, and systemic inflammation in the context of Alzheimer's disease. A particular focus is made on the role of TREM2-related microglial function and the NLRP3 inflammasome, complement-mediated synaptic pruning, astrocyte crosstalk, and the limitations of the M1/M2 and A1/A2 concepts. A distinction is made between biomarkers of core AD pathophysiology and those specific to neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration. An emphasis is placed on the clinical utility of plasma p-tau217 in combination with Aβ42/Aβ40, GFAP, NfL, sTREM2, YKL-40, and neuroinflammation imaging. With respect to therapeutics, an effort is made to focus on the need to harness desirable inflammatory pathways while specifically targeting deleterious processes rather than adopting an overarching anti-inflammatory approach. Single-cell, spatial, multi-omics, and biomarker-driven approaches may enable patient stratification based on underlying pathophysiology, allowing for stage-specific combination therapeutic strategies. Overall, studies presented in this review highlight a precision-neuroimmunology concept in which neuroinflammatory processes are both triggers and effectors of disease pathology and can be selectively modulated for clinical benefit.

papers.title: The β-cells in type 1 diabetes mellitus: findings from human pancreas studies.
papers.authors: Eizirik DL, Martin-Vazquez E, Roca-Rivada A, Yi X.
papers.abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by long-term and dynamic interactions between the immune system and pancreatic β-cells, ultimately leading to severe insulin deficiency. A paradigm shift in T1DM research has occurred in the past few years, with research now focusing on the human disease because of access to human pancreatic tissue and pancreas-draining lymph nodes. Advances in high-resolution imaging, single-cell and spatial multi-omics, and histopathology based on artificial intelligence have profoundly reshaped our understanding of disease initiation and progression. These studies revealed that β-cell loss and/or dysfunction might begin earlier than previously appreciated, preferentially affecting small β-cell-rich islets and insulin-positive cell clusters, with larger islets showing transient resistance. Substantial β-cell mass often persists at diagnosis, accompanied by functional impairment rather than immediate cell death. Across disease stages, β-cells exhibit conserved molecular signatures dominated by interferon signalling, enhanced antigen presentation and adaptive immune-evasion programmes, with evidence of heterogeneity linked to age, disease duration and immune context. Parallel analyses of pancreatic lymph nodes show early immune dysregulation, including altered regulatory T cell signatures and expansion of stem-like cytotoxic T cell populations, even before overt hyperglycaemia. Together, these findings support an integrated model of T1DM progression that enables alignment of clinical staging with evolving β-cell and immune phenotypes.

papers.title: Glycome remodeling programs pathogenic γδ T17 cell responses in autoimmunity.
papers.authors: Santos-Pereira B, Nogueira R, Tafesse Y, Correia-Silva A, Leite-Gomes E, Sanchez Sanchez G, Luppens X, Young LEA, Cavadas B, Vasconcelos C, Oliveira D, Lé A, Torres J, Campar A, Serodio JF, Marinho A, Alves JD, Torres T, Drake RR, Vermijlen D, Alves I, Pinho SS.
papers.abstract: Glycans play fundamental roles in T cell biology; however, the glycome landscape of γδ T cells remains to be unlocked. Despite the growing importance of γδ T cells in host defense, tissue homeostasis, and diseases, the glycosylation mechanisms guiding their activation, commitment, and function remain poorly defined. By performing single-cell RNA sequencing, we revealed that type 3/γδ T17/interleukin-17A (IL-17A)-committed γδ T cells rely on ( N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase 1 ) MGAT1 - MGAT5 -mediated branched N-glycosylation. We further demonstrated that the absence of branched N -glycans on γδ T cells acts as a peripheral signal, driving an IL-17A-pro-inflammatory phenotype, alongside a shift to a Vγ4 + subset and the imprinting of innate-like properties. This altered glycoform of type 3 γδ T cells was shown to induce severe psoriasis. γδ T cells from patients with autoimmune and inflammatory diseases exhibited a deficiency in branched N -glycans. Glycan supplementation can reprogram γδ T cells toward a less-pathogenic state, highlighting N -glycans as a previously unrecognized immune checkpoint for γδ T cells.

papers.title: Identification of SGK1 as a candidate regulator associated with myeloid cell senescence in ME/CFS: An integrative transcriptomic and experimental study.
papers.authors: Jin Y, Qin R, Li W, Liu J, Chen X.
papers.abstract: Background Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a complex illness lacking objective diagnostic biomarkers and clear pathophysiological understanding. Patients exhibit immune dysregulation and chronic inflammation reminiscent of aging phenotypes, yet the role of myeloid cell senescence in this disease remains unexplored. Methods A stepwise integrative transcriptomic and computational strategy was employed. Differentially expressed genes were identified from the bulk transcriptomic dataset GSE14577. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis was performed to identify key modules correlated with the ME/CFS phenotype. Candidate genes were obtained by intersecting these modules with aging-related genes from the GenAge database. Core hub genes were further selected using LASSO regression and random forest machine learning algorithms. Cell type-specific expression was mapped using single-cell RNA sequencing data GSE214283, and functional validation was conducted via siRNA knockdown in a THP-1 cell senescence model. Results Integrative analysis identified HMGCR and SGK1 as core hub genes. Functional enrichment analysis revealed that candidate genes were enriched in pathways related to cellular senescence and inflammation. Single-cell transcriptomics analysis suggested that SGK1 expression was enriched in myeloid cell populations, including monocytes and neutrophils, in individuals with ME/CFS, whereas HMGCR showed a broader expression pattern. Single-gene GSEA indicated that SGK1 was associated with autophagy and lysosomal function. In vitro experiments showed that SGK1 expression was significantly upregulated in D-galactose-induced senescent THP-1 cells, and SGK1 knockdown markedly reduced the mRNA expression levels of senescence markers p16, p21, and p53. Conclusion This study identifies SGK1 as a candidate molecule associated with myeloid cell senescence-related alterations in ME/CFS. Integrated transcriptomic, single-cell, and experimental analyses suggest a potential link between SGK1 expression and aging-associated immune alterations. However, further validation in primary ME/CFS-derived immune cells and clinical cohorts is required to determine the biological significance and clinical relevance of SGK1.

papers.title: Fenvalerate Induces Airway Epithelial Injury Through CHRM3-Associated NF-κB Activation.
papers.authors: Yang Y, Li J, Liu T, Sheng M, Liu J, Yang Z, Chu H, Jia A, Xu W.
papers.abstract: Fenvalerate (FEN) is a widely used pyrethroid insecticide with potential respiratory toxicity; however, its contribution to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)-related pathological processes remains unclear. We investigated molecular mechanisms linking FEN exposure to airway epithelial injury. COPD transcriptomic datasets were integrated with predicted FEN targets, and candidate genes were prioritized using machine-learning algorithms. Immune infiltration and single-cell transcriptomic analyses were used to examine immune associations and cell-type-specific expression. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations assessed potential FEN-target interactions, followed by validation in BEAS-2B human bronchial epithelial cells. Intersecting FEN-COPD genes were enriched in inflammatory, immune-regulatory, neuroactive ligand-receptor, and epithelial injury-related pathways. Eight candidate genes showed distinct expression patterns across airway epithelial and immune cell populations. Computational analyses supported a potentially stable FEN-CHRM3 interaction. In BEAS-2B cells, FEN reduced viability, increased IL-6 and IL-8 secretion, promoted apoptosis, upregulated CHRM3, and enhanced IκBα and p65 phosphorylation. Pharmacological inhibition of CHRM3 or NF-κB partially attenuated these responses. Thus, FEN-induced epithelial inflammation and apoptosis may involve CHRM3-associated NF-κB activation, providing mechanistic insight into pesticide-related respiratory toxicity.

papers.title: Single-cell multi-omics in IPF and COPD: from atlas to impact.
papers.authors: Mehta P, He C, Mawar CMA, Yan X, Rosas IO, Kaminski N.
papers.abstract: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics technologies are transforming our understanding of the normal lung cellular repertoire as well the molecular and cellular networks of chronic lung diseases. In this review we focus on idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). We briefly review technologies and discuss technical and analytical challenges, including strategies to optimise batch correction, dataset integration, and sample-aware differential gene expression; we describe global lung reference atlases, enabled by large-scale data-sharing, providing accessible frameworks for cross-study validation, lineage and trajectory inference, and inter-disease comparisons; and we outline the major findings in COPD and IPF. In IPF, mechanistic insights include: (i) loss of the normal alveolar niche (ii) aberrant basaloid epithelial cells linked to failed regeneration, expansion of (iii) profibrotic SPP1+ macrophages and (iv) disease-associated CTHRC1 + and HAS1 hi fibroblast subtypes, that localise to fibrotic niches, and (v) extensive vascular and immune remodelling. In COPD these approaches demonstrate: (i) loss of aerocytes; (ii) expansion of MMP -expressing macrophages, (iii) activated neutrophil influx and (iv) B-cell lymphoid follicle activation and endothelial inflammation (iv) some overlapping features with IPF. We highlight gaps and future opportunities, including under-representation of early disease stages, incomplete resolution of neutrophils, tissue-resident immune compartments, and cross-organ integration. Looking forward, integration with clinical phenotypes and imaging is accelerating translation towards precision medicine, enabling biomarker discovery, cellular endotyping, and therapeutic prioritisation. Advances in multimodal profiling, computational pipelines, next generation technologies, open science initiatives and artificial intelligence will propel the field toward predictive, patient-specific insight and mechanistically informed, stratified trial design.

papers.title: Single-cell-resolved dynamic immune remodeling following Omicron infection and recovery in vaccinated individuals.
papers.authors: Khare K, Kumar S, Chattopadhyay P, Halder S, Bano M, Gupta A, Patel A, Soni J, Tarai B, Budhiraja S, Pandey R.
papers.abstract: Breakthrough SARS-CoV-2 Omicron infections occur despite vaccination, yet post-infection immune recovery remains incompletely understood. Here, we performed longitudinal single-cell transcriptomic and targeted proteomic profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy individuals and vaccinated patients during infection, early recovery, and 3-month post-recovery. Omicron infection induced coordinated immune remodeling with contraction of T and B cell compartments; expansion of plasma, regulatory T, and dendritic cells; and suppression of inflammatory and metabolic pathways, including TNFα-NF-κB and mTORC1 signaling. Innate populations rebounded rapidly, whereas adaptive compartments recovered slowly with sustained suppression of IL-2 , IL-12 , and IL-15 modules. Chemokine surges ( CXCL1 , CXCL5 , and CXCL8 ) resolved during convalescence, whereas selective cytokines ( CCL5 and CCL8 ) and interleukins ( IL-6 , IL-18 , and IL-24 ) persisted. Trajectory analysis revealed non-uniform remodeling of T cell states with persistent differentiation signatures across naive, effector, and memory compartments. Overall, vaccination tempered early immune collapse and accelerated innate rebound, highlighting interleukin-linked checkpoints and metabolic regulation underlying post-vaccination immune resilience.

papers.title: Computational Design of a TCR-like Human V H Domain Antibody That Specifically Recognizes a WT1-Derived Peptide Presented by Class I Major Histocompatibility Complex.
papers.authors: Oh TS, Kim SW, Ahn S, Suh S, Lee J, Bae Y, Lee H, Kim YS, Jeong BS, Oh BH.
papers.abstract: T cell receptor (TCR)-like antibodies that recognize a peptide-major histocompatibility complex (pMHC) can enable precise targeting of cancer cells, but developing single-domain binders with high specificity and affinity is challenging. Here, we report the computational design and experimental validation of a TCR-like human heavy chain variable (V H ) domain antibody that specifically recognizes the Wilms' tumor 1 protein (WT1)-derived peptide RMFPNAPYL presented by HLA-A*02:01/β2-microglobulin (RMF/HLA-A*02). Starting from the crystal structure of a Fab antibody bound to RMF/HLA-A*02, we repurposed the soluble trastuzumab-derived V H scaffold to bind RMF/HLA-A*02. The resulting V H domain, αRMF_V H , spans all 9 peptide residues and showed no binding to a control pMHC with a different peptide. Fusion of 1 or 2 αRMF_V H molecules to human serum albumin domain III yielded monovalent and bivalent constructs with good biophysical properties. The monovalent construct bound selectively to RMF/HLA-A*02 with 81 nM affinity, and when expressed as part of a chimeric antigen receptor on T cells, it functioned as an antigen-recognition domain to selectively activate T cells in the presence of RMF/HLA-A*02-positive cells. The bivalent construct exhibited a dramatically increased apparent binding affinity of 0.37 nM. When both constructs were engineered into the bispecific T cell engager (TCE) format containing an anti-CD3 Fv, the bivalent TCE induced antigen-dependent cytotoxicity much more effectively than the monovalent TCE. These results demonstrate a viable strategy to develop high-specificity, peptide-focused TCR-like V H domain antibodies that can be readily extended into potent bivalent TCEs for pMHC-targeted therapeutics.

papers.title: Bispecific NK-Cell Engager Targeting TP53 Mutation Through Integration of a TCR-mimic Antibody.
papers.authors: Wu H, Zhao Z, Zhang L, Xiong X, Yang M, Ge W, Zhi D, Cao X, Yi C, Qiao Y, Cao J, Mei Y, Jiao S, Liu Q, Zhou H, Xu Z, Suo G.
papers.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are valuable for cancer immunotherapy because they kill tumor cells without prior sensitization or human leukocyte antigen (HLA) restriction. However, their efficacy is often limited by immune-evasion, especially major histocompatibility complex I (MHC-I)-mediated NK cell inhibition. NK cell engagers (NKCEs) can redirect NK cells to tumor for more effective immunotherapy, but most current NKCEs target tumor-associated antigens (TAAs), risking on-target, off-tumor toxicity in clinical applications. Neoantigens, as tumor-specific antigens (TSAs) arising from somatic mutations and presented by MHC-I on tumor cell surfaces, represent ideal tumor-specific target. Here, we engineered NKCEs built on neoantigen-targeting TCR-mimic antibodies (TCRm-Abs) to enhance tumor-specific NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity. Using a high-throughput hydrogel-based microwell single-cell chip (HMSC-chip) coupled with T2 cell-based de-selection, we identified C33-Ab, a functional TCRm-Ab specific for p53 R175H /HLA-A*02:01, from ∼500,000 hybridoma cells within 8 weeks. Based on this TCRm-Ab, we constructed a bispecific NKCE (C33×CD16), a single-chain diabody (scDb) linking C33-Ab to an anti-CD16 scFv. C33×CD16 specifically bridges NK cells with p53 R175H /HLA-A*02:01-positive cancer cells. It potently enhanced NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity in vitro and antitumor efficacy in vivo upon adoptive NK-cell transfer. This TCRm-Ab-based bispecific NKCE offers a promising strategy for tumor-specific NK cell-mediated immunotherapy by targeting intracellular oncogenic hotspot mutations.

papers.title: Repertoire diversity and dynamics of peripheral Th17 after allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
papers.authors: Tamaki M, Nakasone H, Kawamura S, Takano K, Misaki Y, Yoshimura K, Okada Y, Tanihara A, Hashino K, Yamamoto K, Nakata Y, Ishikawa T, Matsuoka A, Meno T, Nakamura Y, Kawamura M, Takeshita J, Yoshino N, Gomyo A, Kusuda M, Kimura SI, Kako S, Kanda Y.
papers.abstract: Th17, a subset of helper T cells that produce interleukin-17 (IL-17), is thought to play a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of chronic graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). However, the kinetics of Th17 following allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) have not been elucidated. In this study, we evaluated the temporal dynamics and diversity of peripherally circulating Th17 after allo-HSCT. The study included 86 patients who survived without disease relapse for 1 year or more, and for whom peripheral blood samples 3 months after allo-HSCT were available. Th17 was detected and sorted by flow cytometry, and T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire was analysed by a next-generation sequencing (NGS) method. Patients with chronic GVHD showed a higher TCR repertoire diversity, while those with severe chronic GVHD showed a lower TCR diversity and Th17/Cluster of Differentiation (CD) 4 ratio. The amino acid sequence in complementarity determining region 3 of Th17-TCR was not apparently different between patients with and without chronic GVHD. Additionally, a higher Th17/CD4 ratio at 3 months was related to a lower incidence of subsequent chronic GVHD. The current study explored the kinetics of peripherally circulating Th17 after allo-HSCT, which might be associated with the development of chronic GVHD.

papers.title: Xenoglycosylation of the HIV-1 Glycan Shield Promotes Cross-Clade Neutralization and Diverse Human Antibody Lineages
papers.authors: He, L.; Lin, X.; Zhang, Y.-N.; Newby, M. L.; DesRoberts, C.; Allen, J. D.; Stanfield, R. D.; Crispin, M.; Wilson, I. A.; Zhu, J.
papers.abstract: Despite advances in HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein (Env)-based vaccine design, eliciting broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs) remains a central challenge. Here, we identify core (1,3)-fucose as a key modulator of neutralizing antibody (NAb) induction and breadth. Uncleaved prefusion-optimized (UFO) trimers and self-assembling protein nanoparticles (SApNPs) produced in High Five (Hi5) insect cells incorporate core (1,3)-fucose into the Env glycan shield. Crystal structures of Hi5-produced BG505 UFO trimers in complex with bNAbs confirm native-like Env architecture and epitope presentation. In wild-type mice, these trimers and SApNPs elicit robust autologous and heterologous NAb responses. We then engineer Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells to co-express three insect- and plant-derived core (1,3)-fucosyltransferases. The resulting immunogens carry fucosylated mammalian glycans and elicit cross-clade NAb responses in mice, supporting an important role for core (1,3)-fucose in broadened neutralization. Env-specific IgE responses suggest engagement of associated immune pathways during vaccination. In ATX-Gx humanized mice, core (1,3)-fucosylated, glycan-trimmed Env elicits detectable cross-clade neutralization by week 11. Single-cell analysis identifies distinct human antibody lineages with cross-clade activity and noncanonical Env recognition. Repertoire and functional analyses uncover putatively related lineage members across two animals within the same group. Together, these findings support xenoglycosylation as a promising, germline-agnostic strategy for HIV-1 vaccine design.

papers.title: Discovery of frameshift-associated TCRs following personalized neoantigen vaccination in a patient with osteosarcoma
papers.authors: Bennett, S. N.; Alley, J.; Shabrang, M.; Garness, J.; McKinnon, K.; Smith, A.; Inabinett, W. B.; Hoos, W. A.; Thompson, M. A.; Rubinsteyn, A. N.; Vincent, B. G.
papers.abstract: Personalized antigen-directed immunotherapies, including personalized cancer vaccines, are emerging as promising therapeutic modalities for a range of cancer types. Immune monitoring can be used to evaluate the efficacy of a vaccine in stimulating the immune response pre- and post-vaccination; however, such approaches typically stop short of identifying which T cell receptors (TCRs) are functionally driving therapeutic responses. Here, we present a case report of immune monitoring and subsequent TCR discovery experiments following administration of personalized cancer vaccines in a patient with locally recurrent osteosarcoma. Whole PBMCs were stimulated with vaccine peptides (>16 AA) in vitro for 11 days, after which IFN{gamma} ELISPOT identified total T cell responses for 12 of 15 tested peptides post-vaccination. In vitro expanded samples were submitted for 10x single-cell TCR sequencing, from which 26 TCRs were chosen for generation of TCR-T cells based on clonal expansion and culture specificity. Of the generated TCR-T cells, 25 produced functional TCRs, 4 of which were specific to vaccine peptides. However, downstream testing revealed each was MHC class-II restricted. To address this, we repeated the in vitro stimulations with co-cultures of isolated CD8+ T cells with autologous dendritic cells, and cultures of whole PBMCs with anti-MHC class-II blocking antibody. These cultures yielded 10 additional TCRs, 2 of which were responsive to a vaccine peptide containing a MAP2 frameshift mutation. These findings demonstrate an effective approach for leveraging post-vaccination expanded antigen-specific T cell populations for discovery of novel T cell receptors for downstream cellular therapies.

papers.title: Network pharmacology and single-cell sequencing analysis of gastrodin in anticancer effects against colorectal cancer by regulating key target genes and the tumor immune microenvironment.
papers.authors: Minjun Z, Dong X, Yuting Z, Zhishang L.
papers.abstract: Background Gastrodin is a natural compound with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antitumor activities; however, its therapeutic role and molecular mechanisms in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain unclear. In this study, we explored the anti-CRC mechanisms of gastrodin through integrated bioinformatics and experimental validation. Methods The potential targets of gastrodin were obtained from public databases. Transcriptomic data of CRC were retrieved from TCGA and GEO datasets, and the differentially expressed genes were screened. The CRC-related genes were subjected to gene-set variation analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and the core genes were identified by the LASSO regression, support vector machine, and random forest algorithms, followed by SHAP analysis. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), immune infiltration analysis, consensus clustering, molecular docking, and in vitro experiments were further performed. Results A total of 628 potential gastrodin targets and 15 overlapping CRC-related genes were identified. Five core hub genes, including NFE2L3, UBE2S, CA9, CCNB1, and CFD, were screened, among which NFE2L3 showed the highest SHAP importance score. The scRNA-seq data indicated cell-type-specific expression patterns of these genes in CRC tissues. Immune infiltration analysis further suggested that gastrodin may regulate the CRC immune microenvironment by regulating the activated B cells, activated CD4⁺ T cells, and other immune cells. Molecular docking revealed favorable binding affinity between gastrodin and the five core proteins. Moreover, NFE2L3 was highly expressed in CRC tissues and cell lines, and its knockdown significantly inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion of the tumor cells. Conclusion Gastrodin may suppress CRC progression by targeting key genes, particularly NFE2L3, and modulating the tumor immune microenvironment. Furthermore, our study has identified the potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for CRC.

papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analysis Reveals Shared Macrophage-Associated Inflammatory Signatures in MASLD/NAFLD and Rheumatoid Arthritis.
papers.authors: Yu W, Nie Q, Wu Y, Lan X, Liu J, Xu D, Guan S.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease/nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (MASLD/NAFLD) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) may share inflammatory mechanisms, although their common cellular basis remains unclear. We integrated bulk transcriptomic datasets (GSE66676 and GSE55235), single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets from murine RA synovium (GSE192504) and NASH liver (GSE129516), disease-association analysis, molecular docking, and in vitro experiments in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages. Bulk transcriptomic analysis identified 630 shared differentially expressed genes, including 344 concordantly upregulated genes enriched in immune response, cytokine and chemokine signaling, phagosome, Toll-like receptor signaling, and Fc receptor-mediated phagocytosis; a strict dual-dataset intersection further defined 18 core genes significantly upregulated in both diseases. Immune-signature analysis indicated altered myeloid cell-associated inflammatory activity in both diseases, and several shared genes, including S100A8, S100A9, FCER1G, FCGR3A, LYZ, and MS4A7, correlated positively with monocyte/macrophage-related signatures. Single-cell analysis identified macrophage subsets with high S100a9 expression and elevated shared myeloid inflammatory signature scores in both RA synovium and NASH liver. Triptolide showed favorable predicted binding to the S100A8/A9 complex and reduced LPS-induced inflammatory cytokine secretion and expression of the six-gene signature in RAW264.7 cells, supporting the hypothesis that S100A9-associated inflammatory macrophage activation represents a candidate target for further investigation. These findings support a shared S100A9-positive inflammatory macrophage-associated program in MASLD/NAFLD and RA, and support the hypothesis that the S100A8/A9 complex represents a candidate target for further investigation.

papers.title: Identification of Transcriptional Signatures Associated with COPD in Immune and Epithelial-Stromal Cells Using Machine Learning Methods.
papers.authors: Ren J, Fan J, Bao Y, Guo W, Feng K, Hu J, Zhou W, Wang D, Lu L, Huang T, Cai YD.
papers.abstract: In the context of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), understanding gene expression patterns across various cell types is pivotal for disease comprehension, therapeutic development, and enhancement of patient prognosis. Nevertheless, the intricate interplay between immune and structural cells, along with their significance in COPD pathogenesis, remains only partially understood. This research employed multiple machine learning techniques to pinpoint marker genes exhibiting pronounced alterations between COPD patients and healthy individuals. We utilized six feature selection algorithms (LASSO, LightGBM, MCFS, RF, CATboost, and XGBoost) and three classification methods (DT, KNN, and RF) to analyze single-cell patient data. Cells were bifurcated into two subsets: immune cells and epithelial-stromal cells. Each cell, encompassing 21,237 genes, was labeled either as a healthy control or COPD. We identified a number of promising genes, such as FKBP5, which encodes a protein crucial for stress response regulation, and SCGB3A1, which is predominantly expressed in the respiratory tract and critical for regulating lung function. Both genes exhibit strong correlations with COPD. The study also underscored the potential roles of HLA-DRB1 and HSP90AA1 in COPD pathogenesis. Our findings underscore the unparalleled potential of machine learning in identifying genetic markers for intricate diseases like COPD, paving the way for targeted therapeutic advancements.

papers.title: NeoBridge: Biophysics-informed neoantigen prioritization and clonal architecture profiling in pancreatic cancer.
papers.authors: Mediavilla AL, Cardoso JP, Álvarez-Benayas J, Sánchez-Arévalo Lobo VJ.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of immunogenic neoantigens remains a bottleneck in personalized cancer vaccine development, particularly in low-mutation-burden tumors such as pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). We developed NeoBridge, a hybrid ensemble integrating gradient boosting and a deep neural network across four biologically grounded feature dimensions: HLA binding and processing, differential agretopicity, tumor neoantigen abundance, and TCR recognition potential. Trained on 11,188 experimentally validated neoantigens, NeoBridge achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.904 on held-out data, with cross-cancer generalization (AUC: 0.73-0.82), including 0.82 in pancreatic cancer, and outperformed established tools. Differential agretopicity emerged as the dominant predictive feature. In 118 PDAC patients with resolved phylogenies and complete follow up, subclonal neoantigen load was associated with worse progression-free survival (p < 0.001) and overall survival (p = 0.038). These findings are hypothesis generating and require prospective immunopeptidomic and functional validation.

papers.title: IRF7 signalling in tanycytes controls brain-body-immune response across the ovarian cycle.
papers.authors: Nampoothiri S, Fernandois D, Journiac N, Delahaye F, Mbouamboua Y, Sauve F, Couralet M, Gallet S, Mroueh N, Serradas Aponte ML, Jouy N, Spenle R, Schmidt-Ullrich R, Corral IM, Mattot V, Almodovar CR, Schlitzer A, Froguel P, Maurage CA, Barbry P, Giacobini P, Mars LT, Bonnefond A, Nogueiras R, Schwaninger M, Prevot V.
papers.abstract: Sex-specific differences in metabolic and immune function are shaped by endocrine-immune interactions, yet the complexity of this relationship remains poorly understood. Here, we identify an immune cell-like state of tanycytes, an ependymoglial cell type lining the third ventricle that mediates brain-body communication 1,2 in both mice and humans. Using single-cell transcriptomics, we provide a high-resolution cellular map of the mouse and human mediobasal hypothalamus with cross-species comparison of tanycytes. We capture dynamic sex-, oestrous cycle- and high-fat diet-dependent transcriptomic changes in tanycytes, including a cyclic interferon response in tanycytes during the physiological oestrous cycle in female mice. We found that the oestrous cycle, with its changing hormonal milieu, especially oestradiol, affected the brain's immune responses, characterized by the temporal and cyclic expression of interferon regulatory factor 7 (Irf7) gene, as well as downstream interferon-stimulated genes such as Cxcl10 in tanycytes of female mice, which are associated with increased infiltration of leukocytes and cytokine responses. Irf7 expression in tanycytes of physiological males remained stable and markedly lower, suggesting a distinct immune activation pattern in the brains of cycling females. By targeting oestrogen and interferon signaling in tanycytes, we show that balanced, cyclic leukocyte infiltration into the median eminence may have a role in oestrous cycle maintenance, whereas Irf7 in tanycytes modulates circulating monocyte proportions, revealing brain-immune system communication through tanycytes. Our findings reveal an immune-associated role for tanycytes, with potential implications for understanding the endocrine and immunological mechanisms underlying sex-biased diseases.

papers.title: SLC25A4 high Hepatocytes Enhance Lifestyle Intervention Response in MASLD by Recruiting Eating Macrophages.
papers.authors: Qian Y, Lai L, Zhang Y, Meng Y, Song Z, Huang B, Song G, Sun B, Yang W.
papers.abstract: While lifestyle interventions (LSI) are the cornerstone of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) management, the molecular mechanisms driving the histological and metabolic regression in LSI-responsive patients remain unclear. C57BL/6N mice were hydrodynamically injected with Slc25a4 and Sleeping Beauty transposon. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) profiled the hepatic immune landscape. Metabolomics and co-culture assays analyzed intercellular crosstalk. Responsive MASLD patients had high SLC25A4 expression, correlating with exercise-induced hepatic steatosis improvement. Slc25a4 overexpression augmented exercise effects. scRNA-seq identified a distinct population of Clec4f + Timd4 + P2ry12 + macrophages, defined as lipid-eating macrophages, in livers of Slc25a4-overexpressing mice. Macrophage depletion reinstated hepatosteatosis in high-fat, high-fructose, and high-cholesterol diet-fed exercised mice with Slc25a4 overexpression. Mechanistically, SLC25A4 mediates mitochondrial ATP exchange and selective ATP efflux. Ectopically overexpressed Slc25a4 activates Pannexin 1 to release ATP, which recruits eating macrophages via P2ry12, clearing lipid-laden hepatocytes. The GDF15-PPARα axis between macrophages and hepatocytes was activated. Macrophage Gdf15 knockdown abrogated Slc25a4-mediated enhanced hepatic fatty acid oxidation (FAO), and hepatic PPARα knockdown abolished this effect as well. Slc25a4 orchestrates an LSI-responsive hepatocyte-macrophage axis: Pannexin 1-mediated ATP release recruits lipid-eating macrophages, whose GDF15 activates PPARα-driven FAO, establishing Slc25a4 as a therapeutic target to restore exercise response in MASLD.

papers.title: Atlas-Guided CD55-Enriched Neutrophil Extracellular Vesicles for Complement-Macrophage Modulation in Diabetic Wounds.
papers.authors: Cui T, Li J, He J, Wang J, Qian Y, Jin Y, Yang L, Tao Z, Li Z, Chen Z, Wang W, Ma X, Wu J.
papers.abstract: Diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation and impaired immune resolution, yet the therapeutic translation of single-cell atlases into rational immunomodulatory strategies remains limited. Here, integration of diabetic-wound single-cell transcriptomic datasets identifies a neutrophil subpopulation enriched in cluster of differentiation 55 (CD55) with complement-regulatory and reparative features. Guided by this atlas-derived signature, activated neutrophil-derived extracellular vesicles (aNEVs) enriched in CD55 are generated under high-glucose and lipopolysaccharide stimulation and incorporated into a microbial transglutaminase-crosslinked gelatin hydrogel for localized delivery and protease-sensitive matrix remodeling. The resulting gelatin/aNEV composite hydrogel (Gel/aNEV) attenuates complement-associated inflammatory signaling, C3a production, oxidative stress, and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression, while promoting reparative macrophage reprogramming and endothelial migration. In diabetic wounds, a single application of Gel/aNEV accelerates wound closure and enhances angiogenesis, collagen remodeling, and tissue regeneration. Integrated transcriptomic-proteomic analyses further reveal coordinated changes in complement, inflammatory, redox, extracellular-matrix, and regenerative programs, supporting a multicomponent therapeutic model. Collectively, this study establishes an atlas-to-therapy framework that uses disease-associated neutrophil states to guide extracellular-vesicle engineering, integrating complement regulation, immune reprogramming, and biomaterial-assisted delivery for diabetic wound repair.

papers.title: Putrescine alters the composition of interstitial dendritic cell subsets by suppressing Cybb-dependent oxidative phosphorylation.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Tan Z, Li D, Lian H.
papers.abstract: Putrescine, a core polyamine, is closely linked to intestinal immune homeostasis and the pathogenesis of intestinal disease, yet its role in shaping dendritic cell (DC) subset differentiation in the intestinal lamina propria and the mechanism behind it remains undefined. Here, we first performed integrated analysis of seven public human single-cell RNA sequencing datasets to profile dendritic cell subsets across colorectal cancer tissues with varied MMR phenotypes. We fed mice a 1% (w/v) putrescine diet to raise intestinal putrescine levels and examined the effects on lamina propria DC subsets using flow cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, transcriptomics, and O2K-based metabolic assays. Elevated putrescine expanded the cDC1 subset (CD103 + CD11b - CD172a - ), contracted the cDC2 subsets (CD103 - CD11b + CD172a + and CD103 + CD11b + CD172a + ), and reduced surface expression of CD11b and CD172a on lamina propria DCs. Single-cell and transcriptomic profiling showed that putrescine reshaped the transcriptional landscape of DC subsets, with marked downregulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) pathways. O2K metabolic analysis confirmed that putrescine lowered ROS output and oxygen consumption rate across several mitochondrial respiratory states, including basal and ATP-coupled respiration, while western blotting showed reduced Cybb expression in lamina propria DCs. Together, these findings indicate that putrescine reshapes intestinal lamina propria DC subset composition by suppressing Cybb, thereby limiting ROS production and OXPHOS activity. This work offers new mechanistic insight into how polyamine metabolism governs intestinal immune homeostasis and points to potential therapeutic targets for intestinal disorders such as colorectal cancer and inflammatory bowel disease.

papers.title: The mtROS-Stat1 axis defines an acinar dysfunctional state linking metabolic stress to immune activation in cigarette smoking-associated dry eye disease.
papers.authors: Cui Z, Liang L, Huang W, Jiang Y, Wang C, Zheng Z, Liu Z, Wang Z, Chen B, Wang X, Wang B.
papers.abstract: Purpose Dry eye disease (DED) is a prevalent ocular disorder in which environmental factors, particularly cigarette smoking (CS), are increasingly implicated. However, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. Methods We integrated cross-sectional data from the UK Biobank with a chronic CS-exposure mouse model and single-nucleus RNA sequencing of the lacrimal gland (LG) tissue. Histological and functional assays were used to characterize ocular surface and LG phenotypes. Transcriptomic analyses were conducted to resolve acinar cell states, define metabolic and inflammatory pathways, and infer cell-cell interactions. Pharmacological interventions targeting mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) and Stat1 signaling were applied to assess therapeutic potential. Results CS was identified as an independent, dose-dependent risk factor for DED and induces progressive LG dysfunction characterized by corneal damage and impaired tear secretion. Single-cell profiling revealed a damage-associated acinar cell (DAAC) state marked by loss of secretory identity and acquisition of an immunogenic phenotype. Mechanistically, we show that mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation suppression eventually activates Stat1 signaling, which functions as a stress-responsive metabolic checkpoint driving the transition of acinar cells into the DAAC state. Functionally, DAACs exhibited enhanced antigen presentation and actively engage immune cells, supporting an epithelial-driven inflammatory model of DED. Targeting either mtROS or Stat1 ameliorated acinar dysfunction, suppress immune activation, and restored tear secretion. Conclusion These findings define a mtROS-Stat1-DAAC axis that links metabolic stress to epithelial dysfunction and immune activation in CS-associated DED. This work provides a mechanistic framework connecting environmental exposure to tissue pathology and highlights potential therapeutic strategies for intervention.

papers.title: Multiomics Characterization of HAO2 Expression and Its Clinical Associations in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Chen H, Ge M, Wang M, Zhang Q, Luo N, Chen D, Bian W.
papers.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) exhibits extensive metabolic reprogramming and tumor microenvironmental heterogeneity, contributing to variable outcomes and treatment responses. Hydroxyacid oxidase 2 (HAO2) has been implicated in metabolic regulation, but its clinical and biological relevance in RCC remains incompletely characterized. We integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, genomic, and single-cell RNA-sequencing data to characterize HAO2 expression, clinicopathological associations, metabolic and immune features, and treatment-related outcomes. Exploratory drug-sensitivity associations were evaluated using the Genomics of Drug Sensitivity in Cancer database and pRRophetic. HAO2 expression was consistently reduced across multiple RCC datasets and showed tumor-normal discrimination with area under the curves ranging from 0.73 to 0.97. Low HAO2 expression was associated with advanced stage and shorter overall survival. HAO2 expression was positively associated with metabolic programs and distinct immune microenvironmental features. In the CheckMate-025 cohort, higher HAO2 expression was associated with longer overall survival in both treatment arms. Single-cell analysis showed reduced HAO2 expression in malignant renal epithelial cells. Exploratory pharmacogenomic analysis identified associations between HAO2 expression and drug sensitivity. HAO2 downregulation is associated with advanced disease, unfavorable survival, and distinct metabolic and immune features in RCC. HAO2 represents a candidate tissue-associated biomarker warranting further experimental and prospective validation.
papers.venue: Omics : a journal of integrative biology

papers.title: integrating single-cell transcriptomics and chromatin accessibility profiling to decipher the molecular landscape of Hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.authors: Pan K, Chen L, Zheng Y.
papers.abstract: Background Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a prevalent and lethal liver malignancy, characterized by high recurrence rates and limited therapeutic options. Current diagnostic and treatment strategies are hindered by drug resistance and a lack of effective biomarkers for early detection. Methods This study aims to elucidate the role of lactylation and fibroblast cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME) of HCC, focusing on their potential as therapeutic targets. Utilizing a comprehensive multi-omics approach, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and single-cell ATAC sequencing (scATAC-seq) data from public databases (GEO, TCGA) to explore transcriptional and epigenetic landscapes at single-cell resolution. Results Our analysis identified fibroblast cells as key players with high lactylation-related pathway activity, and CREB1 as a central transcription factor regulating lactylation-associated genes in these cells. The CREB1 regulatory network was associated with specific immune cell infiltration patterns, drug sensitivity profiles, and enrichment in critical signaling pathways such as Chemokine, TNF, NF-κB, and EMT. These findings underscore the pivotal role of lactylation-driven epigenetic regulation in fibroblasts, influencing the HCC immune microenvironment and disease progression.

papers.title: Follistatin-like Protein 1 Contributes to Acute Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury by Enhancing Neuroinflammation Through the Modulation of Interferon Regulatory Factor 5-Mediated Macrophage Activation.
papers.authors: Luo Y, Ni S, Peng L, Zhu L, Chen T, Wang P, Li Z.
papers.abstract: Background and Purpose : Follistatin-like protein 1 (Fstl1) is a secreted glycoprotein with context-dependent inflammatory activity. We investigated whether Fstl1 is a reproducible feature of traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) and whether it regulates macrophage activation through interferon regulatory factor 5 (IRF5). Methods : A target-blind analysis integrated four public SCI bulk transcriptomic cohorts with single-cell and spatial datasets. Findings were tested in wild-type and Fstl1+/- mice after SCI using spinal cord RNA sequencing, molecular and histological assays, behavioral testing, and bone marrow-derived macrophages with IRF5 gain- and loss-of-function. Adult-induced Postn-CreER-mediated Fstl1 deletion was evaluated in fibroblast-macrophage non-contact co-cultures. Results : The public-data screen reduced 440 cross-cohort candidates to four non-structural extracellular genes, including Fstl1. Fstl1 was consistently upregulated across SCI cohorts, correlated with myeloid signatures, and was predominantly associated with non-myeloid cell sources in single-cell data. Experimental SCI increased spinal Fstl1 and inflammatory cytokines, whereas partial Fstl1 depletion reduced tissue damage and improved locomotor recovery. Fibroblast Fstl1 deletion reduced macrophage iNOS, Il6, and Tnf and increased Arg-1 and Il10 in co-culture. Spinal cord RNA sequencing showed broad remodeling of immune and tissue-related programs after Fstl1 depletion. Computational perturbation and experimental validation identified IRF5 as a downstream mediator. Recombinant Fstl1 increased IRF5, iNOS, and CD80 while reducing Arg-1 and CD163; IRF5 silencing reversed these changes. Conclusions : Fstl1 is a reproducible SCI-associated extracellular candidate that supports IRF5-dependent inflammatory macrophage activation. Targeting the Fstl1-IRF5 axis may help limit secondary neuroinflammation after SCI.

papers.title: Metabolic Dysfunction and T-Cell Exhaustion in Colorectal Cancer: Mechanisms, Microenvironment Remodeling, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
papers.authors: Jeon J, Baek HS, Park K, Park MN, Heo NH, Cheon S, Kim G, Kim S.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide. Metabolic disorders such as obesity, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and metabolic syndrome are associated with CRC risk. Metabolic abnormalities may contribute to colorectal tumorigenesis and reshape the tumor immune microenvironment, which in turn influence immune dysfunction and therapeutic resistance. Exhausted CD8 + T cells exhibit impaired effector function, sustained inhibitory receptor expression, and transcriptional and epigenetic reprogramming. Metabolic stressors within the CRC microenvironment may modulate T-cell function and exhaustion-associated states. Additionally, other immune populations (natural killer cells, macrophages, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, dendritic cells, and regulatory T cells) may develop distinct dysfunctional or immunosuppressive states. Recent single-cell and spatial studies have indicated the heterogeneity of these immunometabolic interactions in CRC. This review examines the interactions of the systemic and tumor-associated metabolic alterations with T-cell exhaustion and other forms of immune dysfunction in CRC. We discuss the influence of glucose, lipid, amino acid, and mitochondrial metabolism, hypoxia, microbiota-derived metabolites, and chronic inflammation in shaping tumor-immune interactions. Finally, we reviewed therapeutic strategies targeting immunometabolic pathways and their potential integration with immune checkpoint blockade. Overall, understanding these interactions may help identify immunometabolic vulnerabilities for informing precise therapeutic strategies for CRC.

papers.title: Tissue Factor Expression Is Associated with Distinct Pattern of Immune-Cell Infiltration in the Ovarian Tumor Microenvironment.
papers.authors: Mohiuddin TM, Binte Hafiz F, Sheng W, Zhang C, Al-Rawe M, Zeppernick F, Tchaikovski S, Meinhold-Heerlein I, Hussain AF.
papers.abstract: Tissue factor (TF) has been implicated in tumor progression and immune regulation, but its cellular sources and relationship with immune infiltration in ovarian cancer remain incompletely defined. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE232314), analyses of The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) ovarian cancer cohort, and multiplex immunofluorescence in an independent 25-case tissue microarray (TMA). Single-cell analysis showed that TF expression was concentrated in tumor epithelial cells and a discrete endothelial subpopulation, with minimal expression in immune and other stromal compartments. In the TCGA cohort, TF expression was not significantly associated with tumor stage, grade, disease-free survival, or overall survival. In TF-stratified analyses, however, high CD8 + T cell infiltration was associated with improved survival in the low-TF expression subgroup (HR = 0.60) but with worse survival in the high-TF subgroup (HR = 1.72); high M1 macrophage infiltration was associated with improved survival only in the low-TF subgroup. TF expression correlated negatively with estimated CD8 + T cell, memory B cell, and M1 macrophage infiltration and positively with naïve B cell infiltration. In the TMA cohort, high-TF tumors showed significantly lower CD56 + NK-cell and CD68 + macrophage infiltration and a lower CD68/CD163 ratio. Together, these findings show cross-sectional associations between TF expression and reduced measured abundance of several antitumor immune populations and a stratum-dependent association between CD8 + T cell infiltration and survival. These associations were not fully concordant between the transcriptomic (TCGA) and protein-level (TMA) cohorts and require prospective, formally tested validation. TF warrants further investigation as a candidate immune-context biomarker in ovarian cancer.

papers.title: 2,234 attempts to harmonize a multi-platform B-cell lymphoma bulk transcriptomic dataset: ComBat is superior by cross-batch prediction quality
papers.authors: Nikitin, D.; Arakelyan, A.
papers.abstract: Background. Cross-platform transcriptomic harmonization benchmarks rely on individual success metric each: correlation with a reference profile, classifier accuracy, or a composite imported from single-cell integration. We found no published study that computes multiple orthogonal metric classes over one set of harmonization approaches and measures overlapping between the best approaches by these metrics. Methods. We used the 2,234 approaches of the recent real-world benchmark on 7,174 B-cell lymphoma transcriptomes. They combine 31 harmonization methods, 14 batch-removal strategies, three imputations and two post-removal settings. We assigned its 87 polarity-adjusted scoring metrics, out of 344 registered, to five classes (global, local, distributional, structural and composite) and added three biology-facing classes: within-cohort marker correlation (L), cross-batch rank agreement of a marker panel (M), and leave-one-batch-out (LOBO) prediction of lymphoma subtypes and normal B cells (N). Each class resulted in top 112 approaches (5%), and we measured overlap by the Jaccard index. Results. Harmonization methods of high harshness such as quantile normalization matched different batches to the same shape of distribution but were inferior by local and global metrics. Local and composite metrics resulted in the largest overlap of best approaches (71 shared). Classes L and M, M and N shared no approach, whereas L and N shared one approach without harmonization under the rare-batches-removed strategy, and all three overlaps were significantly below the random expectation. Class N resulted in the ComBat family in 84 of its 112 places. Class M elected only 10_mnn and 12_scanorama, methods that completely corrupted biology by correlation. Conclusions. Best transcriptomic harmonization approach is highly contingent on the quality metrics used, with metric classes trade-offing between each other. We provide a six-step recipe for metric classes, their thresholds and the cross-batch tests for selecting the best approaches.

papers.title: Podocyte Biology in Pediatric Glomerular Disease: From Slit Diaphragm Assembly to Genotype-Guided Therapy-A Narrative Review.
papers.authors: Todorović P, Kopilaš A, Racetin A, Maglica M, Rizikalo A, Raguž F, Kelam N, Vukojević K.
papers.abstract: The podocyte is a terminally differentiated cell whose foot processes and slit diaphragm form the final layer of the glomerular filtration barrier. Because podocytes are not effectively replaced after birth, and nephron number is fixed before it, their cumulative loss converts congenital and steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and Alport syndrome into a shared trajectory towards chronic kidney disease. This narrative review, based on a structured search of three databases with the cited evidence classified as pediatric, adult, mixed or preclinical, connects podocyte biology with pediatric nephrology. We follow maturation and the modules whose disruption produces disease, a genetic architecture in which diagnostic yield falls steeply with age at onset, and the convergence of genetic, mechanical, metabolic and immune insults on podocyte depletion. Single-cell and spatial atlases, organoids, glomerulus-on-a-chip systems and human tissue are compared as partly discordant platforms. A molecular result currently changes a small, defined set of clinical decisions. No podocyte-derived urinary marker has been shown in children to add information beyond proteinuria and filtration rate, anti-nephrin antibody assays are not yet standardized, and kidney biopsy remains the reference standard. We set out an integrated diagnostic pathway, state the limitations of the evidence and define research priorities.

papers.title: FOXC2 regulates macrophage polarization and osteosarcoma progression via the CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling axis.
papers.authors: Zhao W, Han Y, Yu X, Liu J, Yuan H, Li J.
papers.abstract: Forkhead box protein C2 (FOXC2) is frequently overexpressed in osteosarcoma (OS) and has been implicated in tumor proliferation and metastasis; however, its role in regulating the tumor immune microenvironment remains poorly understood. In this study, integrative bioinformatics analyses of the TCGA-SARC (The Cancer Genome Atlas sarcoma cohort) dataset were performed to evaluate the clinical significance of FOXC2 in OS. High FOXC2 expression was significantly associated with poorer overall survival in patients with OS (p < 0.001). Functional experiments demonstrated that FOXC2 knockdown significantly reduced the overall viable cell/metabolic signal, migration, and invasion in U-2 OS and SaOS-2 cells (p < 0.05). Mechanistically, FOXC2 was found to regulate the CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling axis. ELISA, RT-qPCR, and western blotting analyses showed that FOXC2 knockdown decreased CXCL12 expression, whereas FOXC2 overexpression significantly increased CXCL12 levels. ChIP-qPCR analysis demonstrated significant enrichment of FOXC2 at the CXCL12 promoter and detectable enrichment at the CXCR4 promoter in SaOS-2 cells, and dual-luciferase reporter assays further showed that FOXC2 overexpression significantly increased CXCL12 promoter activity whereas FOXC2 knockdown reduced it, supporting direct transcriptional regulation of the CXCL12/CXCR4 axis by FOXC2. In macrophage co-culture experiments, FOXC2 knockdown promoted M1-like macrophage polarization and reduced M2-like macrophage markers, whereas activation of CXCR4 partially reversed these effects. Flow cytometric analysis further confirmed that FOXC2 knockdown significantly increased the M1/M2 macrophage ratio. In vivo, FOXC2 knockdown markedly reduced tumor growth and lung metastases in a xenograft mouse model, with tumor volume and lung metastatic burden reduced by approximately 50% and 43%, respectively. Tumor tissues from FOXC2-knockdown mice exhibited increased M1-like macrophage infiltration and reduced M2-like macrophage markers. Together, these findings demonstrate that FOXC2 regulates macrophage polarization and OS progression through transcriptional modulation of the CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling axis, highlighting FOXC2 as a potential regulator of the tumor immune microenvironment in OS. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

papers.title: Identification of biomarkers related to lymph node metastasis and prognosis in thyroid cancer based on integrated bioinformatics exploration.
papers.authors: Hu X, Ge D, Ma X, Yang Y.
papers.abstract: Objective Thyroid Carcinoma (THCA) is a common endocrine malignancy, and Lymph Node Metastasis (LNM) is a critical determinant of poor prognosis. This study aimed to identify LNM-related biomarkers and establish a prognostic model for THCA patients using integrated bioinformatics approaches. Methods Clinical data from SEER were analyzed to identify prognostic factors in THCA. Transcriptomic data from TCGA were used to identify differentially expressed genes between LNM and non-LNM samples. Survival analysis, machine learning (Boruta and LASSO), and functional enrichment were applied to screen candidate biomarkers. Immune infiltration and a ceRNA network were also explored. Results Six independent prognostic factors were identified from SEER (n = 38,955): age, gender, marital status, race, pathologic T-stage, and pathologic M-stage. A nomogram incorporating these factors showed good predictive performance (AUC = 0.744). Transcriptomic analysis revealed 332 LNM-related genes. Through integrative machine learning, six biomarkers ‒ CLDN10, OTOS, NEXMIF, ACOT6, ASXL3, and SLC4A4 ‒ were selected. These genes were predominantly enriched in immune response and metabolic pathways. M0 macrophages and resting dendritic cells showed significant abundance differences between LNM and NLNM samples, with CLDN10 positively correlated with resting dendritic cells (R = 0.47, adjusted p Conclusion We identified six candidate LNM-related biomarkers and clinical factors associated with THCA prognosis. These findings provide a basis for further investigation into LNM mechanisms and may offer new perspectives for prognostic assessment, though independent validation is required.

figure.caption: Survival analysis and the difference between LNM and NLNM patients. (A) The OS curve for LNM and NLNM patients. (B) The CSS curve for LNM and NLNM patients. (C) Nomogram analysis result for the seven risk factors. The * point represented significant difference. (D) ROC curve for evaluating the predictive ability of nomogram analysis model. (E) DCA result for the combined factors and individual factors. (F) The clinical impact curve analysis between “Number of high-risk” curve and “Number of high-risk with event” curve.
