papers.title: Predictive and mechanistic evaluation of ODE-informed machine learning for systemic lupus erythematosus disease-activity stratification.
papers.authors: Li H, Wu LY, Yang A, Wang Q, Song Q, Dai Y, Zhou W, Zeng GY, Lee SP.
papers.abstract: Background Mechanistic consistency does not necessarily imply improved prediction. We evaluated ordinary differential equation (ODE)-informed machine learning for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) disease-activity stratification, assessing predictive utility and mechanistic consistency separately. Methods GSE65391 data classified 131 patients as high (n = 56) or low (n = 75) disease activity. A published four-state ODE generated anti-inflammatory, immune-complex, tissue-damage, and pro-inflammatory features. Architecture-matched Random Forest (RF) models were compared using feature ablation and outer-fold evaluation. Directionality, perturbation, and parameter sensitivity assessed mechanistic consistency; two independent SLE datasets supported exploratory proxy comparisons. Results RF + ODE initially achieved AUROC 0.7133 versus 0.5940 for RF alone (ΔAUROC=+0.1193; 95% CI, 0.0209-0.2140). Removing the outcome-coupled ODE residual reduced AUROC to 0.6708. Archived out-of-fold evaluation and independent outer-fold reimplementation yielded AUROCs of 0.6019 and 0.6529, respectively; neither established robust incremental discrimination. The reimplementation excluded held-out outcomes from predictor generation. Within the calibrated representation, anti-inflammatory, immune-complex, and pro-inflammatory states showed consistent disease-activity directionality, with strong immune-complex-pro-inflammatory coupling (Spearman ρ=0.912). Perturbation and parameter-sensitivity analyses supported stability of selected relationships. External modality-specific proxies showed exploratory directional analogy without validating source-defined states. Conclusions The apparent predictive advantage attenuated under stricter evaluation, while selected state relationships remained stable under tested perturbations and parameter variation. The published ODE provided a structured representation for examining dynamical relationships, with incremental predictive value assessed separately. Mechanistic consistency and predictive utility should be evaluated as distinct dimensions.

papers.title: Machine Learning Models Combining [ 68 Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET Radiomics and Clinical Features to Predict Overall Survival for Metastatic Castration-resistant Prostate Cancer Treated with [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA Radioligand Therapy.
papers.authors: Edouard L, Papillon L, Ferrer L, Godbert Y, Meyer M, Prega-Renaud V, Subreville C, Anizan N, Benziane-Ouaritini N, Gallinato O, Cabart M, Teyssonneau D, Roubaud G, Colin T, Schwartz P.
papers.abstract: Purpose Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) remains incurable despite recent therapeutic advances. [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT (lutetium-177 labelled prostate-specific membrane antigen radioligand therapy) provides meaningful clinical benefit in selected patients. However, ∼30% of the patients do not respond to [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT. Although several baseline prognostic factors are well known, reliable pretherapeutic predictive biomarkers are still lacking. We developed and compared several predictive machine learning (ML) models integrating clinical, biochemical, and imaging data, including [ 68 Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET (gallium-68 labelled prostate-specific membrane antigen ligand positron emission tomography) radiomic features, to estimate overall survival (OS) in patients with mCRPC treated with [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT. Methods This retrospective monocentric study included 102 patients with mCRPC treated with [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA between January 2022 and March 2024. Five lesions per patient were segmented on their pretherapeutic [ 68 Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/computed tomography (CT) scans. Radiomic features were extracted following Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative guidelines. Multimodal ML models integrating clinical, genomic, biochemical, and imaging features (including radiomics) were developed to predict OS. Results Median OS of the total cohort was 11.2 mo. Intralesional homogeneity, characterized by the second-order radiomic feature normalized inverse difference moment, was associated with shorter OS (p = 0.025). The best-performing ML model achieved a 12-mo area under the curve (AUC) of 0.778 by combining 22 clinical, biochemical, genomic, and radiomic features. The model leveraging PET data alone achieved strong performance, with an AUC comparable to the clinical model (0.715 vs 0.766). Conclusions ML models based on [ 68 Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT, including radiomic features, offer a noninvasive, standardized, and widely accessible approach to predict OS in patients with mCRPC treated with [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT. This study highlights the strong predictive potential of PSMA PET imaging for patient stratification in a real-world setting.

papers.title: Development of a chimeric multi-epitope vaccine targeting surface-exposed proteins of Chlamydia psittaci through immunoinformatics and structural vaccinology.
papers.authors: Yehia RS, Asim M, Makki HH, AlMustafa H.
papers.abstract: Chlamydia psittaci is an obligate intracellular zoonotic pathogen that causes psittacosis and severe respiratory illness in humans. Despite its clinical importance, no licensed vaccine is currently available, and antibiotic treatment may not provide long-term protection or prevent recurrent infection. To address this challenge, a computational strategy integrating structural vaccinology and immunoinformatics was used to design a multi-epitope vaccine targeting the major outer membrane porin and the virulence-associated pGP3-D protein of C. psittaci. Cytotoxic T-cell and helper T-cell epitopes were identified and screened to select antigenic candidates. The selected epitopes were joined using linker sequences together with β-defensin-3 and PADRE. The vaccine construct was evaluated using physicochemical analysis, three-dimensional structural modeling, interaction analysis with TLR2, a 500 ns molecular dynamics simulation, MM-GBSA binding free-energy analysis, immune simulation, and in silico cloning. The designed vaccine was predicted to possess favorable antigenicity, a non-allergenic profile, suitable physicochemical properties, and a global population coverage of 92.15%. Computational analyses suggested stable interaction with TLR2 and indicated structural stability of the vaccine-receptor complex during the simulation. Immune simulation predicted increased IgG levels, memory B-cell formation, activation of CD8 + T lymphocytes, and a cytokine profile consistent with Th1-type immune responses. These findings suggest that the proposed construct represents a computationally designed multi-epitope vaccine candidate that requires further evaluation through experimental studies to determine its safety, immunogenicity, and protective efficacy against C. psittaci.

papers.title: Long Noncoding RNA: An Uncharted Territory in Plant Diseases and Immunity.
papers.authors: Jeevan B, Biswas S, Shivappa R, Sarkar S, Kar MK, Molla KA.
papers.abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) are a class of transcripts longer than 200 nucleotides with little or no protein-coding capacity. They represent a substantial fraction of eukaryotic genomes and function as molecular architects that coordinate diverse biological processes and physiological plasticity, including multilayered plant defence systems, through versatile regulatory interactions at multiple levels of gene regulation. Recent advances in high-throughput RNA sequencing technologies have greatly expanded the identification of plant lncRNAs, revealing their diverse roles as scaffolds, decoys, guides, and regulatory molecules. These lncRNAs are increasingly recognised as integral components of plant immune systems, contributing critically to host defence mechanisms. This review highlights recent progress in lncRNA identification using computational pipelines as well as emerging artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) based approaches. We further explore current insights into the regulatory functions of lncRNAs during host-pathogen interactions. Notably, we discuss a paradigm-shifting discovery in lncRNA biology, the finding that many lncRNAs, once presumed to be non-coding, contain small open reading frames (sORFs) that encode functional micropeptides. Modern predictive modelling has been crucial to identify these sORFs and their peptide products and to show that lncRNAs have multiple functions as regulatory transcripts and peptide precursors in plant immunity.

papers.title: Altered cholangiocyte subsets with neural pathway enrichment in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
papers.authors: Liu L, Hu G, Gu F, Zhu Q, Li C, Di X, Zou M, Li X.
papers.abstract: Hepatocytes have been extensively studied in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), yet the role of cholangiocytes remains underexplored. We utilized a comprehensive approach that integrates high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA), cellular interaction evaluation, machine learning techniques, immune cell infiltration analysis, and Mendelian randomization to investigate both single-cell sequencing data and bulk sequencing datasets. Single-cell analysis identified significant alterations in cholangiocyte subpopulations in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) patients, including an increase in cholangiocytes with elevated SEMA3 pathway expression. The hdWGCNA analysis identified the green module, which is enriched with genes associated with neural pathways pertinent to MASH. Seven machine learning models assessed the diagnostic feasibility of key genes in the green module for MASLD spectrum. Immune infiltration analysis highlighted complex interactions between cholangiocytes enriched for neural-related pathways and immune cells, particularly neutrophils and monocytes. Patient stratification identified two distinct subtypes within the MASLD spectrum, with subtype 2 exhibiting enhanced activity in neural-related pathways. Mendelian randomization analysis identified PLEKHA5 as a candidate causal gene for MASLD, suggesting a potential role in neural mechanisms (SEL1L3 showed a suggestive association, P = 0.0413). Collectively, this hypothesis-generating bioinformatics study elucidates distinct characteristics of cholangiocyte subpopulations in MASH, revealing neural pathway alterations that may contribute to disease pathogenesis and providing a foundation for future investigation into cholangiocyte-related mechanisms in MASLD.

papers.title: Viability-Dependent and Structural Modulation of IL-10 Secretion in THP-1 Cells by Lactobacillus gasseri and Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus.
papers.authors: Akrami M, Akrami M, Haeri P, Amini A, Haghdoost E, NikJamal T.
papers.abstract: Emerging evidence indicates that probiotic-mediated immunomodulation is not exclusively dependent on microbial viability, but is also significantly driven by structural components and postbiotic factors. This study systematically evaluated the viability-dependent versus structure-dependent regulation of Interleukin-10 (IL-10) in THP-1 monocytes by comparing alive, partially inactivated, and fully killed states of Lactobacillus gasseri and Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus. Distinct bacterial preparations were generated via heat, ultraviolet (UV) irradiation, sonication, and chemical inactivation. We assessed IL-10 protein secretion (ELISA), transcriptional kinetics (RT-qPCR), and single-cell cytokine expression (flow cytometry), while ensuring cellular compatibility through MTT viability assays. The results demonstrate that both viable and non-viable preparations significantly induce IL-10 secretion. However, live preparations elicited a more robust and rapid transcriptional response, with peak IL-10 mRNA expression occurring at 16-20 h post-stimulation. Notably, mixed-strain conditions exhibited a pronounced combinatorial enhancement of IL-10 production at both the protein and single-cell levels. While structural microbial components are sufficient to trigger anti-inflammatory IL-10 responses, active microbial viability markedly amplifies the magnitude and kinetics of this regulation. These findings provide a mechanistic foundation for the rational design of precision paraprobiotic and probiotic formulations in immune-mediated therapies.

papers.title: Low-frequency parasitized cells in bone marrow alter myelopoiesis following immunization with the live attenuated Leishmania major Cen -/- vaccine.
papers.authors: Azodi N, Pacheco-Fernandez T, Klenow L, Markle H, Tirrell N, Murray A, Brino M, Kumar S, Acharyya N, Silberstein E, Satoskar AR, Karaiskos S, Nakhasi HL, Gannavaram S.
papers.abstract: Leishmaniasis lacks an effective vaccine. We developed a live-attenuated Leishmania major Centrin-deficient strain ( LmCen -/- ) that is safe and protective in murine and canine models through IFN-γ-producing effector T cells. Because persistent low-level infection supports durable immunity, we investigated latent parasites and immune remodeling in the bone marrow. Dual single-cell RNA sequencing detected parasitized bone marrow cells 28 days after intradermal inoculation with either virulent LmWT or attenuated LmCen -/- . Flow cytometry showed increased myelopoiesis following LmCen -/- immunization compared with LmWT infection. Cell-cell communication analysis implicated enhanced granulin-Sort3 signaling as a potential driver of this response. Bone marrow monocytes from LmCen -/- -immunized mice efficiently cleared virulent LmWT parasites in co-culture, consistent with the induction of trained innate immunity. These findings identify the bone marrow as an active site of anti- Leishmania immune programming and suggest that LmCen -/- vaccination promotes durable protection through coordinated adaptive and innate mechanisms.

papers.title: Perinatal nicotine exposure disrupts hematopoietic stem cell development and elevates influenza severity in adulthood.
papers.authors: Rommel MGE, Cool T, Rodriguez Y Baena A, Saini S, Medina P, Mattingly C, Bachinsky E, Chattopadhyaya S, Manso BA, Rajendiran S, Worthington AK, Poscablo DM, Deguzman A, Wimer PQ, Voelker IM, Berger-Cahn T, Langroudi L, Svendsen AF, Shariati A, Carpenter S, Boyd DF, Forsberg EC.
papers.abstract: Developmental exposures profoundly shape lifelong health by altering disease resilience later in life. One potential cause of increased disease susceptibility is an altered immune system, originating in epigenetically maladaptive hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). Here, we establish perinatal nicotine exposure (PNE) as a mouse model of developmental maladaptive immunity, wherein early-life environmental insults permanently alter HSCs. We show that PNE selectively disrupts the establishment of HSCs and tissue-resident, but not circulating, immune cells. Remarkably, the specific decrease of HSCs and lung-resident immune cells persists into adulthood. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed durable molecular reprogramming of adult PNE HSCs, with inverse regulation of positive trained immunity signatures. Functionally, adult PNE offspring challenged with respiratory virus exhibit exacerbated immune maladaptation, marked by increased weight loss, deteriorated lung pathology, hyper-permeability of pulmonary vasculature, tissue-resident macrophage depletion, and exaggerated neutrophil recruitment. Together, our findings establish that PNE imprints durable maladaptive immunity involving changes in HSCs and their progeny, suggesting a hematopoietic origin for the PNE-induced respiratory vulnerability.

papers.title: MACC1 in colorectal cancer: a claim-level evidence audit from metastasis driver to proposed microenvironmental regulator.
papers.authors: Yang R, Deng R, Lin H, Huang D, Su T, Song X, Liang B, Xie L.
papers.abstract: Metastasis-associated in colon cancer 1 (MACC1) is an established regulator of colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and metastatic competence, but its proposed role in the tumour microenvironment is less certain. We performed a critical claim-level audit of original studies, classifying evidence by cancer-type match, manipulated cellular compartment, direct MACC1 perturbation, functional recipient cell endpoint, and immune context. The audit identifies convergent CRC evidence for tumour cell-intrinsic functions and inflammatory regulation of tumour cell MACC1. It also supports MACC1-dependent extracellular vesicle communication between CRC cells. By contrast, direct immune or stromal causality in CRC is not yet demonstrated: the available macrophage result is pharmacologically conditioned, functional immune and fibroblast mechanisms come from other cancers, and CRC immune associations are mainly computational. We define the conclusions permitted by each evidence class, specify clinical guardrails for prognostic and treatment-predictive claims, and propose two experiments that could establish or falsify cell-specific microenvironmental functions.
papers.venue: Clinical & translational oncology : official publication of the Federation of Spanish Oncology Societies and of the National Cancer Institute of Mexico

papers.title: Immunoaffinity-enriched extracellular vesicle proteomics for high-grade serous ovarian cancer - A UKOPS nested case-control analysis.
papers.authors: Salomon C, Lai A, Guanzon D, Scholz-Romero K, Godbole N, Palma C, Apostolidou S, Gentry-Maharaj A, Rice GE, Menon U.
papers.abstract: Objective To determine whether plasma and serum extracellular vesicles (EV) are interchangeable for immunoaffinity-enriched proteomic profiling in high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC), and whether an EV protein signature improves diagnostic performance beyond CA-125 for detecting ovarian cancer. Methods We performed immunoaffinity-enriched proteomic profiling of EV subpopulations from 243 paired EDTA plasma and serum samples in a nested case-control cohort from the UK Ovarian Cancer Population Study (controls, benign, borderline, and HGSOC). Analyses assessed proteomic depth, plasma-serum concordance, and diagnostic performance using machine learning. Results Plasma-derived EV subpopulations showed greater proteomic depth than serum, with 6439 versus 5451 protein groups identified and 2838 versus 840 proteins detected at 50% prevalence. Protein intensities were highly concordant between matrices (r = 0.86, p Conclusions Surface epitope-targeted EV subpopulation enrichment yields specific proteomic profiling of HGSOC with highly concordant biomarker signatures across plasma and serum, supporting their interchangeable use in clinical and biobank settings. The EV-augmented CA-125 model outperformed CA-125 alone, with recurrent EV proteins reflecting mucin-mediated immune evasion, and metabolic reprogramming, underscoring the translational potential of this approach for blood-based ovarian cancer detection.

papers.title: Multimodal Visual Question Answering System for Survival Prognosis in PSMA-Targeted Radiopharmaceutical Therapy.
papers.authors: Kassar M, Hu J, Rauscher I, Gomes CV, Wendler T, Ziegler S, Afshar-Oromieh A, Weber WA, Rominger A, Navab N, Eiber M, Seifert R, Shi K.
papers.abstract: Large language models show great promise for clinical decision support but generally lack medical imaging integration. Therefore, vision-language models have been proposed, but there is little evidence on their performance, particularly compared with conventional machine learning. Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted radiopharmaceutical therapy is a well-established treatment for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), but it is still not known which patients will be good long-term responders. Therefore, this study proposes a physician-inspired visual question answering (VQA) framework that emulates the structured integration of PSMA-directed imaging and clinical data used in routine clinical assessment for overall survival prognostication. Methods: As a proof of concept, we conducted a retrospective, multicenter study across 2 academic institutions that included 110 patients with mCRPC who were treated with either [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA I&T or [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA-617. Our VQA approach incorporates a 3-dimensional image encoder, the domain-specific language model RadBERT, and a cross-modal transformer to process baseline and interim (after 2 cycles) PET and SPECT images, clinical data, and clinical query. The model was trained to predict 24-mo survival, and performance was compared with state-of-the-art approaches. External validation was performed with the [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 cohort. Results: The VQA model outperformed all state-of-the-art approaches while showing accuracy comparable to the query-free attention multimodal fusion model. Specifically, it achieved 81.8% accuracy (95% CI, 0.52-0.95) when integrating SPECT or PET images with prostate-specific antigen measurements. External validation of the VQA showed 71.9% accuracy (95% CI, 0.53-0.86) after few-shot fine-tuning, with further improvement over all state-of-the-art approaches in survival stratification. The VQA approach showed the closest calibration with the ground-truth survival distribution, with no significant differences observed (log-rank test, P = 0.76). Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed the highest area under the curve (0.75) among the evaluated models. Together, these findings suggest that the VQA approach demonstrated adaptability across different PSMA ligands while maintaining slightly improved yet comparable overall survival prognostic performance. Conclusion: By adopting a physician-inspired assessment workflow, the VQA framework shows advantages in integrating imaging and laboratory data for clinical decision support compared with conventional machine learning. The preliminary results indicate that VQA-based approaches warrant future evaluation for survival prognostication in patients with mCRPC who are receiving PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy.

papers.title: AI-Guided Histopathological and Molecular Phenotyping of Salivary Glands in Sjögren's Disease: Subtyping, Mechanistic Insights, and Translational Implications-A Systematic Review and Structured Functional Synthesis.
papers.authors: Ardila CM, Pineda-Vélez E, Vivares-Builes AM.
papers.abstract: Background/objectives Salivary-gland biopsy is central to Sjögren's disease (SjD) assessment, but conventional measures incompletely capture glandular heterogeneity. This systematic review evaluated artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) applications to SjD salivary-gland histopathology and molecular profiling, including biological and translational validation. Methods PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched. Eligible studies used salivary-gland tissue as the primary analytical substrate or provided substantive glandular validation of systemic AI/ML findings. Evidence was synthesized functionally because of methodological heterogeneity. Results Twenty-five studies were included. AI/ML identified histopathological and molecular phenotypes spanning immune/interferon activation, tissue architecture and immune-cell organization, epithelial stress and metabolic/cell-death remodeling, and translational response. Only a limited subset progressed beyond computational or tissue-level confirmation to functional perturbation, pharmacological testing, in vivo validation, or human treatment-response assessment. Recurrent public-dataset reuse, small cohorts, heterogeneous pipelines, and limited independent validation constrained reproducibility. Conclusions AI/ML supports multidimensional SjD glandular phenotyping and shows emerging translational potential, but demonstrated clinical or therapeutic utility remains unestablished. Prospective multicenter validation is required before AI-derived glandular phenotypes can inform routine patient stratification or therapeutic decision-making.

papers.title: Revealing pan-cancer clonal niches of T cells from single-cell RNA sequencing using contrastive learning
papers.authors: Shorer, O.; Pinhasi, A.; Amit, R.; Yizhak, K.
papers.abstract: T-cell clonal organization is central to anti-tumor immunity, yet its functional characterization typically requires paired single-cell RNA and TCR sequencing (scRNA/TCR-seq). Existing multimodal methods integrate transcriptome and TCR information but are limited when TCR data are unavailable. Here we present CloneTrast, a supervised contrastive-learning framework that uses paired scRNA/TCR-seq during training to learn clonal-functional states from gene expression, while requiring only scRNA-seq at inference. Using paired scRNA/TCR-seq profiles from 2.6 million human T cells across 16 cancer types, CloneTrast identified distinct T-cell clonal niches not explained solely by TCR sequence similarity or conventional cell-state annotations. Among these, an NK-like T-cell niche enriched for tumor-blood shared TCRs was consistently associated with poor immunotherapy response at the pan-cancer level. Analysis of antigen-specific T-cell clones revealed that tumor-resident and blood-borne antigen-specific T cells were preferentially associated with distinct clonal niches. Overall, CloneTrast enables scalable and interpretable inference of clonal organization from single-cell transcriptomes.

papers.title: Single-cell Transcriptomics in Autoimmune Diseases: Mechanistic Insights, Cross-disease Convergence, and Translational Challenges in Rheumatoid Arthritis, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Type 1 Diabetes, and Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.authors: Nguyen TH, Nguyen TD, Hoang OT, Can TT, Nguyen MT, Tran MH, Chu HC, Nguyen DV.
papers.abstract: Autoimmune diseases are characterized by loss of immune tolerance and substantial heterogeneity across patients, tissues, and disease stages. Although bulk transcriptomic studies have identified important inflammatory pathways, they cannot directly resolve rare, transitional, and tissue-contextualized cell states that may be relevant to disease mechanisms and therapeutic response. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables transcriptomic profiling at cellular resolution, while complementary multimodal, receptor-repertoire, epigenomic, and spatial approaches can link cellular states to protein phenotype, clonal architecture, regulatory programs, and tissue context. This review critically examines recent single-cell studies in rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis, type 1 diabetes, and multiple sclerosis. Rather than providing a descriptive catalogue of published studies, we assess the strength of available evidence by distinguishing independently replicated findings from observations supported by limited studies, and cross-sectional associations from longitudinal, treatment-response, and functional evidence. Across the selected diseases, studies repeatedly report inflammatory programs involving interferon signaling, chemokine-mediated immune recruitment, and stromal-immune interactions; however, evidence for convergence at the cell-state and regulatory-network levels remains limited, and the extent to which shared signatures represent common pathogenic mechanisms rather than inflammatory context remains uncertain. We evaluate the translational potential of scRNA-seq for biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and treatment response prediction, while considering evidence from related tissue-based molecular stratification approaches, including the R4RA randomized trial in rheumatoid arthritis. R4RA provides prospective randomized evidence that synovial molecular features can enrich for differential therapeutic responses, but its use of bulk synovial transcriptomics and histopathology does not constitute prospective validation of single-cell-derived biomarkers. We further highlight cohort biases, reproducibility challenges, dissociation artifacts, computational ambiguity, and privacy concerns that constrain immediate clinical implementation. Together, these advances position single-cell profiling as a mechanistic discovery platform with substantial translational promise, contingent on standardization, validation across diverse cohorts, and integration with functional perturbation approaches.

papers.title: How compartmentalization and proliferation shape the splenic T cell repertoire during an immune response to a complex antigen in mice.
papers.authors: Buytenhuijs F, Tune C, Smits TC, Schampel A, Schierloh LK, Pagel R, Westermann J, Textor J.
papers.abstract: The adaptive immune system recognizes billions of unique antigens using highly variable T cell receptors (TCRs). To what extent TCR features shape the spatial distribution of the TCR repertoire (TCR-R) within lymphoid organs remains unclear. Here, we compared the TCR-R composition in T cell zones (TCZ), B cell zones (BCZ), and germinal centers (GC) of the spleen by analyzing the complementarity-determining region 3 of the beta chain (CDR3β) in microdissected splenic compartments from naïve and immunized mice. While we found substantial differences in TCR-R composition between these compartments, these differences largely disappeared once the effects of compartment size and proliferation were accounted for: During steady state, the few T cells found in BCZs strongly resemble random subsets of those found in TCZs. After immunization, expanded clones started appearing in the TCZ at day 3 and later shifted to the BCZ. GCs harbored even further expanded clones that were grouped into clusters with high sequence similarity. TCR-R differences during the immune response were well explained by a Galton-Watson model of T cell proliferation, suggesting that this could be the central factor shaping the observed TCR-R differences. Similarly, while TCR length and closeness to germline initially showed more pronounced differences between the compartments, our models of random distribution and proliferation explained these differences almost entirely. Hence, our findings suggest that splenic TCR-Rs are shaped predominantly by compartment size and proliferation rates rather than TCR sequence features. This would imply that quantitative assessment of TCR-R dynamics across heterogeneous spatial compartments during an immune response is only possible when these effects are explicitly accounted for.

(A) Splenic section of a naïve mouse stained for T cells (TCRβ, brown) and B cells (B220, blue) to identify the TCZ and BCZ. The inset highlights T cells (TCRβ, brown, arrows) within the BCZ. (B) Number of T cells per section area (mm 2 ) in the TCZ (black) and BCZ (blue), with means and individual animal data indicated (n = 8 mice). P value: two-tailed paired t test. (C) Laser microdissection was used to isolate both TCZ (black) and BCZ (blue), followed by next-generation sequencing of the T cell receptor beta-chain to determine the number of different clonotypes (unique amino acid sequences); means and individual animal data are indicated (n = 8 mice). papers.title: Multi-Frame Reconstruction via Clutter Filtering for Computational Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound Microflow Imaging.
papers.authors: Liang D, Chen D, Qian X, Zhong Y, Xia Y, Zhang J.
papers.abstract: Objective Existing computational reconstruction methods for plane-wave ultrasound imaging (PWI) often neglect the interference of strong tissue signals with weak flow-related scattering signals in microflow imaging. This study aims to develop a multi-frame computational ultrasound reconstruction technique that integrates multi-frame sparse constraints with RF signal preprocessing strategies to facilitate the suppression of tissue signals and background noise. Methods We propose multi-frame reconstruction of contrast-enhanced ultrasound microflow imaging. First, to prevent tissue signals from diluting the sparsity of multi-frame data, we apply singular value decomposition directly to the raw radio-frequency data, attenuating tissue-dominated components before beamforming. This yields sparser data and increases the relative contribution of flow-related components in the optimization. Results The method was evaluated in contrast-enhanced microflow simulations and an exploratory in vivo experiment involving one rabbit. Under the tested conditions, VrUSi reduced background signals and produced narrower apparent intensity profiles than delay-and-sum and single-frame computational reconstruction. In the single-rabbit experiment, VrUSi yielded higher image-domain BCR values and smaller apparent-profile FWHM values across the analyzed temporal windows. These metrics are interpreted as background suppression and apparent profile compactness under the tested conditions, rather than as evidence of improved physical contrast or spatial resolution. The findings support feasibility only for visualizing flow-related structures in the tested rabbit lower-limb acquisition.

papers.title: Noncanonical CD11b on CD8+ T cells promotes cytotoxic effector function
papers.authors: Etxaniz, J.; Bosch, A.; Prieto, E.; Perez Gutierrez, L.; Yu, K.; Velasco, P.; Egia, L.; Oyenarte, I.; Lee, S. Y.; De Blas, A.; Eguren Santamaria, I.; Jimenez Barbero, J.; F. Sanmamed, M.; Caffarel, M.; Aransay, A. M.; Gros, A.; Cespedes Donoso, P.; Palazon, A.; Ereno-Orbea, J.; Antonana-Vildosola, A.
papers.abstract: Cancer immunosurveillance largely relies on effector CD8+ T cells, yet surface determinants of cytotoxic competence within tumor-reactive populations remain incompletely defined. Using single-cell surface proteomics in a mouse breast cancer model, we identified a tumor-enriched subset of antigen-experienced CD8+ T cells expressing CD11b, a prototypic myeloid integrin. CD11b CD8 T cells were detected across mouse tumor models and human solid tumors and, within tumor-reactive populations, CD11b marked cells with greater cytotoxic potential. Following activation, naive CD8+ T cells induced ITGAM transcription and CD18-dependent CD11b surface expression. Mechanistically, CD11b localized to the peripheral adhesive ring of the immune synapse and promoted lytic-granule secretion. Accordingly, CD11b+ T cells exhibited enhanced TCR- and CAR-mediated tumor cell killing, whereas CD11b deletion impaired T cell antitumor activity. Together, these findings identify CD11b as an inducible, noncanonical component of the T cell immune synapse that marks cytotoxic competence and promotes antitumor T cell function.

papers.title: Translational Challenges and Strategies for Antibody Therapeutics in Glioblastoma.
papers.authors: Zhou Y, Li Y, Chen Y, Zhao P, Wang B, Zhu H, Sun H, Zhang T, Zhang A, Pan Y, Wang K.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains difficult to control. Monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) have transformed the treatment of several extracranial cancers, but they have not consistently improved survival in GBM. This narrative review examines the main biological and translational barriers to antibody-based therapy. It also evaluates strategies to overcome them. We reviewed preclinical, translational, and clinical evidence on antibody delivery, target stability, the tumor microenvironment, target discovery, and emerging antibody formats. Heterogeneous blood-brain and blood-tumor barriers produce uneven intratumoral exposure, especially at infiltrative margins. Spatial and temporal heterogeneity promotes antigen loss and treatment escape. Lymphocyte dysfunction, myeloid dominance, and suppressive vascular and metabolic programs further limit immune activity. Receptor-mediated transcytosis and focused ultrasound may improve delivery. Single-cell and spatial profiling, surfaceome and endocytome proteomics, longitudinal sampling, and causal inference may improve target selection. Depending on their design, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) can deliver cytotoxic payloads, whereas bispecific constructs can enable immune redirection, dual-target recognition, or receptor-mediated transport. However, clinical benefit remains limited by construct design, target accessibility, regional exposure, toxicity, and inadequate biomarker selection. Successful translation requires modality-specific alignment of exposure at the relevant site of action, target requirements, immune dependence, molecular design, and safety. Biomarker-guided patient selection, spatial pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic validation, and early evidence of clinical benefit are also essential.

figure.caption: Major barriers to monoclonal antibody efficacy in glioblastoma. ( a ) The intact blood–brain barrier (BBB) and heterogeneously leaky blood–tumor barrier (BTB) produce low or patchy regional antibody exposure. The dashed arrow indicates restricted antibody entry across the intact BBB, whereas the solid arrow indicates relatively greater antibody entry through leaky regions of the BTB. ( b ) Target heterogeneity and treatment-associated antigen loss promote clonal selection and resistant recurrence. ( c ) The schematic depicts PD-L1 on a suppressive myeloid cell engaging PD-1 on a cytotoxic T cell, CD39/CD73-mediated conversion of extracellular ATP to immunosuppressive adenosine, and myeloid-derived TGF-β and IL-10 restraining T-cell activity. papers.title: Early-life human lymphopoiesis generates a distinct B-cell lineage
papers.authors: Nazzari, A. F.; Kothari, K.; Yang, J.; Kosters, A.; Chaudhry, P.; Glass, I. A.; Birth Defects and Research Laboratory (BDRL), ; Ghosn, E.
papers.abstract: We characterize the first wave of human B-lymphopoiesis across gestation (n=42 donors) and identify a developmentally and functionally distinct B-cell lineage that shapes antibody specificity before birth. The earliest lymphoid progenitors engage an evolutionarily conserved genetic program enriched for imprinted genes associated with embryogenesis in mice and humans. These progenitors arise in the yolk sac and acquire Early B-cell Factor 1 (EBF1) in the embryonic liver, initiating B-lymphopoiesis before Hematopoietic Stem Cells emerge. Functionally, these early-life B-lymphoid progenitors (eBLPs; CD81hiTdT-IL3R+) respond to IL-3 to promote B-cell fate commitment and generate two waves of stereotyped public B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoires, shaping adaptive immunity at birth. The same molecular program and public BCRs are recapitulated during B-cell differentiation from pluripotent stem cells in vitro and after transplantation into humanized mice, where they generate antibody-secreting cells and SOX4+ B cells resembling infant lymphocytes. Developmental origin therefore intrinsically programs B-cell identity and antibody specificity.

papers.title: An ER Retrieval-and-Release System Reveals Ligand-Independent Basal Signaling by Cell Surface TCRs
papers.authors: Juraske, C.; Beyer, S.; Hartmann, S.; Peschkov, D.; Moraes Ribeiro, E.; Ebrahimiyan, H.; Ruoff, K.; Schmid, F. R.; Morath, A.; Dorer, M.; Drepper, F.; Alarcon, B.; Fiala, G.; Basiri, M.; Lillemeier, B.; Huesgen, P. F.; Timmermann, V.; Schamel, W.
papers.abstract: The T cell receptor (TCR) machinery comprises the ligand-binding TCR{beta} and the CD3 signaling dimers. Individual subunits are synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and only the fully assembled TCRs reach the cell surface. We engineered a system to retained CD3{varepsilon} is in the ER. This allowed only partial TCR assembly, while continuous retrieval of CD3{varepsilon} from the Golgi back to the ER enabled complete assembly. Synchronous TCR release by biotin addition caused a transient increase in surface TCR abundance that gradually returned to steady-state levels. Mathematical modeling revealed that TCR levels were controlled by feedback mechanisms. Notably, surface-localized, but not ER-localized, TCRs spontaneously generated ligand-independent basal signaling. Phosphoproteomic analyses revealed that this signal is similar, but not identical, to ligand-induced TCR activation signals, with distinct phosphorylation patterns already evident at the CD3 subunits. Our findings establish the TCR retrieval-and-release system as a tool to investigate ligand-independent basal TCR signaling.

papers.title: Proteome-based computational identification of cathepsin B as a TLR1/2-binding virulence factor in Naegleria fowleri and design of a novel multi-epitope vaccine candidate.
papers.authors: Chakraborty A, Malarvizhi GL, Dutta D, Chakraborty P, Bayry J, Mukherjee S.
papers.abstract: Primary Amoebic Meningoencephalitis (PAM), also known as Naegleriasis, has historically been rare but is re-emerging as a major public health concern. This acute, often fatal infection is caused by a free-living freshwater amoebic protozoan Naegleria fowleri, which invades the host central nervous system (CNS), inducing severe neuroinflammation. The immunopathogenesis of PAM remains poorly understood. Herein, the entire N. fowleri proteome was computationally analyzed, revealing Cathepsin B as a putative virulence factor with a potential to form a stable complex with human TLR1/2. This finding was further supported by molecular dynamics simulation analyses of the complex. Interestingly, Cathepsin B has been reported to mediate amoebic invasion of the host nasal mucosa, which reinforces our prediction. Based on these findings, a novel vaccine construct was designed using immunoreactive T and B cell epitopes from Cathepsin B and coupled with different TLR adjuvants. Computational analyses demonstrated the strong binding affinity of TLR4 adjuvant-coupled multi-epitope vaccine with TLR4, forming the most stable interactions. Theoretical immune simulation studies revealed that this vaccine elicits robust IgM and IgG responses upon triple administration, maintains B cell memory and triggers the expression of IFN-γ. Our data thus provide insight into the pathogenesis of PAM and offer a promising lead toward the development of an effective vaccine to combat the disease, which currently lacks reliable and effective treatments.

papers.title: Integrative Multi-Database Bioinformatics Characterization of FANCE in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Prognostic, Epigenetic, Immune, and ncRNA Associations.
papers.authors: Kim YC, Lee KS, Kim HR, Kim J.
papers.abstract: Background and Objectives: The Fanconi anemia complementation group E (FANCE) is a protein component of the Fanconi anemia (FA) DNA repair complex and contributes to genome integrity. However, its molecular and clinical relevance in liver hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC) remains incompletely understood. This study characterized the FANCE expression, prognosis, epigenetics, immune responses, noncoding RNA (ncRNA) networks, and other related molecular processes in LIHC. Materials and Methods: An integrative multi-database bioinformatics analysis was conducted using public databases and web-based platforms. FANCE expression, DNA methylation, co-expression profiles, and functional enrichment; immune cell infiltration; miRNA-ncRNA, chemical-gene, and protein-protein interactions; treatment response; and survival were evaluated. Results: FANCE expression was higher in LIHC than in non-tumor liver tissues, and this was linked to shorter survival duration. Promoter methylation was lower in LIHC, and select CpG sites were related to FANCE expression and survival. Immune analyses identified heterogeneous relationships between FANCE and inferred immune cell populations. hsa-miR-101-3p was reduced in LIHC, negatively correlated with FANCE, and linked to prolonged survival; subsequent network analysis identified candidate lncRNAs, small ncRNAs, circRNA-linked genes, and pseudogenes. FANCE-related transcriptional profiles were enriched in the cell cycle, DNA replication, FA, and other DNA-repair processes, whereas negatively correlated genes were mainly linked to hepatic metabolic functions. Exploratory treatments identified drug-dependent survival patterns related to FANCE expression and elevated levels in responders to specific immune-checkpoint inhibitors, although the discriminatory performance was modest. Conclusions: Increased FANCE expression in LIHC was linked to molecular features involving DNA methylation, immune cell composition, ncRNA-related interactions, and DNA repair programs as well as shorter survival. These findings provide an integrated molecular context for FANCE in LIHC but do not establish a causal regulation or therapeutic predictive value. Independent clinical and experimental validation studies are warranted to determine its biological and clinical significance.

papers.title: Keratinocyte FABP5 mediates saturated fat-induced MAPK/CCL20 signaling in psoriatic inflammation
papers.authors: Yu, J.; Hao, J.; Avellino, A.; Jiang, X.; Han, X.; Jabbari, A.; Li, B.
papers.abstract: Saturated fats in high-fat diets (HFDs) have been associated with increased risk and severity of psoriasis. However, the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms remain to be further defined. Here, using a unique mouse strain with keratinocyte-specific deletion of fatty acid-binding protein 5 (FABP5) (Fabp5f/fKrt6a-Cre), we reported that keratinocyte FABP5 deletion significantly attenuated saturated HFD-exacerbated psoriatic symptoms. Immunological analyses demonstrated that FABP5 specific deletion in keratinocytes selectively reduced skin TCR {gamma} {delta} dim cell accumulation and IL-17A production. Further skin bulk-RNA and single-cell RNA sequence analyses showed a strong association of keratinocyte FABP5 with increased activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathways under saturated HFD-induced obesity. Mechanistically, saturated fatty-acids (SFAs) induce FABP5-dependent MAPK activation and CCL20 production in keratinocytes, promoting the recruitment and activation of IL-17-producing {gamma}{delta} T cells in the skin. Together, these findings suggest a previously undefined FABP5/MAPK/CCL20 signaling axis that links saturated fats to exacerbated psoriatic inflammation.

papers.title: MDK + cancer-associated fibroblasts promote immunotherapy resistance through mitochondrial reprogramming in breast cancer.
papers.authors: Deng W, Fan Y, Zhang H, Wu S, Zhang K, Luo Y, Tian W, Guan H, Tang H, Zhu L, Ma Z, He R, Zou Y.
papers.abstract: Immunotherapy has improved outcomes for patients with breast cancer, yet therapeutic resistance remains a major clinical challenge. Therefore, we integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data from breast cancer cohorts treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors to identify resistance-associated cellular populations and pathways, with validation across five independent bulk RNA-seq immunotherapy cohorts. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) were isolated from anti-PD-1-resistant breast tumors for functional studies, including in vitro co-culture and in vivo models. Mitochondrial function and metabolic alterations were assessed by flow cytometry, transmission electron microscopy, ATP and adenosine quantification, and JC-1 staining. Tumor mitochondrial metabolism was markedly upregulated in anti-PD-1 non-responders and consistently associated with poor therapeutic response across validation cohorts. MDK-expressing CAFs were enriched in resistant tumors, exhibited strong interactions with tumor cells, and were negatively associated with intratumoral CD8 + T cell infiltration. Single-cell source contribution and depletion analyses identified CAF-derived MDK as the major paracrine mediator linking stromal signaling to tumor metabolic adaptation and immune suppression. Mechanistically, MDK activated SDC1-dependent PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling in cancer cells, promoting mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming, ATP production, and CD39/CD73-dependent extracellular adenosine accumulation, thereby suppressing CD8 + T cell cytotoxicity. Receptor-depletion experiments further identified SDC1 as the principal functional receptor mediating these effects. Importantly, CAF-specific MDK depletion or pharmacological MDK inhibition enhanced anti-PD-1 efficacy and restored CD8 + T cell effector activity in vivo. Collectively, MDK + CAFs facilitate anti-PD-1 resistance via mitochondrial rewiring and adenosine-mediated immunosuppression, supporting the MDK-SDC1 axis as a potential therapeutic target for overcoming resistance and improving immunotherapy efficacy in breast cancer.

papers.title: Extracellular vesicle-associated LMP1 from EBV-positive nasopharyngeal carcinoma induces LIF-mediated immunosuppressive macrophage polarization and impairs anti-tumor immunity.
papers.authors: Liu TT, Chang KP, Li MH, Sui YH, Tsai FY, Chen HC, Huang CH, Chen YW, Jiang SS, Liu SC.
papers.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is characterized by a highly infiltrated yet immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), in which tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) contribute to disease progression. Here, we identify an extracellular vesicle (EV)-mediated LMP1-NF-κB-LIF signaling axis that promotes macrophage reprogramming and immune suppression in NPC. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that EV exposure induces transcriptional remodeling across tumor and immune-cell populations, accompanied by an increased proportion of TAMs within the myeloid compartment. NPC-derived EVs were taken up by macrophages, where EV-associated LMP1 induced NF-κB activation, LIF expression, and polarization toward an immunosuppressive phenotype. Loss- and gain-of-function studies, together with structure-function analyses of the LMP1 CTAR1/CTAR2 domains, further supported the requirement of these CTAR domains for efficient NF-κB activation and LIF induction. Functionally, EV-educated macrophages exhibited impaired phagocytic activity and promoted inhibitory T-cell responses. In zebrafish, 3D spheroid, and mouse xenograft models, EV-educated macrophages promoted NPC growth and vascular dissemination, whereas blockade of LIF signaling with soluble LIFR attenuated these effects. Tumor LIF expression positively correlated with CTLA4 expression. In NPC tissues, LIF expression was preferentially associated with stromal macrophages, and elevated stromal LIF expression was associated with metastasis, advanced nodal disease, and advanced clinical stage. Stromal immune-cell LMP1 expression also correlated with LIF expression and was higher in patients who developed metastasis. Collectively, these findings support an EV-associated LMP1-NF-κB-LIF axis that links EBV-positive NPC cells to macrophage-mediated immune suppression and tumor progression and provide a basis for further investigating this pathway as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: A self-amplifying IL-1β-CCL2 circuit between macrophages and cancer-associated fibroblasts drives colorectal cancer progression.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Bao W, Li J, Jiang R, Jiang C, Li S.
papers.abstract: Reciprocal interactions between immune and stromal cells are increasingly recognized as major determinants of colorectal cancer (CRC) progression. However, the specific macrophage and fibroblast states cooperating to establish and sustain a tumor-promoting microenvironment remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify a self-reinforcing inflammatory circuit linking monocyte-derived IL-1β + macrophages with IL1R1 + cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in CRC. Integrated single-cell transcriptomic analyses of human CRC revealed a marked expansion of IL1B-associated inflammatory macrophages and IL1R1 + inflammatory CAFs, with their respective and combined transcriptional signatures associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Pseudotime analysis and Ms4a3 lineage tracing supported a predominantly monocyte-derived origin of IL-1β + macrophages in the tumor microenvironment. Mechanistically, macrophage-derived IL-1β activated IL1R1 signaling in fibroblasts, promoting the acquisition and expansion of an inflammatory CAF state. Myeloid Il1b deletion or fibroblast-lineage Il1r1 deletion disrupted this interaction and suppressed tumor growth in vivo. In turn, IL1R1 + CAFs produced abundant CCL2, which recruited CCR2 + monocytes and replenished the IL-1β + macrophage population. Fibroblast-lineage Ccl2 deletion, myeloid Ccr2 deletion, and CCL2 rescue experiments established the functional requirement of the CCL2-CCR2 axis for closure of this reciprocal circuit. Acquisition of the IL-1β + inflammatory macrophage program was further supported by coordinated NF-κB and AP-1 activity, with RELA and JUN/FOS contributing to IL1B transcriptional regulation. Finally, therapeutic blockade of either IL-1β or CCL2 disrupted the macrophage-CAF circuit, increased intratumoral CD8 + T-cell responses, and enhanced the antitumor efficacy of anti-PD-1 therapy. Collectively, our findings establish the IL-1β-IL1R1-CCL2-CCR2 axis as a self-amplifying immune-stromal circuit that sustains a tumor-promoting and immunosuppressive microenvironment in CRC. By demonstrating that disruption of this circuit restores antitumor immune activity and sensitizes tumors to PD-1 blockade, our study provides a mechanistic and preclinical rationale for targeting IL-1β-CCL2-mediated macrophage-CAF crosstalk as a combination strategy to improve immunotherapy responses in CRC.

papers.title: The role of rapamycin in neural tube defects: insights from bioinformatics analysis and experimental validation.
papers.authors: Li S, Guo J, Cao W, Wang X, Guan Z, Zhu Z, Yang A, Wang J.
papers.abstract: Neural tube defects (NTDs) are the most severe congenital malformations of the central nervous system. Fetal developmental homeostasis disruptions heighten NTDs risk through aberrant maternal-fetal signaling and periconceptional medication exposure. Rapamycin, an inhibitor of the mTOR signaling pathway, is a widely used clinical drug whose effects on embryonic neural development remain unclear. This study aimed to identify the potential drug targets for rapamycin in embryonic neural development. 18 rapamycin-NTDs targets were obtained by the network pharmacology approach. Functional enrichment analyses discovered they were associated with cell migration. AVPR2, CYP2C19, EPHB4, MMP9 and OXTR were identified as pivotal regulators mediating the effects of rapamycin on NTDs through machine learning. Immune infiltration analysis revealed the proportion of follicular helper T cells in the NTDs group was significantly lower and the pivotal genes were closely related with immune cell populations. Through single-cell RNA sequencing analysis, we identified 7 major cell types and confirmed the expression of rapamycin-NTDs key genes across them. Rapamycin-induced NTDs murine model displayed the NTDs incidence was 21.5% following 0.5 mg/kg rapamycin exposure. Subsequent animal and cell experiments confirmed that MMP9 exhibited the strongest correlation in rapamycin-induced NTDs, which could regulate cell migration. Our results suggested that rapamycin may impair cell migration by suppressing MMP9, thereby contributing to the development of NTDs. These findings provide an experimental basis for elucidating the potential mechanisms of rapamycin in embryonic neural development. MMP9 might represent a target strategy for prevention and a potential biomarker for the early diagnosis of mTOR pathway abnormality or rapamycin-induced NTDs.

papers.title: Hypoxia-mediated glioblastoma cell-macrophage crosstalk via the TIMP1-LRP1 axis induces immunosuppression.
papers.authors: Chen H, Yang Y, Chen S, Zhang X, Li S, Chai G, Nie P, Ye H, Zhang C, Zhang J, Yu W, Zhou P, Wang M, Chen J, Wang F.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma is characterized by hypoxia, immune suppression, and poor clinical outcome. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, human glioblastoma specimens, and murine models to define hypoxia-enriched tumor-associated macrophages (hTAMs) and their interaction with hypoxic glioblastoma cells (hGBM cells). hTAMs displayed an immunosuppressive transcriptional program, were enriched in mesenchymal glioblastoma, and were associated with worse survival. Hypoxia increased TIMP1 expression in glioblastoma cells, and tumor-derived TIMP1 engaged LRP1 on macrophages, promoted AKT Ser473 phosphorylation, and shifted macrophage states toward an immunosuppressive phenotype. In orthotopic murine glioma models, tumor-intrinsic Timp1 depletion reduced immunosuppressive macrophage accumulation and prolonged survival. These findings identify a hypoxia-associated tumor-macrophage signaling axis that links glioblastoma adaptation to immune suppression and supports therapeutic targeting of the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: PFOS exposure and periodontitis from adolescent burden to genetic and multiomics evidence.
papers.authors: Wan H, Wang Z, Peng H, Wang X, Xiong L, Zou X.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis can develop early in life and may be influenced by persistent environmental exposures. We integrated Global Burden of Disease 2021 data, Mendelian randomization, transcriptomics, machine learning, immune profiling, single-cell analysis, molecular modeling, and in vitro validation to investigate links between perfluorooctane sulfonate exposure and periodontitis. Periodontal disease burden remained substantial among individuals aged 5-20 years and varied across sociodemographic strata. Genetically predicted PFOS exposure was associated with increased periodontitis risk by inverse-variance weighted Mendelian randomization. Multi-omics analyses identified 151 shared targets enriched in immune-inflammatory pathways and prioritized a ten-gene signature with strong diagnostic discrimination. Single-cell analysis implicated migration inhibitory factor (MIF)-centered immune communication, whereas molecular modeling supported stable PFOS-STK17B interactions. PFOS exposure in human gingival fibroblasts increased expression of the ten prioritized genes. These findings connect population burden with genetic, molecular, and experimental evidence supporting immune-inflammatory mechanisms linking PFOS exposure to periodontitis.

papers.title: Convergent microglial and astrocytic responses across diverse stress paradigms: Integrating inflammation, metabolism, and behavior.
papers.authors: Suk K.
papers.abstract: The central nervous system responds to diverse challenges through convergent glial mechanisms, yet most reviews examine single stressor paradigms in isolation. This review uniquely integrates current knowledge across five major stress categories (psychosocial, immune/inflammatory, infectious, injury/damage, and metabolic), revealing both shared pathways and stimulus-specific glial responses that have not been systematically compared. Because microglia and astrocytes are the principal immune-metabolic sensors mediating these responses, this review is centered on these two cell types, while acknowledging that oligodendrocytes, oligodendrocyte precursor cells, and ependymal cells also participate in stress-related glial pathology, particularly with respect to white matter and cerebrospinal fluid homeostasis. While all stressors activate common inflammatory cascades including NF-κB signaling, complement activation, and inflammasome assembly, they elicit distinguishable molecular signatures. For instance, psychosocial stress uniquely engages type I interferon responses driving microglial synapse elimination. Viral infections produce severe metabolic reprogramming, hijacking host metabolism to support viral replication while depleting cellular NAD + and ATP. Autoimmune inflammation generates lipid-laden disease-associated microglia with upregulated cholesterol metabolism genes. Unlike previous reviews focusing solely on inflammation or metabolism, we emphasize their bidirectional integration as a unifying principle. Inflammatory signals trigger metabolic shifts toward aerobic glycolysis, generating lactate serving dual functions as neuronal fuel and inflammatory mediator. This metabolic reprogramming, orchestrated by pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase, hypoxia-inducible factor-1α, and mTOR, creates feedback loops linking glial dysfunction to neuronal alterations. Complement-mediated synaptic pruning, disrupted neuron-glia metabolic coupling, and impaired neurotrophic support converge to produce depression, cognitive impairment, and sickness behaviors. Individual variability reflects interactions among genetic factors, sex, age, and blood-brain barrier integrity. This cross-paradigm comparative approach identifies high-value therapeutic targets applicable across multiple conditions rather than single diseases. We propose integrated intervention strategies simultaneously targeting inflammatory and metabolic pathways, guided by single-cell profiling for personalized medicine tailored to individual patient molecular signatures. We further discuss the conceptual overlaps inherent to the five-category classification scheme adopted here and outline the limitations of extrapolating across heterogeneous stress paradigms, glial cell types, and species.

papers.title: Overcoming adaptive resistance to cancer immunotherapy: molecular targeting strategies for the tumor microenvironment.
papers.authors: To KKW, Ma T, Wang L, Cho WC.
papers.abstract: Introduction Immunotherapy resistance is mediated by mechanisms distinct from those underlying conventional chemotherapy, including tumor-intrinsic alterations, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, and other host factors, that collectively constrain durable responses. Areas covered This review provides a systematic evaluation of molecular targeting strategies aimed at overcoming immunotherapy resistance. We examine the principal resistance mechanisms including antigen loss, upregulation of alternative checkpoints (LAG-3, TIM-3, TIGIT), metabolic T-cell impairment, myeloid-derived suppressor cell and regulatory T-cell infiltration, cancer stem cell-driven evasion, epigenetic silencing, and T-cell exhaustion. Novel pharmacological approaches for resistance circumvention, including next-generation checkpoint blockers, bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, epigenetic and metabolic modulators, microenvironment-remodeling agents, and PROTAC-based checkpoint degraders, are critically assessed with an aim to link preclinical mechanistic evidence to clinical outcomes. Expert opinion Despite the increasing number of combination immunotherapy strategies, durable clinical benefit remains limited for many patients. We attribute this to tumor heterogeneity, adaptive feedback, and inadequate biomarker-guided patient selection. Future progress will require systems-level approaches integrating single-cell and spatial multi-omics with adaptive, pharmacodynamically informed clinical trial designs. Ultimately, improving long-term outcomes will depend on the ability to predict and intercept tumor-immune co-evolution before resistance becomes established.

papers.title: Macrophage- or neutrophil-expressed UPP1 drives tumor growth and immune suppression in the tumor microenvironment.
papers.authors: Li Y, Ran Q, Xiong A, Jiang M, Xu F, Wei Y, Gu J, Li G, Ge D, Lu C.
papers.abstract: Uridine phosphorylase 1 (UPP1) has recently emerged as a metabolic regulator with critical roles in tumor cell biology. However, its expression pattern and functional significance in nonmalignant components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain largely unexplored. Here, we performed a comprehensive pan-cancer single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealing that UPP1 is highly expressed not only in tumor cells but also in tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and neutrophils (TANs). Clinically, UPP1 expression in TAMs and TANs correlates with poor prognosis and diminished response to immunotherapy across multiple cancer types. Mechanistically, UPP1 up-regulation could be driven by NF-κB signaling. Functionally, UPP1 reprograms macrophages toward a tumor-promoting phenotype, characterized by enhanced glycolysis, ATP-adenosine signaling activation, and increased production of immunosuppressive cytokines such as granulocyte colony-stimulating factor. In neutrophils, UPP1 also supports TAN polarization, influences neutrophil extracellular trap release, and contributes to broad immunosuppressive remodeling. In vivo, targeting UPP1 in macrophages or neutrophils reprograms the immune landscape and restrains tumor progression. Together, our findings uncover a previously underappreciated role of UPP1 in nonmalignant immune populations and establish it as a key immune mediator within the TME, offering a potentially promising therapeutic target for enhancing antitumor immunity.

papers.title: Intranasal HSV‑1 infection drives region‑specific interferon‑dominant microglial remodeling.
papers.authors: Frietze S, Lunn C, Oldham D, Boyd JR, Bubak AN, Saucedo AB, Nagel MA, Restrepo D, Bruce KD, Niemeyer CS.
papers.abstract: Herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) is a neurotropic pathogen capable of invading the central nervous system (CNS) and is associated with chronic neuroinflammation, cognitive impairment, and neurodegenerative disease. While microglia orchestrate the initial immune response to HSV‑1, the molecular mechanisms that regulate their sustained neuroinflammatory activity in vivo remain poorly understood. To define the transcriptional and epigenetic mechanisms that shape microglial responses during acute HSV-1 infection in vivo, we have, for the first time, integrated single‑nucleus RNA sequencing, chromatin accessibility profiling, and spatial proteomics and transcriptomics in an intranasal HSV‑1 infection model. Single-cell multiome analysis of CD11b⁺ nuclei identified transcriptionally and epigenetically distinct microglial and macrophage populations. HSV-1 infection redistributed monocyte-lineage states, with a marked overrepresentation of interferon (IFN)‑responsive microglia and macrophage-associated populations characterized by amplification of Stat1/2, Irf1, and Cebpb rather than reflecting uniform inflammatory activation. In parallel, homeostatic microglial gene signatures (e.g., ApoE, Cst3) were reduced following HSV-1 infection. Spatial transcriptomics localized HSV‑1 antigen to discrete brainstem regions, which were enriched for predicted STAT1/2, IRF1, and CEBPB‑regulated targets identified through single‑nuclei analysis, demonstrating that these inferred transcriptional networks are activated within anatomically defined regions in vivo. Complementary spatial proteomics further confirmed increased microglial activation and astrocytic responses specifically within HSV-1 antigen-positive regions. Together, these integrated multiomic analyses demonstrate that HSV-1 induces localized transcriptional and epigenetic remodeling of microglia dominated by IFN-driven regulatory programs and a loss of homeostatic signatures. By linking single-cell regulatory architecture to spatially restricted tissue responses, our findings provide mechanistic insight into how localized viral infection sustains neuroinflammation, contributing to long-term neurological vulnerability and neurodegenerative disease risk.
