papers.title: Cirrhosis-associated immune dysfunction reflects impaired intestinal CD8ab⁺ intraepithelial lymphocyte compartmentalization
papers.authors: Akkaya, C.; van Sligtenhorst, M.; Shaukat, S.; Modave, E.; Dumarey, A.; Caxali, G. H.; Verbiest, A.; de Meyere, L.; Vrancken, S.; van Meerbeeck, L.; van Melkebeke, L.; Dedoncker, N.; Humblet-Baron, S.; Burton, O. T.; Liston, A.; Shimobayashi, M.; Vanuytsel, T.; van der Merwe, S.; Yshii, L.; Denadai-Souza, A.
papers.abstract: Bacterial infections drive decompensation and mortality in cirrhosis, yet the mechanisms underlying cirrhosis-associated immune dysfunction remain unclear. Current models invoke adaptive immune exhaustion, whereas intestinal intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs), which mediate epithelial surveillance and microbial containment, remain unexplored. We combined spectral flow cytometry of paired duodenal biopsies and blood, plasma proteomics, immunofluorescence and single-cell RNA sequencing in healthy volunteers and patients with compensated or decompensated cirrhosis. The healthy duodenal epithelium was dominated by CD8 alpha beta IELs, which were depleted in cirrhosis, whereas innate cytotoxic populations expanded. CD8 alpha beta IEL loss correlated with plasma markers of bacterial translocation. Residual IELs showed attenuated antimicrobial programs, confirmed by reduced granulysin protein, and enriched cytotoxic pathways. IEL depletion was accompanied by reduced CCR9 on circulating and mucosal CD8 T cells and elevated plasma CCL25. Exposing blood mononuclear cells to patient-level CCL25 concentrations reduced surface CCR9, indicating ligand-driven desensitization. In contrast, circulating lymphocytes retained functional competence and lacked exhaustion markers. Cirrhosis-associated immune dysfunction thus reflects failed intestinal compartmentalization of CD8 alpha beta T cells, linked to disruption of the CCL25-CCR9 axis, rather than systemic exhaustion.

papers.title: Non-canonical IL-2 signaling facilitates peripheral regulatory T cell differentiation
papers.authors: Meecham, A.; Kim, S. H. J.; Fernandes de Lima, M. H.; Tang, M.; Liao, B.; Chan, S.; Lee, H.-s.; Lu, L.-F.; Zhang, Z.; Jefferies, C.; Guma, M.; Lopez-Ramirez, M.-A.; Ginsberg, M. H.
papers.abstract: Non-canonical IL-2 signaling, termed Monoclonal antibody or Matrix-directed Alternative Cytokine Signaling (MACS), is mediated by a CD25-chemokine receptor complex and operates in concert with the canonical JAK-STAT5 pathway; however, its role in T cell homeostasis remains poorly defined. Here, we uncover a role for MACS in regulatory T cell (Treg) differentiation and functional specification. We generated Il2E66K/E66K mice in which CD25-CCR7 assembly is disrupted and IL-2-induced STAT5 phosphorylation is preserved. Immunophenotyping analysis by flow cytometry revealed that MACS deficiency reduces the accumulation of Nrp1- Foxp3+ Tregs in gut-associated lymphoid tissues from 24-weeks-old Il2E66K/E66K mutant mice. Single-cell transcriptomics, functional suppression assays, and in vitro differentiation revealed that MACS engagement drives Treg differentiation and sustains effector Treg programs - marked by robust IL-10 expression - in part via an AP-1-dependent transcriptional network. These findings establish IL-2 MACS as a distinct signal directing peripheral immune tolerance and highlight a potential node for targeted immunomodulation.

papers.title: CAR T cells from code to clinic: Framing modeling approaches with current translational research goals.
papers.authors: Sant'Anna LE, Roy R, Schwab JC, Perez JI, Mayalu MN.
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has transformed treatment of resistant cancers, yet it faces major limitations such as variable patient responses, relapse, and safety issues. Optimizing CAR T cell treatment regimens and genetic design could offer solutions to some of these problems, but the resulting design space is often too large to explore experimentally alone. Mathematical modeling-spanning ordinary differential equation (ODE), agent-based, statistical, and machine learning methods-provides a framework to link mechanistic understanding of CAR T cells to predictive design and clinical decision-making. Here, we present a perspective that organizes modeling approaches around key translational challenges in CAR T therapy, evaluating the strengths, limitations, and data gaps of current approaches. We outline a roadmap for clinicians and modelers alike, highlighting advances in machine learning, multiscale modeling, control theory, and alternative cell types as emerging opportunities in model-guided design of next-generation cell therapies.

papers.title: ShenqiYichang decoction enhances colorectal cancer immune efficacy via IDO1 mediated reduction of Treg infiltration.
papers.authors: Yang Y, Li L, Fang Y, Yang Z, Xue R, Gao M, Zhou L, Zhang J, Zhang D.
papers.abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance ShenqiYichang decoction (SQYCD) is a traditional Chinese formula indicated for colorectal cancer (CRC). Studies have shown that SQYCD potentiates antitumor immunity and enhances the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Aim of the study This study aimed to investigate the mechanism of SQYCD in enhancing ICIs efficacy against microsatellite stability (MSS) CRC. Materials and methods An in vivo CT26 tumor-bearing mouse model was established. The antitumor efficacy of SQYCD alone and in combination with ICIs was evaluated, and Treg infiltration was detected by immunofluorescence. Network pharmacology and bioinformatics were used to screen potential targets of SQYCD for MSS CRC. In vitro, MSS CRC cell lines were used for CCK-8 to assess cell proliferation. A CT26-Treg co-culture system was used to analyze Treg proportion by flow cytometry. Western blot, qRT-PCR, ELISA, and Co-IP assays were used to assess the IDO1/Kyn/p-AKT axis and IDO1-PI3K interactions. UPLC-Q-TOF/MS and molecular docking were subsequently employed to identify the key absorbed components involved in the IDO1-PI3K pathway regulated by SQYCD. Results In vivo, SQYCD alone did not affect the proliferation of MSS CRC cells but inhibited Treg infiltration. When combined with ICIs, SQYCD enhanced the efficacy of ICIs, significantly inhibiting tumor cell proliferation and further reducing Treg infiltration. Network pharmacology and bioinformatics analysis suggested IDO1 as a potential target of SQYCD in MSS CRC. In vitro, SQYCD-containing serum did not reduce MSS CRC cell proliferation but decreased Treg proportion in the CT26-Treg co-culture system. SQYCD also promoted IL-2 levels while downregulating IL-10 and TGF-β levels. Mechanistically, SQYCD suppressed the IDO1/Kyn pathway and p-AKT expression. Additionally, components of SQYCD significantly reduced the IDO1-PI3K interaction. LC-MS and molecular docking results suggested that esculetin, glycitin, and hydroxygenkwanin may be the active components of SQYCD that reduce the IDO1-PI3K interaction. Conclusion SQYCD reduces Treg infiltration by inhibiting both the IDO1/Kyn/p-AKT and the IDO1-PI3K interaction, consequently enhancing the efficacy of ICIs.

papers.title: Virus-like particle vaccines: from antigen architecture to antigen presentation and adaptive immune responses.
papers.authors: Zhang Z, Zheng H, Liu L.
papers.abstract: Introduction Virus-like particles (VLPs) mimic key structural features of native viruses while lacking a replication-competent viral genome, combining favorable safety with multivalent antigen presentation and strong immunogenicity. Yet, how VLP design influences the quality and persistence of adaptive immunity remains incompletely understood. Areas covered This review examines relevant literature identified through targeted searches on recent advances in VLP engineering, with emphasis on particle architecture, antigen-display strategies, and structural determinants of immune recognition. We discuss how VLPs facilitate antigen presentation by antigen-presenting cells and shape CD4 + and CD8 + T-cell responses, immune memory, and T follicular helper cell-B-cell interactions within germinal centers. Emerging approaches linking VLP design with humoral and cellular immunity are also considered. Expert opinion The next generation of VLP vaccines will require a transition from empirical enhancement of immunogenicity toward precision engineering of immune responses. A major challenge is to establish robust and transferable structure-immunity relationships while addressing manufacturing feasibility, quality control, potency assessment, and product comparability. Advances in computational protein design, structural biology, and high-dimensional immune profiling are expected to enable increasingly quantitative and mechanism-based optimization of VLP platforms. However, fully predictive control over human immune responses will remain a complex challenge.

papers.title: Orthogonal Fc engineering enables multiplexed delivery of mRNA-encoded bispecific antibodies that constrain viral escape.
papers.authors: Wec AZ, Cho A, Pecetta S, Hu X, Bender MF, Laciak AR, Hou J, Jian F, Korkmaz EN, Sharma A, Bopp N, Sazinsky S, Montes-Berrueta D, Speidel T, Lee D, Jagadeesh Reddy PB, Cao Y, Carfi A, Schief WR, Walker LM.
papers.abstract: The continuous antigenic evolution of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has repeatedly undermined the effectiveness of monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapies, underscoring the need for innovative approaches that improve therapeutic mAb breadth and durability of protection. Here, we engineered messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA)-encoded bispecific antibodies (bsAbs) that, upon intravenous administration in lipid nanoparticles, achieved high serum concentrations, extended half-life, and serum neutralizing titers exceeding 1:10,000 in human neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn)-expressing mice. To enhance resilience to viral escape, we used structure-guided computational design to introduce Fc modifications that promoted selective homodimerization, thereby enabling codelivery of multiple mRNA-encoded bsAbs with cognate heavy chain pairing. In vivo expression of a triple bsAb combination resulted in broad serum neutralization of historical and contemporary SARS-CoV-2 variants, including the highly mutated BA.3.2.2 lineage. Preexposure prophylaxis with the mRNA-delivered bsAb combination conferred protection against SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1.5 challenge, preventing weight loss and decreasing viral burden in the lungs compared with vehicle control treatment. Together, the results provide proof of principle for mRNA-based delivery of Fc-engineered bsAb combinations to combat SARS-CoV-2 and potentially other rapidly evolving pathogens.

papers.title: OmniScore: Universal Scoring of Diverse Biomolecular Complexes via Equivariant Geometry-Aware Discrete Representation Learning
papers.authors: Bui, T.-C.; Hong, Y.; Song, J.; Tao, Y.; Chung, I.; Park, J. G.; Ko, J.; Lee, J.
papers.abstract: Biomolecular structures provide a common physical basis for understanding molecular function and interactions. However, computational models typically specialize in individual molecular classes or tasks, hindering a unified representation of structural information across biological systems. Here we introduce OmniScore, a universal geometric encoder that learns shared representations of proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules and their complexes. Pretraining integrates geometric graph encoding, sequential modeling and tokenization with structural and physicochemical supervision. The frozen pretrained encoder supports complex-level model quality assessment and interaction prediction, as well as residue-level prediction, through task-specific heads. OmniScore outperforms the evaluated antibody--antigen quality-assessment baselines and also improves RNA structure ranking over baselines. For peptide-major histocompatibility complex interaction prediction, the OmniScore embeddings complement structure-prediction confidence metrics to improve predictive performance. Together, these findings support OmniScore as a shared geometric foundation for biomolecular representation and scoring across molecular classes and prediction scales, which may facilitate multi-component therapeutics development.

papers.title: BCell-Epitope-Prediction: A local, reproducible pipeline for multi-epitope vaccine design: integration and structural validation against a panel of PDB antigen-antibody complexes
papers.authors: Sierra Vera, E. L. E.; Pueche Granados, B.; Gomez, C. E.; Sorzano, C. O. S.
papers.abstract: Epitope-based subunit vaccine design requires chaining together heterogeneous analyses: B-cell antigenicity, topological accessibility, self-tolerance, allergenicity, T-helper/T-cytotoxic immunogenicity, and literature corroboration, historically scattered across separate, often web-only tools. This work presents a computational pipeline that integrates fourteen external tools across eight main phases, runs locally without network calls, and uses content-based self-caching. B-cell antigenicity is assessed via four engines (BepiPred-3.0, EpiDope, DiscoTope-3.0, and ScanNet), whose per-residue scores are fused into a single signal before thresholding. Validation used a panel of seventeen real antigen-antibody complexes from the Protein Data Bank spanning five pathogenic species, with ground truth from structural contact and independent literature verification. Fusing the four engines' scores, completed to a fixed candidate count, outperforms the best individual engine in F1 while reducing predicted residue volume. T-helper and T-cytotoxic immunogenicity are evaluated over each antigen's complete sequence, independently of the B-cell candidates. The final construct retains a B-cell epitope in 13 of 17 structures, and a T-cell block in 13 of 17 antigens, of which 6 match literature-documented epitopes and 2 more show partial correspondence.

papers.title: Cross-scale genetic analysis prioritizes shared regulatory variation, cell-type contributions, co-expression programs, and exon-level patterns in atopic dermatitis and asthma.
papers.authors: Liao CC, Li JM.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) and asthma frequently co-occur, yet the regulatory mechanisms connecting cutaneous and airway inflammation remain unclear. We integrated European genome-wide association statistics for AD (22,474 cases; 774,187 controls) and asthma (56,167 cases; 352,255 controls) with expression and splicing quantitative trait loci (QTLs), immune single-cell expression QTLs, single-cell transcriptomes, and spatial transcriptomics. The AD dataset compared lesional skin with healthy controls, whereas the asthma dataset paired allergen and diluent challenges in four participants. Each was analyzed within its own design, and cross-disease comparison used independently derived annotations and gene sets. Regulatory QTL enrichment implicated skin, lung, fibroblast, and immune-related tissues. Cell-stratified Mendelian randomization identified multi-instrument associations in memory B cells (odds ratio = 1.35, 95% confidence interval 1.18-1.56; false discovery rate = 1.1 × 10⁻⁴) and immature/naïve B cells (1.26, 1.10-1.45); single-instrument estimates were exploratory regardless of false discovery rate, and no association has been independently replicated. T-cell co-expression analysis identified three cross-disease module overlaps-translational, metabolic-cytoskeletal, and cytotoxic effector-each significant after multiple-testing correction across 42 module comparisons. Airway transcripts in the asthma T-cell compartment were attributed predominantly to ambient RNA. Bayesian colocalization identified signals at 19 AD and 72 asthma loci and 112 shared genes. Integrated evidence prioritized SLC22A4, CTSW, IL1R1, RMI2, and IRF1; four ranked in the top five under all eight scoring schemes and IRF1 under seven, and all five retained top-ten ranking in ≥ 98.9% of 10,000 moderately concentrated randomized weightings. These results prioritize shared regulatory candidates for validation.

papers.title: A review on MMP-2 modulating agents from natural and synthetic sources and their role in inflammatory bowel disease.
papers.authors: Ragunath M, Ardra S, Balde A, Nazeer RA.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), encompassing Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, is characterized by chronic intestinal inflammation, epithelial barrier dysfunction, immune dysregulation, and aberrant extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Matrix metalloproteinase-2 (MMP-2), a zinc-dependent gelatinase, has emerged as a critical regulator of intestinal homeostasis owing to its dual role in tissue repair and inflammatory tissue destruction. Unlike several inducible matrix metalloproteinases, MMP-2 is constitutively expressed and tightly regulated through interactions with membrane-type MMPs, tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs), cytokines, redox signalling, and microbial factors. Dysregulated MMP-2 activity contributes to epithelial barrier disruption, leukocyte infiltration, chronic inflammation, fibrosis, and disease progression in IBD. This review summarizes the current understanding of MMP-2 biology, activation mechanisms, and immunopharmacological functions in intestinal inflammation, while critically evaluating therapeutic strategies aimed at its modulation. Particular emphasis is placed on natural and synthetic MMP-2 modulators, including animal-derived peptides and endogenous inhibitors, plant-derived polyphenols, flavonoids, alkaloids, terpenoids, and rationally designed small-molecule and peptidomimetic inhibitors. Emerging nanocarrier-based and targeted delivery systems are also discussed as approaches to enhance selectivity and minimize systemic toxicity. Furthermore, the review highlights the limitations of broad-spectrum MMP inhibition and underscores the need for site-specific modulation that preserves physiological tissue remodeling while suppressing pathological activity. Advances in precision medicine, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, organoid-based disease models, and microbiome-informed therapeutic strategies are expected to facilitate the development of next-generation MMP-2-targeted interventions. Collectively, MMP-2 represents a promising yet complex therapeutic target whose successful modulation may improve long-term outcomes in IBD.

papers.title: ATG16L2 as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in kidney renal clear cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Xu X, Zhou C, Zhang R, Fan C, Wang Q.
papers.abstract: Kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (KIRC) carries substantial clinical challenges. This study examined ATG16L2 , an autophagy-related gene family member, across TCGA, CPTAC, GEO, and an independent cohort to assess its expression patterns, clinicopathological associations, and prognostic relevance. Immune landscapes were characterized through CIBERSORT, ESTIMATE, xCell, and single-cell analyses. Functional investigations employed shRNA-mediated knockdown in KIRC cell lines and xenograft models, with attention to the Notch signaling pathway. ATG16L2 was elevated in KIRC and associated with advanced disease and poorer survival. Its expression correlated with altered immune infiltration and immune checkpoint levels. Silencing ATG16L2 attenuated proliferative, migratory, and invasive capacities, partly through Notch pathway modulation. These findings position ATG16L2 as a prognostic indicator and immune microenvironment modulator in KIRC, with implications for therapeutic strategies targeting the ATG16L2-Notch axis.

papers.title: Tumor DNA methylation subtypes and expression levels of CFISH predict response and overall survival to immunochemotherapy.
papers.authors: Fuchs HS, Xie P, James SA, Cao Z, Carroll TM, Inoue M, Siejka-Zielińska P, Kim S, Jacobs BA, Shepherd E, Wang E, Chadwick JA, Amess B, Parkes D, Lord SR, Mukherjee S, Underwood T, Karydis I, Petty R, Griffiths L, McCann KJ, Wilding S, Griffiths G, Pike C, Lawrence M, McGowan DR, Bradley KM, Kriaucionis S, Song CX, Owen RP, Schuster-Boeckler B, Middleton MR, Lu X, LUD2015-005 Project Team.
papers.abstract: Background Predicting patient response to immunochemotherapy is vital but challenging and poorly studied in the (neo)adjuvant setting. We showed that tumor monocyte content (TMC) predicts overall survival of advanced esophageal cancer (OC) in response to immunochemotherapy. We report clinical outcomes of 35 operable OC patients receiving ICI-based therapy and molecular profiling of the unique phase-2 LUD2015-005 trial treating 73 OC patients (38 advanced/inoperable and 35 operable) in the (neo)adjuvant setting. Methods LUD2015-005 trial patients were treated with 4-week immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-only before combination with standard of care. Paired and longitudinally collected biopsies of tumor and multiple adjacent normal sites were bi-dissected to extract DNA and RNA. Whole-genome, methylome, single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data generated from the entire LUD2015-005 cohort were used for cell-deconvolution and data integration analysis. Findings Neoadjuvant ICI-based combination therapy of operable OC in the LUD2015-005 trial revealed improved overall outcomes. Tumor monocytes contribute to tumor immune microenvironment (TiME) remodeling and associate with tumor reactive CD8 + T cells upon ICI+ chemotherapy/chemoradiotherapy. We identified five DNA-methylation subtypes with distinct TiME and a TMC-related five-gene signature CFISH (CXCL8, FCN1, IFI30, SLC11A1, and HLA-DRA) as highly predictive biomarkers of overall survival in OC and beyond. Conclusions These findings highlight the importance of the myeloid compartment in ICI response and the potential of CFISH and tumor DNA methylation in patient stratification for immunochemotherapy. Funding This work is mainly funded by Ludwig Institute for Cancer Research, CRUK Grants A21998 and C30423/A2541, and NIHR Oxford Biomedical Research Center. AstraZeneca UK Limited provided durvalumab and tremelimumab for LUD2015-005.

papers.title: Bridging the Translational Gap in Sex-Specific Alzheimer's Disease Using Human iPSC-Based Neural Cell Models.
papers.authors: Supakul S, Phisalaphong R, Changchai M, Okano H.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) exhibits marked sex differences in disease prevalence, progression, and therapeutic responsiveness, with women disproportionately affected by both cognitive decline and neuropathological burden. Although sex hormones such as estrogen, progesterone, and testosterone have demonstrated neuroprotective effects in experimental systems, clinical outcomes of hormone-based interventions remain inconsistent. Emerging evidence further indicates that sex-specific molecular programs extend beyond endocrine signaling alone and include cell type-specific transcriptional architectures established across the lifespan. Recent single-cell transcriptomic studies have suggested that biological sex fundamentally shapes multicellular brain vulnerability. However, prevailing preclinical systems incompletely model human endocrine aging, sex chromosome biology, and patient-specific genetic heterogeneity, thereby limiting translational relevance. Human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived neural systems provide a new platform for mechanistically interrogating sex-specific pathways within human genetic backgrounds. By preserving donor-specific genetic backgrounds and sex chromosome complement, iPSC-derived neurons, astrocytes, microglia, and multicellular systems enable controlled investigation of hormone-responsive phenotypes, APOE-associated mechanisms, and cell type-specific transcriptional programs. However, their developmental immaturity and incomplete representation of systemic aging, vascular, immune, and endocrine physiology limit direct extrapolation to patients. Integration of these cellular systems with human omics datasets, neuropathological observations, and clinical studies may therefore help address specific components of the translational gap in AD.

papers.title: Mechanical Compression-Induced Peripheral Neuropathic Pain: From Astrocyte Mechanosensing and Phenotypic Reprogramming to CCL2-CCR2 Axis-Targeted Therapies.
papers.authors: Shen Y, He M, Wang B, Liu Z, Wu S, Chen LH, Ai K, Lv H, Sheng W, Zhang Z, Lv Z, Lv L.
papers.abstract: Neuropathic pain (NP) arising from mechanical nerve compression is driven by central sensitization, in which reactive astrocytes and chemokine-mediated neuro-glial crosstalk act as master regulators. Among candidate chemokine axes, the C-C motif chemokine ligand 2 (CCL2) and its receptor, C-C chemokine receptor type 2 (CCR2), most directly couple astrocyte activation to nociceptive signaling, and aberrant activation of this axis is conserved across diverse compression paradigms. This review synthesizes current evidence on how mechanical compression is translated into persistent pain via astrocytes. We first outline the methodological foundations and anatomical diversity of compression models, together with advances and limitations in astrocyte profiling. We then trace how mechanosensitive receptors and ion channels initiate astrocytic activation and examine the multicellular origins of CCL2 and its intracellular and epigenetic regulation. Equally important are single-cell-resolved phenotypic heterogeneity beyond the A1/A2 dichotomy, sexual dimorphism in astrocytic versus microglial pathways and the collapse of homeostatic, non-inflammatory astrocyte functions. Downstream, astrocyte-derived CCL2 engages neuronal and microglial CCR2 and together with interleukin (IL) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) cytokine cascades, drives feed-forward glial crosstalk and sensitization of spinal and supraspinal circuits. Building on this framework, we evaluate a range of strategies targeting the axis, spanning small-molecule inhibitors, natural products, gene-silencing and precision-delivery platforms, and combinatorial regimens. We also highlight the clinical translational gap, exemplified by the discontinued anti-CCL2 monoclonal antibody carlumab, the Phase II analgesic failure of the CCR2 antagonist AZD2423, the halted CCR2/CCR5 antagonist PF-04634817, and the absence of JAK inhibitors from pain randomized controlled trials. Finally, we identify three translational bottlenecks: limited tools for resolving astrocyte states in vivo, insufficient large-animal pharmacological validation, and compensatory chemokine-receptor redundancy. We further outline directions for next-generation, multi-modal interventions.

papers.title: GM-CSF modulates conserved ILC-like transcriptional states and myeloid cell signaling during ulceration in Crohns disease
papers.authors: Morrison, J. K.; Sabic, K.; Maskey, N.; Talware, S.; Hsu, N.-y.; Chasteau, C.; Aslinger, E.; Herb, J. T.; Nayar, S.; Levantovsky, R.; Tastad, C.; Moss, R.; Soto, A.; Garcia-barros, M.; Ntunzwenimana, J.; Glass, M.; Bao, M.; Zhang, J.; Gettler, K.; Han, H.; Stevens, J.; Tavares, L.; Thin, T. H.; Khaitov, S.; Greenstein, A.; Brody, R.; Chu, J.; Mortha, A.; Cho, J. H.; Chuang, L.-s.
papers.abstract: Macrophage (M-), granulocyte (G-), and granulocyte-macrophage (GM-) colony-stimulating factors (CSFs) regulate myeloid cell function, yet their relative roles during inflammation remain poorly defined. To investigate how CSFs are spatially organized in Crohn's disease, we performed Xenium single-cell spatial transcriptomics on ileal tissues, revealing cell-type-specific expression and source-target interactions for each CSF. GM-CSF, unlike M-CSF or G-CSF, was locally enriched in ulcerated regions and associated with STAT5 phosphorylation within macrophage aggregates. To study functional consequences of GM-CSF signaling, we developed a csf2rb-/- zebrafish model of intestinal injury. Loss of GM-CSF signaling exacerbated epithelial damage and inflammation, whereas recombinant human GM-CSF limited injury and was associated with a reduced DSS-induced increase in putative ILC1-like cells, preservation of putative ILC3-like cells, and increased IL-22 production. Cross-species single-cell analysis revealed conserved ILC-like transcriptional states and GM-CSF-responsive myeloid transcriptional programs. Together, these findings demonstrate a protective role for GM-CSF during intestinal inflammation and support a model in which spatially localized GM-CSF signaling and associated myeloid and ILC-like cell states contribute to intestinal immune homeostasis in Crohn's disease.

papers.title: Interleukin-1β as a central driver of inflammation: Mechanistic insight into activation, receptor signaling, and therapeutic inhibition.
papers.authors: Tamang R, Kumari P, Gupta M.
papers.abstract: Interleukin-1β (IL-1β) is a major pro-inflammatory cytokine that links innate immune sensing, inflammasome activation, and downstream inflammatory signaling. Dysregulated production or signaling of IL-1β contributes to a broad range of disorders, including monogenic autoinflammatory syndromes, rheumatic diseases, cardiovascular and metabolic disorders, and neurodegenerative conditions. Consequently, the IL-1β/interleukin-1 receptor type I (IL-1RI) signaling axis has emerged as an important therapeutic target in inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases. This review discusses the key molecular mechanisms governing IL-1β biosynthesis, inflammasome-mediated activation, receptor recognition, and downstream signal transduction. It also highlights the experimentally validated receptor-binding hotspots, molecular determinants governing ligand recognition, receptor activation, and assembly of the signaling-competent IL-1β/IL-1RI/IL-1RAcP complex, followed by a description of modern computational approaches, including molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, pharmacophore modelling, QSAR, virtual screening, and artificial intelligence-assisted drug discovery. The emerging therapeutic strategies, including FDA-approved biologics, natural product-derived modulators, synthetic small-molecule inhibitors, drug-repurposing approaches, and recent advances in structure-based computational drug discovery, are also described. By bridging fundamental cytokine biology with translational therapeutics and structure-guided drug design, this review provides a contemporary perspective on IL-1β signaling and highlights future opportunities for the development of precision immunotherapies targeting IL-1β.

papers.title: Zinc peroxide-coated gold nanorods as the therapeutic adjuvants for photothermal enhanced chemodynamic therapy and metalloimmunotherapy against tumor.
papers.authors: Yi H, Jiang C, Pan ZY, Fu N, Guo L, Zhan Z, Li J, Zhao X, Zhang L, Zheng Y, Zhang DY.
papers.abstract: Introduction Traditional tumor therapies have limited efficacy, leading to a high mortality rate. Although immunotherapy holds considerable therapeutic promise, clinical immunotherapy for solid tumors only elicits durable responses in a minority of patients. This limitation is largely attributed to the highly immunosuppressive nature of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Notably, conventional chemodynamic therapy (CDT) is hampered by endogenous hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) shortage in tumor cells, and AZP compensates this defect via in-situ H 2 O 2 self-supplementation to amplify hydroxyl radical generation. Objectives To develop a nanoplatform capable of systematically enhancing anti-tumor immunity, we rationally constructed a PEGylated zinc peroxide-coated gold nanorod (AZP) as a therapeutic adjuvant with acid-responsive properties for the combination therapy of cancer. Methods Gold nanorod-based adjuvants coated with zinc peroxide were successfully prepared via chemical oxidation, followed by PEGylation. The morphology and size of the AZP were characterized using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and hydrodynamic diameter measurements. The elemental composition of AZP was determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis. The acid-responsive degradation and photothermally enhanced catalytic properties of AZP were evaluated using TEM, inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry, absorption spectroscopy, and thermal imaging tracing. The therapeutic mechanism of AZP at the cellular level was investigated through a series of experiments, including TEM, fluorescence imaging, immunofluorescence assays, Seahorse analysis, western blotting, and bioinformatics approaches, which comprehensively clarified the anti-tumor mechanism of AZP. Bilateral tumor and metastatic tumor models were established to verify the anti-tumor efficacy and mechanism of AZP at the animal level. Specifically, fluorescence imaging, immunofluorescence staining, tissue staining analysis, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and flow cytometry were performed to assess the in vivo therapeutic effects. Results In the acidic TME, the AZP nanoplatform releases H 2 O 2 and zinc ions, which increases the reactive oxygen species level in cancer cells. Additionally, due to its photothermally enhanced peroxidase-like activity, AZP induces the generation of more hydroxyl radicals under light irradiation. These effects synergistically disrupt lysosomes and mitochondria in tumor cells, block autophagy, and ultimately lead to tumor cell death. Furthermore, zinc supplementation by AZP enhances the activation of the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase and stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway. Meanwhile, the combined treatment induces immunogenic cell death of cancer cells, which promotes the release of tumor-associated antigens and activates robust anti-tumor immune responses. Notably, intratumoral injection of the AZP adjuvant combined with irradiation effectively eradicates in situ tumors. When further combined with PD-1 antibody, this regimen can induce anti-tumor immunity, significantly inhibiting tumor growth, metastasis, and recurrence in a murine model without causing obvious toxicity. Conclusion The AZP nanoplatform exhibits excellent therapeutic efficacy, providing a rational design strategy for a potent adjuvant that integrates photothermally enhanced chemodynamic therapy and metalloimmunotherapy for the treatment of solid tumors.

papers.title: Advancing the Translational Pipeline: From In Vivo and In Vitro 2D Models to Next-Generation Cell Culture Models for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Modelling and Drug Discovery.
papers.authors: Carata E, Mariano S, Tenuzzo BA, Panzarini E.
papers.abstract: Background : Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is still a global health challenge, as there is no effective treatment due to the inadequacy of conventional experimental platforms for comprehending pathogenic mechanisms and developing therapy. Objectives : This review details the recent progress and clinical utility of next-generation iPSC-derived 3D in vitro systems integrated with microfluidics, CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, multi-omics readouts, and AI-based machine learning, which are emerging as transformative platforms for recapitulating key ALS pathological hallmarks. Methods : A literature search was performed using PubMed and Web of Science, including only English-language publications. All the published papers collected covered the period from January 2015 to June 2026. Results : Human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) cerebral organoids, assembloids, and organ-on-a-chip technologies are revolutionizing research into ALS by providing a way to model the complex spatial organization, cellular heterogeneity, and neural network dynamics of the human brain. Moreover, recent bioengineering advancements enable the inclusion of functional neurovascular units, the integration of resident immune cells (microglia), and the use of 3D bioprinting to accelerate the functional maturation of age-related phenotypes. CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing, OMICS, and machine learning improve tools for studying ALS and identifying therapeutic targets. Conclusions : Novel cell culture models may bridge the gap between preclinical animal models and human clinical trials and reduce the duration and costs of translation. Future work is likely to integrate bioprinting with organ-on-chip microfluidics, CRISPR-based genetic editing, and multi-omics readouts to build increasingly faithful, patient-specific ALS models for both basic research and precision therapeutics.

papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analyses Identify a T Cell-Mediated Tumor Killing Gene Signature for Prognostic Stratification and Immune Characterization in Breast Cancer.
papers.authors: Zhu Y, Chen Y, Wu J.
papers.abstract: Background T cell-mediated tumor killing (TTK) is a central mechanism for antitumor immunity. However, the prognostic value of genes regulating TTK sensitivity (GSTTKs) in breast cancer (BC), along with their impact on the immune microenvironment and T-cell dynamics, remains to be systematically elucidated. Methods Using gene expression data from public databases, we identified prognosis-related key GSTTKs. A risk model was developed through LASSO regression and validated in an independent external dataset. We then evaluated the independent prognostic value of the risk score and clinical features, and constructed a nomogram for survival prediction. Immune characteristics and immunotherapy response were assessed using CIBERSORT and TIDE algorithms. Furthermore, scRNA-seq data were integrated to elucidate T-cell communication networks and differentiation trajectories. Immunohistochemistry was performed to validate the protein expression patterns of the key GSTTKs. Results We constructed a stable prognostic risk model comprising 5 GSTTKs (KCTD5, COL17A1, LRTM2, DOK7, and CXCR3). Patients were classified into high- and low-risk groups, with significantly different survival outcomes. Risk score, age, stage, and M were independent prognostic factors, and integrating them into a nomogram effectively predicted 1-, 3-, and 5-year survival. The two risk groups differed significantly in immune infiltration and immune checkpoint expression, with high-risk group showing elevated TIDE scores. scRNA-seq analysis further revealed a higher T-cell proportion in the low-risk group, interacting with macrophages via the CCL5-CCR1 pathway. Additionally, CXCR3 was dynamically expressed along T-cell differentiation trajectories. Conclusion This study identified five GSTTK-related signatures in BC, revealing their association with immune heterogeneity and T-cell-specific regulation. These preliminary findings may inform prognostic evaluation, but warrant further validation before clinical translation, given the retrospective design, reliance on public datasets, lack of functional validation, and limited immunohistochemical samples.

papers.title: NET-Associated Transcriptional Signatures and T-Cell Functional States During Allogeneic CAR-γδT-Cell Therapy: A Longitudinal Single-Cell Analysis.
papers.authors: Yao L, Liu Z, Wang Y, Gu W, Bai YF.
papers.abstract: Background CAR T-cell therapy has transformed the treatment of hematologic malignancies, although conventional autologous αβ CAR-T products remain limited by complex manufacturing, variable persistence, and relapse risk. γδT cells provide a promising donor source for next-generation off-the-shelf CAR-T therapies due to their MHC-independent tumor recognition, potent cytotoxicity, and minimal risk of graft-versus-host disease; however, the determinants of treatment durability following allogeneic CAR-γδT-cell therapy remain poorly defined. NETs have recently emerged as key immunoregulatory components of the TME, where excessive NET formation sustains inflammation, reshapes immune-stromal interactions, and impairs lymphocyte function, yet their impact on CAR-T-cell fate is largely unknown. Methods In this study, we performed longitudinal single-cell transcriptomic profiling of patients treated with allogeneic CAR-γδT cells and integrated ligand-receptor inference, pathway enrichment, and transcriptional regulatory analyses. Results We identified a 69-gene NET-associated transcriptional signature in the neutrophil population captured in PBMC samples. The NET-associated transcriptional score increased longitudinally in the single patient who subsequently relapsed, whereas longitudinal patterns varied across individual patients. Exploratory analyses identified associations between NET-associated transcriptional activity and T-cell functional programs, including an inverse association with proliferation. NicheNet, pathway enrichment, and SCENIC analyses highlighted candidate inflammatory and regulatory programs involving IL-1-related signaling, adhesion pathways, SMAD3 regulon activity, and E2F-related proliferative programs. Analysis of an independent cohort provided supportive evidence for related inflammatory transcriptional patterns, although differences in therapeutic platform and cellular composition limited direct validation. Discussion Together, these findings suggest that NET-associated inflammatory states may be linked to peripheral immune remodeling and altered circulating T-cell functional states during CAR-γδT-cell therapy. Larger longitudinal cohorts, more comprehensive clinical annotation, and orthogonal measurements of NET formation are needed to establish the clinical and mechanistic significance of these associations.

papers.title: BCR repertoire analysis and cloning of antibody candidates targeting native and Asp7-isomerized β-amyloid
papers.authors: Nikolaev, N. A.; Kolobova, E. A.; Myshkin, M. Y.; Shagina, I. A.; Barsova, E. V.; Kechko, O. I.; Grogoreva, T. V.; Mitkevich, V. A.; Merzlyak, E. M.; Kozin, S.; Makarov, A. A.; Chudakov, D. M.; Lukyanov, S. A.; Grigorova, I. L.; Britanova, O. V.
papers.abstract: Computational approaches are increasingly used to prioritize monoclonal antibody (mAB) candidates from BCR-seq datasets. However, the reliable identification of B cells encoding antibodies against rare antigenic epitopes remains challenging. We employed a repertoire-guided workflow combining antigen-tetramer sorting of B cells from immunized mice, followed by low-input bulk BCR-seq, which yielded informative clonal repertoires. Clustering analysis allowed us to prioritize IGH and IGK clonotypes potentially targeting {beta}-amyloid and the isoAsp7 proteoform (isoD7-A{beta}1-16), implicated in Alzheimer's disease. We observed recurrent IGHV8-12 and IGKV1-117 usage, consistent with canonical mouse anti-A{beta} responses. Focusing on isoD7-A{beta} -associated candidates, we selected fourteen candidate IGH--IGK combinations for recombinant expression including variants containing IGKV8-21, IGKV8-19, IGKV2-112 together with IGHV1-75, IGHV10-1 or IGHV8-12. Several recombinant mABs showed detectable binding activity to isoD7-A{beta}, including a candidate with preferential recognition of isoD7-A{beta}, supporting the feasibility of the approach but underscoring the challenge of accurate chain pairing. These results provide proof of principle that repertoire-guided analysis can prioritize candidate IGH and IGK chains and propose possible heavy-light chain combinations based on their co-representation across samples while experimental testing remains necessary to identify antibodies with preferential recognition of isoD7-A{beta}.

papers.title: Immune and cellular determinants of response to HMA-venetoclax regimens in acute myeloid leukemia.
papers.authors: Marchetti A, Lazzaroni F, Da Via' MC, Lionetti M, Maggioni G, Campagna A, Ventura D, Croci GA, Marella A, Maeda A, Matera A, Calvi E, Scopetti M, Viviani F, Rampi N, Bonometti D, Benzoni E, Zappa M, Fabris S, Barbieri M, Pioggia S, Leoni C, Ricchiuti A, Porta MGD, Sciumè M, Passamonti F, Fracchiolla NS, Bolli N.
papers.abstract: Hypomethylating agents (HMAs) combined with Venetoclax have reshaped the therapeutic landscape of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), yet the biological determinants of response remain unclear. We integrated clinical and genomic profiling in 132 newly diagnosed or relapsed/refractory AML patients treated with HMA-Venetoclax and performed single-cell RNA sequencing and T cell receptor (TCR) profiling in 10 newly diagnosed cases to define cellular and immune correlates of response. Response rates and survival aligned with published data. DNA Sequencing confirmed the favorable impact of IDH2 and the poor prognosis of TP53 mutations. scRNA-seq and TCR analysis showed that responders exhibited expansion of cytotoxic CD8 + T cells, increased TCR clonal diversity, and activation of antigen-presentation pathways. Nonresponders displayed baseline inflammatory signaling, impaired myeloid maturation, and a suppressive microenvironment enriched in IDO1 + dendritic cells. Resistant AMLs showed stem-like dedifferentiation and sustained EMT. LAG-3 expression marked dysfunctional T cell states and emerged as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target.

papers.title: Combined Bulk and Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Reveals Alterations in the Immune Microenvironment and Candidate Immune-Related Genes Associated With Diagnosis and Relapse in Childhood B-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
papers.authors: Han L, Zhao H, Mu X, Zheng H, Guo Q.
papers.abstract: Background The association between relapse and remodeling of the bone marrow immune microenvironment in pediatric B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) remains incompletely understood. This study aims to characterize the transcriptional and cellular alterations associated with B-ALL relapse and identify immune-related genes (IRGs) associated with disease recurrence. Methods Bulk (GSE3910 and GSE28460) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) (GSE130116) data were obtained from the GEO database, whereas IRGs were retrieved from ImmPort database. GSE3910 dataset was analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs), followed by functional enrichment and immune infiltration analysis. scRNA-seq data were used for cell annotation and cell-cell communication analysis to identify key immune shifts. Candidate genes were identified through the intersection of scRNA-seq DEGs, bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq) DEGs, and IRGs. Gene-gene interaction (GGI) and transcription factor analyses, and external validation using GSE28460 were subsequently performed. Results A total of 544 DEGs were identified from DEG3910. Functional enrichment analysis indicated that relapse was associated with enhanced cell proliferation, immune stress, and inflammatory responses. scRNA-seq analysis revealed substantial microenvironmental heterogeneity. Cell-cell communication analysis identified alternations in signaling networks during relapse, particularly toward T and natural killer cells. Pathways related to prostaglandin and NEGR signaling were notably enriched in relapse samples. Integrative analysis identified seven IRGs (ELANE, S100A8, MNDA, S100A9, S100A12, PSAP, and FCN1) associated with relapse and were predominantly associated with myeloid cells. Conclusion Relapsed pediatric B-ALL may be associated with heterogeneous alterations in immune microenvironment and intercellular communication. The identified genes may represent relapse-associated molecular features and warrant further functional investigation.

papers.title: Donor-aware integrative single-cell analysis distinguishes consistent memory B-cell programmes from donor-sensitive state boundaries in untreated rheumatoid arthritis.
papers.authors: Zhang C, Xin H, Wen Q, Li C, Chen G, Zhu B.
papers.abstract: Single-cell transcriptomics resolves immune-cell heterogeneity, but whether cluster boundaries or coordinated programmes are the more transferable unit across donors remains uncertain. We reanalyzed 14,414 circulating memory B cells from four untreated rheumatoid arthritis donors. Harmony increased mean local donor entropy from 0.506 to 0.912, while original labels showed only moderate agreement with uncorrected and Harmony reclustering (adjusted Rand indices 0.508 and 0.473). Conditional label permutations and analyses based on pan-B-centred residuals or state-marker genes supported donor-level consistency for most major states, but identified C3-PECAM1 and the rare C10-IFN state as weakly specific or quality-control-sensitive. In training-only donor-held-out transfer, accuracy was 66.0-70.5% and adjusted Rand index was 0.432-0.525, indicating partial transfer rather than independent state recovery. Removal of DoubletFinder-predicted doublets preserved 15-20 of each state's top 20 pseudobulk markers and did not change programme rank order across states. Rank-based UCell scores agreed with AddModuleScore in both datasets. In an independent cohort of 5,725 memory B cells from 34 donors, adapted programme scores could be quantified, but no disease-activity or serological association remained significant after correction; treatment and unavailable disease-duration data limited clinical interpretation. These results distinguish recurrent donor-level transcriptional structure from analysis-sensitive state boundaries and support programme-level interpretation without claiming independent cell-state validation or biomarker utility.

papers.title: Single-cell mapping of human plasma cell fate reveals a commitment checkpoint and Cav-1β expression associated with mTORC1 machinery.
papers.authors: Caron G, Desmots F, Chabaud M, Lemarié M, Olivier V, Chatonnet F, Nonn C, Jadeau C, Léonard S, Monvoisin C, Santamaria K, Blouin CM, Attaf N, Gharsalli T, Milpied P, Lamaze C, Pangault C, Haas M, Fest T.
papers.abstract: Human B cell differentiation into antibody-secreting plasma cells (PCs) requires coordinated transcriptional and organelle remodeling. Using single-cell transcriptomics in an in vitro human B cell differentiation system, we identified a Day-8 commitment checkpoint separating PC, memory B cell, and germinal center-like trajectories and defined an XBP1-associated transcriptional program linked to organelle remodeling. Within this program, CAV1 was induced during PC commitment and encoded a non-caveolar Cav-1β isoform expressed in plasmablasts and PCs. Proteomic analyses showed that Cav-1β associates with endoplasmic reticulum, secretory, and nutrient-sensing proteins, including components of the V-ATPase-RAGulator-RAG complex. CAV1 silencing had modest effects on PC differentiation but did not alter acute mTORC1 activation or antibody secretion. These findings place Cav-1β within the membrane and organelle remodeling program of human PCs and highlight how intracellular architecture may be coupled to metabolic and secretory adaptation during plasma cell differentiation.

papers.title: Disease-specific and therapy-driven alterations in immunoglobulin G heavy-chain repertoire in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from pemphigus vulgaris and bullous pemphigoid patients.
papers.authors: Zhou W, Feng D, Wang Q, Hu Z, Zhang G, Zhao M.
papers.abstract: Background Pemphigus vulgaris (PV) and bullous pemphigoid (BP) are two subtypes of autoimmune bullous disorders (AIBD), characterized by abnormal B cell activation and autoantibody production. Glucocorticoids (GC) and rituximab (RTX) are main treatment agents for AIBD. However,the effects of GC and RTX therapies on B cell receptor (BCR) repertoire need clarification. Methods The study included 18 AIBD patients (13 PV, 5 BP) and 9 healthy controls (HC). Of 13 PV, 9 were newly diagnosed/relapsed (4 responsive to GC monotherapy), 4 were GC-refractory but responsive to RTX-GC therapy. All BP were newly diagnosed/relapsed (4 responsive to GC). High throughput profiling of immunoglobulin G heavy-chain (IGHG) repertoire in peripheral blood mononuclear cells of all subjects was done.Comparative analysis identified differential changes in IGHG repertoire features between treatment-naïve/relapsed AIBD patients and HC, as well as pre- and post-therapeutic interventions. Results AIBD patients differed from HC in skewed IGHV/D/J usage, decreased clone diversity (more dominant clones), and distinct CDR3 amino acid patterns of IGHG repertoire. GC-responsive BP/PV patients had slight changes in IGHG repertoire profiles between pre- and post-treatment. However, the four GC-refractory PV patients who responded to GC-RTX combination therapy showed notable decreased clone diversity, elevated proportions of dominant clones, high interindividual clonal heterogeneity, and reduced public clones when compared to the pre-treatment states. Conclusions PV and BP patients exhibited disease-specific IGHG repertoire alterations. GC-RTX therapy has stronger effects than GC monotherapy, leading to more pronounced IGHG repertoire remodeling. This study offers valuable insights for both immunopharmacological investigations and immunotherapy development in autoimmune bullous disorders.

papers.title: TOMM5 is associated with oral cancer progression: a multi-omics analysis from single-cell atlas to in vitro validation.
papers.authors: Gao L, Li JD, Chen YY, Tan GL, Zeng JJ, Lin X, Liang L, Xia S, Wu GJ, Chen G.
papers.abstract: Aims Translocase of Outer Mitochondrial Membrane 5 (TOMM5), a mitochondrial outer membrane translocase subunit implicated in tumorigenesis, remains unexplored in oral cancer. Herein, we aimed to decipher the role of TOMM5 in oral cancer. Methods This study comprehensively explored the expression profile, clinical significance, and functional roles of TOMM5 in oral carcinogenesis with global RNA-seq and microarray datasets. In vitro experiments were performed for evaluating the impact of TOMM5 knockdown on the biological functions of oral cancer cells. Distribution heterogeneity of TOMM5 expression and related cellular trajectory was analyzed through scRNA-seq. The therapeutic implications of TOMM5 for oral cancer were analyzed through drug sensitivity prediction and tumor immune dysfunction and exclusion (TIDE) scoring. Results TOMM5 was significantly overexpressed in oral cancer tissues and demonstrated moderate diagnostic accuracy. TOMM5 knockdown significantly suppressed aggressive biological behaviors of oral cancer cells. ScRNA-seq data revealed predominant TOMM5 expression in B cells, decreasing with differentiation, and linked distinct pathway activities to specific cellular compartments. High TOMM5 expression was linked to reduced immune cell infiltration and sensitivity to Paclitaxel/Vincristine. Conclusions Overexpressed TOMM5 shows potential as a biomarker in oral cancer, correlating with tumor progression and immune infiltration.

papers.title: Structure-guided computational design and mechanistic understanding of the p95HER2-targeting NAZ-mAb antibody and its variants.
papers.authors: Rawat P, Kyte JA, Greiff V, Dorraji E.
papers.abstract: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is an oncogenic receptor tyrosine kinase in breast cancer and other malignancies. A subset of HER2-positive tumours expresses 611-CTF-p95HER2, a tumour-specific, hyperactive truncated isoform associated with metastasis and treatment resistance that lacks most of the extracellular domain targeted by conventional HER2-directed antibodies. We previously developed NAZ-mAb (formerly known as Oslo-2), a monoclonal antibody against 611-CTF-p95HER2. Here, we describe a computational antibody-engineering workflow for designing variants of NAZ-mAb. Starting from the sequence alone, we modelled the NAZ-mAb-611-CTF-p95HER2 complex, generated a combinatorial mutational landscape using FoldX 5.0, and prioritized candidate variants using predicted interaction energy and developability criteria. Two variants representing distinct design strategies were selected for validation: an aromatic double mutant, NAZ-mAb v1 (L:S31W/L:H107W), and a conservative single mutant, NAZ-mAb v2 (L:S31M). Both variants were successfully expressed as recombinant IgGs; NAZ-mAb v2 achieved a five-fold higher recombinant expression yield than parental NAZ-mAb, while both variants retained antigen binding with a higher apparent signal than the parental antibody in indirect ELISA. However, Biacore two-state kinetic analysis revealed weaker affinities than the parental antibody (K D NAZ-mAb v1: 326.1 nM, NAZ-mAb v2: 94.5 nM vs parental NAZ-mAb: 53.3 nM). These findings show that the computational workflow can generate antigen-engaging NAZ-mAb variants, while also highlighting the limitations of fixed-backbone interaction-energy ranking as a predictor of binding affinity and yield. This study provides a practical framework and a cautionary benchmark for computationally driven, developability-aware antibody engineering in the absence of experimental structural data.

papers.title: Clonal heterogeneity in human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and its impact on tumor progression.
papers.authors: Kalfakakou D, Cameron DC, Kawaler EA, Tsuda M, Wang L, Su Q, Kim S, Manolakos E, Jing X, Hajdu C, Tamayo DL, Shim Y, Ackermann A, Weissinger D, Zimny H, Hernandez R, Beier M, Dimartino D, Meyn P, Rice K, Selvaraj S, Loomis C, Heguy A, Lund AW, Carter H, Sears RC, Welling TH, Dolgalev I, Tsirigos A, Simeone DM.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is an aggressive cancer characterized by profound desmoplasia and cellular heterogeneity, which cannot be fully resolved using traditional bulk sequencing approaches. To understand how this heterogeneity contributes to PDAC biology, we analyzed a large cohort of primary tumors (n = 62) profiled using single-cell RNA sequencing (443,451 single cells), including a subset of 11 tumors with matched spatial transcriptomics (53,236 spots), to map clonal, transcriptional and spatial diversity. Moreover, our sample set includes a unique cohort of matched samples from six tumors collected before and after treatment with chemotherapy. Our analysis revealed notable intratumoral heterogeneity, with multiple genetically distinct neoplastic clones coexisting within individual tumors. We observed clone-specific ligand-receptor programs that are modulated by genomic dosage: amplifications of ligands or receptors enriched corresponding interactions, while deletions suppressed them, with genetically encoded differences supported by spatial transcriptomics and multiplex immunofluorescence. Phylogenetic integration identified focal 8q24 (MYC) amplification as recurrently associated with classical-to-basal transitions occurring within tumor lineages at a frequency above chance; these transitions were accompanied by coordinated depletion of immune-response programs. Functional perturbation experiments in murine and primary human models showed that MYC knockdown reactivates classical transcriptional programs and restores immune-response pathways, supporting a role for MYC in maintaining a basal, immune-depleted state. Spatial analyses further revealed dispersed clones enriched for epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition activity and immune suppression, correlating with metastatic potential and colonization of lymph node niches. These dispersed clones shifted toward a basal phenotype, contributing to disease progression. Our findings highlight the critical role of clonal diversity, transcriptional plasticity and tumor microenvironment interactions in shaping human PDAC biology. This work provides a detailed view of the molecular and spatial heterogeneity of PDAC and offers potential avenues for therapeutic intervention targeting clonal evolution and the mechanisms driving metastasis.

papers.title: SPP1 + TAMs drive colorectal tumorigenesis through an ARG2-orchestrated metabolic-immune crosstalk.
papers.authors: Song L, Yan T, Lu SY, Tong T, Wang Z, Zhou CB, Zhuang ZY, Xie Y, Leng X, Zhang C, Chen Y, Gu WQ, Cui Y, Zhang ZZ, Chen J, Chen H, Hong J, Chen H, Chen YX, Fang JY.
papers.abstract: Rising incidence of colorectal cancer (CRC) and limited therapeutic options highlight the urgent need to define the drivers of its progression. The SPP1 + tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) subset identified by single-cell transcriptomics is a functionally dominant population that extends beyond the classical M1/M2 paradigm. Here, we dissected the molecular mechanisms by which SPP1 + TAMs reprogram tumor progression and determined whether the gut microbiota regulates this process in colorectal cancer. Using a multi-platform strategy integrating clinical specimens, murine models and CRC cell lines, we found that SPP1 + TAMs increase progressively during CRC evolution and exhibit crosstalk with malignant epithelial cells, and their abundance is associated with adverse clinical outcome. Integrative analysis reveals a significant positive correlation between SPP1 and ARG2 expression. Further, TAM-derived SPP1 engages CD44 on CRC cells to induce ARG2 expression. Mechanistically, ARG2 facilitates the interaction between USP10 and c-Myc to deubiquitinate and stabilize c-Myc, which transactivates the glycolytic enzyme HK2, driving Warburg metabolism that fuels CRC cell proliferation. Moreover, ARG2 secreted by CRC cells is internalized by TAMs, which reciprocally upregulates SPP1, creating a feed-forward loop that drives a pro-tumorigenic microenvironment. Notably, Bifidobacterium longum downregulates CD44 expression on tumor cells, thereby disrupting the SPP1-ARG2 axis and attenuating CRC progression. These findings identify the SPP1-ARG2 circuit as a therapeutic target and propose B. longum as a microbiome-derived precision adjuvant therapy for CRC suppression.

papers.title: Single-cell spatial transcriptomics identifies SERPINE1 as a vascular endothelial mediator of cisplatin resistance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Su H, Zhang Y, Wang J, Liu L, Zhao Y.
papers.abstract: Background Cisplatin resistance remains a major obstacle in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), yet the contribution of the vascular microenvironment and its variation across HPV statuses remains unclear. Methods We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and bioinformatics analyses to characterize cisplatin resistance-associated cellular states in HNSCC. Cisplatin resistance scoring, pseudotime analysis, transcriptional regulatory network analysis, and cell-cell communication analysis were used to identify resistant subpopulations. Spatial localization, survival analysis, immune infiltration assessment, and drug sensitivity prediction were further performed to evaluate key candidate genes. Results Cisplatin resistance signals were preferentially enriched in tumor endothelial cells and were stronger in HPV-negative HNSCC. Endothelial cells with high resistance scores exhibited enhanced angiogenesis, extracellular matrix remodeling, hypoxia, and inflammatory programs. Multidimensional screening identified SERPINE1 as a key resistance-associated endothelial gene, showing significant upregulation and positive correlation with resistance scores. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses consistently demonstrated vascular-associated enrichment of SERPINE1, particularly in HPV-negative tumors. High SERPINE1 expression was associated with poor survival and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Drug sensitivity prediction suggested increased sensitivity of SERPINE1-high tumors to EGFR/SRC- and MAPK-pathway inhibitors, whereas no significant differences were observed for conventional cytotoxic agents. Conclusion SERPINE1 defines a tumor endothelial state associated with cisplatin resistance in HNSCC and may contribute to HPV-related differences in the vascular microenvironment, providing a potential basis for therapeutic stratification.
