papers.title: Immunoinformatics-based design and in silico evaluation of a multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Naegleria fowleri.
papers.authors: Velumani K, Umapathi S, Malla A, Shanmugaraj B.
papers.abstract: Primary amoebic meningoencephalitis (PAM) is caused by Naegleria fowleri, a free-living amoeba. It is a fatal infection with more than 95% mortality rate. Even though several combinations of antimicrobial agents were used to treat the condition, the overall survival remains poor and no effective vaccine is currently available. In this study, an immunoinformatic approach was utilized for designing a multi-epitope vaccine against N. fowleri. The sequences of antigenic proteins were retrieved for epitope prediction. The computational prediction identified 400 CTL, 590 HTL, and 65 B-cell high-binding epitopes. After evaluating their antigenicity, allergenicity and toxicity, 5 CTL, 5 HTL and 3 B-cell epitopes were selected and assembled into a multi-epitope vaccine construct using linkers and a human β-defensin-3 adjuvant. The 3D structure of the vaccine was predicted using AlphaFold and refined with GalaxyRefine. Ramachandran plot analysis indicated that 96.5% of the residues of the refined vaccine are present in the most favored regions, indicating good stereochemical quality. The molecular docking analysis was performed using HADDOCK to evaluate the interaction between the vaccine and the Toll-like Receptors (TLRs), which predicted favorable binding affinities of -15.6 kcal/mol, -14.2 kcal/mol, and - 13.1 kcal/mol for TLR1 & 2, TLR3, and TLR4, respectively. The codon was optimized using JCat and cloned into the pET-28a(+) plasmid. The in silico immune simulation analysis predicted potential humoral and cellular immune responses to the vaccine construct. Overall, the proposed multi-epitope vaccine represents a promising computational candidate, however, further experimental validations have to be performed to confirm its efficacy against the pathogen.

papers.title: Design and in silico evaluation of PV-GNProtecta: an mRNA multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Puumala virus using immunoinformatics and structural analysis.
papers.authors: Hossain T, Al Mahmud A, Afrin M, Rahman S, Tahia SS, Mahdeen AA, Masum MHU.
papers.abstract: Puumala virus (PUUV), the principal causative agent of nephropathia epidemica (NE), poses a significant public health threat due to its zoonotic transmission, renal complications, and the lack of an approved vaccine. In this study, an immunoinformatics-driven mRNA multi-epitope vaccine, PV-GNProtecta, was designed using conserved regions of the viral glycoprotein (G) and nucleoprotein (N). Highly antigenic, non-allergenic, and non-toxic T-cell and B-cell epitopes were identified and assembled with appropriate adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity. Population coverage analysis suggested broad HLA responsiveness across diverse populations. The vaccine construct exhibited favorable physicochemical properties, including stability, solubility, and antigenicity. Structural validation predicted high model quality, with 95.5% of residues located in favored Ramachandran regions and an ERRAT score of 91.4. Molecular docking and MM-GBSA analyses predicted favorable computational interactions between PV-GNProtecta and TLR4, while a 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation provided computational insights into the dynamic behavior of the vaccine-TLR4 complex. Codon optimization suggested compatibility of the designed sequence with an Escherichia coli-based expression framework. Immune simulation predicted potential humoral and cellular immune response patterns, including changes in IgG, IFN-γ, and IL-2 levels. The designed mRNA sequence exhibited favorable predicted secondary structural characteristics; however, further experimental evaluation is required to assess translational efficiency and stability. Although this study is limited to computational analyses and requires experimental validation, the findings suggest that PV-GNProtecta may represent a potential candidate for further investigation against PUUV infection.

papers.title: Integrated bioinformatics analysis identifies an immune-related gene signature associated with non-obstructive azoospermia.
papers.authors: Zhong Y, Ye S, Lai H, Zeng X, Song G, Qiu X.
papers.abstract: Non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) is a severe male infertility disorder. This study aims to identify immune-related biomarkers for explore immune-related molecular signatures associated with NOA. Here, we integrated transcriptomic data from four independent cohorts (GSE145467, GSE45885, GSE45887, GSE9210) using an integrative pipeline combining differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and consensus-based multi-machine learning to identify an immune-related gene signature associated with NOA. We identified 16 immune-related differentially expressed genes through WGCNA, which were refined into a 12-gene panel-Hub NOA.Sig (CD14, CD19, CMTM2, CXCL16, HSPA1L, HSPA2, IGF1, IL13, POMC, RBP1, STAB2, TYROBP)-using five feature selection algorithms (Bagged Trees, Bayesian, Boruta, LASSO, LVQ). A Random Forest classifier based on Hub NOA.Sig yielded good classification performance with an AUC of 0.87. This signature offers a transcriptomic reference for characterizing NOA heterogeneity and exploring immune-related molecular features. Single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA) revealed significant alterations in six immune cell populations-including effector memory CD4 ⁺ /CD8 ⁺ T cells, regulatory T cells, and plasmacytoid dendritic cells-and demonstrated strong correlations between hub genes and specific immune infiltrates. Furthermore, drug-gene interaction screening and molecular docking predicted loperamide-POMC, acitretin-RBP1, and retinol-RBP1 as candidate drug-gene pairs for subsequent experimental validation. This work provides transcriptomic clues and candidate molecular targets for future mechanistic investigations into NOA-related male infertility.

papers.title: Exercise-driven glucocorticoid signaling acts as a systemic circuit breaker to reprogram microglia and resolve post-stroke inflammation.
papers.authors: Liu Z, Zhang W, Si X, Zhao J, Xia Y, Qiao H, Wang J, Chai G, Hao J, Hou S.
papers.abstract: Following ischemic stroke, neuroinflammation drives severe secondary immunopathology, yet how systemic interventions coordinate peripheral and central immunity for neuroprotection remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate that acute-phase exercise accelerates motor rehabilitation and neural repair by activating the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis to function as a potent systemic circuit breaker. Systemically, exercise-driven glucocorticoids, validated via targeted receptor blockade, induce profound spleen atrophy to restrict the peripheral immune pool, effectively depriving the ischemic brain of infiltrating leukocytes. By leveraging high-resolution single-cell transcriptomics, we identify microglia as the primary, highly sensitive central sensors of this glucocorticoid-mediated immunosuppression. These endocrine-reprogrammed microglia transition from a highly pro-inflammatory state toward a regulated, homeostatic quiescence. Mechanistically, they decisively blunt interferon (IFN) signaling to abrogate CXCL9/10-CXCR3 chemotaxis, attenuate antigen presentation and co-stimulation, thereby arresting the recruitment and in situ activation of effector T and B cells. Furthermore, this early suppression of neuroinflammation limits neural tissue damage, preserving the broader neuroglial niche in a quiescent, physiological state. Accordingly, the reactive repair signals typically provided by microglia to astrocytes and oligodendrocytes are substantially attenuated, underscoring that early protection from neuroinflammation effectively obviates the need for intense compensatory repair. Collectively, our findings delineate a novel systemic-to-central neuroimmune axis. By demonstrating how exercise harnesses systemic endocrine signals to interrupt the pathological inflammatory cascade, we highlight microglial glucocorticoid signaling as a precise therapeutic target for post-stroke neuroimmune modulation.

papers.title: Tumor-associated immunosenescence: Mechanisms, biomarkers and age-adaptive immunotherapy.
papers.authors: Wu H, Yang Z, Zhang H, Jin Y, Ji S, Zhang Z, Sun G, Zhang X.
papers.abstract: Immunosenescence alters immune-cell composition, signaling, metabolism, and regenerative capacity, but chronological age alone does not reliably predict response to cancer immunotherapy. In older adults, thymic involution, hematopoietic remodeling, inflammaging, and the accumulation of dysfunctional lymphoid and myeloid populations interact with tumor-derived suppressive signals. We organize these processes within an Immunosenescence-Immunotherapy Interference Axis linking systemic immune aging, local tumor remodeling, and treatment-specific vulnerabilities. Evidence is reviewed for senescence-like and exhausted CD8 + T cells, NK-cell dysfunction, age-associated macrophage states, loss of T-cell receptor diversity, and their relationship to immune checkpoint blockade. We then assess blood, tissue, and single-cell biomarkers that may distinguish biological immune age from chronological age, with particular attention to the limitations of single-marker classification. Finally, we critically evaluate senolytics, cytokine support, co-stimulatory approaches, and metabolic modulation as potential adjuncts to immunotherapy. The available evidence supports biomarker-informed, age-adaptive trial design, but prospective validation is required before immune-rejuvenation strategies can be recommended in routine oncology.

papers.title: Key genes and pathways of pulmonary hypertension identified by integrating bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing.
papers.authors: Wu P, Huan J, Liu C, Jin H, Wang R, Wang Y, Cao C, Zhang B.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive vascular disease, yet the underlying cell-type-specific molecular networks and diagnostic biomarkers remain incompletely defined. Integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomics, we identified 14 pulmonary cell types in PH, with smooth muscle cells (SMCs) as a central communication hub interacting with monocytes and macrophages. High-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) revealed 4 SMC modules enriched in extracellular matrix organization, TGF-β, and HIF-1 pathways. A five-gene diagnostic signature distinguished PH from controls with an area under the curve of 0.895. Immune infiltration and enrichment analysis showed that activated CD4 memory T cells, activated dendritic cells, and resting mast cells increased in the PH group, while angiogenesis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition pathway were upregulated. In hypoxic human pulmonary artery SMCs, milk fat globule-epidermal growth factor-8 (MFGE8), secreted frizzled-related protein 2 (SFRP2), S100 calcium-binding protein A11 (S100A11), and procollagen C-endopeptidase enhancer 2 (PCOLCE2) were upregulated, and their knockdown suppressed proliferation, highlighting them as potential biomarkers and drivers of vascular remodeling, revealing a new molecular mechanism for PH and providing insights for potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Allergen-induced trained immunity in alveolar macrophages predisposes to long-lasting airway hypersensitivity.
papers.authors: Tong L, Song W, Su L, Li M, He J, Dai L, Li H, Wu X, Zhao Q, Shen X, Zhang Y, Yao Y, Wang Q, Chen Z.
papers.abstract: Allergic asthma is characterized by airway hypersensitivity to various allergens and chronic airway inflammation. The mechanisms underlying such a prolonged and broad-responsive airway hypersensitivity remain not fully understood. In this study, we systematically investigated the role of allergen-induced trained immunity in tissue resident alveolar macrophages (AMs) and its impact on long-lasting airway hypersensitivity. Here, we utilized flow cytometry and single-cell transcriptomics to analyze immune cell dynamics in murine asthma model, and we compare the differences between allergen-experienced AMs and naïve AMs. Specifically, we introduce and delve into the concept of allergen-induced trained immunity within these particular cells (Trained alveolar macrophages, Tr-AMs). Our findings demonstrated that Tr-AMs preferentially produce pro-eosinophilic chemokines upon subsequent allergen exposure and, therefore, induce exacerbated eosinophilic inflammation in the lung. The induction of Tr-AMs was potentially associated with their interactions with other immune cells, such as natural killer cells, dendritic cells, and Th2 cells. Both IFN-γ and IL-4 are critical for AM activation, we found that their simultaneous action on AMs induced the development of an MHCII + CD206 + Tr-AM phenotype, which was specialized in producing pro-eosinophilic chemokines, including CCL24 (eotaxin-2) and CCL5 (RANTES). This study highlights the establishment and roles of Tr-AMs in pro-asthmatic airway hypersensitivity, providing a new understanding of the pathogenesis and recurrence of allergic asthma.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics and machine learning characterize LTA4H-linked lipid metabolism and inflammatory signatures in the knee osteoarthritis IPFP/synovium compartment.
papers.authors: Chen X, Li S, Wang X, Chen W, Qi S, Zhao J.
papers.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a whole-joint disease characterized by inflammation, immune dysregulation, and metabolic imbalance. To define lipid metabolism-related transcriptional heterogeneity within the infrapatellar fat pad (IPFP)/synovium compartment, we integrated publicly available single-cell transcriptomic data from IPFP/synovium-derived joint cells with bulk synovial transcriptomic datasets from patients with KOA and controls. Lipid metabolism-related scores were derived using multiple single-cell scoring algorithms, and candidate genes were identified through score-associated analyses, differential expression, protein-protein interaction analysis, and five machine-learning approaches, followed by external bulk validation and single-cell characterization. Myeloid cells showed the most consistent KOA-associated increases in lipid metabolism-related transcriptional scores. Fifty composite-score-associated genes were identified and were enriched in lipid metabolic, lysosomal, and PPAR-related pathways. Cross-screening prioritized PLIN2, LTA4H, and PPT1, with LTA4H showing the strongest association with lipid metabolism-related transcriptional scores. LTA4H was predominantly enriched in myeloid cells, particularly monocytes and inflammatory macrophages, and was increased in KOA myeloid cells and high-score cells. Cell-cell communication, myeloid subclustering, and pseudotime analyses linked LTA4H-positive myeloid cells to inflammatory signaling and the transition from monocytes toward inflammatory macrophages. In silico knockout analysis further implicated LTA4H in regulatory programs related to leukocyte migration, chemotaxis, phagocytosis, and cytokine receptor binding. In a rat KOA model, LTA4H protein expression was increased in knee synovial tissues and spatially colocalized with CD68-positive macrophages. These findings define a myeloid-cell-centered context for LTA4H in KOA and link its expression to lipid metabolism-related transcriptional features and inflammatory myeloid-cell states.

papers.title: Longitudinal peripheral immune dynamics during anti-programmed cell death 1 neoadjuvant therapy in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Li L, Meng L, Chen X, Li J, Li P, Dong B, Huang C, Zhou W, Li N, Sun G, Li J, Tan G, Jiang L, Tian D.
papers.abstract: Introduction Anti-programmed cell death 1 (PD-1)-based neoadjuvant therapy is increasingly used for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), but paired peripheral immune dynamics and their exploratory relationship to response remain incompletely characterized. Methods We performed a retrospective longitudinal flow-cytometry study of 39 patients with ESCC treated with anti-PD-1-based neoadjuvant therapy, including 20 patients with paired pre-treatment and post-treatment/preoperative peripheral immune profiles. The primary paired analysis tested 75 marker-defined immune features using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Exploratory extensions included response-associated changes in candidate immune features, clinical burden context, baseline-dependence, and public tissue-context bioinformatics. Public tissue data were used only as descriptive tissue context. Results Four features reached FDR q + CD8 T cells, PD-1 + Vδ1 γδ T cells, PD-1 + Vδ2 γδ T cells, and CD19 + B cells. PD-1-defined features were interpreted as assay-defined detectable PD-1 staining readouts because therapeutic anti-PD-1 receptor occupancy or epitope masking may affect post-treatment staining. CD19 + B cells remained the non-PD-1 q + natural killer (NK) cells was the strongest nominal exploratory and hypothesis-generating signal. Discussion These data support treatment-associated marker-defined peripheral immune dynamics and generate response-linked hypotheses requiring prospective validation.

papers.title: Autophagy as a potential link between progesterone responsiveness and endometrial immune function in recurrent implantation failure.
papers.authors: Guo L, Xie J, Wang M, Ma S, Zhang X, Guan Y.
papers.abstract: Recurrent implantation failure (RIF) describes a clinical outcome rather than a single diagnosis or immune disorder. During progesterone-driven decidualization, changes in stromal metabolism and epithelial secretion accompany the production of signals that support uterine natural killer (uNK) cell residency. Autophagy contributes to these changes, although its role in RIF is unresolved. Genetic studies in mice and human stromal cells implicate autophagy-related proteins in progesterone responses and decidual differentiation. Some RIF tissue studies, however, report increased autophagy-associated signals. Increased flux accompanies impaired progesterone responses in some stromal models and improved decidualization in others. These contrasting findings may reflect the need to maintain autophagic activity within a suitable range for each cell compartment and cycle phase, rather than a uniform deficit. Progesterone-responsive stromal cells release interleukin 15 (IL-15) and related signals that recruit and program uNK cells. Their residency may also depend on epithelial secretion, adhesion, and matrix remodeling. In cycling human endometrium, activated uNK cells contribute to tissue quality control by clearing senescent maternal decidual cells; the embryo is not the target of this process. Single-cell and spatial studies of RIF endometrium have identified altered epithelial, stromal, and NK states. Whether progesterone resistance causes these cellular changes and, in turn, implantation failure remains unknown. This review examines the evidence for these relationships and the experiments needed to assess autophagic flux beyond static markers and uNK function beyond cell abundance. Current evidence does not support routine NK testing or autophagy-directed treatment in RIF.

papers.title: Spatial architecture shapes programmed cell death-associated immune niches and therapeutic resistance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Yin Y, Wang J, Li D, Qiu D.
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by VHL-HIF pathway alterations, lipid remodeling, abnormal angiogenesis, and marked immune heterogeneity. These features create a highly vascular yet unevenly perfused microenvironment in which vascular dysfunction, hypoxia, stromal barriers, and myeloid clearance influence whether cell death becomes immunologically productive. Although immune checkpoint inhibitor combinations, vascular endothelial growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors, and HIF-2α inhibitors have improved outcomes, primary and acquired resistance and discordant responses among lesions remain common. Bulk PD-L1 expression, immune-cell abundance, and cell-death-related transcript signatures do not resolve this heterogeneity. Following current nomenclature, regulated cell death (RCD) is the mechanistically preferred umbrella term; we retain programmed cell death (PCD) in the conceptual label because it remains widely used in the RCC oncology literature, while requiring RCD execution-level evidence for mechanistic claims. Single-cell and spatial multi-omics studies increasingly show that the identity of the dying cell, execution of the death program, accessibility of death-derived material, and the recipient immune cells operate as a coupled local system. We define a PCD-associated immune niche as a spatial tissue state in which representative, non-exclusive immune-routing axes can direct tumor-cell death toward cDC1-mediated cross-presentation and adaptive antitumor immunity, TAM-dominant efferocytosis and tissue repair, or intermediate mixed states. This Review focuses predominantly on ccRCC, evaluates ferroptosis, apoptosis, pyroptosis, necroptosis, and PANoptosis, and briefly considers emerging RCD modalities for which ccRCC evidence is less mature. We further propose composite spatial biomarkers and mechanism-guided combinations that link cellular source, execution evidence, immune routing, and clinical outcome.

papers.title: Fibroblast-Derived PLA2G12A Amplifies Mast Cell Activation Through Extracellular Phospholipid Remodeling.
papers.authors: Taketomi Y, Miki Y, Higashi T, Nagasaki Y, Kano K, Arita M, Aoki J, Murakami M.
papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate intercellular communication, yet whether extracellular phospholipid metabolism on EV membranes regulates immune activation remains incompletely understood. Through comparative phenotypic analyses of multiple secreted phospholipase A 2 (sPLA 2 )-deficient mouse strains, we identified PLA2G12A as a stromal regulator of extracellular lipid metabolism that promotes IgE/antigen-dependent mast cell activation. Pla2g12a deficiency attenuated passive cutaneous and systemic anaphylaxis and selectively impaired IgE-dependent, but not IgE-independent, mast cell responses. Single-cell RNA-sequencing of mouse and human skin revealed that PLA2G12A is expressed in broad subsets of stromal fibroblasts, including papillary fibroblasts adjacent to mast cells, implicating a specialized stromal niche in mast cell regulation. Consistently, mast cell-intrinsic PLA2G12A was dispensable, whereas fibroblast-targeted deletion of Pla2g12a phenocopied global Pla2g12a deficiency. Lipidomic analyses during IgE-mediated anaphylaxis revealed a significant reduction in lysophospholipids, accompanied by minimal changes in oxylipins, in Pla2g12a -deficient skin. Mechanistically, fibroblast-derived PLA2G12A hydrolyzed phospholipids in EV-enriched fractions to generate multiple lysophospholipids, and treatment with either the PLA2G12A-treated EV-enriched fraction or exogenous lysophospholipids restored impaired IgE-dependent anaphylactic responses in Pla2g12a -deficient mice. Collectively, these findings establish sPLA 2 -driven extracellular phospholipid remodeling as a mechanism by which stromal niches regulate allergic inflammation.

papers.title: Host-Microbe Crosstalk in Sjögren's Disease: Epithelial Type I Interferon Amplification, Loss of Short-Chain Fatty Acid Restraint, and the Effector-Phase Focus of Validated Therapy.
papers.authors: Yu M, Jo D, Hwang Y, Han K.
papers.abstract: Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a systemic autoimmune disease of the exocrine glands, long framed as a lymphocyte-driven disorder in which immune cells destroy the target tissue. Genomic, epigenetic, microbiome, and single-cell and spatial studies have since shown the glandular epithelium and the microbial environment to be active participants rather than passive bystanders. This review asks whether host susceptibility and microbiome change can be joined into one continuous axis, following it from genetic and epigenetic susceptibility, through microbiome change read functionally rather than taxonomically, to the crosstalk that converts microbial signals into a host response and the cell states carrying it in human tissue. Two axes run through the whole sequence: the type I interferon (IFN) response and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) metabolism. Read against them, every disease-modifying therapy with validated efficacy so far acts in the downstream B-cell effector axis, whereas the upstream IFN axis has yielded no established treatment. Because the microbial layer and the salivary gland transcriptome or proteome have never been measured in the same patients, the model proposed here remains a testable hypothesis rather than a completed causal chain. The aim is to specify that model, the falsification conditions it carries, and the study design its verification requires.

papers.title: Integrative Molecular Profiling and Single-Cell Characterization of LHFPL5 Reveal Cancer-Specific Regulatory Features in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma and Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Al-Nakhle HH, Doha ZO.
papers.abstract: Background and Objectives : LHFPL5 encodes a four-pass transmembrane protein essential for cochlear mechanotransduction, but its molecular behavior in cancer remains poorly defined. We characterized the genomic, epigenetic, transcriptomic, immune, and cellular context of LHFPL5 in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (KIRC) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), along with its associations with clinical outcomes. Materials and Methods : Retrospective analyses integrated TCGA RNA sequencing, clinical, DNA methylation, copy number, tumor purity, and immune deconvolution data. Transcriptome-wide associations and Hallmark enrichment defined LHFPL5 -associated programs. Continuous-expression Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) per standard-deviation increase, adjusted for age, sex, and pathological stage. GEO cohorts assessed external reproducibility, matched TCGA expression pipelines assessed processing sensitivity, and three non-TCGA single-cell datasets examined cellular localization. Results : LHFPL5 showed distinct molecular contexts in KIRC and LUAD. In KIRC, higher expression remained associated with poorer overall survival after clinical adjustment (528 patients; 174 deaths; HR = 1.36, 95% CI 1.21-1.53; p = 2.42 × 10 -7 ), while subtype and immune fractions showed limited statistical overlap with the association. In LUAD, expression covaried with copy-number state and showed a weak inverse relationship with first-exon methylation. Proliferation-related transcriptional programs were associated with survival, although enrichment support depended on the multiple-testing procedure. The primary STAR-derived LUAD analysis was null (485 patients; 177 deaths; HR = 1.02, 95% CI 0.89-1.18; p = 0.770), and survival inference varied with RNA processing. External adjusted replication was inconclusive. Single-cell detection was sparse in KIRC and one LUAD dataset; another LUAD cohort showed more frequent epithelial detection without resolved malignant-cell identity. Conclusions : LHFPL5 exhibits cancer-specific molecular architecture. LUAD showed copy-number, methylation, and proliferation-related associations, whereas KIRC showed a distinct molecular context with an independent survival signal. These findings support context-dependent LHFPL5 regulation and prioritize genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptional mechanisms for functional investigation.

papers.title: Bulk and single-cell analysis of FAM72D reveals its prognostic and functional relevance in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.authors: Zhao C, Yin Q, Yu J, Duan W, Li Y, Jian Q.
papers.abstract: Family with sequence similarity 72 member D (FAM72D) has been implicated in proliferative programs in several malignancies, but its clinical significance, cellular distribution and underlying biological programs in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain insufficiently characterized. FAM72D expression and its clinical relevance were evaluated using The Cancer Genome Atlas-liver hepatocellular carcinoma (TCGA-LIHC) cohort and three independent GEO cohorts. Cox regression, patient-level bootstrap validation, calibration analysis and decision curve analysis were used to assess its prognostic contribution. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses were performed to define the cellular distribution of FAM72D. Differential-expression, functional-enrichment, protein-protein interaction and SCENIC analyses were used to characterize FAM72D-centered transcriptional programs. Immune-related analyses were conducted using tumor immune estimation resource and tumor immune dysfunction and exclusion (TIDE) and the functional effects of FAM72D silencing were examined in HuH7 cells. FAM72D was consistently upregulated in HCC tissues in TCGA and three independent GEO cohorts and was associated with adverse clinicopathological characteristics. Higher FAM72D expression was independently associated with unfavorable overall survival in the multivariable TCGA model (hazard ratio 2.02; 95% confidence interval 1.45-2.81; P 2 /M, mitotic, DNA-replication and DNA-repair activity. Bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses converged on a coordinated proliferative program characterized by enhanced cell-cycle signaling and forkhead box M1 (FOXM1) regulon activity. High FAM72D expression was also coupled to increased immune-checkpoint expression, reduced estimated CD8+ T-cell abundance and higher TIDE scores. Silencing FAM72D reduced HuH7-cell viability, colony formation and migration and increased apoptosis. FAM72D expression is associated with unfavorable prognosis and a proliferative malignant-cell state in HCC. The combined clinical, transcriptomic, single-cell, immune-related and functional findings support further evaluation of FAM72D as a candidate prognostic marker and a feature of proliferative HCC-cell programs.

papers.title: T cell engagers convert acute tumor killing into endogenous vaccination
papers.authors: Lecuit, M. M.; Corre, B.; Garcia, Z.; Lemaitre, F.; Vaysse, A.; Alonso, R.; Goudot, C.; Arnaud, B.; Feldmann, L. C.; Moraes Cabe, C.; Seffer, V.; Guermonprez, P.; Grandjean, C. L.; Guerin, M. V.; Bousso, P.
papers.abstract: T cell engagers (TCEs) redirect T cells to kill tumors by cross-linking CD3{varepsilon} to a tumor antigen, independently of T cell receptor specificity. Some patients achieve remissions that persist long after drug clearance, but whether TCEs can couple acute cytotoxicity to the generation of lasting adaptive immunity remains unknown. Here, using an immunocompetent mouse model for clinical-grade human TCEs, we show that TCE-mediated killing initiates an endogenous vaccination cascade. Intravital two-photon imaging reveals a perforin-dependent cytotoxic wave that peaks within 24 hours, then subsides despite massive T cell accumulation. Single-cell transcriptomics and adoptive transfers demonstrate that memory CD8 T cells, the principal effector reservoir in mouse and human, transit through a progenitor-like state before differentiating into cytotoxic effectors with recall competence. Crucially, tumor lysis fuels cross-priming of tumor-specific CD8 T cells by XCR1 type 1 conventional dendritic cells, a cDC1-dependent step essential for durable tumor control and protective memory upon rechallenge.

papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomics Reveals Region-Specific Host Responses in Amoebic Gill Disease of Atlantic Salmon
papers.authors: Liu, Y. W.; Cheaib, B.; Bacigalupo, A.; Robertson, B.; Sinton, M.; Quintana, J.; Thomson, G.; Morrison, V.; Nixon, C.; Krol, E.; Martin, S.; Rodger, H.; West, A. C.; Bickerdike, R.; Egan, F.; Ruane, N.; Barrett, M.; Llewellyn, M.
papers.abstract: Amoebic gill disease (AGD), caused by the parasite Neoparamoeba perurans, is a major welfare and economic burden for the Atlantic salmon aquaculture industry. However, the spatial organisation of immune functions within the gill, the site of infection, remains poorly resolved. Here, we present the first spatial transcriptomic atlas of the Atlantic salmon gill affected by AGD, generated using 10x Genomics Visium on four AGD-positive fish, confirmed by gill scoring and quantitative PCR for parasite load. As no uninfected gills were included, this study maps the anatomical and immunological organisation of AGD-affected gills rather than defining AGD-specific pathology. Unsupervised clustering of spatial gene expression resolved distinct transcriptional domains that grouped into four principal anatomical compartments of the gill, including (i) epithelial and lamellar regions defined by keratin and osmoregulatory gene expression, (ii) gill arch regions enriched for connective tissue and smooth muscle markers, (iii) an erythroid-associated vascular cluster, and (iv) a skeletal muscle cluster with signatures of glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation. Across these domains, we identified a spatially organised and diffused immune landscape, with pattern recognition receptors, antimicrobial effectors and chemokines concentrated at the filament surface, and immunoglobulin light chain transcripts consistent with B lymphocyte activity enriched toward the gill arch. Integration of the spatial data with a published single-nucleus reference atlas using reference-based deconvolution resolved the cellular identity underlying these domains and revealed frequent co-localisation of immune and structural cell types, suggesting regulated cell to cell communication within the gill-associated lymphoid tissue. Overall, our results show that the Atlantic salmon gill is not a transcriptionally uniform surface but a regionally specialised organ, with immune functions distributed across, and specialised within, distinct anatomical compartments

papers.title: Tissue-resident memory T cells are diminished in the Kaposi sarcoma tumor microenvironment of people living with HIV
papers.authors: Lagodka, A.; Winkler, F.; Brazdilova, K.; Loewe, R.; Grabmeier-Pfistershammer, K.; Eidsmo, L.; Saluzzo, S.; Strobl, J.
papers.abstract: Kaposi sarcoma (KS) is a rare neoplasm and an AIDS-defining diagnosis in people living with HIV (PLWH). Although and chronic infection with Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) contributes to KS progression, the local immune mechanisms that are lost during tumor progression remain incompletely understood. Here, we systematically characterized global patterns in the KS tumor microenvironment (TME) in both PLWH and HIV-negative individuals. Spatial transcriptomics revealed distinct niches comprising of tumor cells, immune cells, and surrounding skin cells. Tumor regions expressed a characteristic endothelial-fibroblastic signature attributable to KS tumor cells (CD34, LYVE1, SCN9A), TME regions expressed marker genes for T cells, B cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts. Analysis of putative cell-cell interactions demonstrated that tumor cells preferentially interact with cells of the TME, including T cells, indicating an important role as hub of cellular communication in KS. Immunofluorescence imaging confirmed increased numbers of T cells, specifically tissue-resident memory T cells (TRM), in KS samples compared to healthy skin, accompanied by a pronounced upregulation of PD-1 expression that was predominantly localized to the TME. Notably, we identified HIV-associated alterations in the KS immune microenvironment: PLWH exhibited loss of CXCR3+ and IFN-gamma producing CD8+ TRM cells in the KS TME compared to HIV-negative patients, a finding consistent with impaired antitumor immunity. Together, our findings reveal HIV-associated disruption of functional anti-tumor immunity in the KS TME of PLWH. Increased PD-1 expression within T cells of the TME highlights potential therapeutic use of immune checkpoint inhibitors in KS.

papers.title: Prognostic value of diabetes-related clinical indices in patients with non-small cell lung cancer and comorbid type 2 diabetes receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy.
papers.authors: Ren Q, Zhang H, Huang D, Zhong H, Wu J, Wang Y, Zhao Y, Luo S, Li Y.
papers.abstract: Background Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) or programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) have transformed the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, diabetes-induced immune dysfunction may attenuate ICI efficacy. Clinical evidence further suggests poorer outcomes in patients with NSCLC and comorbid type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Reliable prognostic tools for this subgroup remain lacking. Methods We conducted a three-part study. First, a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was performed to assess the causal relationship between T2DM and PD-L1. Second, Cox regression was applied to evaluate associations between diabetes-related clinical indices and progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Third, machine learning models were developed to predict prognosis using diabetes-related features. Results MR analysis supported a causal association between T2DM and PD-L1. Cox regression identified HbA1c as significantly associated with PFS. Among the machine learning models, the support vector machine (SVM) achieved the best performance for predicting PFS (AUC = 0.935, 95% CI: 0.872-0.997; C-index: 0.763). For OS prediction, the best-performing model was a random forest model based on HbA1c (AUC = 0.863, 95% CI: 0.736-0.990; C-index: 0.618). Conclusion Diabetes-related indices-particularly HbA1c-are meaningful prognostic markers in patients with NSCLC and comorbid T2DM receiving ICI therapy. The proposed machine learning models may support individualized outcome prediction and clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Revealing Biomarkers and Candidate Drugs for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Using Bioinformatics and Deep Learning.
papers.authors: Wu T, Wang A, Xu J.
papers.abstract: Background There is a dearth of precise treatments capable of effectively decelerating the progression of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Consequently, there is an urgent necessity to discover novel potential biomarkers and rapidly translatable therapeutic drugs. Methods The GSE57148, GSE38974, and GSE173896 datasets were included in this study. Cell clustering and annotation were conducted via Seurat, and disease-related genes were screened through an integrated approach combining Scissor-based prioritization, differential expression profiling, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Subsequently, 12 machine learning algorithms were used to construct models and identify biomarkers. The mechanisms of immune microenvironment remodeling were analyzed through cell communication and pseudo-time series analysis. Furthermore, an in vitro COPD model was constructed based on BEAS-2B cells and validated by RT-qPCR. Finally, a deep learning model and molecular docking were utilized to conduct AI-driven drug repurposing screening targeting biomarkers. Results A total of 67 intersection genes were obtained. APRT, COX8A, EDF1 and RPL37 were identified as biomarkers for COPD. Further cell communication analysis revealed that CD4 naive T cells mediate immune microenvironment remodeling via the HLA-E-CD94/NKG2A inhibitory axis. Additionally, in vitro experiments confirmed that APRT, COX8A, and EDF1 were significantly underexpressed in the model group. Among these, EDF1 represented a previously unreported candidate biomarker in COPD and was therefore selected as a putative target for AI-driven drug repurposing. Deep learning and molecular docking targeting the novel target EDF1 identified several FDA - approved drugs with binding energies ≤ -5.0 kcal/mol. Among these drugs, doxycycline exhibited a stable binding conformation and strong binding activity with EDF1, indicating high potential for drug repurposing. Conclusion This study identified four potential biomarkers for COPD and screened several candidate drugs targeting EDF1, providing new targets and translational strategies for the early diagnosis and precision treatment of COPD. EDF1 is a novel candidate target not previously reported in COPD; however, functional validation is required before it can be considered a therapeutic target.
papers.venue: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

papers.title: Identification and validation of biomarkers related to oxidative stress in pediatric sepsis utilizing WGCNA and multiple machine learning algorithms.
papers.authors: Liu Y, Luo G.
papers.abstract: Background This research aimed to identify novel oxidative stress (OS)-related biomarkers and develop predictive models for the early detection of pediatric sepsis. Methods Five open-access datasets from the gene expression omnibus database were analyzed, which included peripheral whole blood samples from children with sepsis and healthy controls. Using bioinformatics approaches, we identified differentially expressed genes (DEGs) associated with OS. We then combined weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and multiple machine learning algorithms (ML) to identify seven candidate genes, constructed a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network to screen six hub genes, and evaluated their correlations with the immune microenvironment. We subsequently evaluated the diagnostic performance of the hub genes using training datasets (GSE26440 and GSE26378) and validation datasets (GSE13904, GSE8121, and GSE9692). Moreover, molecular docking analysis revealed interactions between hub gene-encoded proteins and small-molecule compounds, which helps predict drug sensitivity. Results The study identified 36 differentially expressed oxidative stress-related genes (OSRGs). Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses highlighted these genes' roles in regulating inflammatory responses and reactive oxygen species metabolism. Seven candidate genes were identified using machine learning algorithms. Subsequently, through protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, six hub genes, namely, GADD45A, HP, MAPK14, PGD, RETN, and S100A9, were identified as having significant diagnostic potential. Immune cell deconvolution analysis of peripheral blood transcriptomes suggested that hub genes related to oxidative stress may be linked to alterations in the composition of peripheral blood immune cells. The diagnostic performance of the six hub genes was validated with area under the curve (AUC) values between 0.908 and 0.982, showing their promising diagnostic performance. Additionally, molecular docking analysis suggested that small molecules Doxycycline, Ralimetinib mesylate, Tasquinimod might interact with the identified hub genes, which opens up new treatment options. Conclusion Our research not only reveals potential diagnostic biomarkers of pediatric sepsis but also sets the stage for future studies. These studies aim to translate our findings into clinical practice, enabling earlier and more accurate diagnoses as well as targeted therapies to improve outcomes for children.

papers.title: Machine learning-based identification of CXCL13 and CXCL10 as key biomarkers in rheumatoid arthritis.
papers.authors: M S, S SA, M S, P N, Salau AO, Usman AG, Yousfan M.
papers.abstract: Background Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is one of the autoimmune diseases that involve joint damage and synovial membrane inflammation. There have been many attempts to examine the utility of biomarkers in the diagnosis of RA, but there is no clinically accepted biomarker for the diagnosis of RA due to its heterogeneity. Thus, in this study, we tried to find RA biomarkers using machine learning and bioinformatics approaches. Methods Three corresponding gene expression datasets (GSE55457, GSE12021, and GSE77298) were downloaded from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. Batch effect correction was carried out using the ComBat function of the sva package in R. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) compared to controls were identified using limma . To identify the biological functions and pathways of DEGs, Gene Ontology, KEGG, and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) were conducted. The protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was constructed in Cytoscape using the STRING database. Genes identified through PPI analysis and further filtered by LASSO and SVM-RFE regressions were considered as diagnostic biomarkers. Additional analysis of hub genes was conducted using the GSE89408 dataset. CIBERSORTx was used to evaluate the immune cell infiltration in RA. Results A total of 440 DEGs were selected, including 197 downregulated and 243 upregulated genes. The DEGs were involved in biological processes and pathways associated with the immune system and were suggested by functional enrichment analysis. GSEA enriched in cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, hematopoietic cell lineage, primary immunodeficiency, and RA pathways. The hub genes CXCL13 and CXCL10 were chosen with the help of a machine learning algorithm. An external independent validation of the hub genes was conducted. In addition, ROC analysis showed a good diagnostic value of the two genes. The analysis of immune cell infiltration showed CXCL13 was associated with multiple immune-cell populations, including plasma cells, T-cell subsets, and M1 macrophages, whereas CXCL10 showed significant associations with M1 macrophages, plasma cells, and selected T-cell subsets. Correlation analysis showed a high correlation between chemokines CXCL13 and CXCL10 and many infiltrated immune cells. Conclusion The present study indicates the potential usefulness of CXCL13 and CXCL10 genes as diagnostic biomarkers in RA. Synovial inflammation in RA is associated with the coordinated action of many genes involved in the recruitment of various immune cells to the inflammatory site. Although the term chemokines were used to designate them, these genes are the genes encoding molecules associated with the migration of particular immune cell types, and CXCR5 and CXCR3 may be considered the potential targets for future research.

papers.title: Development of REC1: A Reverse Vaccinology-Derived Multi-Epitope Vaccine Candidate Against Brucellosis.
papers.authors: Liu S, Dai Y, Huang F, Gao Z, Chen Z, Long M, Li S.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives : Brucellosis is a widespread intracellular zoonosis that continues to impose substantial public-health and economic burdens in endemic regions. No human brucellosis vaccine has yet been approved, and most existing multi-epitope candidates rely solely on computational predictions, without population-specific human leukocyte antigen (HLA) optimization or in vivo epitope validation. REC1 is therefore an early-stage, proof-of-concept, human-oriented multi-epitope candidate, with epitopes screened against high-frequency HLA alleles in the Chinese population. This study developed a multi-epitope vaccine candidate, REC1, using an integrated reverse-vaccinology workflow. Methods : We predicted Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) I and II epitopes against high-frequency HLA alleles representative of the Chinese population (AFND). Population coverage of the final incorporated epitope set was estimated with the IEDB Population Coverage tool under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, while paired HLA-DQ heterodimers, which the tool cannot model, were evaluated independently from Chinese DQA1-DQB1 haplotype frequencies. Epitopes supported by in vivo immunoreactivity were then assembled into the modular REC1 construct, which we characterized in silico for physicochemical properties, structural architecture, and simulated immune responses. Results : IFN-γ ELISpot shortlisted seven MHC-I and five MHC-II candidate immunoreactive epitopes derived from five Brucella antigens, of which five MHC-I and five MHC-II (one per antigen) were incorporated into REC1. The incorporated set was predicted to cover 91.17% of the China Oriental population on a conservative class I+II estimate (98.88% when HLA-DP was included; the HLA-DQ component alone covered 58-79%, 68.17% in Han). Epitope-level BLAST showed that all twelve shortlisted epitopes were 100% conserved across major Brucella species, except that the two Omp31 epitopes are absent from the Omp31-deleted B. abortus . The 35.86 kDa REC1 construct was predicted to be highly stable (instability index = 25.25) and hydrophilic, with a distinct architecture in which the carrier domain is ordered and the epitope region is disordered. Immune simulations suggested that REC1 can induce Th1-polarized humoral and cellular responses and may support long-term immunological memory. Molecular docking predicted that the L7/L12 carrier forms well-defined interfaces with TLR2, CD14, C1q, and DC-SIGN, and a representative peptide-MHC model confirmed canonical groove binding of a CTL epitope. Conclusions : REC1 exhibits favorable in silico properties, and its embedded peptides show IFN-γ immunogenicity in mice (candidate immunoreactive epitopes), lending preliminary support to its value as a multi-epitope vaccine candidate. HLA-matched validation and challenge studies are still needed to establish protective efficacy. Our study also offers a validated reverse vaccinology framework for future brucellosis vaccine development.

papers.title: Identification of priority gaseous component in biodiesel exhaust and its potential pulmonary hazards: a data-driven screening and validation strategy.
papers.authors: Kou Z, Yu H, Lu L, Li Z, Zhang J, Chen Y, Zhang X, Li D, Wei J, Jin X, Qu G, Zheng Y.
papers.abstract: Biodiesel is increasingly adopted as a renewable low-carbon fuel, yet the pulmonary toxicity of its exhaust-particularly the gaseous components-remains a critical knowledge gap. To address this, we developed an integrative strategy combining data-driven prioritization with experimental validation. Herein, we employ a multidimensional risk-ranking system that predicts pulmonary fibrosis as the top-ranked adverse outcome (weighted score: 1.00) and ranks formaldehyde as the highest-priority toxicant (weighted score: 0.94). Component-outcome association analysis further predicts aldehydes, particularly formaldehyde, as the top candidate driving pulmonary fibrosis, with an estimated 28% contribution. Both in vivo and in vitro validations demonstrate that biodiesel exhaust (BDE) gas exposure induces substantial pulmonary fibrogenic toxicity, with formaldehyde directly driving epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in lung epithelial cells. By integrating quantitative proteomics with computational network toxicology, we identify TGF-β1 as a key mediator linking formaldehyde to fibrotic remodeling. This conclusion is further suppported by the upregulation of Tgfb1 expression both in vivo and in vitro. Moreover, analysis of a human Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) single-cell dataset highlighted immature neutrophils as a candidate immune subset enriched for the formaldehyde-pulmonary fibrosis-associated gene signature. Overall, this study systematizes the pulmonary toxicity profile of BDE gaseous components and provides an evidence-based foundation for incorporating BDE-derived aldehydes, specifically formaldehyde, into health risk assessments and future emission control policies for biodiesel.

papers.title: CD147+ Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts Promote PD-L1 Expression in Hepatocellular Carcinoma via TIMP2/MMP2/IL-6 Signaling.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Lv B, Su X, Zhang S, Ma C, Li D, Liu J, Zhang H, Sha Z, Zhai W, Fang Y, Tang M, Shen H, Wu L.
papers.abstract: Background Targeting CD147 on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) have been identified as critical components of the tumor microenvironment. The role of CD147 in CAFs is still unclear, and this study aims to explore its function. Methods We analyzed single-cell RNA-seq data to identify CD147 expression in CAFs. Flow cytometry and multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC) were used to validate protein levels. CD147 function was assessed via shRNA/overexpression. Protein interactions were examined by molecular docking and co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP). Organoid co-culture system was established to study tumor-immune interactions. Results Single-cell sequencing and mIHC analyses have confirmed the presence of CD147+CAFs within tumor and adjacent tissues, with tumor-derived CAFs exhibiting elevated CD147 transcript levels. The proportion of CD147+ CAFs varied among patients and demonstrated no significant correlation with CD147 expression in HCC cells. Functionally, CD147+ CAFs secreted higher levels of IL-6 compared to CD147- counterparts. We elucidated a mechanism wherein CD147 on CAFs competitively binds to the tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase 2 (TIMP2), thereby diminishing TIMP2-mediated inhibition of matrix metalloproteinase 2 (MMP2). Free MMP2 enhances IL-6 secretion via the integrin α5β1 signaling pathway. IL-6 subsequently upregulates PD-L1 expression on HCC cells. This phenomenon was validated both in vitro and organoid co-culture model, where a higher burden of CD147+ CAFs correlated with increased levels of IL-6 and PD-L1. Conclusions Our study delineates a novel CAF-driven immunosuppressive pathway in HCC, where CD147+ CAFs enhance tumor cell PD-L1 expression and susceptibility to immune checkpoint blockade via a TIMP2/MMP2/IL-6 axis. Clinical significance CD147 has been primarily viewed as a therapeutic marker on HCC cells and has supported the development of CD147-targeted treatment strategies. This study shows that CD147 is also expressed in CAFs and functions as an independent regulator of the immune microenvironment by promoting IL 6 secretion and tumor PD-L1 upregulation. Importantly, CD147 expression in CAFs is not correlated with its expression in tumor cells. These findings suggest that evaluation of CD147 in both tumor and stromal compartments may improve patient stratification and may identify additional patients who could potentially benefit from CD147-targeted or combination immunotherapy approaches.

papers.title: Sparse neuronal C4 elevation induces network-wide transcriptomic and lipid-droplet remodeling in the cortical microenvironment.
papers.authors: Sánchez-Carbonell M, Bolshakova S, Ávila-Pagán JE, Sabir YA, Griffin-Derr C, Stich DG, Cieslewicz SV, Carmen Sifuentes SE, Phadke RA, Brack A, Hasche-Kluender A, Caley P, Dias C, Cruz-Martín A.
papers.abstract: The complement component C4 regulates synaptic refinement and plasticity in the brain and has been implicated in multiple neurological and psychiatric disorders, with especially strong genetic evidence linking elevated C4A expression to schizophrenia. However, it remains unclear whether localized C4 elevation in a small neuronal population is sufficient to reshape broader cortical gene-regulatory programs and cellular phenotypes. To address this question, we overexpressed mouse C4 in approximately 2% of prefrontal cortical neurons using in utero electroporation and performed bulk RNA sequencing on microdissected prefrontal cortex. Despite the sparse manipulation, C4-OE was associated with broad transcriptional remodeling across tissue composed predominantly of untransfected cells, including coordinated changes in cholesterol biosynthesis, axon- and synaptic-associated programs, vascular/ECM pathways, and immune- and stress-related responses. Comparison with a schizophrenia synaptic proteomic dataset identified limited global correspondence but selective gene- and pathway-level overlap in specific molecular programs. Reference-based projection of directional DEG signatures onto a cortical single-cell transcriptomic reference further identified cell-type-associated structure, including prominent astrocyte- and vascular-associated axes and distinct lipid/metabolic, vascular/endothelial-interferon-associated, and immune/stress correlation domains. Spatial validation with MFISH showed increased Hmgcr expression in neighboring GFP-negative cells, while PLIN2 imaging revealed increased DAPI-associated/perinuclear lipid-droplet burden within the local C4-OE field. Together, these findings support a model in which sparse neuronal C4 elevation is associated with broader remodeling of the local cortical environment, including a non-cell-autonomous component involving neighboring-cell lipid-associated responses. These results expand the interpretation of C4 risk biology beyond synapse elimination alone and suggest that focal immune-gene dysregulation can engage lipid-homeostatic, stress-related, and cell-type-associated transcriptional programs relevant to cortical circuit vulnerability.

figure.label: Fig 2
figure.caption: Sparse neuronal C4 elevation induces gene-level transcriptional changes associated with lipid metabolism, complement signaling, and synaptic plasticity. (A ) Volcano plot of differential gene expression between C4-OE and Control cortical samples. Each point represents a gene; the x-axis shows DESeq2 log 2 fold change for C4-OE versus Control and the y-axis shows −log 10 adjusted P value. Genes with adjusted P 2 fold change ±1 are included as visual references and were not used to define differential expression. Selected genes associated with lipid metabolism, complement/immune signaling, synaptic plasticity, and cellular stress are labeled. (B) Heatmap of the 50 genes with the smallest DESeq2 adjusted P values. DESeq2-normalized counts were log 2 -transformed after addition of a pseudocount of 1 and Z-scored independently for each gene across samples. Columns represent individual samples and are annotated by genotype and sex; rows and columns were hierarchically clustered. Colors indicate gene-wise Z-scored expression using a display range of −1.5 to +1.5 Z.

papers.title: House dust mite drives biphasic immunomodulation of inflammatory dendritic epidermal cells via glucose metabolism in atopic dermatitis.
papers.authors: Zhao Y, Gao C, Sui X, Ge L, Wang H, Deng S, Chen Q, Liu L, Tian J, Mu T, Wang L, Song Z.
papers.abstract: Background The impact of environmental antigens, specifically house dust mite (HDM) and Staphylococcus aureus enterotoxin B (SEB), on the metabolism of inflammatory dendritic epidermal cells (IDECs) and its role in atopic dermatitis (AD) pathogenesis is poorly understood. This study aimed to characterize IDECs metabolism in AD and study how antigen exposure drives metabolic reprogramming and immune responses. Methods We first analyzed the single-cell RNA transcriptome sequencing data to explore metabolic profiles in IDECs from AD patients. Subsequently, we evaluated the effects of HDM alone or in combination with SEB for 24 h on the energy metabolism, maturation and cytokines secretion of monocytes-derived IDECs (moIDECs) in vitro . Finally, we investigated the dynamic changes of functional and glucose metabolism in moIDECs in vitro treated with HDM at different time points (6 h, 24 h, 48 h, 72 h). Results In AD skin lesions, inflammation- and metabolism-related genes of IDECs are abnormally expressed, and multiple metabolic pathways, including glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, are significantly dysregulated. HDM alone or in combination with SEB activated the glycolysis, induced the upregulation of maturation markers (CD80/83/86) of moIDECs in vitro , and promoted the production of inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-23, IL-10, IL-12 and TNF-α), whereas SEB alone showed no significant effect. Furthermore, we found that HDM dynamically regulated inflammatory immune response of moIDECs. In the early phase (6-24 h), a pro-inflammatory profile predominated, observed with peak levels of IL-6, IFN-γ, IL-18, IL-12, TNF-α and IL-23. This subsequently transitions into the late phase (48-72 h) characterized by an anti-inflammatory shift, marked by elevated IL-10, classical tolerogenic molecules (IDO1, PDL1, and ILT3), and a profile consistent with the potential to induce regulatory T cells (Tregs). Concurrently, metabolic adaptations were observed, with glycolysis peaking at 24 h. Conclusion HDM-driven AD progression is correlated with changes in glucose metabolism and a biphasic immune shift in IDECs. Targeting HDM-responsive metabolic pathways like glycolysis might offer novel therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Gut microbiota, microbial metabolites, and mucosal barrier dysfunction in benign anorectal disorders and ulcerative colitis: shared mechanisms, clinical links, and precision interventions.
papers.authors: Yuan H, Zhao M, Wang Y, Shen C, Liu D, Wang C, Liu J.
papers.abstract: Benign anorectal disorders and ulcerative colitis (UC) are typically managed as separate clinical conditions, despite growing recognition of overlapping pathophysiological features. Constipation, hemorrhoidal disease, anal fistula and colonic mucosal inflammation may converge on partially shared molecular pathways involving microbial dysbiosis, altered microbial metabolite generation, epithelial barrier impairment, immune activation, stromal remodeling and dysregulated tissue repair, although the strength of mechanistic evidence varies substantially among these conditions. This review synthesizes advances from the past decade to propose a translational molecular medicine framework for investigating potential molecular connections among anatomically distinct anorectal and colonic disorders, without assuming shared causal origins. Clinical and pathological associations between disordered defecation, hemorrhoidal vascular remodeling, fistula persistence and UC are contextualized alongside current insights into gut and anorectal microbiota dysbiosis, short-chain fatty acid signaling, bile acid metabolism, tryptophan metabolite activity, gas-producing microbial communities, mucus biology, tight junction function, innate and adaptive immune responses, and fibro-inflammatory repair processes. Integrating microbiome profiling, metabolomics, transcriptomics, single-cell and spatial analyses with causal inference provides a cross-disease framework for resolving convergent molecular states associated with recurrence, healing and therapeutic response. By moving beyond disease-by-disease description, this strategy may uncover biomarkers and actionable pathways otherwise overlooked, supporting mechanism-informed prevention, perioperative optimization and individualized intervention across anorectal disorders and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD).

papers.title: Baseline growth kinetics of pulmonary metastases in head and neck adenoid cystic carcinoma: analysis of correlated clinical and molecular factors.
papers.authors: Liu HF, Jiang LY, Ma TY, Zhao Y, Li TY, Wang XL, Zhang SJ, Yang GL, Zhou J, Yan ZY, Chen XH.
papers.abstract: Objective To establish baseline growth rates of lung nodules in untreated head and neck adenoid cystic carcinoma(ACC) patients and analyze associated clinical and molecular factors influencing these rates. Methods CT was used to calculate the diameter of 74 pulmonary metastatic nodules in 37 patients under natural state. The diameter growth rate of lung metastatic nodules was fitted with a linear regression equation, and the differences in the progression rate of lung metastasis among patients were compared. Additionally, clinical features such as location, pathological subtypes, and staging were also collected to compare their correlation with the growth rate of lung metastatic nodules. Subsequently, single-cell sequencing data from three lung metastatic nodules of differing diameters within the same case were analyzed. Results We defined three different states based on the progression of lung metastases: rapid progression was defined as a monthly diameter increase of more than 1 mm in 16.2% (6/37) of the patients; slow progression was defined as a monthly diameter increase between 0.3-1 mm in 56.8% (21/37) of the patients; and stable state was defined as a monthly diameter increase of less than 0.3 mm in 27.0% (10/37) of the patients. In addition, factors such as low expression of TP63, a higher pathological grade (Grade III), and a nodule diameter greater than 10mm at initial diagnosis of lung metastasis were identified as significant predictors for a faster diameter growth rate (P Conclusion The findings of this study suggest that baseline characteristics based on the growth rate of pulmonary metastatic nodules may be used to help stratify the progression rate of lung metastasis. In particular, based on our observations, for patients with pulmonary metastatic lesions presenting with a nodule diameter > 10 mm, pathological grade III, and low TP63 expression at initial diagnosis, clinicians might consider adopting closer follow-up monitoring or potentially initiating intervention measures earlier. Additionally, for rapidly growing pulmonary metastatic nodules, it may be worth considering targeted therapy against hypoxic/anti-angiogenic pathways or combination with immunotherapy aimed at restoring or enhancing local immune responses.

papers.title: Whole-Genome Resequencing Reveals Genomic Signatures Underlying High-Altitude Adaptation in Ethiopian Indigenous Cattle.
papers.authors: Ma R, Li D, Lu Y, Wang B, Deng W, Gao Z.
papers.abstract: High-altitude environments impose severe physiological challenges on mammals, yet the genetic basis of adaptation in Ethiopian indigenous cattle remains poorly understood. Here, we analyzed whole-genome resequencing data from 70 Ethiopian indigenous cattle representing seven breeds (Abigar, Barka, Boran, Felata, Fogera, Gojjam-Highland, and Horro) distributed across elevations ranging from 523 to 3410 m, obtained from the NCBI Sequence Read Archive. After alignment to the ARS-UCD2.0 reference genome, we identified 49,196,624 high-confidence SNPs and performed population genomic analyses (PCA, phylogenetic reconstruction, and ADMIXTURE), along with genome-wide selection scans using FST and nucleotide diversity (θπ), and in silico virtual knockout of candidate genes in bovine lung single-cell transcriptomics. Population structure analyses revealed marked genetic differentiation between low- and mid-to-high-altitude populations, with substantial genetic connectivity and shared ancestry among high-altitude groups. We identified 398 candidate selective regions showing concordant FST and θπ signals, encompassing 1816 candidate genes, significantly enriched in hypoxia-related and vascular remodeling pathways (phospholipase D, Ras, ErbB, Wnt, Hedgehog). Two hub candidate genes, PIK3CA and RHOA , were prioritized; virtual perturbation of PIK3CA altered extracellular matrix, focal adhesion, and integrin networks, whereas RHOA perturbation activated immune and inflammatory programs (NF-κB, phagocytosis, chemokine pathways) with upregulation of TYROBP , IL1B , TLR4 , and NLRP3 . Our findings indicate that Ethiopian cattle have evolved distinct genomic signatures associated with adaptation to chronic high-altitude environments, in which PIK3CA and RHOA may represent candidate regulators associated with extracellular matrix organization and immune-related transcriptional regulation, respectively, thereby providing new insights into mammalian adaptation to extreme environments.

papers.title: CCL24 Blockade with Nebokitug Modulates Inflammation and Fibrosis Signatures in Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.
papers.authors: Aricha R, Snir T, Lawler J, Mor A.
papers.abstract: Background and aims Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease characterized by progressive inflammation, fibrosis, and innate immune dysregulation, with no approved therapies. Nebokitug (CM-101), a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting CCL24, demonstrated anti-inflammatory, anti-fibrotic, and anti-cholestatic activity in a Phase 2 clinical trial in patients with PSC. We performed comprehensive serum proteomic analyses to characterize the mechanistic effects of the CCL24 blockade following treatment with nebokitug. Methods Serum samples from study patients treated with nebokitug 10 mg/kg (n = 21), 20 mg/kg (n = 27), or placebo (n = 18) were analyzed using the Olink Explore 3072 proximity extension assay. Differential protein expression, pathway enrichment, and liver-specific proteome analyses were performed. Proteins corresponding to four PSC-specific gene expression programs (GEPs), identified previously by single-cell liver transcriptomics, were evaluated. An Elastic Net machine learning model was trained to classify treatment response defined by changes in Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) scores, liver stiffness measurements, and PRO-C3 test results. Results Nebokitug induced dose-dependent modulation of proteins involved in chemotaxis, leukocyte recruitment, extracellular matrix remodeling, cytokine signaling, and collagen organization. Proteins representing PSC-specific GEPs related to fibrosis, extracellular matrix remodeling, macrophage activation, myofibroblast biology, and immune activation and were reduced following nebokitug treatment, particularly in patients with moderate-to-advanced disease treated with the 20 mg/kg dose. A machine-learning model accurately identified responders (mean AUROC = 0.92), with liver-specific proteins representing the dominant predictive signature. Consistent with this finding, analysis of liver-specific proteins demonstrated clear separation between responders and non-responders in the 20 mg/kg group ( p = 0.0001), further linking treatment response to modulation of liver-specific biology. Conclusions Comprehensive proteomic profiling demonstrates that a CCL24 blockade with nebokitug modulates key biological pathways driving PSC. These findings provide mechanistic support for nebokitug's effect in PSC and further validate CCL24 as a promising therapeutic target in this indication.
