papers.title: Clinical Efficacy of Tislelizumab Plus Gemcitabine-Nab-Paclitaxel for Borderline Resectable Pancreatic Cancer and Chemoresistance Analysis: A Prospective Pilot Study.
papers.authors: He Y, Peng X, Jiang C, Li J, Li S, Xiang X, You N, Yang X, Tang Y, Huang X, Zheng L.
papers.abstract: Background Neoadjuvant therapy can improve the survival outcomes of patients with borderline resectable pancreatic cancer (BRPC). However, standard neoadjuvant regimens remain lacking. This study evaluated the clinical feasibility of tislelizumab plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel in the neoadjuvant setting for BRPC. Patients and methods In this prospective study, patients with BRPC preoperatively received three cycles of tislelizumab plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel, and continued postoperatively. The primary endpoints were R0 resection rate and treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). Exploratory objectives were resistance to this regimen. Results Of 30 enrolled patients, 80.0% (24/30) completed neoadjuvant therapy and underwent surgical resection. R0 resection was achieved in 80.0% (24/30) of the patients and in 100.00% (24/24) of those resected. The 12-month OS and RFS rates were 87.5% (95% CI 64.3-95.8%) and 82.8% (95% CI 60-95.8%), respectively, with median RFS of 28 months (95% CI 16.9-39.1). Most TRAEs were grade I-II, with no serious events. Quantitative proteomics combined with machine learning identified NT5DC2, FAM3D, CXCL5, and TMT1B as candidate biomarkers of resistance to this neoadjuvant regimen. In paired pre- and postoperative tissues from treatment-sensitive patients, CD8 + T-cell infiltration tended to increase and CD163 + M2-like macrophages were significantly upregulated after surgery. Conclusions Neoadjuvant tislelizumab plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel is promising for improving the resection rate in BRPC, with a favorable safety profile. NT5DC2, FAM3D, CXCL5, and TMT1B may serve as candidate biomarkers of preoperative drug resistance, and tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) analysis further reveals immune microenvironment remodeling in postoperative tumors from treatment-sensitive patients. These findings warrant validation in larger-scale studies. Trial Registration Chinese Clinical Trial registry (ChiCTR2200063680).

papers.title: A Metabolic Cluster-Derived Risk Model for Prognostic Stratification, Immunometabolic Profiling, and Therapeutic Sensitivity Prediction in Prostate Cancer.
papers.authors: Liu W, Wang C, Su T, Zhang J, Wu Y.
papers.abstract: Purpose Metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of prostate cancer; however, the clinical utility of metabolism-related genes for prognostic stratification remains limited. Patients and methods Prostate cancer patients from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) databases were stratified into metabolism-associated clusters based on metabolism-related gene expression. Genes differentially expressed between clusters were used to construct a prognostic risk model via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Associations with clinicopathological features, genomic alterations, metabolic activity, immune status, and therapeutic response were systematically evaluated. Computational analyses included tumor immune dysfunction and exclusion (TIDE) and the immunophenoscore for predicting immunotherapy response, pRRophetic and CellMiner for assessing drug sensitivity, and the Connectivity Map for screening candidate compounds. Exploratory assessments were performed using immunohistochemistry (IHC) in a 20-patient cohort with follow-up data and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) in an independent 14-patient cohort. Results Two metabolism-associated clusters with distinct survival outcomes and molecular features were identified. A three-gene signature stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups, with the high-risk group showing poorer survival, greater tumor aggressiveness, elevated tumor mutational burden and microsatellite instability, and enhanced metabolic pathway activity. This group also exhibited an immunosuppressive microenvironment and was predicted to have reduced responsiveness to some immunotherapies and endocrine therapies, along with increased resistance to specific chemotherapeutic agents. In silico analyses suggested several candidate small molecules for further evaluation in the high-risk group. The IHC- and qPCR-based exploratory experiments showed associations between the derived scores and clinicopathological features, providing preliminary support for the transcriptomic signature. Conclusion This metabolic cluster-derived three-gene model may support prognostic stratification and characterization of immunometabolic heterogeneity in prostate cancer. The observed associations between metabolic heterogeneity and computationally predicted therapeutic sensitivity provide a rationale for further investigation of potential treatment strategies.

papers.title: A Combined Network Toxicology and Docking Study to Identify Putative Molecular Targets Linking Styrene Exposure to Atherosclerosis.
papers.authors: Yan S, Shen G, Huang YQ, He GD.
papers.abstract: Background Styrene is a ubiquitous volatile organic compound linked to hematologic and vascular alterations; however, the molecular mechanisms connecting exposure to atherosclerosis remain poorly characterized. Methods We integrated peripheral blood mononuclear cell transcriptomic profiles (GSE23746) with toxicogenomic data from the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database, applying support vector machine recursive feature elimination and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator machine learning algorithms to identify core targets at the styrene-atherosclerosis intersection. Immune infiltration was assessed using CIBERSORT and single-sample gene set enrichment analysis, and molecular docking evaluated binding potential. Results Four model genes-CCND3, CCR1, MYC, and MYD88-were identified and constituted a diagnostic signature with high accuracy (area under the curve > 0.9). These genes were enriched in IL-17 and NF-κB inflammatory pathways and correlated with distinct immune cell alterations, particularly neutrophils and T cell subsets. Molecular docking predicted direct, moderate-affinity binding of styrene to CCND3 (Vina score = -6.4 kcal/mol), involving multiple contacts within the cyclin domain. Discussion The convergence of transcriptomic screening and molecular docking identifies CCND3 as a putative target for styrene-protein interaction and suggests a mechanistic hypothesis linking styrene to atherosclerosis via inflammatory and immune dysregulation. The computational framework provides a basis for future experimental validation. Conclusion This computational framework generates the hypothesis that styrene may contribute to atherosclerosis through coordinated perturbations of immune signaling and cell cycle regulation, with CCND3 representing a candidate molecular target for future experimental validation in styrene-exposed populations.

papers.title: Characterisation of Genetically-Derived Patient Clusters Highlights Genetic Heterogeneity of Inflammatory Bowel Disease
papers.authors: Vazquez Lopez, F.; Kadhim, A. Z.; Green, Z.; Nazari, I.; Cheng, G.; Cohen, L. J.; Chou, J. M.; Beattie, R. M.; Ennis, S.; Ashton, J. J.
papers.abstract: Background and aims. Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) is a complex immune-mediated condition with a strong genetic contribution. The genetics of IBD are highly complex, with inflammation, autoimmunity, and mucosal immunity pathways involved in its pathogenicity. GenePy is a gene-level disease burden metric. The integration of clinical and genetic data and the application of machine learning methods can aid patient stratification for personalised care. Methods. Lists of consensus IBD pathway genes were curated. GenePy scores were computed from whole exome sequencing data. A K-Means algorithm was optimised using clustering quality and stability metrics on the GenePy scores of genes in each IBD pathway, and the results replicated in three independent IBD cohorts (SPARC IBD, MSCCR IBD, and Southampton IBD). Chi-square tests assessed the association between cluster assignment and phenotypic features, and were multiple test corrected via Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. Results. A strong association was replicated for NOD signalling genes driving IBD subtype, Crohns disease behaviour, and IBD surgery across all cohorts, as well as granuloma in Southampton IBD. This was mainly driven by NOD2. Similar genetic clustering patterns were observed across all cohorts, with additional phenotypic enrichment in clusters driven by NLRP1 (surgery in MSCCR IBD), and nominally significant enrichment for disease behaviour linked to BIRC2 (B2 in Southampton IBD and B2B3 in SPARC IBD). Conclusions. This analysis identified a common genetic architecture across NOD signalling genes across IBD cohorts, replicated a signal for NOD2 as a monogenic driver of disease with a strong phenotypic enrichment, and identified other putative genetic drivers of IBD, such as the NLRP1 gene.

papers.title: Expression patterns of CD24 and CD27 resolve the origins and gradual differentiation of CD11c + atypical memory B-cells after malaria infection.
papers.authors: Courey-Ghaouzi AD, Kleberg L, Mousavian Z, Lautenbach MJ, Pirronello M, Phad GE, Forsell MNE, Färnert A, Sundling C.
papers.abstract: Atypical B-cells (ABCs) are observed across infections, yet their ontogeny and differentiation remain unclear. Using high-dimensional flow cytometry, single-cell transcriptomics, V(D)J sequencing, and functional assays in samples from individuals with malaria and healthy donors, we identify markers of cellular origin while tracking ABC differentiation. Early ABCs express CD11c and arise predominantly from memory B-cells. Two intermediate states originate from germinal center-derived and marginal zone-like B-cells. Pseudotime and lineage analyses reveal trajectories marked by progressive loss of CD24 and CD27, which is recapitulated in vitro, defining bona fide differentiation programs. Differentiation culminates in late ABCs lacking CD24, CD27, and CD21, while expressing CD11c, T-bet, and NKG7 at high levels, exhibiting partial overlap with double-negative-2 B-cells. Early and intermediate stages show greater plasma-cell differentiation potential and cytokine production capacity, whereas later stages acquire transcriptomic signatures of antigen presentation and association with microbial particles, defining stage-dependent functions that reconcile conflicting ABC roles. Comparable ABC populations occur in healthy blood and tonsils, with tissue-associated class switching and CD86 expression consistent with recent T-cell interaction. This framework consolidates ABC definitions along a single differentiation axis and clarifies their cellular origins.

papers.title: Molecular, spatial, and AI-enabled technologies for predicting neoadjuvant therapy response in locally advanced rectal cancer.
papers.authors: Boot GF, Masotti C, Corrò C, Schraepen C, Williams HL, Wright TA, Ishaqwala F, Steele CW, Rasschaert G, Lafarge MW, Domingo E, Zlobec I, Perez RO, Roxburgh CS, Maughan TS, Tejpar S, Koessler T, Koelzer VH.
papers.abstract: Pretreatment prediction of neoadjuvant response remains an unresolved challenge in locally advanced rectal cancer, where management is moving towards risk-adapted and response-oriented treatment strategies. Prediction remains difficult because response reflects interacting tumour-intrinsic, immune, stromal, and spatial processes that are incompletely captured by standard clinical and radiological assessment. From a technology-centred perspective, in this Review we assess how molecular, spatial, image-based, and artificial intelligence-enabled approaches are being used to study and predict response to neoadjuvant treatment from pretreatment biopsies and how readily they may be translated into clinical workflows. Genomic profiling has its clearest current clinical role in identifying hypermutated immune-responsive subgroups, whereas broader genomic, epigenomic, and immune-repertoire markers remain largely investigational. Bulk transcriptomics has generated multiple response signatures with variable reproducibility but has consistently highlighted immune activation, interferon signalling, stromal remodelling, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition as recurrent response-associated programmes; its most feasible clinical route is likely through targeted expression panels rather than open-ended transcriptome profiling. Higher-resolution approaches such as spatial transcriptomic and proteomic platforms refine these observations by localising signals to tumour, immune, and stromal compartments and capturing therapy-induced tissue reorganisation, but they are currently best positioned for deepening biological understanding and nominating rational treatment combinations for future testing. Established platforms such as digital pathology are closer to routine deployment as they build on clinically embedded workflows, although response-prediction algorithms still require robust external validation, calibration, and regulatory-grade implementation. Patient-derived models provide functional systems for testing candidate biomarkers and resistance mechanisms. Multimodal artificial intelligence may support response prediction by identifying complementary signals across data types and distilling complex signatures into parsimonious models suitable for clinical translation. Progress will depend on harmonised, longitudinal, multi-centre studies that couple biological depth with assay standardisation, model reduction, and prospective evidence that response predictors improve patient management. © 2026 The Author(s). papers.title: kitAb: an automated framework for assay-specific antibody developability modeling and large-scale landscape analysis
papers.authors: Trofimova, E.; Shaburova, E.; Antonets, D.; Ramensky, V.
papers.abstract: Antibody developability is determined by multiple physicochemical properties, and the relevance of individual properties varies among experimental assays. Existing computational approaches, however, often provide fixed assessments or rely on computationally intensive descriptors. We present kitAb, an open-source framework for scalable physicochemical characterization of antibody Fv regions and assay-specific developability modeling. kitAb calculates 59 interpretable sequence- and structure-based descriptors and integrates them with automated feature selection and regression. We evaluated kitAb across ten public datasets comprising 46 experimental endpoints, using sequence-aware or predefined splits where feasible. Predictive performance was strongly assay-dependent. In nested evaluations with sequence-aware or predefined data splits, models using kitAb descriptors achieved predictive performance comparable on average to those using PROPERMAB descriptors, while outperforming models based on TAP or sequence-only features. In a single-structure CPU timing benchmark, kitAb descriptor calculation was approximately 11-fold faster than PROPERMAB. Predictive performance was similar across the three structure-generation backends, and broader AutoML searches did not substantially improve mean performance. We further applied the same descriptor representation to approximately 3.4 million paired natural antibodies and 706 Phase II or later therapeutic antibodies. Repertoire-scale analysis revealed systematic differences in surface charge, hydrophobic and aromatic organization, CDR length and germline-associated physicochemical profiles. The kitAb code and analysis workflows are openly available at https://github.com/katyachemistry/kitAb/.

papers.title: Dual Host-Pathogen Screening of the Lung During Severe Influenza Using Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.authors: Tong MZW, Skinner OP, Zhu C, Wanrooy BJ, Kerr AS, Ruan Z, Williams CG, Zhang H, Wakim LM, Haque A.
papers.abstract: Here, we assessed whether spatially resolved capture of polyadenylated mRNA permitted simultaneous screening of host and viral responses in situ. Fresh-frozen lung samples from mice infected with H1N1 influenza A strain, PR8, were processed via genome-wide, spatial transcriptomics (ST) at 10-μm resolution. To determine if specific cell-types were detectable within the ST data, we first performed cellular deconvolution using publicly available, single-cell RNA-seq data of immune and non-immune cells from PR8-infected lungs. This revealed expected structures such as rings of epithelial cells lining airways, and at Day 10 post-infection (p.i.) unexpected structures dominated by B cells. We next screened ST data alone for groups of genes displaying similar spatial expression patterns. This again identified at Day 10 p.i. cellular aggregates enriched for genes associated with B cell biology. Mapping these gene signatures to a B cell transcriptomic atlas suggested plasmablasts had emerged early in the lung, which was confirmed by flow cytometry. Finally, by mapping ST data to the influenza A genome, we observed widespread expression of all 10 viral transcripts across samples at Day 4 but not Day 10 p.i., consistent with viral clearance. Cellular deconvolution analysis at Day 4 p.i. revealed proportions of every detected cell-type harbored viral transcripts, suggesting indiscriminate infection across the specific area of tissue examined. Subsequent whole-section immunohistochemical assessment further supported the phenomenon of localized indiscriminate infection, with these areas found adjacent to minimally infected zones. Thus, spatial screening of mRNA in tissues can simultaneously inform upon viral pathogenesis and host responses to infection.

papers.title: SPP1-CD44-Mediated Crosstalk Between Endothelial and Macrophage Subpopulations Promotes Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Progression Through S100A6 Upregulation.
papers.authors: Zhou Y, Guo S, Zhou W, Wang W.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) progression is driven by complex cellular interactions within the tumor microenvironment (TME), where endothelial cell (EC)-tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) crosstalk significantly influences angiogenesis and immune modulation, although the specific subsets and consequences remain unclear. Here, we integrated four single-cell RNA sequencing datasets (50 PDAC; 21 normal adjacent tissues) to profile EC and macrophage subpopulations, subsequently employing CellChat to decipher intercellular communication networks and identify altered ligand-receptor interactions in PDAC. Correlation and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses (TCGA-PAAD) assessed associations and prognostic value, while functional validation used EdU, CCK-8, and Transwell assays on PDAC cells. We identified a distinct endothelial subset (EC0) and macrophage subset (Mac2) with enhanced interaction signals in PDAC. This EC0-Mac2 crosstalk correlated with significant S100A6 upregulation, which was associated with poor patient prognosis. Exogenous S100A6 treatment markedly enhanced PDAC cell proliferation and migration in vitro. In conclusion, EC-Mac crosstalk may promote PDAC progression via S100A6, and this interaction pattern warrants further investigation as a candidate prognostic biomarker and potential target for disrupting stromal communication.

papers.title: Identification of CLOCK and MARK2 as Candidate Blood-Based Biomarkers in Type 2 Diabetes: An Integrated Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Study.
papers.authors: Yang L, Tang J, Zhang D, Yun P.
papers.abstract: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is often accompanied by nervous system complications. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying T2DM remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify candidate blood-based biomarkers associated with T2DM by screening a neural-related gene set through integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood. The present analysis focused on the systemic expression patterns of the selected genes in peripheral blood as indicators of T2DM-associated immunometabolic dysregulation, rather than on neurological involvement. The neural-related gene set was used only as a predefined screening starting point. Methods: We employed a three-tier validation framework comprising (1) a training cohort (GSE15932, 8 T2DM patients vs. 8 controls) for biomarker discovery using differential expression analysis and machine learning (XGBoost, random forest, and PPI network topology); (2) an independent validation cohort (GSE184050, 50 T2DM patients vs. 65 controls) for cross-dataset diagnostic performance assessment (ROC analysis); and (3) an experimental validation cohort (5 T2DM patients vs. 5 controls) for independent clinical confirmation by RT-qPCR. Additionally, single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE268210) was used to investigate cell type-specific expression and immune regulatory networks. Results: By combining multiple screening methods and cross-dataset validation, we identified CLOCK and MARK2 as key candidate genes from the neural-related gene set. CLOCK and MARK2 showed high discriminatory performance in the discovery cohort, whereas their AUCs were 0.613 and 0.653, respectively, in the validation cohort, indicating limited standalone discriminatory ability. Both genes are highly expressed in peripheral blood monocytes and are associated with MIF-(CD74+CXCR4)-mediated cell communication, TNFA-NFκB inflammatory signaling, and activation of oxidative phosphorylation pathways. Finally, RT-qPCR in clinical samples confirmed that both genes were indeed upregulated ( p Conclusions: CLOCK and MARK2 were identified as candidate T2DM-associated blood-based biomarkers with reproducible expression differences across datasets. Their discriminatory performance was more modest in the independent validation cohort, indicating limited standalone diagnostic utility. Single-cell and computational analyses further suggested potential immunometabolic relevance. Because neurological phenotyping, cognitive assessment, and direct measures of nervous system involvement were not available in this study, any relationship between these genes and the neurological manifestations of T2DM remains speculative and hypothesis-generating, and requires prospective validation in cohorts with matched neurocognitive data.

papers.title: Rational hapten design enables monoclonal antibody-based immunoassays for class-selective detection of phthalate esters in edible oils.
papers.authors: Feng Q, Liu L, Wu A, Xu X, Kuang H, Xu C, Xu L.
papers.abstract: Phthalate esters (PAEs) are frequently detected in edible oils, necessitating rapid detection methods. However, the small molecular size and high structural similarity of PAEs make it challenging to develop antibodies that combine analytical sensitivity with group-selective recognition. Herein, a monoclonal antibody (mAb) with group-selective recognition toward dibutyl phthalate (DBP), diallyl phthalate (DAP), and diethyl phthalate (DEP) was generated through rational hapten design guided by computational analysis. Based on this mAb, an indirect competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ic-ELISA) and a colloidal gold immunochromatographic strip (ICS) were developed for rapid quantitative detection. The optimized ic-ELISA exhibited half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC 50 ) values of 20.4, 80.1, and 110.4 ng/mL for DBP, DAP, and DEP, respectively, while showing <1% cross-reactivity with other tested phthalate analogues. The ICS enabled visual detection within 15 min, with visual limit of detections (vLODs) of 20, 100, and 200 ng/mL for DBP, DAP, and DEP in edible oils, respectively. By integrating computationally guided hapten design with complementary quantitative and rapid screening formats, this study provides a practical platform for class-selective screening of PAEs in edible oils and a useful strategy for developing group-recognizing antibodies against structurally related small-molecule contaminants.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Nanobody Engineering for Pathogen Recognition: From Functional Epitope Prioritization to Multimodal Foundation Models.
papers.authors: Hu RS, Ehsan M, Luo W, Zhou J, Xiao YL, Wang HX, Li CY, Gu K.
papers.abstract: Nanobodies are compact and stable proteins derived from the variable domain of camelid heavy-chain-only antibodies (VHH). Advances in structural biology, molecular modeling, and artificial intelligence (AI) are shifting VHH discovery from empirical selection toward data-driven design. However, predicted binding alone does not ensure biological activity or successful translation, particularly for antigenically variable pathogens. Complementing recent reviews that broadly survey computational VHH modeling and optimization, this review focuses on how antigen biology and functional epitope prioritization can guide the design of pathogen-targeting VHHs. We organize the field along a structure-function-translation continuum, connecting the structural basis of VHH recognition and available data resources with conventional discovery, antigen-guided de novo design, and sequence-structure learning. We further examine how developability, recombinant production, multispecificity, humanization, structural dynamics, and antigenic variation shape the progression from predicted binders to functional VHHs. Finally, we discuss how multimodal foundation models could integrate these dimensions to support the design of functional, manufacturable, and escape-resilient VHHs.

papers.title: Benchmarking interface confidence as a selection criterion for computational nanobody design against survivin's BIR-domain groove
papers.authors: Gately, C.; Guan, X.; Ding, X.
papers.abstract: Designed binders are routinely filtered on predicted interface confidence, which reports how self-consistently a model places an interface, not where it lies. We designed 200 nanobody loops against the survivin BIR-domain groove, co-folded 196, and checked epitope contact in every predicted complex. Confidence showed no detectable association with epitope engagement ({rho} = +0.100, 95% CI -0.04 to +0.24, n = 196); its highest and lowest quartiles failed alike (odds ratio 0.97, 95% CI 0.41 to 2.26). It tracked instead the run's other confidence estimates ({rho} = +0.61). Twelve-seed replication separated two candidates the criteria had not: one reached the complete epitope in 10 of 12 runs, the other never. Across 155 predictions the top-ranked model was no better than one drawn at random from its five (P = 0.610), though only 3 of 31 failed on every model. Nothing was assayed; nb_cand_057 is an in silico candidate only.

papers.title: AI-Driven Design of Next-Generation Immunoinformatics Multi-Epitope Subunit Vaccine Targeting the Most Virulent Mpox Proteome: A Structural and Kinetic Validation Framework
papers.authors: Emon, M.; Siddiqque, N. H.; Haque, M. E.
papers.abstract: The resurgence of the Mpox virus (MPXV) highlights the urgent need for scalable, mutation-resistant countermeasures. Slow development timelines hinder traditional empirical vaccine discovery, while conventional vaccinology often yields high false-positive rates because it relies on static, linear sequence-based screening. These classical informatics filters consistently fail to predict physical structural stability or the dynamic presentation of immune cells under physiological conditions, creating a distinct translational gap between computational design and in vitro efficacy. To address these limitations, here we engineered an advanced, AI-augmented vaccine discovery pipeline targeting the most virulent components of the MPXV proteome. We systematically screened eight critical viral targets essential for replication, membrane morphogenesis, and host-cell entry to map highly conserved T-cell and B-cell epitopes. Moving beyond standard heuristic filtering, we implemented a high-fidelity deep learning validation layer: ESM-2 protein language models (pLMs) were deployed to calculate pseudo-perplexity scores across chimeric linker junctions (EAAAK, GPGPG) to guarantee structural naturalness, MHCflurry ensemble models successfully verified active intracellular antigen presentation, and structure-informed graph neural networks (GNNs) simulated the physical node-attention dynamics of the immune synapse. Finally, recurrent neural networks (RNNs)-driven mRNA kinetic modeling optimized translation initiation rates and minimum free energy profiles during in silico cloning. This multi-layered pipeline successfully yielded three structurally refined, multi-epitope vaccine constructs optimized for maximum global population coverage. ESM-2 structural validation confirmed exceptionally low perplexity scores at structural junctions, indicating that the engineered chimaeras have native-like stability and a minimized risk of proteolysis. GNN-based immune synapse modeling demonstrated highly stable binding kinetics and robust binding free energies between the target epitopes and human HLA alleles. Furthermore, RNN kinetic optimizations established that the cDNA sequences are optimized for high-yield expression in heterologous expression hosts without risk of ribosomal stalling or translational bottlenecks. This study establishes a deep learning-augmented framework that bridges the gap between theoretical sequence optimization and biopharmaceutical scalability. By validating the structural naturalness, real-world immunogenicity, and manufacturing kinetics of our vaccine chimeras, this framework presents a robust, proactive paradigm for rapid vaccine architecture against emerging orthopoxvirus threats.

papers.title: In silico subtractive genomics and reverse vaccinology approach reveal outer membrane proteins OMP47 and LptD as dual-purpose drug and vaccine targets in Pasteurella multocida Pm70
papers.authors: Khan Chowdhury, A. R.; Islam, S.; Farid, A.; Lamia, F.; Ahmad, T. F.; Hossain, N. J.; Paul, A. R.; Afrin, T.; Elias, S. M.
papers.abstract: Drug targets and vaccines for bacterial diseases are challenging to develop. Computational subtractive genomics and reverse vaccinology offer a viable substitute for conventional drug and vaccine development approaches. In recent years, Pasteurella multocida, a Gram-negative pathogen responsible for severe infections in humans along with major diseases in livestock and poultry, has developed resistance to multiple drugs. As a result, there is an urgent demand for research into reliable, efficient, highly potent, and cost-effective strategies to combat the rise of Pasteurella multocida infections. To address this, the present study integrated an in silico subtractive genomics and reverse vaccinology workflow to pinpoint proteins with potential value as both drug and vaccine targets. From the complete Pasteurella multocida Pm70 proteome, we identified 446 proteins that had no similarities with human proteins, out of which 129 were found to be essential for the pathogens survival. These 129 proteins are therefore potential candidates for drug development. Further metabolic pathway analysis, virulence potential, subcellular localization, and structural analyses revealed two outer membrane proteins, namely, 47 kDa outer membrane protein and lipopolysaccharide-assembly protein LptD, as promising candidates for therapeutic development. Subsequent antigenicity analysis revealed both outer membrane proteins as potential vaccine targets, exhibiting highly favorable antigenicity scores. Candidate B- and T-cell epitopes were systematically mapped from these two targets based on antigenicity, immunogenicity, toxicity, and allergenicity potential and only high-confidence epitopes were assembled using adjuvants and class-specific linkers to construct the final multi-epitope vaccine (MEV). The designed MEV construct was demonstrated to be highly antigenic, non-toxic and non-allergenic to humans, while possessing favorable structural and physicochemical properties, and exhibited strong binding interactions with human toll-like receptors with minimal molecular deformability. Although further experimental validation is recommended to fully assess their efficacy, the present study establishes a solid foundation for the development of novel therapeutics and vaccine candidates against P. multocida, ultimately contributing to the reduction of its rising infections.

papers.title: Reversal of Chronic Stress-Induced Inflammaging by Bazi Bushen Formula Through AMPK-Sirtuins Axis Activation and Myeloid Reset.
papers.authors: Li M, Chen Z, Wang L, Wang Z, Zhang S, Niu K, Shen X, Lu X, Zhang R, Jiang Y, Li Y, Dai Y, Tang X, Hou B, Shi M, Wang X, Guo Z, Xing X, Kang N, Li H, Kang T, Bischof E, Hou Y, Jia Z.
papers.abstract: Chronic stress potentially accelerates aging and increases age-related disease risk. However, the underlying mechanisms and organ specificity remain unclear. Utilizing a 12-month unpredictable chronic mild stress (UCMS) mouse model, we revealed chronic stress significantly exacerbates systemic inflammation, causing widespread tissue damage and lifespan shortening. Integrated single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of multiple tissues suggests a common feature of lymphocyte reduction and myeloid cell expansion. The lungs and kidneys exhibited pronounced stress responses, including epigenetic dysregulation and mitochondrial dysfunction. Both β-nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) and compound medicine Bazi Bushen (BZBS) effectively alleviate the UCMS-induced aging phenotypes. BZBS restores immune system homeostasis and reduces stress/inflammation levels in various tissues. Bioactive compounds from BZBS constituents -Schisandra chinensis (Turcz.) Baill. and Cnidium monnieri (L.) Cusson- improved mitochondrial function via AMPK-SIRT-PGC-1α signaling activation. The present study underscores the importance of early intervention in chronic stress to prevent or delay age-related diseases, with significant implications for public health strategies aimed at healthy aging.

papers.title: Anti-inflammatory IL-4 shapes the architecture of presynaptic glutamatergic puncta of human and murine sensory neurons for pain sensitivity.
papers.authors: Zimmermann D, Schöpf CL, Ucar B, Vasconcelos D, Kern G, Musso G, Dotta S, Marvaldi L, Eijkelkamp N, Kummer K, Zur Nedden S, Kalpachidou T, Zeidler M, Palecek J, Kress M.
papers.abstract: The pleiotropic anti-inflammatory cytokine interleukin 4 (IL-4) not only modulates immune responses but also plays important roles in the nervous system by mediating itch, antinociception and neuroregeneration. Here, we assessed the expression and function of IL-4, its receptors, and downstream signaling pathways in human induced pluripotent stem cell derived nociceptors (iNocs), organotypic mouse spinal cord cultures, and in in vivo models. In silico analyses of human and mouse dorsal root ganglion (DRG) single cell transcriptomes revealed that a specific subpopulation of murine and human sensory neurons expressed IL4R and IL13RA1 (but very little IL2RG) receptor subunits highlighting conserved neuron responsiveness to IL-4. In iNocs, exogenous IL-4 induced de novo formation of presynaptic vGLUT1-positive puncta. Pharmacological inhibition of Janus kinases 1/2, STAT6, protein kinase C isoforms, or the translation initiation factor eIF4E significantly attenuated the IL-4-associated increase in vGLUT1-positive puncta. Transcriptomic profiling of iNocs revealed IL-4-regulated biological processes associated with neuronal development and synaptic organization. Consistently, IL-4 increased mean-firing-rate in iNocs and increased vGLUT1 expression in mouse organotypic spinal cord cultures treated with IL-4, in vitro. Intrathecal or intranasal IL-4 treatment enhanced both, inhibitory and excitatory synaptic activity in acute spinal cord slices, and this was associated with a decrease in mechanical and thermal sensitivity but normal sensorimotor coordination in vivo. These findings position IL-4 as key regulator of presynaptic glutamatergic organization for primary afferent neuron connectivity in the spinal dorsal horn and support a critical role for IL-4 in the excitation - inhibition balance of pain processing spinal neuronal networks.

papers.title: The gene expression signature of multinucleated giant cells in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice.
papers.authors: Hirai H, Hayashida K, Sanjoba C, Fujii W, Yamagishi J, Goto Y.
papers.abstract: Multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) are associated with chronic inflammation and infectious diseases, but their biological characteristics in vivo remain poorly understood because intact cells are difficult to isolate from tissues. In visceral leishmaniasis, heavily parasitized, hemophagocytic MGCs are observed in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice, suggesting that these cells may contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology. In this study, we established a method for isolating intact MGCs from the spleens of chronically infected BALB/c mice and performed transcriptomic analysis of manually collected single cells. Gentle enzymatic digestion of infected spleens enabled the recovery of large, multinucleated, F4/80-positive cells, indicating that size-based manual selection efficiently enriched for MGCs. Principal component analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data from 10 isolated MGCs showed that most MGCs formed a cluster distinct from those of naïve and infected bulk-spleen samples and RAW264.7 macrophage cells. Differential expression analysis identified genes that were upregulated during infection and further enriched in MGCs, including Ccl8, Cd63, Cebpb, and Fabp5, which are associated with macrophage activation and immune regulation. These findings provide a practical approach for isolating splenic MGCs and offer preliminary insight into the transcriptional features of L. donovani-induced MGCs in vivo.

papers.title: A renal cyst-clear cell renal cell carcinoma comorbidity analysis identifies a FOXM1-positive epithelial COL6A1-CD44 axis that remodels fibroblasts.
papers.authors: Lv H, Ge C, Jin Y, Fang Y, Liu W, Zhang Y, Zhang H, Fang C, Qu L, Lu X, Zhang W, Zhang N, Jiang A, Wu L, Wang L.
papers.abstract: Background Renal cystic conditions are heterogeneous. We used a broad renal cyst-associated disease-gene framework to identify molecular programs shared with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), without modeling a specific cystic disorder or direct cyst-to-cancer progression. Methods We identified 237 shared genes between renal cyst disease and ccRCC (TCGA-KIRC), performed functional enrichment, Mendelian randomization, and built a random survival forest (RSF) risk score benchmarked against published signatures and immunotherapy cohorts. Single-cell (Scissor, SCENIC, scTenifoldKnk virtual FOXM1 knockout) and spatial transcriptomics (RCTD, CellChat) were integrated with fibroblast subclustering and oncoPredict drug screening. Candidate FOXM1 inhibitors were prioritized by docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics, with isovitexin validated functionally. Results The shared program was enriched for epithelial development and ECM remodeling. Two direction-specific Mendelian randomization analyses supported associations between genetic liability to kidney cancer and related renal cystic phenotypes. The RSF score showed robust prognostic discrimination across cohorts and separated immunotherapy outcomes. High-risk tumors were enriched for Tregs, B cells, and fibroblasts. FOXM1+ malignant epithelium represented the high-risk state, with elevated CNV burden and regulon activity; virtual FOXM1 knockout identified COL6A1 and CD44 among 129 significant non-target perturbation hits. Convergent single-cell and spatial analyses nominated a COL6A1-CD44 communication axis associated with fibroblast remodeling, with F5_SFRP2 + fibroblasts as the most plausible receiving state. These fibroblasts showed ECM-remodeling, adverse prognosis, and pathway activation. Isovitexin emerged as a lead FOXM1-targeting compound, significantly suppressing ccRCC proliferation, migration, and invasion. Conclusions These findings support a testable communication model involving FOXM1+ epithelium, COL6A1-CD44 and F5_SFRP2+ fibroblasts. The in vitro results also support further evaluation of isovitexin in ccRCC.

papers.title: Concurrent de novo inference of cell types and gene regulatory networks with NetMap
papers.authors: Hartebrodt, A.; Oubounyt, M.; de Almeida, G. P.; Reim, T.; Wenke, N.; Baumbach, J.; Zehn, D.; Blumenthal, D. B.
papers.abstract: Existing methods for GRN inference based on single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data typically require prior cell type calling and then infer GRNs at cell type resolution. This risks propagation of errors from cell annotation to GRN inference. Moreover, it makes existing methods blind to regulatory programs that are shared between different cell types, as well as to subtle differences in regulatory activity between cells of the same type. To address these limitations, we present NetMap, a pipeline that jointly infers cell-level GRNs and clusters cells based on shared regulatory programs, combining state-of-the-art single-cell autoencoders and explainable artificial intelligence methods. NetMap outperforms existing methods on synthetic data with a known ground-truth GRN and is able to reliably detect biologically plausible regulons on real data. Moreover, requiring only a small set of user-provided marker genes, NetMap can be used for GRN structure-informed probabilistic cell type assignment. We demonstrate the utility of this approach using PBMC data, where we achieve near perfect clustering and cell type recovery performance compared with manually created cell type labels. Finally, we applied NetMap to a data set with naive, activated and exhausted T-cells, and were able to verify that NetMap retrieves relevant T-cell state signatures from the data, with two approaches. NetMap can be installed as a python package from https://github.com/bionetslab/netmap and is compatible with the scverse system. Scripts to reproduce our results can be found at https://github.com/bionetslab/netmap-evaluation.

papers.title: Metabolic Milieu and Susceptibility: The Combined Benefits of Targeting AMPK and ACE2 for Metabolic Disorders and COVID-19.
papers.authors: Tata FY, Nxumalo MB, Ntanzi N, Mushebenge AG, Khan RB, Kumalo HM.
papers.abstract: The convergence of metabolic dysfunction and infectious diseases has become increasingly evident, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) emerge as pivotal molecular regulators linking metabolic homeostasis, endothelial integrity, immune modulation, and viral pathogenesis. Metabolic diseases such as diabetes, obesity, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease are marked by insulin resistance, chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, and endothelial dysfunction, collectively increasing susceptibility to severe viral infections and outcomes. This review examines experimental, computational, and translational evidence exploring the interplay between AMPK and ACE2, focusing on metabolic, vascular, and inflammatory pathways relevant to viral infections. Recent findings show a bidirectional functional relationship between AMPK and ACE2, where AMPK phosphorylation supports ACE2 expression and function, and ACE2 signaling reciprocally enhances AMPK activity, forming a protective metabolic-vascular loop. Disruption of this axis, particularly through SARS-CoV-2-induced ACE2 degradation, exacerbates metabolic deterioration, vascular damage, and exaggerated inflammatory responses. Preclinical and in silico studies show that pharmacological AMPK activators, including metformin and bioactive flavonoids, demonstrate pleiotropic metabolic, anti-inflammatory, endothelial protective, and potential antiviral activities, hinting at the therapeutic potential of modulating the AMPK-ACE2 axis, despite the limited clinical application of flavonoids. The AMPK-ACE2 axis represents an important molecular link between metabolic regulation, renovascular health, and immune defense mechanisms. This evaluation connects AMPK and ACE2 from isolated signaling nodes into a coordinated pharmacological axis with implications for interventions in cardiometabolic and viral diseases. Future research should prioritize mechanistic validation and conduct integrated experimental and clinical investigations to establish AMPK-ACE2 co-targeting as a viable therapeutic strategy for mitigating cardiometabolic disease burden and enhancing resilience against viral infections.

papers.title: Single-cell gene networks nominate IKZF1 as an Alzheimer's disease microglial regulator.
papers.authors: Özkurt Ç.
papers.abstract: BackgroundMicroglia drive neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet no approved therapy targets this compartment. Human genome-wide association studies consistently implicate innate immune loci in AD risk, establishing microglial transcriptional programs as therapeutically relevant but pharmacologically underexploited targets.ObjectiveWe sought to identify transcription factors (TFs) governing microglial state transitions computationally and to nominate structurally tractable drug repurposing candidates.MethodsWe applied trajectory inference (PAGA), pseudobulk DESeq2, pySCENIC gene regulatory network (GRN) inference, CellChat, and virtual screening of 1962 approved compounds to 236,002 microglial nuclei from 84 donors (SEA-AD atlas).Results IKZF1 was the sole target TF retained under cisTarget v10 motif constraints, with peak regulon activity in LateAD-DAM (pseudotime ρ = + 0.309) and replication in an independent bulk cohort (GSE95587; adjusted p = 0.004). CellChat identified SLIT2→ROBO2 from multiple neuron subtypes (predominantly inhibitory interneurons) as the top predicted pathway to microglia. Tafamidis (→IRF8) and diflunisal (→PPARG) were top virtual screening hits; all evaluated compounds failed the pre-specified selectivity threshold.Conclusions IKZF1 is prioritized as a candidate late-disease microglial TF, supported by six convergent evidence dimensions including independent bulk replication. Tafamidis and diflunisal are low-confidence repurposing hypotheses requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: Immunosuppressant-refractory Multifaceted Immune Dysregulations for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
papers.authors: Xia CR, Qian JY, Ding Y, Zhao JL, Wang Q, Tian XP, Zeng XF, Gao G, Li MT.
papers.abstract: While the systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), a severe autoimmune disease, is known to relapse frequently after treatment, none of the previous single-cell studies have examined the immune dynamics and their potential contribution to this relapse in the real clinical setting. To address this issue, here we employed single-cell multi-omics profiling to delineate immune repertoire dynamics during the immunosuppressant-based standard of care. Further analysis showed that the canonical therapy fails to restore various critical abnormalities, including the drop in mutational load of B and plasma cells, and the clonal expansion of CD4+ Th1 and CD8+ memory T cells. We also integrated our data with published SLE datasets to compile a comprehensive SLE immune atlas of about 1.6 million cells. Our study provides valuable data and sheds light on the underlying multifaceted unresolved dysregulation upon SLE immunosuppressant therapy under the real clinical setting; such dysregulation may further contribute to the high post-treatment relapse rate and thus call for additional target-specific treatment strategies.

papers.title: BLIMP1 shapes germinal center B cell clonal diversity by gating chromatin accessibility during light-to-dark zone transition
papers.authors: Vijay, G. M.; Ramaswami, B.; Gierlack, S.; Pease, N. A.; Rothstein, D.; Singh, H.
papers.abstract: Germinal center (GC) B cell responses are defined by many positive regulators of affinity maturation, but few components that restrain clonal dominance, notably Nr4a1, are known. We reveal an unsuspected role for Blimp1 (Prdm1), a plasma cell determinant, as a feedback regulator of affinity maturation. Single cell RNA-seq and B cell receptor (BCR) seq showed that B cell specific Prdm1 loss drives an exaggerated GC reaction with larger clones, increased somatic hypermutation, and greater clonal dominance, independent of Nr4a1. Single cell chromatin profiling with base-resolution modeling indicated that Blimp1 represses expression of BCR-signaling genes, gating chromatin accessibility at ISRE, EICE, NFKB, and Oct motifs. In the absence of Blimp1, enhanced BCR signaling augments activities of transcription factors that promote G1/S transition during light-zone (LZ) selection and fuel dark-zone (DZ) expansion. Thus, Blimp1 attenuates BCR signaling and constrains the LZ to DZ transition, fine-tuning clonal competition thereby maintaining repertoire diversity.

papers.title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identifies a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated risk program for pulmonary metastasis/relapse in osteosarcoma.
papers.authors: Li Z, Yang B, Liu S, Yu S.
papers.abstract: Background Pulmonary metastasis/relapse (PM/R) is a major cause of osteosarcoma treatment failure. We aimed to develop a compact transcriptomic PM/R risk score and characterize associated immune and single-cell programs. Methods TARGET-OS bulk RNA-seq was used for discovery and GSE21257 for external validation. Differential expression, multi-algorithm feature selection and LASSO regression were used to construct the score. Clinical associations were assessed by PM/R classification, survival and calibration analyses. Immune signature scoring, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), single-cell projection, in silico virtual HERC5 knockout, PROGENy/DoRothEA, CellChat and exploratory drug-reversal analyses were used for biological interpretation. Results A 9-gene score comprising HERC5, GPR141, SLC45A4, LCN15, MXI1, UCK2, KRTAP13-2, KCNK6 and TRABD2A showed high apparent discrimination in TARGET-OS (AUC = 0.922). A reduced seven-gene GSE21257 implementation achieved an AUC of 0.728. High-risk tumors were enriched for PM/R and had poorer event-free survival (HR = 3.14, 95% CI, 1.60-6.16) and overall survival (HR = 3.75, 95% CI, 1.60-8.79). High-risk disease showed reduced antigen-presentation, IFN-gamma, T-cell, CD8 T-cell, NK-cell and cytotoxicity signatures. WGCNA identified a protective immune module, while single-cell and in silico virtual-knockout analyses prioritized HERC5 as a candidate immune-associated node linked to antigen-presentation genes. Regulatory and communication analyses suggested reduced JAK-STAT/IRF activity and SPP1/MIF-centered microenvironmental signaling. Conclusions This study defines a PM/R-focused transcriptomic risk score and links high-risk osteosarcoma to immune attenuation and a HERC5-associated antigen-presentation program, providing a framework for future validation.

figure.label: Fig. 1
figure.caption: Transcriptomic discovery of pulmonary metastasis/relapse-associated programs in osteosarcoma. a, Overview of the TARGET-OS discovery cohort comparing primary osteosarcoma samples classified as PM/R-negative or PM/R-positive according to pulmonary involvement at diagnosis or during follow-up. b, Principal-component analysis of variance-stabilized RNA-seq expression profiles, colored by PM/R status. c, Volcano plot showing differentially expressed genes between PM/R-positive and PM/R-negative tumors, with significantly upregulated and downregulated genes highlighted according to the prespecified false-discovery rate and fold-change thresholds. d, Heatmap of representative top differentially expressed genes across TARGET-OS samples ordered by PM/R status. Values are row-scaled expression z-scores. e, Gene-set enrichment analysis of ranked differential-expression statistics, showing biological programs associated with the PM/R phenotype. Positive normalized enrichment scores indicate enrichment in PM/R-positive tumors, whereas negative scores indicate enrichment in PM/R-negative tumors. Differential expression was performed with DESeq2, and enrichment was assessed using preranked gene-set analysis with multiple-testing correction.
