papers.title: Identification of Immune-Related Hub Genes as Candidate Biomarkers for Preeclampsia: Integrative Transcriptomic and Machine Learning Approaches.
papers.authors: Hu X, Liu L, Yin T, Huang X, Yu H, Yan Y, Zhong T, Du M, Zhao F.
papers.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a major cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and is increasingly recognized as a disorder involving immune dysregulation. However, reliable candidate biomarkers and key molecular alterations associated with PE remain unclear. We integrated multiple public placental transcriptomic datasets from patients with PE and normotensive controls. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis and eight machine-learning algorithms were used to identify stable immune-related candidate genes, followed by immune infiltration analysis, single-cell analysis, SHAP interpretation, and in silico gene knockout analysis. A six-gene logistic regression model was evaluated in the same merged placental dataset used for feature selection and explored in a small independent peripheral-blood cohort. Frequency-based integration across the eight algorithms identified a six-gene signature comprising ACSS3, F13A1, MCTP1, PTGFR, SLC16A10, and TNFRSF11A. The model showed apparent discrimination in the merged placental dataset (AUC = 0.869, 95% CI: 0.820-0.919) and exploratory cross-tissue discrimination in the peripheral-blood cohort (AUC = 0.860, 95% CI: 0.691-1.000). Immunohistochemical analysis of placental tissues from five women with PE and five normotensive controls showed lower protein abundance of all six candidates in PE, consistent with the bulk transcriptomic findings. Single-cell analysis indicated heterogeneous cell-type-dependent expression patterns, while in silico knockout analysis suggested potential macrophage-associated regulatory effects. Collectively, these exploratory findings identify a six-gene immune-related candidate signature associated with PE that requires validation in larger, prospectively collected cohorts before clinical application.

papers.title: The Cellular and Immune Context of YTHDC1 in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Single-Cell and Multicohort Study.
papers.authors: Luo S, Wen D, Zhang J, Liu Z, Lu J, Deng J, Zeng H, Lou S, Li Y, Lv L.
papers.abstract: Background YTHDC1 is a nuclear N6-methyladenosine reader involved in RNA processing. Its abundance, cellular distribution, and relationship with the immune microenvironment in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain incompletely characterized. Methods We integrated paired tumor-adjacent transcriptomic and proteomic cohorts, three single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets containing 249,080 quality-controlled cells, four outcome cohorts, three immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) cohorts, paired clinical specimens, and cell-based YTHDC1-knockdown assays. Patient-level analyses covered hepatocyte programs, immune states, expression-supported ligand-receptor axes, survival, ICI response, and exploratory single-cell network perturbation. Results YTHDC1 protein abundance was higher in 160 paired CPTAC samples (Hedges' g = 1.21, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.01-1.42), whereas RNA effects varied across cohorts. Single-cell analysis localized YTHDC1 across hepatic and immune compartments and identified patient-level associations with hepatocyte, lymphoid, and myeloid programs. SPP1-CD44 received the strongest cross-cohort expression support among prespecified hepatocyte-to-myeloid axes. A transferred hepatocyte state showed a pooled tumor-adjacent effect of g = 0.42 (95% CI 0.04-0.80), and higher YTHDC1 abundance was associated with poorer overall survival in study-aware univariable models (hazard ratio 1.20, 95% CI 1.06-1.36). In 37 ICI-treated patients, the pooled responder-nonresponder effect for YTHDC1 was small ( g = 0.05, 95% CI -0.60 to 0.71). Exploratory virtual knockout showed modest cross-cohort agreement in network perturbation ranks. Paired clinical tissues supported increased YTHDC1 mRNA and protein abundance, and YTHDC1 silencing reduced proliferation-related readouts and THP-1 migration in two HCC cell lines. Conclusions YTHDC1 is increased at the protein level in HCC and is situated within identifiable hepatocyte and immune programs. Functional assays support its contribution to HCC cell proliferation and tumor cell-dependent macrophage-like cell migration under the tested conditions.

papers.title: Whole-Genome Sequencing and Single-Cell Transcriptomics Identify Human Leukocyte Antigen Loci and a COG5 Variant in Aortic Dissection.
papers.authors: Lin J, Wu S, Lin C, Jin S, Chen L, Luo J, Xu S, Jin L, Yu M, Zheng Y, Si Y.
papers.abstract: Background Aortic dissection (AD) is a lethal cardiovascular emergency with a complex and underexplored genetic basis. Methods We performed whole-genome sequencing on 151 patients with sporadic Stanford type B AD and 965 healthy controls in a Chinese population as a discovery phase analysis to assess both common and rare variants. Cross-ancestry meta-analyses incorporating 4 external genome-wide association data sets were used to identify population-specific risk loci. To pinpoint functional candidates, we integrated epigenomic profiles and single-cell transcriptomes from human aortic tissues. Results Whole-genome sequencing analysis identified 21 candidate common loci and 2 low-frequency variants associated with AD in this discovery cohort. Two candidate common variants in the human leukocyte antigen region (rs9260945 near HLA-A and rs9276409 within HLA-DQA2 ) showed strong associations and colocalized with regulatory elements in aortic and immune cells, indicating immune-mediated vascular pathology. A low-frequency missense variant in the COG5 gene (rs1203229795, effect allele frequency=0.019) emerged as an independent AD risk factor, likely affecting extracellular matrix glycosylation. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of AD-associated variants in human aortic tissues demonstrated enhanced interactions among fibroblasts, vascular smooth muscle cells, and macrophages, supporting their roles in AD pathogenesis. Integrated gene-based and expression analyses further highlighted TPM4 , a marker of vascular smooth muscle cell dedifferentiation, as a putative susceptibility gene in AD. Conclusions This multiomics investigation expands the genetic landscape of sporadic AD in Chinese individuals, revealing immune-related human leukocyte antigen loci and a functionally supported candidate COG5 variant. Our findings offer new insights into AD pathogenesis and identify candidate targets for future diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
papers.venue: Journal of the American Heart Association

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics elucidates trajectories associated with transformation in malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors.
papers.authors: Mirchia K, Bhattacharya A, Viken JK, Eilers G, Pan S, Zhu I, Zhang D, Siddika A, Monga V, Wustrack R, Na BS, Carmichael I, Phillips JJ, Jacques L, Perry A, Lucas CG, Pekmezci M, Vasudevan HN.
papers.abstract: Background Tumor invasion and malignant transformation are spatiotemporally coordinated processes that shape clinical behavior, diagnostic classification, and treatment response. Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNSTs) are aggressive tumors that can arise sporadically or in people with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF-1) yet how distinct spatial niches underlie MPNST intra-tumor heterogeneity, local invasion or malignant transformation from benign precursors are not fully understood. Methods We integrate spatial analysis of 50,896 transcriptomes from 15 human MPNSTs with deep learning image analysis to define the interplay between genetic alterations, the immune microenvironment, and epigenetic cell fate regulation in MPNST invasion and transformation. Results Spatial transcriptomics reveal distinct infiltrating immune cells and immunomodulatory spatial clusters in sporadic compared to NF-1 associated MPNSTs. Local invasion is marked by spatially defined immunomodulatory and dedifferentiation programs. Analysis of two NF-1 associated MPNSTs with contiguous morphologically defined neurofibroma and MPNST components demonstrates NF-1 associated tumors identified a similar malignant transformation process associated with dynamic immune infiltration, chromosome 9p loss, and dedifferentiation concomitant with increased cell proliferation. Finally, deep learning morphology encoders were trained on spatial transcriptomic data to predict spatial transcriptomic cluster identity and chromosome 9p loss from hematoxylin and eosin stained (H&E) images although the generalizability of such encoders remains a challenge. Conclusions Our data provide a spatial framework for peripheral nerve sheath tumor transformation although the limited sample size of the present cohort will require additional validation of the proposed model.

papers.title: Beyond Histocompatibility: Donor Tissue Immune States and Their Role in Heart Transplantation.
papers.authors: Urbanowicz T, Kowalewski M, Suwalski P, Raffa GM.
papers.abstract: Heart transplantation transfers not only donor alloantigens and functional myocardium but also a pre-existing tissue environment shaped by resident immune, vascular, stromal, and parenchymal populations. This review examines the hypothesis that the biological state of donor tissue influences subsequent recipient immunity and contributes to heterogeneity in allograft outcomes. Donor-resident macrophages, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, extracellular matrix, and tissue-resident lymphocytes constitute an immunologically active myocardial niche that encounters ischemia-reperfusion injury and recipient immune effectors immediately after implantation. Experimental and human studies demonstrate the dynamic coexistence and replacement of donor- and recipient-derived immune populations, with recipient cells acquiring phenotypes within the graft microenvironment. We distinguish transient donor-tissue activation from genuine tissue immune memory, which would require persistence of an exposure-induced molecular or functional state and an altered response to a subsequent challenge. Potential mechanisms include trained innate immunity, epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming, endothelial inflammatory memory, and persistent stromal-immune interactions. We propose that allograft biology be investigated at the level of the donor-recipient immune pair and outline longitudinal single-cell, spatial, and cell-of-origin approaches to test this concept in human heart transplantation.

papers.title: Intestinal T-cell migration: unraveling mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
papers.authors: Sun Y, Liu Y, Xie L, Zhu L, Peng W.
papers.abstract: Background Intestinal T-cell migration links mucosal immunity with systemic immune homeostasis and contributes to immune surveillance, barrier defense, and peripheral tissue inflammation. Advances in single-cell omics, spatial analysis, and intravital imaging are reshaping our understanding of its subset specificity and tissue selectivity. Aim of review This review summarizes the molecular mechanisms, microenvironmental regulation, pathological significance along the gut-organ axes, and related therapeutic strategies of intestinal T-cell migration, with a particular focus on how migratory imbalance contributes to intestinal and extraintestinal immune-mediated diseases. Key scientific concepts reviewed Intestinal T-cell migration is jointly driven by gut imprinting, S1P-S1PR-mediated egress, chemokine-guided trafficking, integrin-dependent adhesion, and cytoskeletal remodeling, and is further regulated by metabolic, epigenetic, and microbial signals. This process is highly dependent on T-cell subset and tissue context: it promotes effector T-cell recruitment and inflammatory amplification in inflammatory bowel disease, manifests as restricted antitumor T-cell infiltration in colorectal cancer, and may contribute to distant tissue injury through the gut-organ axes. Existing S1PR modulators, integrin antagonists, and chemokine-targeted strategies have demonstrated the therapeutic tractability of migratory pathways; however, pathway redundancy, tissue heterogeneity, and impairment of protective immunity continue to limit their application. Future strategies should move beyond broad suppression of migration toward subset-, tissue-, and disease stage-specific precision modulation, combined with microbiota-based interventions and biomarker-guided stratification to improve therapeutic efficacy.

papers.title: A Single-Cell Transcriptomic Map Reveals Platelet-Rich Plasma-Induced Endometrial Microenvironment Remodeling in Recurrent Implantation Failure.
papers.authors: Jiang Y, Jiang J, Zhang H, Liu J, Xing J, Huang C, Zhu Y, He F, Wang Z, Yan G, Jiang R.
papers.abstract: Intrauterine infusion of platelet-rich plasma shows clinical promise as a regenerative therapy for patients with repeated implantation failure, yet the precise cellular and molecular mechanisms governing its in vivo effects on the human endometrium remain poorly understood. To elucidate these mechanisms at high resolution, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing on paired endometrial biopsies collected from patients during the proliferative phase, both before and shortly after intrauterine platelet-rich plasma infusion. Our analysis reveals that platelet-rich plasma acts as a potent modulator of the endometrial microenvironment by inducing extensive transcriptional reprogramming within resident cell populations. Alongside the direct stimulatory effects of PRP on various cell lineages, stromal cells emerged as key mediators contributing to this regenerative response, suppressing developmental plasticity pathways while concomitantly upregulating functions crucial for tissue regeneration, including cytoskeletal remodeling, pro-angiogenic signaling, and immune modulation. These reprogrammed stromal cells are predicted to serve as functional hubs, potentially driving enhanced paracrine networks that support robust angiogenesis through endothelial cell expansion and promote a growth-favorable epithelial phenotype via secreted growth factors. Notably, platelet-rich plasma infusion also induced a marked expansion and activation of specific tissue-resident natural killer cell subsets, indicating a recalibration of the local immune landscape. This study highlights that platelet-rich plasma orchestrates a multifaceted regenerative program where direct cellular stimulation converges with reprogrammed stromal-driven paracrine signaling to facilitate vascularization, epithelial growth, and immunological recalibration in the endometrium.

papers.title: Metabolic reprogramming in cancer-associated fibroblasts: orchestrating the tumor immune microenvironment and response to immune checkpoint blockade.
papers.authors: Gan L, Liu Z, Cao L, Meng X, Liu X, Wang X, He Y.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has reshaped the therapeutic landscape of solid tumors. However, durable clinical benefit remains limited to a subset of patients because of primary or acquired resistance. Beyond tumor-intrinsic factors, the tumor microenvironment (TME) plays a critical role in shaping responsiveness to immunotherapy. As a major stromal component, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) contribute to immune suppression through dynamic metabolic reprogramming and modulate the spatial organization and functional state of immune cells. Recent advances in single-cell transcriptomics, spatial omics, and metabolomic profiling have provided new insights into the metabolic heterogeneity of CAF subsets and their interactions with immune cells. Metabolic reprogramming not only sustains CAF activation but also remodels the local immune environment through nutrient competition, metabolite accumulation, and coordination with extracellular matrix remodeling. These processes reinforce immunosuppression within the TME and contribute to resistance to ICB. This review integrates emerging multi-omics insights into CAF metabolic heterogeneity, summarizes how metabolic reprogramming shapes tumor immunity, and discusses therapeutic strategies targeting CAF metabolism to enhance immunotherapy efficacy, together with the major challenges facing clinical translation.

papers.title: CD8⁺ T Cell infiltration and spatial organization in cancer: mechanisms, barriers, and therapeutic strategies.
papers.authors: Milian L, Geindreau M, Pignol C, Vegran F.
papers.abstract: The infiltration of tumors by CD8⁺ T lymphocytes is a critical determinant of antitumor immunity and response to immunotherapy. However, the presence of tumor-specific CD8⁺ T cells does not necessarily translate into effective tumor control, as multiple biological barriers can prevent their recruitment, spatial distribution, persistence, and functional activity. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the multistep mechanisms regulating CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, from immune priming and systemic trafficking to vascular entry, intratumoral migration, and tissue residency. We discuss how alterations in chemokine networks, dysfunctional tumor vasculature, extracellular matrix remodeling, stromal barriers, and immunosuppressive signals collectively drive immune exclusion and resistance to therapy. Unlike previous reviews that have focused on individual aspects of T-cell trafficking, tumor immune contexture, or immune exclusion, we integrate these interconnected mechanisms as successive biological checkpoints and link them to therapeutic strategies aimed at overcoming specific barriers. These include restoration of antigen presentation and dendritic cell function, reprogramming of chemokine pathways, vascular normalization, stromal remodeling, innate immune activation, and induction of tertiary lymphoid structures. This integrated framework highlights why increasing CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration alone may be insufficient and supports the development of rational, sequential, and spatially guided combination strategies. Advances in spatial transcriptomics, single-cell technologies, and multiplex imaging are expected to enable personalized identification of dominant immune barriers and rational design of combination therapies. Ultimately, the goal is shifting from simply activating T cells toward engineering tumor ecosystems that support sustained CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, organization, and effector function.

papers.title: Genetic Susceptibility in Dry Eye Disease: Immunogenetic Evidence, Current Limitations, and Future Directions.
papers.authors: Capobianco M, Zeppieri M, Cappellani F, Gagliano C, Consoli RA, Mangiagli S, Roszkowska AM.
papers.abstract: Dry eye disease is a multifactorial disorder which is heterogeneous in nature, caused by interactions among ocular surface abnormalities, systemic diseases, environmental factors and host susceptibility. The inherited variation related to the pathophysiology of dry eye disease is not very well characterized, but known mechanisms include inflammation, tear film instability, neurosensory dysfunction and lacrimal and meibomian gland changes. Studies exploring the contribution of genetics suggest that dry eye disease (DED) and specific ocular surface endophenotypes are heritable. Candidate-gene and human leukocyte antigen association studies have reinforced contributions from pathways associated with innate and adaptive immunity, inflammatory regulation and neural function, and glandular homeostasis, but many associations require replication in larger, more diverse populations. Genome-wide association studies and biobank-based assessments have recently begun to shed light on the polygenic architecture of Dry Eye Disease (DED) and its genetic overlap with other related conditions worldwide. This paper evaluates critically the current evidence on DED heritability, candidate susceptibility genes, HLA associations, genome-wide signals, polygenic risk models and genetic pleiotropy. It will cover how transcriptomic, epigenomic, and single-cell approaches can link inherited susceptibility loci to disease-relevant cell states and molecular pathways across the ocular surface unit, including the cornea, conjunctiva, lacrimal gland, and meibomian glands. The study would stress phenotypic heterogeneity, ancestry-related limitations, and inconsistent diagnostic definitions. In the end, we will evaluate opportunities and existing constraints in the incorporation of genomic information with clinical endophenotypes and environmental exposures to support risk stratification, biomarker discovery, identification of therapeutic targets, and the development of future ocular surface precision medicine.

papers.title: Point-Process Modelling of Cell-Type Interaction Structure in CosMx Glioma Data for Hypothesis-Driven Tumor Inference from scRNA-seq
papers.authors: Carcanholo, F. P.; Cassiano, M. H. A.; Panepucci, E. M.; Laurini, M. P.; Malta, T. M.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits marked spatial heterogeneity that is lost after tissue dissociation for single-cell RNA sequencing. Here, we developed a spatial-statistical framework to characterize tumor-microenvironment organization and derive molecularly predictable spatial phenotypes from CosMx data. Eight GBM specimens comprising 2,427,362 cells, 15 cell populations, and four malignant states were analyzed, revealing substantial inter-patient differences in cellular composition and density. Fine finite-element meshes best preserved continuous spatial intensity and supported whole-tissue Log-Gaussian Cox Process modelling. Immune populations, including macrophages, microglia, monocytes, cDCs, neutrophils, and T cells, showed spatial attraction toward malignant states. These models generated cell-level measures of conditional intensity and tumor-proximity probability. Transcript abundances and metabolic pathway scores served as the sole predictive features to model these spatial phenotypes. Transcriptomic representations outperformed metabolic pathway scores. Leave-one-patient-out validation reduced predictive performance, and patient-wise harmonization failed to restore cross-patient transportability. Spatial outcome distributions varied between specimens, indicating that molecular-spatial relationships are strongly conditioned by patient-specific tumor architecture. Predicted interaction scores stratified transcriptional subclusters within cell types in external non-spatial single-cell datasets. This framework links spatial point-process phenotypes to molecular states and provides a basis for inferring spatial context from non-spatial single-cell data. Generalizing these models requires larger and more diverse spatial cohorts.

papers.title: Restoration of deficient IL-15 signaling enhances innate lymphoid cell immunity in brain metastasis
papers.authors: McMullen, T. P.; Naef, P.; Zagni, E.; Tian, L.; Zhao, E.; Wechter, N.; Longworth, A. J.; Adam, I.; Insua-Rodriguez, J.; Savage, H.; Hur, I.; Garcia, S. A.; Ma, D.; Liew, M. H.; Mallya, S.; Kessenbrock, K.; O'Sullivan, T. E.; Mohyeldin, A.; Yu, J.; Lawson, D. A.
papers.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells and type 1 innate lymphoid cells (ILC1s), collectively known as group 1 innate lymphoid cells (ILCs), are critical mediators of anti-tumor immunity, yet their role in brain metastasis remains poorly defined. Using single-cell RNA sequencing and functional depletion models, we show that group 1 ILCs fail to provide adequate tumor control in breast cancer brain metastasis (BCBM). In contrast to the liver, where diverse, functionally competent group 1 ILC populations facilitate excellent metastatic control, group 1 ILCs in BCBM show limited diversity and profound tissue-specific dysfunction such that their depletion had no effect on tumor burden despite modest parenchymal infiltration. We attribute this group 1 ILC dysfunction to severely restricted IL-15 availability, with IL-15R protein detected at 500-fold lower concentration in the brain than in the liver. Local IL-15 complex administration restored group 1 ILC accumulation, cytotoxicity, and tissue residency, significantly reducing brain metastatic burden independent of T cells. Intracranial delivery of IL-15-secreting induced pluripotent stem-cell-derived (iPSC)-NK cells, already in clinical testing for non-small cell lung cancer, significantly reduced tumor burden. Collectively, these findings reveal how tissue-specific differences in cytokine availability shape group 1 ILC population diversity and disease response, establishing localized IL-15 signaling as a compelling strategy to unlock innate immunity against intracranial malignancies.

papers.title: Deciphering the mechanisms of resveratrol in knee osteoarthritis treatment: insights from bioinformatics and experimental validation.
papers.authors: Huang C, Ye X, Liu X, Liu F, Li Y, Chen X, Hao P, San X.
papers.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is the most prevalent chronic joint disorder in orthopedics, with its underlying pathogenic genes and effective treatment methods remaining unclear. Resveratrol (RES), a potent bioactive natural polyphenol, has been shown to effectively alleviate KOA; however, its complex regulatory mechanisms require further investigation. This research seeks to clarify the molecular mechanisms by which RES contributes to the treatment of KOA, utilizing a blend of bioinformatics approaches and experimental validation. First, gene expression profiles related to KOA were obtained from the GEO database. Subsequently, differential gene analysis was conducted on the samples, and modular genes linked to KOA were extracted through the application of a weighted gene co-expression network. The LASSO algorithm was utilized to identify crucial pathogenic genes in KOA, which were later confirmed using clinical samples. Targets for RES were sourced from traditional Chinese medicine databases, and the therapeutic targets for KOA treatment were determined by finding the intersection of these sources. An enrichment analysis was carried out based on the therapeutic targets identified. Molecular docking studies were conducted to further assess the binding affinity of key therapeutic genes with RES. Lastly, animal experiments were implemented to substantiate the molecular mechanisms by which RES acts in the treatment of KOA. We identified 460 module genes and 10 key predictive genes through LASSO analysis. The findings from the enrichment analysis concerning potential therapeutic targets for RES in the treatment of KOA reveal that the significant genes implicated include VEGFA, IL6, MAPK3, IL1B, CASP3, and AKT1. Subsequent validation with clinical samples revealed that IL6, MAPK3, IL1B, CASP3, and AKT1 were significantly elevated during the progression of KOA, while VEGFA was markedly reduced in the context of KOA. The outcomes of the GO and KEGG analyses suggest that the primary biological processes implicated encompass apoptosis, the FoxO signaling pathway, the IL-17 signaling pathway, cellular senescence, and the NF-κB signaling pathway. The findings from the immune infiltration analysis indicate that resting CD4 memory T cells, memory B cells, resting mast cells, eosinophils, and activated mast cells may have important functions in the immune mechanisms related to KOA. The results of animal experiments demonstrate that RES effectively inhibits the expression of inflammatory factors such as IL-6, MAPK3, IL-1β, CASP3, and AKT1 during the progression of KOA, promotes the expression of VEGFA, and concurrently suppresses the FoxO signaling pathway and the IL-17 signaling pathway, thereby reducing cartilage damage induced by MIA and delaying the progression of KOA. In summary, RES can regulate the expression of genes including VEGFA, IL-6, MAPK3, IL-1β, CASP3, and AKT1, inhibit the FoxO signaling pathway and the IL-17 signaling pathway, alleviate cartilage damage induced by MIA, and delay the progression of KOA.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis and explainable machine learning reveal the potential mechanisms of acupuncture in Crohn's disease.
papers.authors: Mo L, Zhou Y, Wu Y, Wei LF, Cai SY, Sun YM, Tang LS, Yuan JY.
papers.abstract: Background Acupuncture has shown clinical benefits in Crohn's disease (CD), but the molecular links between acupuncture-responsive endogenous mediators and CD-related targets remain unclear. Methods We integrated literature-derived acupuncture-responsive endogenous mediators with transcriptomic data from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). Differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were used to identify CD-associated signature genes, which were intersected with predicted mediator targets. Eight machine-learning algorithms with repeated nested cross-validation and independent external validation were used to prioritize candidate targets, followed by SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interpretation. Immune-cell composition was estimated using Cell-type Identification by Estimating Relative Subsets of RNA Transcripts (CIBERSORT), and molecular docking was performed between the prioritized target and acupuncture-responsive endogenous mediators. Results Ten acupuncture-responsive endogenous mediators and six shared candidate targets were identified. Random forest (RF) achieved the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) in repeated nested cross-validation (0.905 ± 0.008), whereas gradient boosting machine (GBM) showed the highest AUC in the independent validation cohort, with an AUC of 0.789 and a 95% confidence interval (CI) of 0.652-0.925. FER ranked among the top three features in all eight models and showed the highest mean absolute SHAP value (0.267). FER expression was positively correlated with neutrophil abundance (ρ=0.268, P Conclusion FER emerged as the prioritized target and was associated with neutrophil and M2 macrophage abundance. The predicted structural compatibility between corticosterone and the FER SH2 domain provides a testable hypothesis for future studies of acupuncture-responsive endogenous mediators in CD.

papers.title: Transcription factor CTCF activates KIAA1199 expression to inhibit ferroptosis and promote malignant behaviors in colorectal cancer based on bioinformatics and machine learning.
papers.authors: Fan X, Meng L, Zheng S, He X.
papers.abstract: Objectives Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a common malignancy of the colon and rectum, but its molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Methods Gene expression omnibus (GEO) database was used to download CRC-related datasets. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), support vector machine (SVM), and random forest (RF) were used to identify key CRC genes. Cell type identification by estimating relative subsets of rna transcripts (CIBERSORT) was used for immune infiltration analysis. Tumor immune estimation resource (TIMER) database was used to assess gene expression across multiple cancers. Human transcription factor target database (hTFtarget) was used to predict regulatory relationships between genes and transcription factors. Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP), dual-luciferase assay, cell transfection, western blot (WB), and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) were used to detect protein-gene binding, transcriptional activity, gene knockdown and overexpression, protein expression, and mRNA expression. JASPAR database was used to identify transcription factor binding sites. Cells were treated with a BODIPY 581/591 C11 kit to assess intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels. The assay kits were employed to determine the levels of ferrous iron (Fe 2+ ), malondialdehyde (MDA), and superoxide dismutase (SOD). Cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8) was performed to measure cell viability. Results Matrix metallopeptidase 7 (MMP7), KIAA1199, and cadherin 3 (CDH3) were identified as potential key CRC genes. Their expression correlated with altered immune cell infiltration patterns. KIAA1199 showed the highest upregulation in CRC tissues. CCCTC-binding factor (CTCF) transcriptionally activated KIAA1199. Knockdown of CTCF decreased the expression of solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11) and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), while increasing ROS, Fe 2+ , and MDA, and decreasing SOD levels. CTCF knockdown combined with KIAA1199 overexpression partially rescued these effects, modulating ferroptosis-related oxidative stress in CRC cells. Conclusion CTCF transcriptionally activates KIAA1199 and regulates ferroptosis-related oxidative stress in CRC cells, providing new insights into the molecular mechanisms of CRC.

papers.title: Catching enhanced flexibility in antibody-antigen recognition: critical evaluation of physics-based and AI-driven methods.
papers.authors: Xu H, Mi R, Bai G, Kang Y, Sun C, Wang Y, Chen C, Ma B.
papers.abstract: Protein conformational dynamics often govern protein-protein interaction mechanisms and function, as flexibility enables adaptation to different environments. Yet, the extent to which current physics‑based and emerging AI‑driven methods can predict flexibility‑dependent physicochemical properties remains to be determined. Here, we studied the HyHEL10 (Hy10) antibody lineage binding to lysozymes with different conformational flexibility. Contrary to traditional models, the affinity-matured Hy10 4X antibody achieves high affinity by actively destabilizing its CDRH1 loop, enabling the capture of mobile antigen variants via entropy-buffered conformational selection. This structural plasticity presents a significant challenge to standard computational protocols. We found that the polarization effect is enhanced with increasing protein flexibility. Our benchmarking of MM/PBSA and AI-driven structure predictors reveals that both approaches initially fail to accurately rank affinities in more flexible systems, primarily due to sampling limitations and inaccurate structure prediction. However, the inclusion of structural templates in Chai-1 effectively mitigated these limitations, leading to enhanced correlation with experimental affinities. In the future, by coupling AI's quick screening with robust physics-based evaluations, we may have a potential pathway for in silico engineering of therapeutic antibodies against the most elusive, shapeshifting targets in the proteome.

papers.title: Advances in genetically engineered and humanized mouse models for dissecting sepsis mechanisms and therapeutic response.
papers.authors: Abbas B, Abbas A, Khan IN, Nazeer S.
papers.abstract: Sepsis remains a major cause of global mortality, yet translation from preclinical studies to effective targeted therapies has been limited. A key barrier is that conventional animal models incompletely capture human immune circuitry and patient heterogeneity. Recent progress in mouse genetics, CRISPR/Cas-based genome editing, conditional alleles (Cre-loxP), and next-generation humanized platforms has expanded the toolkit for functional interrogation of host pathways that shape sepsis outcomes. Germline and cell-type-restricted perturbations have helped map roles for pattern-recognition signaling, inflammasome modules, cell-death effectors, and immune checkpoints, while also showing that the same pathway can produce different phenotypes depending on cellular context. Cross-species differences in innate immune gene networks and caspase biology motivate validation in humanized systems and integration with human genetic evidence. Emerging "wildling" and genetically diverse panels provide complementary approaches to model environmental exposure and host variation. Coupling these platforms with single-cell multi-omics and endotype stratification can link genotype-to-phenotype mechanisms with biomarker-informed therapeutic testing.

papers.title: A mature tertiary lymphoid structure-associated spatial niche is inversely associated with ACC1-related lipid metabolism in neoadjuvant-treated hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.authors: Wang R, Shen B, Wu Y, Zhao S, Xu W, Liu W, Wang J.
papers.abstract: Tumor heterogeneity in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is shaped by spatially organized immune and metabolic ecosystems that may influence therapeutic response. However, how mature tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) niches relate to tumor metabolic heterogeneity remains poorly defined. We integrated seven 10x Visium sections from patients with locally advanced HCC treated with neoadjuvant cabozantinib plus nivolumab, a single-cell reference atlas, three independent bulk cohorts, and a pathological validation cohort of 69 HCC specimens. Reference-based deconvolution and neighborhood-composition clustering identified eleven recurrent multicellular niches, including a B-cell-, plasma-cell-, and T-cell-enriched mature TLS-associated niche (Niche5). Niche5 showed greater spatial aggregation in pathological responders, accompanied by stronger CCL21-CCR7, CXCL13-CXCR5, and CCL19-CCR7 signaling. Within Niche5, fatty-acid metabolism was inversely correlated with the TLS program (Spearman r=-0.35) and chemokine-ligand expression. A six-gene Niche5-derived signature selected using a machine-learning framework stratified overall survival across three independent cohorts. Among fatty-acid-metabolism enzymes, ACACA, encoding ACC1, showed the most reproducible negative association with TLS chemokines, antigen presentation, CD8-positive T-cell programs, and survival. Multiplex immunofluorescence and immunohistochemistry confirmed mature TLS architecture and demonstrated spatial separation between TLS and ACC1-, FABP5-, and PLIN2-enriched tumor compartments. In the validation cohort, TLS-positive tumors showed lower ACC1, FABP5, and PLIN2 expression but higher CCL21, CXCL13, and CCR7 expression, while high ACC1 expression was independently associated with reduced TLS positivity. Together, these findings provide exploratory evidence of immune-metabolic spatial heterogeneity in HCC and identify an inverse, associative relationship between mature TLS organization and ACC1-related lipid metabolism.

papers.title: A surviving beta cell subpopulation enriched in patients with T1D
papers.authors: Spurrell, M.; Tobiasova, Z.; Pober, J. S.; Tsang, J.; Herold, K. C.
papers.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is characterized by the autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells. While most beta cells are lost, a subset of beta cells persists years and even decades after disease onset. Studying these surviving cells is challenging, and thus how they escape immune killing remains poorly understood. Here, we applied a gene regulatory network inference-based clustering approach on existing islet scRNAseq data from cadaveric donors with T1D, autoantibody positive donors at risk for T1D, and non-diabetic donors to analyze beta cells from patients with established T1D. This approach identified a novel beta cell subtype enriched in T1D donors defined by the activity of several transcription factors which have well-characterized roles in beta cell survival, most notably IRF1. We found increased expression of immunomodulatory genes (e.g. SOCS1/3, HLA-E) as well as decreased expression of autoantigens and secretory genes, suggesting loss of cellular identity. We identified inflammatory cytokines as a driver of this phenotype by reanalyzing public data from primary human beta cells stimulated with inflammatory cytokines in vitro. We find a similar transcriptional program active in a subset of alpha cells, consistent with cell-extrinsic inflammatory cytokine signaling in vivo. We additionally use immunofluorescence to validate these findings. Overall, this study defines the features of surviving beta cells in patients with T1D, revealing several genes and pathways active in these cells as potential targets for T1D prevention and reversal.

papers.title: Research progress on the mechanism and clinical significance of immunoediting in the malignant transformation of oral leukoplakia.
papers.authors: Wang J, Ma Y, Ren J, Wang R, Wang Y, Yang M, Jia Y, Chai J, Xing W, Wang Y, Zhang F.
papers.abstract: The insidious malignant transformation of oral leukoplakia (OLK) into oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) represents a critical clinical bottleneck in head and neck oncology. Grounded in the cancer immunoediting theory of "elimination-equilibrium-escape," this review systematically reconstructs the spatiotemporal continuum of OLK transitioning toward malignant conversion. We comprehensively dissect the localized immunosuppressive network centered on T cell exhaustion, Natural killer cell inactivation, M2 macrophage polarization, antigen-presenting cell defects, and the dual roles of fibroblasts, elucidating the interactive mechanisms that drive mucosal barrier collapse and immune escape. Accordingly, this paper focuses on the translational pathways of leveraging multimodal deep learning algorithms and big data oncology to integrate heterogeneous omics data, thereby constructing chairside precision decision-making systems. This review ultimately aims to offer a new perspective on the clinical management of oral premalignant lesions, rendering the transition from traditional "reactive surveillance" to algorithm-driven "precision cancer interception" clinically feasible.

papers.title: Identification and In Vitro Validation of Metabolic Reprogramming-Related Hub Genes for the Diagnosis of Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
papers.authors: Xue J, Zhang Z, Wei W, Zhang A, Zhou X, Wu Q, Chen S, Deng J, Zhang X.
papers.abstract: Background: Metabolic reprogramming plays a vital role in subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). This study aims to identify biomarkers related to metabolic reprogramming in SAH. Methods: Transcriptome datasets (GSE36791 and GSE73378) were downloaded from the GEO database, and the metabolic reprogramming-related genes were retrieved from the Molecular Signatures Database. Candidate genes were identified by intersecting differentially expressed genes, WGCNA module genes, and metabolic genes. Hub genes were screened via CytoHubba, machine learning, and Mendelian randomization. ROC curves were generated to evaluate the diagnostic performance of the hub genes. Additionally, functional enrichment analysis, circulating immune-cell composition analysis, and drug prediction were performed. A cellular SAH model (U251 cells) and clinical samples were used for RT-qPCR validation. Results: Three hub genes (IMPDH2, RPL4, and HSPA1A) were identified to develop a nomogram model, which showed good diagnostic value (AUC = 0.850) in the training dataset GSE36791. Functional analyses revealed that hub genes were involved in multiple processes, including ribosome biosynthesis, purine metabolism, and immune regulation. Circulating immune-cell composition analysis showed that neutrophils were significantly enriched in SAH patients. Molecular docking suggested favorable binding affinities of mycophenolate-IMPDH2, ataluren-RPL4, and carbamazepine-HSPA1A. In clinical samples (eight SAH patients and eight controls), IMPDH2 and RPL4 were downregulated, whereas HSPA1A was upregulated. In the cellular SAH model, IMPDH2 and HSPA1A showed expression trends consistent with the clinical samples, whereas RPL4 did not show a statistically significant difference. Conclusions: These findings suggest that IMPDH2, RPL4, and HSPA1A may serve as potential diagnostic biomarkers for SAH and as candidate genes for further investigation.

papers.title: A single-cell profile of the porcine immune repertoire: concurrent profiling of T cell receptor and B cell receptor V(D)J sequences in health.
papers.authors: Zhang H, Zhang Q, Zhang H, Wang P, Geng R, Pan R, Li C, Shi F, Liu J, Wu Y, Cao Y.
papers.abstract: Adaptive immune diversity is shaped by the complex organization of T cell receptor (TCR) and B cell receptor (BCR) repertoires across tissues. However, a systematic cross-tissue immune repertoire profiling in healthy pigs is still lacking. In this study, we used 3 14-day-old Duroc × Landrace × Yorkshire (DLY) crossbred piglets, all of which were male. After sample purification, a total of 71,731 cells were retained. We established single-cell profiling integrating paired BCR and TCR repertoires across 11 immune-associated tissues using single-cell RNA sequencing combined with V(D)J sequencing based on DLY crossbred piglets. Diverse populations of immune cells were identified, with significant tissue-specific heterogeneity being revealed in lymphatic, mucosal, and circulatory organs. Immune repertoire analysis demonstrated biased V(D)J gene usage, conserved complementarity-determining region 3 (CDR3) length distributions, preferential receptor pairing patterns, and extensive clonotype diversity. Cross-tissue analyses further revealed coordinated clonotype sharing and distinct clonal expansion patterns among immune cell subsets. In addition, using the Pig-specific V(D)J primers we designed, the sequencing results have achieved a modest improvement in the detection of immunoglobulin alleles compared to previous studies. It is expected to provide a more reliable technical solution for related research. Collectively, this work provides a comprehensive reference profiling of the healthy DLY crossbred piglet adaptive immune system and offers valuable resources for future studies of porcine immunology, infectious diseases, and vaccine responses.

papers.title: TCR clonotyping of paired blood and tonsillar T-follicular cells reveals the mixed origin of CD38 high Tfrs.
papers.authors: Sokolova SR, Grigoriants VA, Shagina IA, Barsova EV, Nomerovskaya MA, Khalifaeva JZ, Gurov AV, Britanova OV, Zvyagin IV, Chudakov DM, Grigorova IL.
papers.abstract: Circulating T follicular regulatory (cTfr) cells are measured as blood biomarkers after vaccination, in autoimmune disease (e.g., lupus, rheumatoid arthritis) and cancer immunotherapy, yet whether they originate from natural Tregs (yielding nTfr) or germinal center T follicular helper (GC Tfh) cells (yielding iTfr) remains unknown. This distinction is critical for interpreting cTfr expansion as Treg-derived regulation versus Tfh-derived negative feedback. To characterize tonsillar follicular T cell heterogeneity and resolve the origins of cTfr cells we applied single-cell multiomics and bulk T cell receptor sequencing (TCRβ-seq) analysis of matched human tonsil and blood. Tonsillar nTfr and iTfr cells distribute across shared transcriptional states, with CD38 expression distinguishing iTfr from nTfr in most contexts. However, within a transitional cluster positioned between activated Tfh and Tfr cells, nTfr-like cells also upregulated CD38, indicating that its specificity for iTfr is not absolute. Peripheral blood CD38 - cTfr cells shared clonotypes exclusively with non-follicular Tregs and lacked overlap with GC Tfh, indicating predominantly Treg origin. CD38 high cTfr cells captured a mixed population: some shared clonotypes with tonsillar GC Tfh (iTfr), while others shared clonotypes with non-follicular Tregs (nTfr). These findings establish that accurate discrimination of iTfr versus nTfr within the CD38 high compartment requires TCR clonal reference to matched tissue.

papers.title: Single-Cell BCR and Transcriptome Analysis Revealed Potent Neutralizing Antibodies in Response to HAdV-4 Infection.
papers.authors: Yu T, Ye X, Zhu Z, Zhang W, Yang Y, Wang J, Lv P, Chi X, Zhang G, Chen Z, Dong Y.
papers.abstract: Human adenovirus type 4 (HAdV-4) is a predominant serotype causing acute respiratory infections, for which no antibody drugs have been clinically approved to date, resulting in an urgent unmet medical need. This study aimed to identify highly potent neutralizing antibodies by dissecting the B cell immune response after infection, thereby laying a foundation for vaccine design and antiviral therapy. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were isolated from a convalescent patient who exhibited the most robust neutralizing antibody titers among 16 HAdV-4 convalescent volunteers. A total of 2710 B cells were isolated from the peripheral blood of this patient, and the characteristics of B cell subsets and B cell receptor (BCR) repertoires were comprehensively analyzed by integrating scRNA-seq and scVDJ-seq technologies. Candidate antibodies were subsequently selected for a series of functional and mechanistic validations based on the characteristics of BCRs and origination. Transcriptomic profiling classified memory B cells into three functionally heterogeneous subpopulations designated as MB sub1, sub2 and sub3. Combined with the characteristics of BCR, 92 selected antibodies from sub2 and sub3 were synthesized for further functional validation. Three potent neutralizing antibodies were successfully identified, among which 1QH7 demonstrated potentially potent virus neutralization capability in vitro and conferred robust in vivo protection in the Stat1 -deficient mouse model. We further employed AlphaFold 3 to predict the complex structure of 1QH7 with the HAdV-4 Hexon protein and validated the key binding residues through site-directed mutagenesis. Additionally, the study elucidated the viral neutralization mechanism mediated by TRIM21. We established an efficient antibody screening strategy based on integration of scRNA-seq and scVDJ-seq and isolated a potent neutralizing antibody, 1QH7. This study lays a solid foundation for the rapid pathogen-bait-free, cell subset-guided screening antibody route for novel emerging infectious disease outbreaks.

papers.title: A single-cell profile of the porcine immune repertoire: concurrent profiling of T cell receptor and B cell receptor V(D)J sequences in health
papers.authors: Zhang H, Zhang Q, Zhang H, Wang P, Geng R, Pan R, Li C, Shi F, Liu J, Wu Y, Cao Y.

figure.label: Fig. 1
figure.caption: Overview of the experimental design and construction. Immune-associated tissues from healthy 14-day-old pigs were collected and used for sequencing. Comprehensive immune repertoire analyses were performed to investigate V(D)J gene usage, CDR3 length distributions, receptor pairing patterns, and so on. By integrating immune repertoire information with single-cell transcriptomic profiles, the relationships between clonotype dynamics, immune cell differences, and tissue distribution were further explored. The use of pig-specific V(D)J primers enabled improved detection sensitivity and broader immunoglobulin allele coverage. This study provided a valuable reference resource for porcine immunology, infectious disease, and vaccine research

papers.title: Study on tumor ecology and precision medicine strategy of oral squamous cell carcinoma based on multi-omics cell atlas.
papers.authors: Meng Q, Huo D, Xu F, Liu N, Fan M, Wu Y, Chen X.
papers.abstract: Introduction Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is characterized by inter- and intratumoral heterogeneity, which complicates patient stratification and treatment. Although single-cell studies have improved the resolution of the OSCC microenvironment, the relationships among cellular states, spatial organization, immune-repertoire dynamics, and patient-level ecosystem patterns remain incompletely understood. Methods We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, single-cell T-cell receptor sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and bulk RNA-sequencing data to characterize OSCC. Results We constructed a multi-omics cellular atlas comprising 88,442 cells and 63 cell subclusters, revealing complementary malignant-cell heterogeneity at the levels of transcriptional subclusters and recurrent meta-programs. Spatial and cell-cell communication analysis identified a reproducible association between PI3+ cancer-associated fibroblasts and APC_Myeloid cells and supported a candidate collagen-associated communication axis within tumor niches. Integration of paired transcriptomic and TCR data delineated a CD8+ T-cell pseudotime continuum accompanied by increasing clonal expansion and exhaustion-associated features, with spatial analysis linking intermediate trajectory states to regulatory T-cell and inflammatory NKT-cell-rich tumor-front regions. Extending the single-cell atlas to bulk cohorts by deconvolution, we defined four OSCC ecotypes and four coordinated cell programs that captured patient-level ecosystem organization and showed distinct molecular and clinical associations. We developed exploratory models for prognosis, recurrence, and immunotherapy sensitivity and established the OSCC Atlas as an online resource for data exploration. Discussion This integrative framework links cellular heterogeneity, spatial organization, immune dynamics, and patient-level ecology, providing testable hypotheses for the biological and clinical stratification of OSCC.

papers.title: Association of donor single-cell cytokine secretion & circulating cytokine levels with the development & trajectory of severe primary graft dysfunction in lung transplantation.
papers.authors: Goel D, Shen CH, Liu Y, Howard LE, Tejan-Sie K, Brady JC, Krynychka K, Hughes B, Hartwig M, Snyder LD, Nixon AB.
papers.abstract: Whether donor immune biology at procurement is associated with primary graft dysfunction (PGD) trajectory is unknown. Pre-transplant donor T-cell function and circulating plasma proteins were profiled to address this gap. Twenty-one recipients were classified as no PGD (NOGD, n=7), recovery after initial PGD3 (RECV, n=5), or sustained PGD3 (SGD, n=9). The polyfunctionality of T-cells isolated from donor peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) after stimulation and plasma levels of 92 proteins were assessed. CD8+ polyfunctionality strength index (PSI) was lowest in RECV (p=0.019), driven by effector and chemoattractive clusters. CD4+ did not differ. SGD showed higher secretion of several proinflammatory mediators, while NOGD had higher TGF-β1 secretion and circulating CD27, and lower IFN-γ. SGD had the lowest circulating HGF and PDGF-B, while RECV had higher PDCD1, IL-33, HGF, and LAMP3. Donor T-cell polyfunctionality and circulating biomarkers correlated with PGD3 trajectory, with RECV associated with an exhausted and anti-inflammatory donor phenotype.
papers.venue: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

papers.title: Single-cell analyses of global cohorts outline determinants of immune aging and link the ratio of GZMK + to GZMB + Tem cells to health trajectories.
papers.authors: Terekhova M, Kleverov M, Francis T, Usoltsev D, Bohacova P, Arthur L, Tsurinov P, Kleverov D, Trinity L, Husarcikova K, Molotkov I, Grabauskas T, Fathi A, Milbourn E, Newton E, Siegel L, Ghanchi A, Tse U, Pollock RD, Duggal NA, Lord JM, Lazarus NR, Ellebedy AH, Ucar D, Harridge SDR, Artomov M, Artyomov MN.
papers.abstract: Human immune aging is heterogeneous, with immune responses becoming increasingly variable over the lifespan. Here, we integrated seven large-scale public single-cell peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) datasets and a newly generated cohort, encompassing 2,609 ostensibly healthy individuals across diverse ages, ancestries, and biological sexes. We identified both conserved and cohort-associated age-associated remodeling across 59 immune populations, together with sex- and ancestry-dependent immune differences. CD8 + T cells emerged as major drivers of aging heterogeneity, with the GZMK + /GZMB + effector memory ratio distinguishing healthy and pathology-associated aging trajectories. This ratio reflected immune remodeling driven by chronic viral exposure, including CMV, and disease-associated immune dysregulation, with the dominant driver varying across populations. Proteomic profiling across four cohorts revealed a Tem GZMB + plasma signature associated with inflammaging, poor self-reported health, all-cause mortality, and increased risk of immune-related, metabolic, and cardiovascular diseases. Together, these findings define clinically relevant immune determinants for monitoring and guiding healthy aging interventions.

papers.title: Repeated malaria exposure reprograms Vδ2+ γδT cell chromatin accessibility and immune function toward a reversible hyporesponsive state
papers.authors: Press, K. D.; Maran, M. I. J.; Ashkar-Masarwa, A.; Camanag, K.; Chen, D.; Shokoohi, V.; Kathiria, A.; Ty, M.; Nideffer, J.; Rek, J.; Nankabirwa, J.; Nankya, F.; Schulze-Hentrich, J.; Ssewanyana, I.; Kamya, M.; Boyle, M.; Greenhouse, B.; Dorsey, G.; Feeney, M.; Greenleaf, W.; Klemm, S.; Muller, F.; Jagannathan, P.
papers.abstract: V{delta}2+ {gamma}{delta} T cells contribute to antimalarial immunity via pro-inflammatory and cytotoxic mechanisms. Among children who have experienced repeated episodes of malaria, V{delta}2+ T cells develop reduced pro-inflammatory function through mechanisms that remain unknown. We hypothesized that recurrent malaria drives coordinated epigenetic and transcriptional remodeling of these semi-innate cells. Using PBMC from Ugandan children in cohorts spanning high and low transmission (10 children) and longitudinally across a marked decline in transmission (20 children, 3 timepoints), we profiled the epigenome and transcriptome of V{delta}2+ T cells by paired bulk ATAC-seq and RNA-seq and by CITE-seq. Higher malaria exposure was associated with reduced V{delta}2+ T cell TNF and IFN{gamma} production and with thousands of differentially accessible chromatin regions. Immunoregulatory genes including LYN, PLCG2, and HAVCR2 (Tim-3) showed increased chromatin accessibility and/or expression at high exposure, whereas pro-inflammatory gene (IFNG, GZMK, IL7R) and AP-1 (JUN/FOS) motif accessibility were increased at low exposure; linkage of regulatory elements with target genes corroborated these associations. Single-cell transcriptional analysis identified a cytotoxic CD8+CD16+CD57+ V{delta}2+ T cell subset. In our in vitro model, repeated stimulation with malaria-infected red blood cells or the phosphoantigen HMBPP was similarly associated with reduced V{delta}2+ T cell degranulation and cytokine production. Diminished responsiveness was predominantly TCR-dependent, accompanied by heightened p38 signaling, and was partially reversed by rest induced by the tyrosine kinase inhibitor dasatinib. Together these data reveal how repeated malaria may reshape cellular immunity by reprogramming V{delta}2+ T cells toward a reversible, hyporesponsive state and highlight targets for therapeutically restoring their function.

papers.title: Single cell RNA-seq analysis identifies junctional adhesion molecule two positive endothelial cells aggravate osteoarthritis by mediating vascular permeability and macrophage adhesion.
papers.authors: Xing Y, Li C, Wang C, Zheng L, Sheng P.
papers.abstract: Background Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease characterized by chronic inflammation and progressive cartilage destruction. Endothelial cell (EC) dysfunction contributes to inflammatory amplification in OA through increased vascular permeability and immune cell recruitment. This study aimed to characterize EC heterogeneity in OA and investigate the role of junctional adhesion molecule 2 (JAM2)-positive ECs in vascular dysfunction and macrophage adhesion. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing data from the Gene Expression Omnibus database were analyzed to identify EC subpopulations in OA. JAM2 expression was validated in human OA synovium, meniscus, and subchondral bone using multiplex immunofluorescence staining. The effects of inflammatory cytokines, including TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, and TGF-β1, on JAM2 expression in ECs were evaluated by qRT-PCR and immunofluorescence. The functional effects of JAM2 blockade on EC migration, tube formation, endothelial permeability, and monocyte adhesion were assessed using in vitro assays. The therapeutic potential of JAM2 blockade was further evaluated in a destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM)-induced mouse model of OA. Results JAM2-positive ECs were enriched in pathways associated with cell adhesion and transendothelial migration. JAM2 expression was significantly increased in OA synovial tissue compared with controls. Among the inflammatory cytokines tested, TNF-α most strongly upregulated JAM2 expression in ECs. TNF-α stimulation impaired EC migration and tube formation, increased endothelial permeability, and enhanced monocyte adhesion, whereas JAM2 blockade partially attenuated these effects in vitro . In the DMM-induced OA model, JAM2 expression was increased in the vascular compartments of the synovium, meniscus, and subchondral bone, while JAM2 blockade attenuated cartilage degeneration and modulated macrophage infiltration. Conclusion JAM2-positive ECs contribute to OA progression by promoting vascular dysfunction and macrophage adhesion. Targeting JAM2-positive ECs may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for alleviating chronic inflammation in OA.
papers.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: A novel CAF-related gene signature for prognostic and immunotherapy response prediction in PDAC based on single-cell RNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq data.
papers.authors: Du X, Li Z, Wang Y, Han L, Sun J, Gong W.
papers.abstract: Increasing evidence shows that cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) contribute to tumor progression, create an immunosuppressive microenvironment, and promote resistance to immunotherapy. However, the CAF-related gene signature in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains largely unexplored. In our study, we constructed a nine-gene CAF-related signature and found that it strongly correlated with the prognosis of PDAC patients in different cohorts. Subsequently, we found that the CAF-related gene signature was associated with the genomic alteration landscape, immune infiltration landscape and responsiveness to immunotherapy. GJB2 had the highest coefficient in our CAF-related gene signature, thus we explored the role of GJB2 in the interactions between CAFs and PDAC cells. The results showed that conditioned medium (CM) derived from the GJB2 knockdown group could suppress the malignant phenotype of PANC1 and MIAPaCa2 cells. In summary, this CAF-related gene signature is useful for prognosis prediction and precision therapy of PDAC patients.

papers.title: Monoclonal Gammopathy in Autoimmune Diseases: Marker, Consequence, Pathogenetic Factor-Or Coincidence?
papers.authors: Műzes G, Sipos F.
papers.abstract: The possible association between monoclonal gammopathy and autoimmune/immune-mediated diseases has received increasing attention in recent years. Several observational studies have reported an increased prevalence of monoclonal gammopathy in certain autoimmune conditions, particularly primary Sjögren's syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis, and systemic lupus erythematosus. However, recent population-based screening data from the iStopMM study found no significant association between autoimmune disease and screen-detected MGUS after adjustment for age and sex, suggesting that ascertainment bias may partly explain associations observed in clinically identified cohorts. The underlying mechanisms may include chronic antigen stimulation, sustained B-cell activation, germinal-center dysregulation, increased T follicular helper cell activity, and BAFF/APRIL-, IL-6-, NF-κB-, and STAT3-mediated signaling pathways. Based on current evidence, the relationship between monoclonal gammopathy and autoimmunity can be interpreted according to four potentially overlapping models: monoclonal gammopathy may serve as a marker of chronic immune activation, develop as a consequence of persistent autoimmune inflammation, act as a pathogenetic factor through the direct effects of the monoclonal immunoglobulin or the underlying clonal B-cell/plasma-cell population, or represent a coincidental finding related to factors such as age, genetic background, or increased diagnostic surveillance. This review summarizes the major epidemiological, pathogenetic, and clinical evidence supporting these interpretations and discusses their potential diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic implications. Finally, we highlight key directions for future research, including longitudinal single-cell and spatial omics approaches, further characterization of the BAFF/APRIL axis, and investigation of PANoptosis as a potential link between chronic inflammation and clonal plasma-cell disorders.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omics Characterization of WASHC2C Reveals Cancer-Specific Molecular, Clinical, Immune, and Cellular Associations.
papers.authors: Al-Nakhle HH.
papers.abstract: WASHC2C encodes a WASH-complex scaffold implicated in actin remodeling, endosomal organization, and intracellular trafficking, yet its cancer-specific molecular and clinical relevance remains insufficiently defined, particularly in the context of the closely related paralogue WASHC2A . An integrated pan-cancer multi-omics analysis was performed incorporating transcriptomic and protein-level evidence, clinicopathological and survival associations, genomic and epigenetic alterations, pathway activity, gene-set enrichment, immune features, immunotherapy-related observations, and single-cell functional states. Primary RNA analyses extracted both paralogues from the same GDC STAR files across eight cancer types, while covariate-adjusted Cox models evaluated LUAD, BLCA, and LIHC. A locked 50-gene co-expression signature was additionally assessed in independent GEO cohort, GSE31210. The harmonized expression analysis comprised 4365 primary tumors and 429 normal specimens and revealed pronounced lineage-specific variation together with strong WASHC2A-WASHC2C co-expression. Although HNSC showed platform-dependent directional differences between STAR and GSCA, the integrated analyses identified LIHC as the clearest prognostic context: higher WASHC2C expression was associated with poorer overall survival in the primary adjusted model (340 patients; 115 deaths; HR = 1.61 per unit log2[TPM + 1], 95% CI 1.18-2.21; FDR = 0.035), although the magnitude of association varied with model specification. Favorable unadjusted observations in LUAD and BLCA were not retained after covariate adjustment, and primary BLCA OS/DSS models were non-estimable. Across cancers, copy-number variation showed a consistent positive relationship with transcript abundance, whereas pathway, immune, methylation, and single-cell associations demonstrated marked tumor-context specificity. In GSE31210, 48 measurable genes from the locked signature were associated with favorable survival in 204 patients, supporting the relevance of the broader co-expression program, although neither WASHC2C nor WASHC2A contributed directly to that score. Collectively, this study establishes a rigorous multi-omic framework for WASHC2C , highlights its lineage-dependent molecular and prognostic relevance, and prioritizes specific cancer contexts-particularly LIHC-for mechanistic and translational investigation. These findings provide a strong foundation for future paralogue-resolved functional studies and independent clinical validation.

papers.title: Autonomous AI research agents in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma immunology: from multimodal evidence to experimental validation.
papers.authors: Li Y, Li Y, Huang R, San ZQ, Ye JF.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most challenging malignancies due to profound biological heterogeneity, complex stromal organization, and limited responsiveness to current immunotherapies. Recent advances in single-cell sequencing, spatial omics, digital pathology, and multimodal profiling have revealed that PDAC immune states are shaped not only by cellular composition but also by spatial organization, treatment context, and patient-specific evolutionary trajectories. However, the increasing complexity and fragmentation of biomedical evidence create substantial challenges for conventional artificial intelligence (AI) approaches that are typically optimized for predefined analytical tasks. Autonomous AI research agents represent an emerging paradigm that extends beyond predictive modeling by integrating scientific reasoning, retrieval of heterogeneous biomedical knowledge, computational tool orchestration, workflow adaptation, and evidence traceability. In this Review, we examine how agentic AI systems may contribute to PDAC immunology research, from characterization of immune ecosystems and spatial cellular interactions to biomarker discovery, neoantigen prioritization, and experimental protocol design. We distinguish AI agents from conventional task-specific models and discuss essential capabilities required for reliable biomedical research, including planning, tool use, verification, memory, provenance tracking, and human oversight. Despite promising technical demonstrations in biomedical domains, direct evidence supporting fully autonomous AI-driven discovery and validation in PDAC remains limited. Therefore, we propose a disease-oriented evaluation framework emphasizing benchmark task design, appropriate human and computational comparators, reproducibility assessment, and experimental validation. Future PDAC-specific AI research agents should prioritize evidence-aware reasoning, multimodal integration, calibrated uncertainty, and transparent computational-experimental workflows. Such systems may ultimately accelerate mechanistic discovery and precision immunology, while maintaining rigorous standards for biological validity, reproducibility, and responsible scientific practice.

figure.label: Figure 1
figure.caption: Conceptual framework linking PDAC immune complexity, multimodal evidence, agentic research orchestration, and experimental validation. PDAC immune heterogeneity encompasses malignant, stromal, and immune-cell states, spatial organization, treatment context, and disease evolution. These features are captured through complementary evidence sources, including bulk and single-cell omics, spatial profiling, pathology, clinical data, and experimental models. Evidence-aware AI research agents may coordinate retrieval, analysis, verification, and provenance tracking under human oversight, generating testable hypotheses for subsequent validation in organoid, animal, pathology, and immune-function systems. CAF, cancer-associated fibroblast; PD-1, programmed cell death protein 1; PD-L1, programmed death-ligand 1.

papers.title: Biomarker-guided immunotherapy in osteosarcoma: from immune microenvironment profiling to patient stratification and combination strategies.
papers.authors: Li Q.
papers.abstract: Osteosarcoma remains a therapeutically difficult malignancy, particularly after metastatic relapse, and immune checkpoint blockade or adoptive cell therapy has not reproduced the durable responses achieved in more immunogenic cancers. The central translational problem is not a complete absence of immune activity, but marked interpatient, intratumoral, and spatial heterogeneity in immune access, antigen presentation, myeloid suppression, stromal exclusion, and target-antigen expression. This Mini Review synthesizes recent single-cell and spatial profiling studies with tissue, circulating, and clinical biomarker evidence to define a practical framework for biomarker-guided immunotherapy. Osteosarcoma ecosystems can contain lymphoid-excluded, myeloid-dominant, angiogenic-hypoxic, checkpoint-rich, and antigen-high states that may coexist within the same patient. Consequently, programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) alone is unlikely to function as a reliable treatment-selection marker. A composite assessment integrating human leukocyte antigen (HLA) class I and antigen-processing competence, CD8/regulatory T-cell topology, macrophage and myeloid-derived suppressor cell programs, vascular and extracellular-matrix barriers, and quantitative surface-antigen density is more biologically defensible. Dynamic measurements, including circulating tumor DNA, soluble B7-H3, exosomal immune signals, and serial imaging, may complement tissue profiling but remain investigational. Clinical experience with checkpoint inhibitors, antiangiogenic combinations, mifamurtide, HER2-directed approaches, and emerging B7-H3-, GD2-, ALPL-1-, CD166-, IL-11Ralpha-, and NKG2D-based cellular therapies underscores the need to match mechanism to phenotype. Prospective studies should therefore use standardized, spatially resolved, and longitudinal biomarker panels to enrich trials, distinguish prognostic from predictive effects, and adapt therapy when immune exclusion or antigen escape emerges.

figure.label: Figure 1
figure.caption: Cellular composition and functional interactions within the tumor microenvironment. The tumor microenvironment (TME) comprises tumor cells, immune cells, stromal cells, extracellular matrix, and vascular components that interact through cytokines, chemokines, exosomes, and growth factors. Within the immune compartment, tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are represented by M1-like, M2-like, and transitional states, while myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) are represented by polymorphonuclear MDSCs (PMN-MDSCs) and monocytic MDSCs (M-MDSCs), together with T cells, NK cells, and dendritic cells. Stromal components include cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), pericytes, endothelial cells, adipocytes, and extracellular matrix. These reciprocal cellular and molecular interactions contribute to tumor proliferation and invasion, angiogenesis, immune suppression, metastatic progression, and therapy resistance.

papers.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Prognostic Model Integrating Inflammatory-Nutritional Biomarkers for Post-Prostatectomy Biochemical Recurrence: Development, Internal Validation, and Translational Target Exploration.
papers.authors: Wang H, Zhang Y, Li Z, Wu J, Cao H, Gan L, Qiu X, Wang W.
papers.abstract: Objective : Biochemical recurrence (BCR) after laparoscopic radical prostatectomy (LRP) significantly affects the long-term survival of prostate cancer (PCa) patients. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model integrating clinicopathological characteristics and preoperative inflammatory and nutritional indices to predict recurrence-free survival (RFS) and explore potential molecular therapeutic targets. Methods : A retrospective cohort of 320 PCa patients undergoing LRP at Beijing Chaoyang Hospital, Capital Medical University was analyzed. We integrated demographic, clinicopathological variables, and seven composite inflammatory/nutritional indices before LRP. A Mime-based machine learning survival pipeline was employed, combining Cox-based feature selection with survival algorithms. Model performance was evaluated using the concordance index (C-index), time-dependent ROC, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was used for model interpretation and deriving clinical cutoffs. Furthermore, intersecting genes of BCR, lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), and prognostic nutritional index (PNI) were identified via GeneCards, followed by drug sensitivity screening and molecular docking. Results : The StepCox[both] combined with Random Survival Forest model demonstrated optimal performance, achieving a validation C-index of 0.788. SHAP analysis identified the top five predictive factors for recurrence: preoperative LMR, PNI score, postoperative Gleason score ≥ 8, positive surgical margin, and lymphovascular invasion. Model-derived cutoffs were determined as LMR = 3.9 and PNI = 48.8. Intersection analysis revealed 1211 shared targets among BCR, LMR, and PNI, with TP53 and PTEN ranking highest. Drug sensitivity analysis and molecular docking suggested potential inhibitory effects of compounds like sabutoclax and dordaviprone on these targets. Conclusions : The proposed model may serve as a robust and interpretable risk stratification for postoperative PCa patients. The integration of clinical phenotyping with exploratory molecular docking offers a translational pathway from prognostic indices to potential therapeutic hypotheses, warranting further prospective validation.

papers.title: JAK-inhibitor treatment induces rapid yet incomplete immune reconstitution in STAT1 gain-of-function.
papers.authors: Iglesias-Herrero C, Roosens W, Galicia G, Cremer J, Marques PE, Devos T, Moens L, Meyts I, Gijsbers R, Schrijvers R.
papers.abstract: Autosomal dominant STAT1 gain-of-function (GOF) is an inborn error of immunity characterized by chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis and variable immune dysregulation. JAK inhibitors are a promising therapy, but their efficacy in STAT1 GOF remains variable. We longitudinally evaluated the clinical and molecular impact of JAK inhibitors in two STAT1 GOF patients, harboring p.R321S and p.T385M mutations, using Cellular Indexing of Transcriptomes and Epitopes by sequencing, flow cytometry, cytokine measurement, and allele-specific expression analysis in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and serum. Rapid yet incomplete immune reconstitution was observed as early as 1 week after treatment initiation. T cells rebalanced to a more homeostatic status and TCR repertoire diversity increased rapidly. However, some immune defects remained, including natural killer deficiency in one patient. The pronounced transcriptional dysregulation in monocytes was not explained by an unbalanced mutant STAT1 expression but improved with JAK-inhibitor treatment. JAK inhibitors provided significant clinical and immunological benefits to STAT1 GOF patients but did not fully restore immune homeostasis. These findings highlight the therapeutic potential and limitations of JAK inhibitors in STAT1 GOF.

(C) Study schema showing visit windows: Pre (before therapy), early (∼1 wk after start), and late (∼6 mo after start). Full dots represent PBMC sampling, and empty dots represent serum sampling.
