papers.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Macrophage Dysfunction and cDC2 Activation in COPD: Candidate Biomarkers for Individualized Nursing Care.
papers.authors: Liu W, Fan L, Yang J.
papers.abstract: Background Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality driven by dysregulated airway immunity. Macrophages and conventional type 2 dendritic cells (cDC2s) are central orchestrators of this process, yet their transcriptional heterogeneity at single-cell resolution and relationship to clinical severity remain incompletely characterized. Methods We performed integrative analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from 45,708 lung immune cells combined with bulk microarray data from 236 lung tissue samples. After Harmony-based batch correction and graph-based clustering, 11 immune cell populations were annotated. Pseudobulk differential expression was performed using DESeq2, functional enrichment by gene set enrichment analysis against MSigDB Hallmark, KEGG, and GO:BP gene sets, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis using STRINGdb. Clinical correlation used Spearman rank correlation between hub gene expression and GOLD stage, FEV1% predicted, emphysema index, and DLCO%. Results Macrophages were depleted in COPD while cDC2s were 4.7-fold expanded. Macrophages exhibited 1,268 differentially expressed genes dominated by IFN-γ response (NES = 2.60) and TNFα/NF-κB activation (NES = 2.41), with concurrent loss of mitochondrial function (NES = -2.40) and lysosomal acidification (NES = -2.25). cDC2s showed strong TNFα/NF-κB (NES = 2.88) and JAK-STAT (NES = 2.36) activation. PPI analysis identified IFNG, IL1B, CCR7, GZMB, and NFKB1 as central hubs. Cross-dataset validation confirmed LRG1, CCR7, IRF4, and TIMP1 as clinically correlated biomarkers. Conclusion This study identifies coordinated macrophage M1 polarization, metabolic dysfunction, and impaired efferocytosis in COPD, with cDC2-driven adaptive immune amplification. Eleven candidate biomarkers are proposed as targets for individualized nursing monitoring and precision respiratory care.
papers.venue: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

papers.title: BioText-SeqFormer: Integrating biomedical semantic representations and protein sequence embeddings for TCR-peptide interaction prediction.
papers.authors: Wang Z, Chen Z, Li D.
papers.abstract: The interaction between T cell receptors (TCRs) and antigenic peptides is central to adaptive immune recognition and is important for cancer immunotherapy, infectious disease research, and vaccine design. Although experimental screening methods are reliable, they are often costly and time-consuming, making it difficult to explore the vast combinatorial space of TCR-peptide pairs. Machine learning and deep learning methods provide efficient alternatives for TCR-peptide binding prediction, but most existing models mainly rely on amino acid sequence representations and make limited use of biomedical semantic information related to immune recognition. This limitation may restrict their ability to characterize complex binding patterns. To address this issue, we propose BioText-SeqFormer, a TCR-peptide interaction prediction framework that integrates task-adapted biomedical language semantic representations with protein sequence embeddings. The model constructs task-related biomedical textual representations and combines them with sequence embeddings extracted by a protein language model. Cross-modal Transformer encoding and the Complementary Fusion-Gating Aggregation (CFGA) module are used to model interactions among semantic, peptide, and TCR sequence features. Experiments on two public datasets, IEDB and McPAS-TCR, show that BioText-SeqFormer achieves stable and competitive predictive performance. Additional Top-k positive predictive value analysis, high-frequency peptide and TCR analysis, 9-mer peptide position-amino acid association analysis, and VDJdb-COVID transfer experiments further demonstrate its candidate screening ability, interpretability, and potential in few-shot transfer scenarios. Overall, this study provides a multimodal strategy for TCR-peptide interaction prediction by integrating language semantics and protein sequence representations.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics reveals transcriptional reprogramming and microenvironmental remodeling in ectopic ACTH/CRH-secreting pheochromocytomas.
papers.authors: Su W, Chen S, Liu J, Lian P, Zhang X, Zhang Y, Han W, Shen Q, Zhang D, Zhou X, Xiao Y, Ling Q, Gao Y, Lu L, Zhang Z.
papers.abstract: Background Ectopic ACTH- and/or CRH-secreting pheochromocytomas (ACTH + CRH + PCCs) are rare tumors that can mimic Cushing's syndrome and complicate the diagnosis and treatment clinically. However, the tumor-intrinsic and microenvironmental features of ACTH + CRH + PCCs remains poorly understood. Methods Fresh tumor specimens from three ACTH + CRH + and three ACTH - CRH - PCCs were profiled by single-cell RNA sequencing. Developmental trajectories and transcriptional regulatory networks were analyzed to investigate tumor-intrinsic programs, while CellChat and NicheNet were used to characterize cell-cell communication and infer ligand-mediated microenvironmental remodeling. Findings were also validated using TCGA datasets and immunohistochemical staining. Results ACTH + CRH + PCCs showed increased POMC and CRH expression and were enriched for a Schwann cell precursor (SCP)-like population positioned at an early pseudotime state. Regulatory network analysis further identified increased CEBPB activity in ACTH + CRH + tumor cells. Microenvironmental analysis revealed enrichment of SELE + endothelial cells and CD8 + T cells in ACTH + CRH + PCCs. Cell-cell communication analysis showed more frequent interactions between ACTH + CRH + tumor cells and SELE + endothelial cells, together with predicted ECM-associated interactions between SELE + endothelial cells and T cells. In contrast, ACTH - CRH - PCCs exhibited stronger VEGFA-related angiogenic signaling, greater enrichment of stromal populations and MRC1 + M2-like macrophages, and more prominent LGALS9-CD45 signaling between macrophages and T cells. Conclusions Our study provides single-cell insights into the tumor-intrinsic and microenvironmental heterogeneity between ACTH + CRH + PCCs and ACTH - CRH - PCCs, revealing distinct tumor cell states and subtype-specific vascular and immune landscapes.

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell and Bulk Transcriptomic Profiling Reveals Ferroptosis-Driven Heterogeneity of Ovarian Cancer Epithelial Cells.
papers.authors: Zhang H, Zhang Z, Wu X, Wang L, Zhao X, Hao R, Wang B.
papers.abstract: Purpose Ovarian cancer (OC) is a highly lethal gynecological malignancy characterized by insidious onset and poor prognosis, with limited validated prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Ferroptosis has been implicated in OC progression. However, most existing ferroptosis-related OC studies are based on bulk transcriptomic data, which fail to resolve the heterogeneity of OC epithelial cells. The relationship between ferroptosis-associated heterogeneity of epithelial cells and the tumor immune microenvironment remains insufficiently characterized at single-cell resolution. Materials and methods We integrated the GSE184880 single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) discovery cohort, the independent GSE235329 scRNA-seq validation cohort, and bulk transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas Ovarian Cancer (TCGA-OV) cohort to analyze epithelial cell subpopulations, ferroptosis activity, differentiation trajectories, and intercellular communication, and to construct a prognostic model. Results OC epithelial cells were clustered into four subpopulations, which were further stratified into ferroptosis-high (EP_0 and EP_3) and ferroptosis-low (EP_1 and EP_2) groups. Key ferroptosis-associated epithelial patterns were reproduced in the independent GSE235329 scRNA-seq cohort. CellChat analysis identified MIF -( CD74 + CXCR4 ) and MIF -( CD74 + CD44 ) as prominent predicted interactions between OC epithelial cells and T cells. A validated three-gene prognostic model ( OGN , RARRES1 , IGFBP7 ) showed prognostic discrimination in the TCGA-OV cohort, with moderate predictive performance in the internal test set. Risk groups also differed in the xCell-estimated infiltration of selected immune and stromal cell populations. Conclusion This study characterizes ferroptosis-associated heterogeneity of epithelial cells in OC at single-cell resolution and identifies candidate prognostic biomarkers and epithelial-immune communication signals that warrant further experimental and clinical validation.

papers.title: Nucleotide Metabolic Reprogramming in Sepsis: From Immune-Cell Fate to Organ Injury and Precision Therapeutics.
papers.authors: Wang C, Shuying F, Jing J, Fuquan F, Huang J.
papers.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by concurrent inflammation, immunosuppression, endothelial dysfunction and metabolic failure. Although current immunometabolic research primarily focuses on glycolysis, mitochondrial respiration and lipid metabolism, nucleotide metabolism links biosynthesis, redox homeostasis, epigenetic regulation and extracellular danger signalling. This Review synthesizes evidence for altered purine and pyrimidine synthesis, ribonucleotide reduction, nucleoside salvage and purinergic signalling across immune-cell populations in sepsis. We distinguish clinical observations from mechanistic evidence in experimental sepsis and hypotheses extrapolated from cancer or immune-mediated disease. Human observational studies support involvement of the extracellular ATP-CD39/CD73-adenosine axis in sepsis, while experimental studies provide complementary mechanistic evidence. By contrast, the roles of DHODH, RRM2 and the uridine-UPP1 salvage pathway remain predominantly preclinical, particularly in ferroptosis and acute organ injury. We propose that nucleotide metabolism functions as a time-, cell- and compartment-dependent regulatory network rather than a uniformly activated pathway. Clinical translation will require longitudinal metabolite-enzyme-receptor profiling, isotope-resolved flux analysis, spatial and single-cell approaches, and biomarker-defined therapeutic windows. Such strategies may enable nucleotide-directed interventions to complement antimicrobial treatment and organ support without compromising protective immunity.

papers.title: Temporal and Cellular Organization of Immune Responses to Live Attenuated Herpes Zoster Vaccination.
papers.authors: Wu J, Jin PF, Qin L, Xue Y, Wei M, Jiang G, Zhang ZS, Cheng R, Li JX.
papers.abstract: Background: Cellular responses to live attenuated herpes zoster vaccination and their variation with age remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to define their temporal and cellular organization and identify immune features that differed between age groups. Methods: Using a nested cohort design, we evaluated conventional humoral and CD4 T cell responses in 100 adults at Day 0 and Day 30. Olink protein profiles were assessed in 50 participants at Day 0 and Day 1, and longitudinal single-cell RNA sequencing was performed in 18 participants at Day 0, Day 1, and Day 30. Results: Vaccination increased gE and VZV antibody levels by Day 30, whereas CD4 T cell cytokine responses were more variable. Olink profiling identified broad early changes shared by both groups and exploratory differences in selected immune and inflammatory proteins. At single-cell resolution, the broadest transcriptional response occurred at Day 1, led mainly by classical monocytes and naive CD4 T cells, followed by a more selective state at Day 30. Differences between age groups involved baseline plasmacytoid dendritic cell abundance and non-classical monocyte regulatory activity, the early conventional dendritic cell type 2 response, and later CD8 T cell and regulatory programs. Conclusions: These findings connect conventional immunogenicity with proteomic and cellular responses and identify selected immune states and pathways that differed between age groups across response phases.

papers.title: Exploring noise in TCR specificity data through supervised learning
papers.authors: Deleuran, S. N.; Basavaraju, Y.; Matuleviciute, R.; Johansen, K. H.; Hadrup, S. R.; Nielsen, M.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of T cell receptor (TCR) specificity can potentially accelerate development of novel immunotherapies, yet public databases used to train these models contain substantial label noise. This uncertainty complicates model evaluation and limits the reliability of predicted TCR-pMHC interactions. In this work, we present a simple supervised machine learning denoising scheme to identify low-quality labels in TCR specificity data. We evaluated the framework using the TCRvdb validation dataset and further corroborated it via structural modeling with AlphaFold 3. Here, our denoising approach successfully identified non-validated TCRs, achieving an average MCC of 0.47 for filtering non-validated examples while retaining high sensitivity for validated examples. Applying our denoising approach to the complete NetTCR training dataset, we observed that data associated with known noisy attributes were significantly enriched in the filtered subset. Furthermore, TCR-pMHC complexes identified as noise consistently produced lower AlphaFold 3 confidence scores, providing independent evidence of misannotation. Experimental validation of 30 selected TCRs further supported the approach, with 80% of TCRs predicted as noise failing to demonstrate functional reactivity. Our findings demonstrate that current performance metrics may be obscured by dataset inaccuracies and provide a method for refining training data in the absence of gold-standard benchmarks.

papers.title: Programmable antigen-presenting scaffolds expand rare tumor-antigen-specific T cells from peripheral blood
papers.authors: DeVilla, J. N.; Binenbaum, Y.; Cieri, N.; Zhang, D. K.; Ji, H.; Martinolli DArcy, V.; Oliveira, G.; Manos, M.; Neuberg, D.; Ritz, J.; Ott, P. A.; Mooney, D.; Wu, C. J.
papers.abstract: Adoptive cellular therapies can be effective against solid tumors but rely on the identification and expansion of rare tumor-reactive T cells (TRTs). Here, we utilize antigen-presenting cell-mimetic scaffolds (APC-ms), a modular biomaterial platform that presents defined peptide-HLA and co-stimulatory ligands on a fluid lipid bilayer to selectively recover rare antigen-specific T cells from peripheral blood. Independent variation of peptide-HLA, co-stimulatory ligands, and cytokine support defined a formulation that enriched MART-1-specific T cells to above 2% of CD8+ T cells in 35 of 50 HLA-A*02:01+ healthy donors from low or undetectable baseline frequencies. Compared with mo-DCs, APC-ms achieved greater fold expansion of MART-1-specific T cells with increased functional avidity and preservation of an early differentiation phenotype, and generated a higher number of MART-1-specific clonotypes. In five of eight patients with treatment-naive melanoma, APC-ms could enrich MART-1-specific T cells to a median of 13.7% of CD8+ cells (range 0.30 - 57.2%) Moreover, APC-ms could expand T cells specific for an HLA-A*24:01-restricted personal neoantigen that were previously undetectable in peripheral blood of a patient with melanoma. These findings establish APC-ms as a tunable platform for the recovery of rare TRTs from peripheral blood, supporting its further development for therapeutic TCR discovery and personalized adoptive cell therapy.

papers.title: Response to Letter Re: A stromal-immune computational pathology signature for prognosis and immune checkpoint inhibitor response in localized, locally advanced and metastatic urothelial carcinoma: A multicenter retrospective study.
papers.authors: Song B, Tokuyama N, Pathak T, Madabhushi A.

papers.title: Identification of shared diagnostic biomarkers and immune-related mechanisms between sepsis and thoracic aortic aneurysm based on integrated bioinformatics and machine learning approaches.
papers.authors: She C, Deng H, Feng Y, Long C, Wu J.
papers.abstract: Background Sepsis and thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) share pathological features of inflammation and vascular dysfunction, yet their molecular connections remain unclear. Methods Transcriptomic datasets of sepsis and TAA from GEO were integrated to identify shared differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Functional enrichment and gene set enrichment analyses were performed to explore potential pathways. Machine learning models were applied to identify candidate genes with discriminatory potential, followed by immune infiltration analysis and assessment of gene expression in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-treated vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). Results A total of 193 shared DEGs were identified, mainly enriched in T cell activation, Th17 differentiation, and oxidative stress-related pathways. Five candidate genes (ARG1, IL18R1, LIX1L, TRIM32, and PRKCH) were selected through sequential machine-learning analysis and showed generally reproducible expression patterns across independent datasets. Their expression was associated with estimated immune cell proportions. In LPS-treated VSMCs, ARG1 and IL18R1 were upregulated, whereas LIX1L was downregulated. Conclusion Sepsis and TAA share common transcriptional signatures involving immune dysregulation and metabolic stress. ARG1 and IL18R1 may represent candidate molecular features associated with inflammatory and vascular responses.

papers.title: Transcriptomic Profiling of Oxidative Stress-Associated Immune and Apoptotic Signatures and In Silico Prediction of Therapeutic Candidates for Sjögren's Syndrome Dry Eye.
papers.authors: Wang J, Qing Q, Zhang J, Shi S, Yang X, Cai X, Wang Z, Jiang W, Zhang Q.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sjögren's syndrome (SS) is a systemic autoimmune disease characterized by lacrimal and salivary gland dysfunction, leading to dry eye and dry mouth. This study aimed to explore the potential associations between oxidative stress-mediated immune and apoptotic responses in Sjögren's syndrome dry eye (SSDE) and to computationally predict theoretical interacting candidates. Methods: We enrolled 16 SSDE patients and 15 healthy controls to assess key clinical parameters. The study utilized conjunctival impression cytology, RNA-seq, and bioinformatics to identify exploratory transcriptomic signatures. Gene expression levels were then assessed using real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). To provide supportive cross-species biological context regarding local oxidative stress status in vivo, malondialdehyde (MDA) levels were quantified in the extraorbital lacrimal glands of an SSDE murine model (NOD mice vs. BALB/c controls, n = 6/group). Furthermore, molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations were conducted to computationally explore potential pharmacological interventions. Results: Exploratory global transcriptomic analysis indicated that differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were prominently enriched in immune responses, inflammatory signaling, and apoptotic pathways, aiding the identification of a candidate transcriptomic signature of oxidative stress-related DEGs. Preliminary immune infiltration profiling suggested that the abundance levels of CD4+ T cells and eosinophils were positively correlated, while M1 and M2 macrophages were negatively correlated. Exploratory ROC analysis suggested the potential discriminative value (AUC 0.7-0.9) for key disease-associated genes, notably CDKN1A and BAX (r = 0.883). RT-qPCR results demonstrated that the transcription levels of CDKN1A , BAX , TGFBR1 , and S100A9 were significantly higher in the SSDE group compared to the healthy control group ( p p Conclusions: Supported by exploratory transcriptomic profiling and supportive in vivo biochemical data, our findings highlight an exploratory molecular association between oxidative stress and an intimately coupled immune-apoptotic axis in SSDE pathogenesis. The computational structural evaluation of ursolic acid and andrographolide provides a hypothesis-generating foundation for future in vitro and in vivo pharmacological investigations.

papers.title: Stigmasterol suppresses macrophage-mediated inflammatory amplification in acute pancreatitis through PPAR-γ-dependent macrophage reprogramming.
papers.authors: Zeng X, Chen J, Yang K, Zhou B, Qin H.
papers.abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance Glycine max (L.) Merr. (G. max; soybean), a widely cultivated medicinal and edible plant, has been traditionally used in Chinese medicine and dietary practices for maintaining digestive health. Stigmasterol (STG), a naturally occurring dietary phytosterol widely distributed in G. max and other edible and medicinal plants, is investigated here as a bioactive dietary constituent rather than as an isolate from a documented traditional remedy specifically used for acute pancreatitis (AP). STG has attracted increasing attention due to its anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory activities; however, its potential role and underlying mechanisms in AP remain unclear. Aim of the study This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of STG against AP and elucidate its role in regulating macrophage-mediated inflammatory amplification. Materials and methods Publicly available transcriptomic, spatial transcriptomic, and single-cell RNA sequencing datasets were downloaded and bioinformatically analyzed to identify key inflammatory pathways and cellular interactions in AP. The protective effects of STG were evaluated in AP mice and compared with ulinastatin (UTI). Network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA) were applied to identify STG targets. RAW264.7 macrophages and AR42J pancreatic acinar cells were used for in vitro validation, including peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPAR-γ) knockdown and co-culture experiments. Results Multi-omics analyses revealed that Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)-mediated nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-κB) signaling is a central inflammatory pathway in AP and is closely associated with macrophage-related high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) signaling. STG treatment alleviated pancreatic injury, inhibited NF-κB activation, and regulated macrophage polarization with comparable efficacy to UTI. Integrated pharmacological analyses and CETSA supported PPAR-γ as a key functional mediator and candidate molecular target of STG. STG regulated macrophage polarization and reduced extracellular HMGB1 release from activated macrophages in a PPAR-γ-dependent manner, accompanied by attenuation of macrophage-mediated TLR4/NF-κB-associated inflammatory responses in pancreatic acinar cells. Conclusions Although further validation in additional experimental models is warranted, STG ameliorates AP through PPAR-γ-dependent remodeling of macrophage immune responses, accompanied by reduced extracellular HMGB1 release and attenuation of TLR4/NF-κB-associated inflammatory signaling.

papers.title: Targeting macrophage-derived oncostatin M preserves cardiomyocyte mitochondrial bioenergetics and contractile function in fulminant myocarditis.
papers.authors: Yan Y, Sun Z, He Y, Zhuang Y, Jiang J.
papers.abstract: Background Fulminant myocarditis (FM) is an acute inflammatory cardiomyopathy with high risk of cardiogenic shock. Current management relies largely on circulatory support, while mechanism-based pharmacological targets remain poorly defined. Methods Cardiac CD45 + single-cell RNA sequencing, whole-heart single-nucleus RNA sequencing, ligand-target inference, spatial validation, and human plasma/myocardial analyses were integrated to define disease-associated cellular interactions. CCR2 + macrophage sorting, macrophage depletion, CVB3-stimulated BMDMs, transcription-factor perturbation, ChIP-qPCR, and promoter assays defined the source and regulation of OSM. OSM signaling was examined using recombinant OSM, OSM-neutralizing antibody, macrophage Osm knockdown, cardiomyocyte Osmr silencing, and STAT3/ERK1/2 inhibition, followed by transcriptomic, mitochondrial, contractile, and in vivo analyses. Results FM featured expansion of CCR2 + inflammatory macrophages, cardiomyocyte inflammatory/stress remodeling, and enhanced macrophage-to-cardiomyocyte OSM-OSMR signaling. Circulating OSM was increased in patients with FM and correlated with higher NT-proBNP and cTnI and lower LVEF. OSM was produced predominantly by CCR2 + macrophages and transcriptionally induced by IRF1 after CVB3 stimulation. Recombinant OSM aggravated mortality, systolic dysfunction, myocardial inflammation, and cardiac injury. In cardiomyocytes, OSM activated OSMR-dependent STAT3/ERK1/2 signaling and impaired mitochondrial bioenergetics, contractility, and Ca² + handling. OSM neutralization and macrophage Osm knockdown improved cardiomyocyte respiration and sarcomere shortening after exposure to CVB3-activated macrophage conditioned medium. In vivo, OSM neutralization improved survival, cardiac function, myocardial inflammation, mitochondrial integrity, and ATP content. Conclusion Macrophage OSM links inflammatory myeloid activation to cardiomyocyte mitochondrial and contractile failure in experimental FM. OSM-OSMR signaling is a candidate mechanism-based pharmacological target for acute inflammatory cardiac dysfunction.

papers.title: Targeting hypoxia-driven histone lactylation in myeloid cells synergizes with CD137 agonism to expand effector-like exhausted CD8+ T cells in glioblastoma.
papers.authors: Ugolini A, Scirocchi F, De Leo A, Badii F, Liu X, Pace A, D'Angelo L, Liu JKC, Etame AB, Ray P, Nuti M, Santoro A, Rughetti A, Vogelbaum MA, Yu X, Veglia F.
papers.abstract: Background Overwhelming presence of immunoregulatory myeloid cells and dysfunctional T cells is a major barrier to effective immunotherapies in glioblastoma (GBM). Therapeutic strategies that simultaneously address myeloid-driven immunosuppression and impaired T cell function are therefore needed to restore antitumor immunity in GBM. Methods We employed single-cell RNA sequencing, immunophenotyping, and functional analyses in an orthotopic murine GBM model (SB28) to investigate how hypoxia shapes the tumor immune microenvironment and limits CD8+ T cell responses. Pharmacologic hypoxia modulation using low-dose axitinib was combined with therapeutic intervention targeting CD137 in two GBM models (SB28, CT2A). Results Monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) and neutrophils constitute the most abundant and functionally immunosuppressive myeloid subsets within the GBM TME. Hypoxia reprogrammed MDMs and neutrophils into immunosuppressive cells, limiting the expansion of CD8+ T cells. Low-dose axitinib reduced intratumoral hypoxia, leading to altered glucose uptake and histone lactylation in MDMs and neutrophils, thereby impairing their immunosuppressive function and promoting the expansion of intratumoral PD-1+CD137+CD8+ T cells, specifically in the SB28 model. CD137 is largely expressed by effector-like exhausted CD8+ T cell subsets (EX-eff). Agonistic targeting of CD137, in combination with axitinib, robustly expanded EX-eff, which was accompanied by durable tumor regression, immunological memory, and long-term survival. Additionally, the abundance of PD-1+CD137+CD8+ T cells correlated with improved disease-free survival in patients with GBM. Conclusion Together, these findings establish a rationale for a combinatorial strategy that couples myeloid cells targeting and CD8+ T cell activation to overcome immunotherapy resistance in GBM.

papers.title: Latexin deletion in the bone marrow niche suppresses leukemia via LIFR downregulation and immune activation.
papers.authors: Zhang C, Yao X, Sui P, Hou L, Yan B, Luchsinger LL, Huang G, Tong S, Zhang Y, Shao B, Qian H, Zheng H, Zhong H, Yang FC, Liang Y.
papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is the most common adult leukemia diagnosis. Bone marrow (BM) niche significantly influences the initiation and progression of AML. However, our knowledge about the effect of leukemic niche on leukemia stem cells (LSC) and leukemogenesis is limited. In this study, we identified an extrinsic-regulatory function of latexin (Lxn) in leukemogenesis. Using a MLL-AF9-induced AML mouse model in WT and Lxn-KO (Lxn-/-) recipient mice, we found that Lxn deletion in the BM niche enhanced the survival of AML mice by suppressing LSCs and reducing blood blasts. Single-cell RNA-seq of stromal cells and cell communication analysis uncovered downregulation of the leukemia inhibitory factor receptor (LIFR) signaling pathway in the Lxn-/- niche, particularly within mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs). Mechanistically, reduced LIFR level in Lxn-/- MSCs upregulated Cxcl9 expression, leading to increased recruitment of CD8 T cells and enhanced cytotoxicity against leukemic cells. Combination of Lxn niche deletion and immune checkpoint inhibitor PD-1 further prolonged survival. The findings have important clinical implications, suggesting that Lxn inhibition could improve the efficacy of AML therapies by targeting the leukemia niche and enhancing immune surveillance.

papers.title: SPP1⁺ macrophage-derived WNT5A contributes to MMP11⁺ myCAF-mediated matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Wang M, Zhang P, Li X, Shao L, Dai S, Chen Z.
papers.abstract: Background Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the leading subtype of non-small cell lung cancer. However, the stromal-immune circuits that coordinate matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in LUAD remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize the stromal-immune interactions associated with LUAD progression and poor response to PD-1 blockade. Methods Bulk transcriptomic datasets, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic data were integrated with clinical immunotherapy cohorts. Weighted gene co‑expression network analysis, survival meta‑analysis, and tissue enrichment scoring identified high‑risk cell subpopulations. Cell‑cell communication, virtual gene knockout, and spatial deconvolution were used to predict ligand‑receptor interactions and colocalization. Multiplex immunohistochemistry of clinical specimens validated spatial relationships. In vitro, MMP11-overexpressing cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and SPP1-overexpressing macrophages (Macs) were generated, and a macrophage-CAF co‑culture system was constructed. Migration, contractility, extracellular matrix deposition, and YAP/INHBA pathway activation was measured. In vivo, a murine tumor model was established and evaluated using in vivo imaging, flow cytometry, atomic force microscopy assay, HE, masson staining, and multiplexed IHC staining. Results MMP11⁺ myofibroblastic CAF (MMP11⁺ myCAF) was identified as a high-risk CAF subset enriched in primary tumor and metastatic lesions, characterized by elevated expression of matrix-remodeling and contractile genes, including MMP11, ACTA2, and TAGLN. Increased abundance of MMP11⁺ myCAF was associated with advanced tumor stage, metastasis, poor overall survival, and reduced benefit from immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). Spatial transcriptomic deconvolution and multiplex immunohistochemistry revealed that MMP11⁺ myCAFs spatially co-localized with SPP1⁺ Mac, a pro-tumor myeloid population enriched in malignant and metastatic LUAD tissues. Ligand-receptor and downstream target analyses identified WNT5A as a key macrophage-derived mediator linking SPP1⁺ Mac to MMP11⁺ myCAF activation. Mechanistically, SPP1⁺ Mac exhibited activation of NFKB2/RELB-associated transcriptional programs, and SPP1 overexpression increased Nfkb2, Relb, and WNT5A protein levels in macrophages. WNT5A stimulation promoted YAP/INHBA-associated signaling in CAFs, enhancing CAF migration, contractility and extracellular matrix deposition. In animal models, activation of WNT5A signaling impaired the therapeutic efficacy of PD-1 blockade, reduced intratumoral CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, and increased MMP11⁺ CAF-associated collagen deposition and tissue stiffness. Conclusions SPP1⁺ Mac-derived WNT5A may contribute to MMP11⁺ myCAF-mediated matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in LUAD, highlighting a potential therapeutic strategy to overcome ICB resistance.

papers.title: CD180-Associated B-Cell Alterations in Type 1 Diabetes and the In Vitro Effects of Chlorogenic Acid: An Integrated Transcriptomic and Experimental Study.
papers.authors: Wang Z, Mijit A, Han R, Li M, Wu Y, Cheng L.
papers.abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is an autoimmune disease involving progressive loss of pancreatic β-cells. Although B cells have been implicated in T1DM progression, the molecular characteristics associated with disease-related B-cell states remain unclear. Here, we investigated B-cell-associated molecular alterations in T1DM and explored the potential immunomodulatory effects of a natural compound. Public T1DM transcriptomic datasets were analyzed using differential expression analysis, WGCNA, and machine-learning approaches. Single-cell RNA sequencing was used to characterize Cd180 expression across B-cell states. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were used to explore potential interactions between CD180 and candidate compounds, and an exploratory DARTS assay was performed to assess CGA-associated changes in CD180 proteolytic susceptibility. CD180 expression was examined in pancreatic tissues from vehicle- and MSA-2-treated NOD mice. The effects of chlorogenic acid (CGA) were evaluated in vitro by exposing B cells to CGA during inflammatory stimulation, followed by washing and co-culture with MIN6 cells in CGA-free medium. Integrated transcriptomic analysis identified four T1DM-associated genes ( CD180 , KCNJ2 , STEAP4 , and ZXDA ), among which CD180 showed the strongest association with B-cell-related immune alterations. Single-cell analysis showed increased Cd180 expression in inflammatory B-cell states together with enrichment of antigen-presentation-related programs. An exploratory DARTS experiment with matched loading-control data suggested altered CD180 proteolytic susceptibility following CGA exposure, although independent reproducibility remains to be established. In vitro, CGA exposure during inflammatory stimulation was associated with reduced CD180 expression in B cells and improved MIN6 cell viability and insulin-secretory responses during subsequent co-culture in CGA-free medium. CD180 is associated with inflammatory B-cell alterations in T1DM and may represent a candidate molecular feature of B-cell dysregulation. CGA treatment was associated with changes in CD180 expression in activated B cells and improved β-cell functional outcomes in vitro. These findings support further investigation of the relationship between CGA and CD180; however, whether the effects of CGA are specifically mediated through CD180 requires further experimental validation.

papers.title: Immune determinants of leuprolide-associated cardiovascular risk in prostate cancer
papers.authors: Gupta, T.; Zeng, F.; Li, M.; Moore, I.; Parihar, V. C.; Yadalam, A. K.; Ahluwalia, A.; Reyes, R. J. C.; Chen, Y.; Hammons, J.; Chung, E.; Xu, H.; Mecorapaj, S.; Lu, M.; Han, R.; Quyyumi, A. A.; Lesinski, G. B.; Waller, E. K.; Olsen, B.; Patel, S. A.; Mandawat, A.; Chaudagar, K.
papers.abstract: Leuprolide, a widely used androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT) for prostate cancer (PC), has been associated with increased cardiovascular events (CVE), although the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Through integrated spatial transcriptomic analyses of murine heart and immune-stromal profiling in patient blood, we identified immune programs linked to leuprolide-associated CVE risk. Spatial analyses revealed the distinct organization of lymphoid (T+B cells) aggregates and inflammatory macrophages in the plaque following leuprolide exposure that accompanied by ventricular hypertrophy, relative to normal vasculature. Parallel profiling of circulatory soluble and cellular components in patients demonstrated CD8+T cell enriched pattern in ~44% of patients, including memory and type 1 cytotoxic subsets that linked to treatment-induced CVE, such as ventricular dysfunctions, but no contribution of adipocytokines. These translational findings highlight the stratification of leuprolide-associated CVE risk in PC patients based on circulating T cell profiling and could guide the risk mitigation with alternative ADT agents.

papers.title: Age-associated transcriptional programs in tumor-associated macrophages are associated with tumor progression in HPV-negative oral cancer
papers.authors: Gujar, H.; Hanache, S.; Aggarwal, S.
papers.abstract: Aging and tobacco exposure are major determinants of risk and outcome in HPV-negative oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), yet the cellular programs linking host factors to tumor immunity remain poorly defined. We reprocessed and reanalyzed previously published single-cell RNA-seq data from 19 HPV-negative OSCC tumors and we identified a robust age- and smoking-associated expansion of SPP1high tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), accompanied by a shift toward a myeloid-dominant and lymphocyte-reduced tumor microenvironment. SPP1high TAMs exhibit a distinct transcriptional state enriched for extracellular-matrix remodeling and metabolic programs and reduced antigen-presentation pathways. They also express inflammatory chemokines such as CXCL2 and CXCL3 and down-regulate the cytotoxic mediator TNFSF10, suggesting a broadly protumor TAM phenotype. Ligand-receptor modeling suggests that SPP1high TAMs act as key communication hubs, with dominant SPP1-CD44 signaling to T-cell subsets. Transcription-factor analysis further implicates a POU2F1/POU2F2/SP1 module in maintaining this state. In the TCGA HNSCC cohort, the association between SPP1 expression and overall survival did not reach statistical significance after adjustment for age and tumor purity. These findings demonstrate that aging and tobacco exposure converge to expand an SPP1high TAM population that remodels the extracellular matrix and suppresses antitumor immunity, highlighting the SPP1-CD44 axis and its upstream regulators as potential therapeutic targets in high-risk OSCC.

papers.title: Epigenetic Memory in Human Diseases: Acquired Chromatin States as Targetable Drivers of Disease Evolution.
papers.authors: Khan SN, Danishuddin, Isah ST, Siddiqui MH, Ahmad A, Kim JJ.
papers.abstract: Clinical heterogeneity remains a major challenge across human diseases, where patients with similar genetic backgrounds frequently exhibit striking differences in disease progression, therapeutic response and clinical outcome. Increasing evidence indicates that these differences cannot be explained by genetic variation alone, positioning epigenetic memory as a critical non-genetic determinant of disease behavior. Epigenetic memory refers to the stable yet reversible propagation of transcriptional states through mechanisms including DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin accessibility, enhancer dynamics and higher-order chromatin organization. In this review, we synthesize emerging mechanistic and translational evidence demonstrating how epigenetic memory integrates environmental, metabolic, inflammatory, infectious and therapeutic cues into persistent cellular programs that drive inter-patient, intra-tumoral and temporal heterogeneity. We discuss its disease-specific manifestations across cancer, immunological, neurological, and metabolic disorders, with particular emphasis on cellular plasticity, stemness, immune evasion, drug-tolerant persister states and relapse. Furthermore, we highlight recent advances in single-cell and spatial epigenomics, liquid-biopsy-based epigenetic biomarkers, CRISPR-mediated epigenome editing and targeted chromatin therapies that collectively establish epigenetic memory as both a measurable biomarker and a therapeutically actionable vulnerability. By framing epigenetic memory as a dynamic interface between genome and environment, this review provides a unified conceptual framework for understanding disease evolution and advancing precision epigenetic medicine.

papers.title: LAIR1 suppresses phagocytosis via SHP2/USP22-mediated MYH9 degradation in glioma-associated microglia/macrophages to drive immunosuppression.
papers.authors: Wang Z, Sun Q, Li C, Sun T, He Z, Wang Y, Li R, Lin X, Jasiulionis MG, Ji N, Zhang Y, Xu H.
papers.abstract: Background Glioma immunotherapy faces major challenges due to the pervasive presence of glioma-associated microglia/macrophages (GAMs) and inadequate T-cell responses. LAIR1 is highly expressed in GAMs and correlates with poor glioma prognosis. This study investigated its role in GAMs and immunosuppression in glioma. Methods LAIR1 expression was analysed via bioinformatics, flow cytometry, and multiplex immunohistochemical staining. Its function was studied using Lair1 -/- mice, engineered BV2 cells, bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs), patient-derived GAMs, and techniques including RNA-seq, PCR array, co-immunoprecipitation, molecular dynamics analysis, and CRISPR/Cas9. Results LAIR1 was predominantly expressed on GAMs, and high infiltration of LAIR1 high GAMs correlated with poor patient survival. In orthotopic glioma models, LAIR1 deficiency reduced tumour burden. LAIR1 high GAMs exhibited an immunosuppressive phenotype, associated with the CD47-SIRPA axis. These GAMs conferred resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy. LAIR1 deficiency enhanced GAM tumoricidal activity in vitro. Mechanistically, collagen I-activated LAIR1 promoted SHP2-dependent dephosphorylation of MYH9 at Ser1943. This inhibited USP22 recruitment, blocking USP22-mediated deubiquitylation and stabilisation of MYH9 and HIF1α, ultimately suppressing GAM phagocytosis. Conclusion LAIR1 is a critical phagocytosis suppressor in GAMs, driving glioma immunosuppression. Targeting LAIR1 represents a promising strategy to restore anti-tumour immunity.

papers.title: Tryptophan metabolism-derived prognostic signature: A potential biomarker for risk stratification and exploratory immunotherapy relevance analysis in prostate cancer.
papers.authors: Gao A, Xu Y, Wang T, Chen L, Wang Q, Zhang S, Fang C, Zheng P.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveProstate cancer (PCa) lacks reliable biomarkers to distinguish indolent from aggressive tumors. Tryptophan metabolism (TM) participates in regulating tumor immunity and malignant progression, yet its prognostic relevance in PCa remains poorly characterized.MethodsTranscriptomic and clinical data of TCGA-PRAD cohort (499 PCa samples and 52 normal prostate tissues) and independent external cohort GSE116918 were collected. Differentially expressed tryptophan metabolism-related genes (TMGs) were screened. Univariate Cox regression and LASSO penalized regression were performed to construct a prognostic signature based on disease-free survival (DFS), which served as the primary modeling endpoint. Kaplan-Meier survival curves and time-dependent ROC analyses were applied to verify its prognostic performance. Hub genes were screened via PPI network, and the biological function of core hub gene CCN5 was further validated through in vitro cell experiments.ResultsA total of 82 differentially expressed TMGs were screened. Three candidate genes (MAOB, ELOVL2, THRSP) were integrated to establish the risk signature, which effectively stratified patients into low- and high-risk subgroups; high-risk patients exhibited significantly inferior DFS (P<0.05). The signature was identified as an independent prognostic predictor for PCa, with a 1-year DFS AUC of 0.997 (95% CI: 0.972-0.999). Bioinformatic prediction preliminarily indicated correlations between the risk model and M0 macrophage infiltration as well as chemotherapeutic sensitivity, while no real clinical chemotherapy response data were available to support these associations. Hub gene CCN5 was significantly downregulated in advanced PCa; cellular functional assays confirmed that CCN5 overexpression suppressed proliferation and migration of PCa cells.ConclusionsThis tryptophan metabolism-related signature independently predicts DFS outcomes of PCa patients and is preliminarily associated with tumor microenvironment features based on computational analysis. CCN5 acts as a tumor-suppressive gene in PCa. The present study provides exploratory bioinformatic evidence for future research on individualized prognostic stratification, rather than direct clinical medication guidance.

papers.title: Identification of Cuproptosis-Related Genes and Immunological Roles in Steroid-Induced Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head.
papers.authors: Zeng J, Li J, Chen R, Fang X, Zhang W.
papers.abstract: Objective Steroid-induced Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head (SONFH) is a disabling disorder arising from chronic glucocorticoid exposure. Cuproptosis, a copper- dependent form of cell death, has been implicated in various diseases, but its role in SONFH remains unclear. This study aimed to characterize cuproptosis-related molecular subtypes and develop a predictive model for SONFH. Methods Using the GSE123568 cohort (30 SONFH cases, 10 controls), we analyzed Differentially Expressed Cuproptosis-related Genes (DE-CRGs) and immune infiltration via CIBERSORT. Unsupervised clustering and Weighted Gene Coexpression Network Analysis (WGCNA) identified molecular subtypes and module genes. Three machine learning models (Random Forest (RF), Generalized Linear Models (GLMs), Support Vector Machines (SVMs)) were compared; the RF model was validated using a nomogram, calibration, decision curve analysis, and the GSE74089 cohort. Target genes were confirmed by immunohistochemistry on clinical femoral head tissue. Results NLRP3, NFE2L2, and PDHB were differentially expressed in SONFH and confirmed by immunohistochemistry. Two molecular clusters with distinct immune infiltration profiles were identified. The RF model performed best (AUC = 0.889), and five predictive genes-KCNE3, SOD1, ACAP1, ALDH2, and ITGAL-were selected. The nomogram demonstrated high predictive accuracy in external validation. Discussion These findings reveal the potential role of cuproptosis-related genes in SONFH pathogenesis and immune regulation, providing biomarkers for molecular subtyping and risk prediction. Conclusion NLRP3, NFE2L2, and PDHB are key modulators of SONFH pathogenesis, and the 5-gene RF-based nomogram offers a novel, effective diagnostic approach for clinical application.

papers.title: The role of ferro-aging genes in periodontitis: novel insights based on bioinformatics analysis.
papers.authors: Chu P, Wu D, Deng J, Chen X.
papers.abstract: Background The concentration of iron ions in gingival crevicular fluid and local periodontal tissues is significantly elevated in periodontitis (PD), presenting a disorder of iron metabolism characterized primarily by iron overload. Excessive free iron can continuously catalyze the generation of reactive oxygen species through the Fenton reaction, providing sustained chemical driving force for lipid peroxidation, thereby constituting a key biochemical basis for the initiation of ferro-aging. However, the specific role of ferro-aging in the pathogenesis of PD and its molecular regulatory network remains unclear. Methods The study obtained PD-related transcriptomic datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. By intersecting the ferro-aging-related gene set (FAG) with differentially expressed genes (DEGs), ferro-aging-related differentially expressed genes (FAGDEGs) in PD were screened. Subsequently, a comprehensive application of Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) and two machine learning algorithms-Random Forest (RF) and Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression-was employed to further screen key ferroptosis-associated genes (KFAGs). Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve was used to evaluate the diagnostic performance of KFAGs, and experimental validation was performed using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Additionally, immune cell infiltration analysis was conducted to explore potential associations between the expression levels of KFAGs and immune cell types. Results This study identified a total of 1379 DEGs, and after intersecting them with FAG, 11 FAGDEGs were obtained. Following screening by WGCNA and machine learning algorithms, 4 KFAGs were ultimately identified: IRF1, SLC1A5, PDE4B, and IL1B. ROC curve analysis results showed that the Area Under the Curve (AUC) of the above four genes was greater than 0.6, indicating their good potential value in the diagnosis of PD. RT-qPCR experimental results demonstrated that the expression trends of these four KFAGs in PD were consistent with the database analysis results. Immune cell infiltration analysis further revealed significant correlations between the expression levels of KFAGs and the abundance or activation status of various immune cell subsets. Conclusion The results of this study indicate that IRF1, SLC1A5, PDE4B, and IL1B are key biomarkers associated with the ferro-aging process in PD. This finding provides new molecular evidence and research directions for further elucidating the synergistic role of iron metabolism disorders and ferro-aging in the pathogenesis of PD.

papers.title: GSTP1 as a senescence-associated diagnostic candidate in prostate cancer: integrative bioinformatics and functional validation.
papers.authors: Li H, Lu S, Wang H, Yu D, Zhang Z, Liu S, Zhong M, Xiao H, Li K.
papers.abstract: Introduction Prostate cancer (PCa) is a common malignancy of the male genitourinary system with high metastatic potential and poor clinical outcomes, for which effective biomarkers and therapeutic targets remain limited. Methods This study employed a multi-omics approach, integrating transcriptome profiles, age-related gene screening, and machine learning techniques, to analyze four GEO datasets, in order to identify key diagnostic biomarkers for prostate cancer (PCa). Results Differentially expressed aging-related genes were identified, with enrichment analyses revealing significant involvement in PCa. Using machine learning algorithms, a robust diagnostic model centered on GSTP1 was developed, demonstrating high predictive performance. GSTP1 depletion drove multiple oncogenic phenotypes, including enhanced proliferation, migration, invasion, and the inhibition of cellular aging and DNA damage, suggesting that GSTP1 may promote cellular senescence while restraining malignant progression. Furthermore, its expression correlated with distinct immunocyte profiles, highlighting a role in shaping the PCa immune landscape. Discussion Our findings confirm that GSTP1 functions as an aging-associated stress response gene, offering new perspectives on prostate cancer pathogenesis and showing promise for advancing therapeutic strategies that target both aging and immune associations. This study provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging aging biomarkers in precision oncology and highlights GSTP1 as a promising candidate for clinical translation in PCa management.

papers.title: Design of multi-epitope vaccine based on G2c genotype PEDV antigen and its immunogenicity and protective effect in piglets.
papers.authors: Luo H, Sun Z, Wang J, Lan L, Wang B.
papers.abstract: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) remains a clinically important enteric virus, causing diarrhea, vomiting, dehydration, and high mortality in piglets. As the currently available vaccines may provide inconsistent protection against genetically heterogeneous field strains, particularly G2c variants, improved immunization strategies are still needed. In this study, a multi-epitope vaccine candidate was designed from the PEDV S, M, and N proteins using an immunoinformatics-based workflow. The final construct incorporated 8 linear B-cell epitopes, 1 CTL epitope, and 5 HTL epitopes, and was predicted to contain 6 discontinuous B-cell epitopes; porcine β-defensin-1 (PBD-1) was used as an adjuvant component and attached to the N-terminus. Computational analyses indicated favorable antigenicity, solubility, and structural stability. In vivo evaluation showed that the SMN peptide vaccine elicited PEDV-specific IgG, IgA, cytokine, and neutralizing-antibody responses. Following challenge with a virulent G2c PEDV strain, all five piglets in each peptide-vaccinated group survived, compared with three of five piglets in the commercial inactivated-vaccine group and none of the five piglets in the PBS group. These results indicate that the MEV candidate induced immune responses and improved protective outcomes in piglets, supporting its further development as a PEDV vaccine.

papers.title: Machine learning classifies subcellular Golgi morphology from imaging flow cytometry during inflammatory activation: an exploratory study
papers.authors: Zhang, X.; Fang, M.; Geng, B.; Che, P.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory activation remodels the Golgi apparatus to meet increased secretory demand, yet whether these structural changes carry computationally accessible information about immune cell state has not been explored. Here we show that machine learning applied to imaging flow cytometry images of the Golgi can distinguish lipopolysaccharide (LPS) treated from control cells. We trained models on Golgi images from human THP-1 monocytes before and 16 h after LPS stimulation in vitro, and from circulating myeloid cells of mice 24 h after intratracheal LPS or saline in vivo. In each dataset, the best-performing model was a deep learning model trained directly on images rather than a classifier using predefined morphometric features. Cross-domain performance varied with the model, transfer direction and use of labelled target data: several deep learning models trained on mouse images classified THP-1 cells above chance without changing model parameters. Grad-CAM highlighted regions within or adjacent to the GM130 fluorescence pattern. These findings indicate that GM130 images carry information associated with LPS treatment that supports classification within and across the two datasets. To our knowledge, this is the first application of supervised deep learning to imaging flow cytometry images of a subcellular organelle for inflammatory phenotyping, establishing organelle level image analysis as a potential complement to molecular assays for immune cell classification.

papers.title: Identification of stroke as the predominant hypoxia-associated cerebrovascular disease: Integrated NHANES evidence and mechanistic insights into JUN-mediated endothelial injury and protection by licarin B.
papers.authors: Yang Q, Huang J, Wu H, Hu Y, Yu Y, Yang W, He Y, Xiong Y.
papers.abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance Hypoxia, a featured condition of high-altitude regions, contributes to the development of a wide range of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. However, the cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease most strongly associated with hypoxia, along with its underlying molecular mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets, remains incompletely understood. Sanwei Tanxiang Powder (SWTX) is a classical Tibetan prescription that has long been used to improve blood circulation and alleviate hypoxia-related cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disorders. Licarin B is a bioactive constituent of SWTX with potential therapeutic value. Aim of the study This study aimed to identify the cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease most strongly associated with hypoxia, investigate its underlying molecular mechanisms, and explore the protective effects and molecular targets of licarin B against hypoxia-associated cerebrovascular injury. Materials and methods We employed an integrative strategy combining population-based epidemiological analysis, transcriptomics, network pharmacology, single-cell RNA sequencing, and experimental validation to systematically investigate hypoxia-associated cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases and their pathogenic mechanisms. Human cerebral microvascular endothelial cells (hCMEC/D3), were used to evaluate the effects of hypoxia and licarin B on oxidative stress, inflammatory responses, nitric oxide production, and endothelial function. The therapeutic efficacy of licarin B was further evaluated in a mouse model of acute ischemic stroke induced by middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). Results Epidemiological analysis identified ischemic stroke as the cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease most strongly associated with hypoxia, as indicated by low hemoglobin levels. Multi-omics analyses revealed that hypoxia-associated stroke-related genes were predominantly enriched in inflammatory and oxidative stress pathways, with JUN identified as a key hypoxia-related stroke gene (HRSG). Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of murine brain tissue further demonstrated that JUN was relatively highly expressed in endothelial cells and positively associated with pro-inflammatory immune cell infiltration. In hCMEC/D3 cells exposed to hypoxia, JNK phosphorylation and JUN expression levels were markedly increased, accompanied by reactive oxygen species accumulation, impaired nitric oxide production, and enhanced expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Network pharmacology and molecular docking identified licarin B, a bioactive constituent of SWTX, as a candidate compound predicted to target JUN. In hypoxia-exposed hCMEC/D3 cells, licarin B significantly suppressed JUN expression, mitigated hypoxia-induced oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, and preserved endothelial barrier integrity, whereas JUN overexpression or JNK activation partially abrogated these protective effects. Furthermore, in a middle cerebral artery occlusion mouse model, licarin B administration reduced cerebral infarct volume, alleviated ischemic brain injury, suppressed the JNK/JUN signaling axis and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression, and improved neurological function. Conclusions This study identifies the hypoxia-JNK/JUN axis as a critical mediator of microvascular endothelial dysfunction during ischemic stroke and highlights licarin B, a bioactive constituent of SWTX, as a promising therapeutic candidate for hypoxia-associated cerebrovascular injury.

papers.title: A spatiotemporal atlas of radiation-induced brain injury reveals dysfunction of the blood-CSF barrier.
papers.authors: Quan C, Gao Y, Liu X, Xiang J, Zhang J, Chen L, Li Y, Gao W, Hao K, He G, Liu D, Wang A, Tian H, Lu H, Ping J, Jiang S, Huang Q, Wu Y, Wu H, Lu Y, Zhou G.
papers.abstract: Radiotherapy for brain tumors frequently induces irreversible cognitive decline, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we present an integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlas of radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) in mice, spanning the acute to chronic phases. We reveal that the early-delayed phase following irradiation represents a critical window during which the blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier (BCSFB) integrity is compromised. This disruption results from the selective depletion of a radiosensitive Tmsb4x + epithelial subpopulation in the choroid plexus, which functions as a gatekeeper for the BCSFB. Consequently, CSF-derived macrophages excessively infiltrate the periventricular niche and engage in spatial crosstalk with interferon-responsive microglia. This dysregulated immune axis sustains chronic neuroinflammation, driving the late-stage neurodegeneration and cognitive impairment. In conclusion, our study establishes a high-resolution spatiotemporal framework and positions the BCSFB as a pivotal immune gateway and a promising therapeutic target for mitigating RIBI.

papers.title: Dysfunctional myeloid states in sepsis across the marrow-to-blood continuum: developmental contribution and peripheral reprogramming.
papers.authors: Chen J, Zhang F, Jin G, Zhang J.
papers.abstract: Sepsis is accompanied by extensive expansion and remodeling of the myeloid compartment, yet a dysfunctional circulating phenotype does not by itself reveal where that dysfunction arose. Immature markers, low-density fractions, HLA-DR-low phenotypes, transcriptional clusters, and direct T-cell suppression describe different biological levels and carry different mechanistic implications. This review examines sepsis-associated myeloid dysfunction as a source-attribution problem across a marrow-to-blood continuum. Clinical-sepsis studies support altered hematopoietic output and lineage-specific maturation, including emergency-granulopoietic programs in circulating hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, whereas controlled human systemic endotoxemia provides separate cross-compartment evidence of impaired monocyte maturation. In vitro , plasma from patients with sepsis can program healthy human progenitors toward suppressive myeloid states. Conversely, endotoxin tolerance, epigenetic and metabolic remodeling, activation, and degranulation can generate additional dysfunction after marrow egress. Several human observations argue against a unitary maturation-failure model. Mature CD10-positive neutrophils can suppress T-cell proliferation even when immature CD10-negative cells do not; low-density neutrophils encompass mixed maturity and activation states, and immature neutrophils are kinetically distinct from LOX-1-positive polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cell (PMN-MDSC)-like populations. Monocyte HLA-DR provides a further example because it functions as a dynamic immune-state readout rather than a measure of developmental maturity. Accordingly, we distinguish five evidentiary layers - hematopoietic origin, developmental state, molecular state, functional phenotype, and patient-level immune phenotype - and use them to reassess neutrophil, monocyte, and MDSC-like states. Current human evidence supports contributions from developmental remodeling and peripheral reprogramming, but their relative importance within the same lineage and patient remains unresolved. Resolving that question will require paired compartment sampling, serial multi-omics, direct functional validation, and clinically meaningful longitudinal outcomes rather than greater reliance on computational trajectories or marker-defined identities alone.

figure.caption: Marrow-to-blood continuum and five evidence layers for interpreting sepsis-associated myeloid dysfunction. (A) Uses the marrow-to-blood sequence as an evidence-organizing framework from hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) through progenitors, lineage allocation, maturation and marrow egress to circulating myeloid states. The blue and orange segments distinguish production-side programs from post-egress remodeling, while the central note emphasizes that direct ancestry from a named human progenitor to a named dysfunctional circulating state remains unresolved. (B) Separates hematopoietic origin, developmental state, molecular state, functional phenotype and patient-level immune phenotype. These layers are related but not interchangeable and require separate validation. The figure is an interpretive framework, not a proven continuous lineage model.

papers.title: Richter Transformation of Chronic Lymphocytic Leukaemia: Biology, Diagnosis, and an Evolving Therapeutic Landscape.
papers.authors: Marquet-Palomanes J, Martin-Moro F, Garcia-Vela JA.
papers.abstract: Richter transformation (RT) is the development of an aggressive lymphoma in a patient with a previous or concomitant diagnosis of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL)/small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL). Most cases are of the diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) type; the Hodgkin lymphoma variant and other lymphoma subtypes are less frequent. RT affects 2-10% of patients with CLL, and survival has historically been measured in months. Approximately 80% of DLBCL-RT cases are clonally related to the underlying CLL and are enriched for unmutated IGHV and high-risk genetic lesions such as TP53 disruption, NOTCH1 mutation, CDKN2A/B loss and MYC activation, and they are associated with poorer outcomes than the minority of clonally unrelated cases, which behave as de novo DLBCL. Multi-omic and single-cell studies indicate that the transformed clone is seeded early. Chemoimmunotherapy produces short-lived responses, and treatment has moved towards targeted and immune-based options including BTK inhibitors, CD20 × CD3 bispecific antibodies, checkpoint-inhibitor combinations and CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, with allogeneic transplantation used as consolidation in fit responders. This review summarises the current data on biology, diagnosis, prognosis and treatment of RT and proposes a practical approach.

papers.title: VINTER: a generative vision-language model for annotating and interrogating spatial tissues
papers.authors: Wu, J.; Xu, W.; Zhuang, Y.; Zhang, Y.; Loza Lopez, M. d. J.; yang, y.; Nakai, K.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics links gene expression to tissue structure, yet current models learn embeddings whose meaning is assigned afterwards or read histology without measured expression. Tissue decisions are therefore rarely made from morphology, genes and neighbourhood together, or examined through them. Here we introduce VINTER, a generative vision-language model aligned on 1.45 million histology-caption pairs that reads histology, measured gene expression and spatial neighbourhood as one sequence. It returns the probability of every tissue class, and because genes enter as text, its molecular evidence can be edited with the image held fixed. Reading all three sources together, VINTER annotated tissue more accurately than spatial-domain methods and a spatial foundation model, and transferred across cohorts without target labels. Editing only the neighbourhood resolved the follicular B-cell and plasma-cell programmes behind its reading of tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) maturation in lung and kidney cancer. Its class probabilities exposed what single labels conceal in triple-negative breast cancer: immune heterogeneity within stroma and cancer hidden beneath benign labels. Without retraining, the same model transferred to Visium HD and single-cell Xenium data and resolved follicular architecture within colorectal cancer TLS. VINTER thus turns spatial annotation into an interrogable reading of tissue across platforms and resolutions.

papers.title: Beyond Tumor Treating Fields: Multimodal Antitumor Action and the Clinical Potential of Pulsed Electromagnetic Fields.
papers.authors: Zeng QW, Liu MJ, Yi LS, Wu S, Zhu PP, Hu HZ, Shao ZQ.
papers.abstract: Pulsed electromagnetic fields (PEMFs) are a noninvasive, safe, and well-tolerated physical therapy modality with established applications in musculoskeletal disorders. Their potential role in oncology has attracted increasing interest. This review synthesizes current evidence on the antitumor mechanisms and experimental effects of PEMFs across diverse cancer models. Reported biological effects include the induction of apoptosis, regulation of intracellular calcium homeostasis, inhibition of angiogenesis, modulation of immune responses, induction of oxidative stress, regulation of autophagy and cellular metabolism, and enhancement of sensitivity to radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Preclinical studies suggest that PEMFs can selectively suppress proliferation and promote cell death in malignant cells while exerting comparatively limited cytotoxicity in normal cells. Evidence has been reported in models of breast cancer, glioma, hepatocellular carcinoma, melanoma, and other malignancies. Although clinical investigations remain preliminary, studies conducted over the past two decades support a favorable safety profile and suggest potential therapeutic efficacy, particularly in combination with chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or immunotherapy. Artificial intelligence and machine learning may facilitate parameter optimization and the development of individualized treatment regimens. Ultimately, the integration of PEMFs into routine oncology practice will require well-designed, large-scale randomized controlled trials to standardize treatment protocols, define clinical indications, and establish their role in multimodal cancer care.

papers.title: A multiomic atlas reveals distinct immune landscapes in preterm and term chronic placental inflammation.
papers.authors: Levenson D, Romero R, Pique-Regi R, Xu Y, Galaz J, Badhan R, Kareus E, Lee S, Ino H, Niesen S, Monticolo F, Shu J, Myers L, Wylie KM, Bhatti G, Tarca AL, Gomez-Lopez N.
papers.abstract: Chronic placental inflammation (CPI), an umbrella term encompassing chronic chorioamnionitis, chronic villitis, and chronic deciduitis, is associated with preterm birth (PTB), yet its cellular and molecular determinants across gestation remain poorly defined. Here, we constructed an integrated multiomic atlas of CPI by profiling placental and extraplacental tissues from preterm and term pregnancies using imaging mass cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire mining. CPI emerged as a gestational age-dependent immune continuum rather than a uniform inflammatory state. Preterm CPI was characterized by infiltration of cytotoxic CD8 + T cells, activated macrophages, and natural killer (NK) cells in the extraplacental membranes. In contrast, term CPI exhibited spatially confined immune niches enriched for homeostatic myeloid cells and regulatory T cells. Multiomic integration revealed active contributions from the developing fetal immune system in preterm CPI, including macrophages, T cells, and mast cells that reshaped maternal-fetal immune cross-talk. Cell-cell-communication analyses uncovered proinflammatory signaling states in preterm CPI and resolution-phase pathways in term CPI, whereas TCR repertoire profiling identified memory clonotypes with viral epitope similarity, consistent with antigen-agnostic activation. Overall, this atlas defines the cellular, spatial, and transcriptional architecture of CPI and provides a framework for translational biomarker discovery and therapeutic intervention development.

papers.title: Monocyte Galectin-9 is associated with CD8⁺ T-cell dysfunction and early relapse after haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
papers.authors: Dai W, Zhao X, Wu L, Pang A, Wang L, Ma S, Geng C, Wang S, Zheng X, Dong F, Hu L, Jiang E, Cheng T, Hao S.
papers.abstract: Background Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is the most common acute leukemia in adults. Haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (haplo-HSCT) stands as a leading curative approach for AML in China. However, relapse remains a major challenge for patient survival, often occurring within six months post-transplant and associated with a five-year mortality rate of up to 80%. Here, we characterized early immune reconstitution after haplo-HSCT and investigated immune features associated with early relapse (ER) in AML. Methods We analyzed two clinical cohorts: patients with AML (n = 44) and aplastic anemia (AA; n = 38), and AML patients with continuous complete remission (CCR, n = 55) versus ER (n = 38). Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on longitudinal peripheral blood and bone marrow samples from AML and AA patients (n = 3 and 4), while single-cell RNA/TCR sequencing was performed on bone marrow samples from CCR and ER patients (n = 3 each). Flow cytometry assessed monocyte Galectin-9 surface expression and CD8⁺ T-cell phenotypes. Galectin-9-associated monocyte-T-cell interactions and the effects of the TIM-3 inhibitor MG-T-19 were evaluated in vitro and in a murine AML model. Results AML and AA patients showed different patterns of early immune reconstitution after haplo-HSCT, including differences in monocyte and T-cell recovery. Within AML, ER patients exhibited increased T-cell representation but reduced basal TNF-α expression and altered exhaustion-associated CD8⁺ T-cell phenotypes before relapse. Monocytes represented a prominent Galectin-9-expressing compartment, and surface Galectin-9 on monocytes was elevated in ER compared with CCR patients as early as day 30 post-transplantation. Exogenous Galectin-9 induced dose-dependent functional and exhaustion-associated changes in CD8⁺ T cells, while Galectin-9-high IFN-conditioned monocytes impaired CD8⁺ T-cell responses in vitro. MG-T-19 partially reversed these alterations, increased CD8⁺ T-cell TNF-α production, and enhanced leukemia-cell apoptosis. In the MLL-AF9 murine AML model, MG-T-19 reduced leukemia burden and prolonged survival. Conclusions Increased monocyte Galectin-9 during early immune reconstitution is associated with subsequent early relapse and CD8⁺ T-cell dysfunction after haplo-HSCT. Further Galectin-9-specific mechanistic studies and prospective clinical validation are warranted to establish its causal relevance and potential utility as an early relapse biomarker.

papers.title: BCL2A1 marks an early, less-exhausted CD8 + tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte state associated with PD-1 blockade response in NSCLC.
papers.authors: Pham HMQ, Chen CL, Feng PH, Lee KY, Hung YP, Lin CF.
papers.abstract: Background The tumor microenvironment exerts intense survival pressure on CD8 + tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), yet the cellular basis for an earlier, less-exhausted state associated with response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains unclear. We previously identified BCL2A1 as a CD8 + TIL-derived marker predictive of a response to PD-1 blockade. Here we combine deep single-cell discovery with experimental validation in primary human T cells to characterise the BCL2A1-associated CD8 + TIL state and its candidate upstream signal. Methods We integrated four transcriptomic cohorts-pre-treatment bulk RNA-seq with CD8 + TIL deconvolution (n=60), on-treatment scRNA-seq/TCR-seq (n=11), longitudinal scRNA-seq/TCR-seq (n=18), and an independent post-treatment cohort (n=59)-with in silico perturbation, pathway, and metabolic-flux analyses, and experimentally tested a key prediction of this state by flow cytometry in primary human CD8 + T cells. Results BCL2A1 high CD8 + TILs showed elevated BCL2A1 expression without coordinated upregulation of anti-apoptotic BCL2-family genes, maintained minimal exhaustion, and occupied an early, BCL6 -, TCF7 -, and NFKB1 -regulated pseudotime state. Across longitudinal and post-treatment cohorts, they formed diverse, low-expansion repertoires rather than dominant expanded clones, with reduced biosynthetic flux (branched-chain amino acid and purine metabolism) consistent with a non-proliferative state. NF-κB signaling was elevated, and TNF-α was nominated as the leading candidate upstream ligand of BCL2A1 . We then experimentally tested this prediction: in primary human CD8 + T cells, TNF-α induced BCL2A1 protein ≈13-fold (44.5% vs. 3.4% BCL2A1 + ; MFI 2.93-fold; P Conclusions Combining integrative single-cell analysis with experimental validation in primary human T cells, we define BCL2A1 as a marker of an early, less-exhausted CD8 + TIL state associated with improved ICB outcomes in NSCLC; a survival-related role is supported by these associations but was not functionally tested.
