papers.title: A Comparison of Mechanisms Driving Lesion Outcomes During Lung Tumor and Tuberculosis Granuloma Formation.
papers.authors: Michael CT, Budak M, Kirschner D.
papers.abstract: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) and tuberculosis (TB) are both deadly diseases that present with spatially complex lung lesions. These lesions share similarities, including spatial interactions between T cells and macrophages. Both SCLC and TB exhibit heterogeneous disease progression and responses to treatment; current experimental methods have few tools to investigate the spatiotemporal evolution of these lesions within human lungs. We have applied our computational agent-based model (ABM), GranSim, to extensively study heterogeneity of TB granuloma formation and treatment efficacy. We introduce TumorSim, an analogous ABM designed to understand heterogeneity of SCLC lung tumors. TumorSim mechanistically captures immune-tumor interactions, many of which are well-studied in isolation, including cytokine-based recruitment of immune cells and PD-1/PD-L1-based inhibition of cytotoxic T cells. Drawing from lung immunology literature, we define and explore wide parameter ranges to characterize TumorSim behavior using global sensitivity analysis. We compare factors that drive both tumor and granuloma outcomes. As model validation, sensitivity analysis captures several well-known correlates of improved SCLC outcomes including macrophage-mediated cytotoxic T-cell recruitment. Surprisingly, both models predict a two-phase formation process occurring with an abrupt change in tumor/granuloma dynamics upon arrival of adaptive immune cells into the lung. Simulations suggest that while C-C motif chemokine ligand 5 (CCL5) is associated with improved tumor control later during tumor growth, CCL5 plays a pro-tumor role early during tumor growth by recruiting regulatory T cells. We find that, like virtual granulomas, TumorSim tumors become enlarged when immunosuppressive mechanisms outweigh pro-inflammatory responses. This novel tumor model enables future studies of both immunotherapeutics and anti-cancer drugs.

papers.title: Construction of a soluble mediator landscape and analysis of its clinical diagnostic potential in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.authors: Li Y.
papers.abstract: Background Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and fatal interstitial lung disease. Current diagnosis primarily relies on imaging and histology, lacking sensitive and specific early biomarkers. Although soluble mediators play pivotal roles in IPF pathogenesis, their systematic characterization and clinical utility remain unclear. This study aimed to construct a soluble mediator-based marker atlas for IPF and evaluate its diagnostic potential. Methods Multiple IPF-related transcriptomic datasets (GSE10667, GSE24206, GSE53845) were integrated from the Gene Expression Omnibus database to identify differentially expressed soluble mediator-related genes (SM-DEGs). Key diagnostic biomarkers were selected using multiple machine learning algorithms, including Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator, Random Forest, Recursive Feature Elimination, and Boruta, combined with protein-protein interaction network analysis. A diagnostic model was constructed and externally validated. The potential biological significance and therapeutic research value of the candidate genes were further explored through molecular subtyping, immune infiltration analysis, ceRNA network construction, and drug-gene association prediction, and the expression of the candidate diagnostic genes was detected by qRT-PCR in an in vitro IPF cell model. Results Sixteen SM-DEGs were identified. By integrating multiple machine learning feature selection methods and PPI network analysis, Cadherin 2 and SPP1 (Secreted Phosphoprotein 1) were finally identified as candidate diagnostic-related feature genes. The infiltration levels of memory B cells, plasma cells, and regulatory T cells in Cluster 2 were higher, and these immune cells may participate in the development of IPF. Drug prediction based on the DGIdb and DrugBank databases showed that most candidate drugs have database-annotated drug-gene associations with SPP1. qRT-PCR demonstrated that CDH2 and SPP1 were significantly upregulated in Transforming Growth Factor-β1-induced human lung fibroblasts. Conclusion This study identified CDH2 and SPP1 as two candidate diagnostic-related genes for IPF, and provided a basis for further research on their clinical diagnostic value and potential biological roles.

papers.title: Diethyl phthalate exposure promotes colon cancer progression through ALDOC mediated proliferation, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and ferroptosis resistance.
papers.authors: Gu Y, Yalikun A, Shen Y, Chen P, Gong H, Liu Q, Wang X, Liu L, Wei S, Xu X, Li J.
papers.abstract: Colon cancer is a global health threat characterized by marked heterogeneity and therapeutic resistance. Although environmental pollutants may contribute to tumor progression, the role of diethyl phthalate (DEP), a widely used plasticizer and endocrine disruptor, remains unclear. By integrating clinical cohort data, bioinformatics, and in vitro and in vivo models, we investigated the oncogenic effects and mechanisms of DEP in colon cancer. Elevated serum DEP was independently associated with shorter overall survival, and DEP exposure accelerated subcutaneous tumor growth in vivo. In vitro, DEP enhanced cell migration and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), while suppressing ferroptosis by reducing intracellular iron accumulation and lipid peroxidation. LASSO regression and tumor immune microenvironment profiling further established a DEP-related prognostic signature associated with an immune-cold phenotype, characterized by reduced CD4 + and CD8 + memory T cells and increased M2 macrophage infiltration. ALDOC was identified as a key downstream mediator of DEP-induced malignancy. DEP markedly upregulated ALDOC, whereas ALDOC knockdown reversed EMT activation, restored ferroptosis sensitivity, and inhibited cell migration. These findings demonstrate that DEP promotes colon cancer progression through the ALDOC/EMT axis and ferroptosis evasion, highlighting ALDOC as a potential therapeutic target.
papers.venue: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association

papers.title: Comprehensive analysis and external validation of a glycolysis-related gene signature as a prognostic index for skin cutaneous melanoma.
papers.authors: Jiang C, Niu S, Li C, Liu A, Zhao M, Wang W, Shen W, Tang X.
papers.abstract: Skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM) is the third most common cause of cancer-related deaths globally. Today, precise biomarkers to predict melanoma prognosis are quite limited. Aerobic glycolysis serves as the primary metabolic pathway for malignancies to meet their rapid growth demands. This study built a glycolysis-associated gene (GAG) signature to evaluate prognosis and immunotherapy response of SKCM. Data acquired from the Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) databases were evaluated to obtain differentially expressed GAGs. With machine learning techniques, four key GAGs (GOT2, CLN6, GYS1, and IDUA) were pinpointed as candidate prognostic biomarkers. Subsequently, a risk model was constructed by incorporating these four GAGs. The risk model could effectively forecast SKCM patient survival and treatment efficacy. Also, the elevated risk scores correlated with diminished immune cell infiltration and impaired immune functions. In addition, the four GAGs all showed influence on immune cell infiltrations of SKCM. Then, the role of predominant hub gene GYS1 and CLN6 was validated using in vitro models. The overexpression of GYS1 and CLN6 could promote viability, invasion, and proliferation of melanoma cells. ELISA and western blot experiments demonstrated that the overexpression of GYS1 lead to higher secretion of proinflammatory cytokine TNF-α and IL-1β, activated the nuclear factor kappa B signaling pathway, and promoted an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Collectively, this study initially pinpointed glycolysis-related genes as prognostic biomarkers for melanoma and elucidated the facilitating role of GYS1 and CLN6 in melanoma, providing deeper insights into pathogenesis of melanoma.

papers.title: Potential Relevance of Bidens pilosa L. to Atopic Dermatitis: Mechanistic Evidence, Drug Development Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
papers.authors: Sopyan I, Lukitaningsih E, Mauludin R, Priani SE, Siagian VHM, Cung J, Syahrul M, Sirait MC.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by epidermal barrier dysfunction, immune dysregulation, oxidative stress, microbial dysbiosis, and persistent inflammation. Although current therapies have improved disease management, long-term treatment remains challenging because of disease relapse, adverse effects, treatment costs, and variability in therapeutic response. These challenges have stimulated interest in botanical agents with diverse phytochemical profiles and potentially complementary biological activities. Bidens pilosa L. has attracted attention because of its diverse phytochemical composition and reported anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antibacterial, and immunomodulatory activities. This narrative review integrates phytochemical, pharmacological, computational, safety, and pharmaceutical evidence to examine the potential relevance of B. pilosa to AD and the challenges associated with its further development. Available evidence indicates that B. pilosa -derived preparations and individual phytoconstituents exhibit multiple biological activities relevant to inflammatory, oxidative, immune, and microbial processes involved in AD. While most pharmacological studies of B. pilosa have been conducted in general inflammatory or non-dermatological models, several AD-relevant studies of individual phytoconstituents reported in B. pilosa provide additional mechanistic support. Computational studies further suggest potential interactions between selected phytoconstituents and AD-related molecular targets, providing hypotheses for further experimental investigation. Overall, the available evidence supports the potential relevance of B. pilosa to AD and provides a rationale for further development, while recognizing the need for greater validation of standardized preparations in AD-specific models. Future studies should prioritize phytochemical standardization, validated AD models, dermal safety assessment, topical formulation development, and clinical evaluation.

papers.title: Reconstructing donor genotypes from scRNA-seq for downstream eQTL and HLA-TCR analysis
papers.authors: Kockelbergh, H.; Astley, J.; Kichula, K. M.; Zhang, Z.; Ng, E. S.; COvid-19 Multi-omics Blood ATlas (COMBAT) Consortium, ; Dendrou, C. A.; Chong, A. Y.; Watson, R. A.; Fairfax, B. P.; Knight, J. C.; Band, G.; Norman, P. J.; Carrington, M. N.; Sansom, S. N.; Mentzer, A. J.; Jostins-Dean, L.; Luo, Y.
papers.abstract: Single-cell eQTL studies can reveal heterogeneous genetic effects on gene expression that vary with cell type, but their wider application has been constrained by the frequent absence of matched genotype data. Here, we present single-cell Transcriptome Allelic Prediction and Association Studies (scTAPAS), a bioinformatic framework for reconstructing donor genotypes directly from single-cell RNA-sequencing reads and downstream genetic analysis. Applying scTAPAS to 5' single-cell RNA-sequencing data from the COVID-19 Multi-omic Blood Atlas (COMBAT), we show that reference-based imputation of sparse RNA-derived genetic information generates genotype dosages sufficiently accurate for association testing. Despite testing only 18.0% of the variants available from conventional array-based genotyping and imputation, scTAPAS recovers 68.6% of cell type-eGene pairs identified using conventional array-based genotypes, with strong concordance in effect sizes. We further show that scTAPAS-derived variants can support imputation of classical HLA alleles and enable HLA-aware QTL analyses, including associations between HLA variation and TCR repertoire at single-cell resolution. Using matched single-cell TCR-sequencing data, we identify CD4+ T cell-specific associations between HLA class II alleles and T-cell receptor (TCR) Va; gene segment usage, highlighting the potential of analyses that complement TCR sequencing at single-cell resolution with HLA types. These results show that genetic information recovered from single-cell RNA sequencing data can support both regulatory and immunogenetic association analyses, expanding the discovery potential of single-cell cohorts for which conventional genotyping or HLA typing is unavailable.

papers.title: Temporal assessment of spatial and single-cell transcriptomes identifies CD226-NECTIN2 T cell-cholangiocyte interaction in bile duct inflammation.
papers.authors: Jördens MS, Nordhus KS, Øgaard J, Amundsen-Isaksen E, Ramberg OH, Yeoh J, Holm K, Jiang X, Luedde T, Karlsen TH, Chung BK, Melum E.
papers.abstract: Background and aims Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) and primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) are inflammatory bile duct disorders affecting mostly young adults that often lead to liver cirrhosis and cancer. Especially for PSC, pathogenic mechanisms remain unclear and treatment options are lacking. To better understand biliary disease processes in bile duct inflammation, we analyzed livers of NOD.c3c4 mice by spatial and single-cell (scRNA-seq) transcriptomics, identifying key cell types, interactions and potential changes over time that were validated in human liver explants. Methods Livers of 10, 20 and 40-week-old male NOD.c3c4 mice were used for spatial transcriptomics and scRNA-seq. Differentially-expressed genes at different time points were analyzed using the CellphoneDB database with a focus on T cell-related interactions. CD226-NECTIN2 interaction was validated using co-culture experiments and antibody treatment in NOD.c3c4 mice. CD226-NECTIN2 in PSC, PBC and alcohol-related liver disease (ALD) explants was analyzed by spatial transcriptomics and immunofluorescence. Results Spatial transcriptomics consistently distinguished inflamed and non-inflamed liver areas in NOD.c3c4 mice at different ages. When combined with scRNA-seq enriched for immune cells and cholangiocytes, key inflammatory cell types were localized to biliary structures. Using differentially-expressed genes and a curated overview of biologically-validated interactions (CellphoneDB), the CD226-NECTIN2 T cell-cholangiocyte interaction was discovered. Knock-down of Nectin2 in vitro and anti-CD226 blocking in NOD.c3c4 mice specifically reduced T cell activation and diseased human liver showed consistent CD226-NECTIN2 co-localization at inflamed bile ducts. Conclusions By combining spatial transcriptomics and scRNA-seq in NOD.c3c4 mice, we generated a pipeline for in-depth identification of potential disease relevant genes and interaction partners. The T cell-cholangiocyte interaction CD226-NECTIN2 was identified, functionally validated and detected in human disease highlighting this interaction as a possible future treatment target. Impact and implications PSC is an intractable immune-mediated cholestatic liver disease that mainly affects young people and has a significant impact on families and the healthcare system due to treatment costs and sick leave. Our study aimed to find new ways of understanding PSC and highlight potential treatment targets by first identifying disease-relevant cell interactions in a mouse model, followed by confirmation in human PSC livers.

papers.title: Abundant CD8 + tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in glioblastoma harbor distinct exhaustion signatures in potentially reactive subsets.
papers.authors: Okamoto T, Mizuta R, Demachi-Okamura A, Muraoka D, Fukushima Y, Ishihara H, Sun Y, Wang Y, Nishida R, Sasaki E, Masago K, Onoguchi K, Tanaka Y, Yamashita Y, Stratford R, Clancy T, Muto O, Tan CL, Otani Y, Takahashi Y, Yamaguchi R, Green EW, Platten M, Date I, Tanaka S, Hashimoto N, Matsushita H.
papers.abstract: Background The effectiveness of immunotherapy against glioblastoma (GBM) remains limited, suggesting that antigen-specific tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are rare. This study aimed to identify tumor-specific T cells in GBM as the basis for antigen-specific immunotherapy. Methods Tumor specimens were collected from 56 patients newly diagnosed with IDH-wildtype GBM. In cases showing prominent intratumoral T-cell infiltration, CD3⁺CD8⁺CD4⁻ T cells were sorted for single-cell RNA and T-cell receptor (TCR) sequencing. Integrated analyses were performed using our single-cell dataset from the Aichi Cancer Center (ACC), publicly available GBM TILs datasets (PA), and lung cancer TILs and malignant pleural effusions datasets (LC). Candidate reactive TCRs were identified using an AI-based algorithm. Results Unsupervised analysis identified a dominant cluster characterized by the strong expression of exhaustion markers, most prominently LAG3, with high TCR clonality. Moreover, LAG3 and CXCL13 expression levels were significantly higher in the ACC TIL-rich subset than the PA dataset. Finally, a prediction algorithm suggested that our TIL-rich subset harbored a markedly higher proportion of potentially reactive T cells than the PA and LC datasets. Conclusions TILs with marked clonal expansion in certain GBM cases may include potentially reactive T cells with distinct exhaustion features, providing a foundation for the development of antigen-specific and LAG-3-targeted immunotherapies.

papers.title: Multimodal biomarkers for early detection and immunotherapy assessment in hepatocellular carcinoma: integrating liquid biopsy, AI-based imaging and tumor immune profiling.
papers.authors: Zhao Y, Chen X, Zhao H.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) commonly develops in chronically diseased liver and remains challenging because of late detection, heterogeneity, recurrence and limited hepatic reserve. Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based combinations improve outcomes in advanced HCC, but durable responses occur in only a subset of patients. This structured narrative review evaluates biomarkers by intended use: surveillance and early detection, pretreatment prognostic stratification, treatment selection, on-treatment monitoring, neoadjuvant response assessment and postoperative minimal residual disease (MRD) detection. Serum alpha-fetoprotein and clinical scores are accessible but largely reflect tumor burden, inflammation or liver function. Cell-free DNA methylation and fragmentomics provide early-detection and tissue-of-origin signals, while circulating tumor DNA tracks molecular burden and clonal evolution. Tissue and spatial profiling clarify immune responsiveness and resistance, whereas radiomics and deep learning noninvasively assess whole-tumor and peritumoral heterogeneity. These modalities are complementary but require distinct evidence standards. Most early-detection studies use case-control or enriched cohorts, and most immunotherapy associations are retrospective, prognostic or monitoring-related. No biomarker yet supports routine selection among ICI regimens. Unlike modality-specific summaries, this review aligns each biomarker with a defined clinical decision and evidentiary category and proposes a longitudinal framework integrating baseline blood, imaging and tissue features with on-treatment dynamics, preoperative reassessment and postoperative molecular surveillance. Clinical translation requires standardized assays, representative multicenter cohorts, locked external validation and biomarker-guided trials demonstrating value beyond established criteria.

papers.title: All-trans retinoic acid-driven immune remodeling in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma revealed by single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.authors: Yang T, Huang Y, Liu Y, Wang Y, Zhu X, Shi H, Dai S, Zhao L, Li L.
papers.abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains a highly lethal malignancy with limited durable responses to current therapies. Our previous work showed that all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) upregulates the deubiquitinase OTUD6B and suppresses ESCC stemness. Here, we integrated in vivo pharmacological treatment, single-cell RNA sequencing, bulk RNA sequencing, immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, and OTUD6B disruption to define how ATRA remodels ESCC tumors. In a syngeneic mEC25 tumor model, ATRA inhibited tumor growth, and the ATRA-plus-anti-PD-1 group showed greater tumor inhibition than the ATRA-alone group. Single-cell profiling of ATRA- and vehicle-treated tumors identified epithelial, stromal, lymphoid, and myeloid compartments and revealed extensive immune remodeling after ATRA treatment. ATRA reduced FOXP3-associated regulatory T-cell features, attenuated M2-like macrophage polarization, and expanded a CD74-high neutrophil state. In epithelial tumor cells, ATRA-regulated genes were enriched in ubiquitination-related protein homeostasis, including protein ubiquitination, ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolism, and proteasome-mediated degradation. These findings prompted transcriptomic analysis of human ESCC cells treated with ATRA or subjected to OTUD6B silencing. ATRA treatment was negatively associated with hallmark epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) enrichment, whereas OTUD6B knockdown was positively associated with EMT enrichment. Importantly, OTUD6B disruption attenuated ATRA-associated tumor suppression and abolished ATRA-induced reductions in CD25 + FOXP3 + regulatory cells and F4/80 + CD206 + macrophages, as well as the induction of CD74 + neutrophils. These data support a possible contribution of OTUD6B to ATRA responsiveness and provide a rationale for further evaluation of ATRA-based immunotherapy combinations in ESCC.
papers.venue: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease

papers.title: Integrative multiomics and machine learning identify uridine as a candidate modulator of MMP7-mediated immune cell infiltration in pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.authors: Bi W, Zhou Y, Gong J, Liu W, Li J, Du J, Nie H, Luo H, Zhang H, Cai Q, Gao C, Zeng L, Jiang J, Hou S, Li L.
papers.abstract: Introduction Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrosing interstitial lung disease (ILD) characterized by immune cell infiltration and extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition. Effective therapies remain limited. Uridine is an endogenous nucleoside with pro-reparative and immunomodulatory effects, but its molecular targets and immune mechanisms in IPF remain unclear. Objectives To identify potential uridine-associated targets in pulmonary fibrosis and to determine whether uridine is associated with matrix metalloproteinase 7 (MMP7)-related immune cell infiltration. Methods Uridine target predictions from multiple databases were integrated with bulk lung transcriptomes from three public ILD cohorts (n = 531). Machine learning with SHAP interpretation prioritized candidate targets. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) evaluated uridine-protein interactions. Single-cell RNA-seq (∼540,000 cells) and spatial transcriptomics (19 IPF, 6 controls) mapped the cellular and spatial distribution of MMP7 and linked MMP7-enriched compartments to immune infiltration signatures. Key findings were validated in a bleomycin (BLM)-induced mouse model and in vitro assays. Results Integrative analyses prioritized five core genes (CA4, MME, MMP7, PTPRB, and TYMS; individual AUCs > 0.85), with MMP7 showing the highest SHAP importance. Higher MMP7 expression was associated with worse survival (HR = 2.93, p -5 ). SPR confirmed direct uridine-MMP7 binding (KD = 6.73 × 10 -6 M). In the BLM model, uridine attenuated fibrotic pathology and immune cell infiltration (total CD45 + cells: 777.8 vs. 3745 in BLM, p = 0.0002), accompanied by changes in MMP7, MIF, and MDK, consistent with modulation of immune microenvironment features. Conclusion Integrative multiomics and machine learning analyses, together with in vitro and in vivo validation, suggest that uridine attenuates pulmonary fibrosis, potentially through modulation of MMP7-associated immune-microenvironment remodeling.

papers.title: Targeting the CD4 + effector memory T cells re-expressing CD45RA suppressor galectin-7: a multi-omics-guided therapeutic strategy for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.authors: Yan T, Liu J, Liu Y, Gu W, Liu J, Li Y, Lv R, Zhang C, Ding J, Zha C, Wang C, Gao F, Huang M, Chen J.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic, progressive interstitial lung disease with limited therapeutic options. Although single-cell and spatial transcriptomics have revealed cellular heterogeneity within the IPF lung microenvironment, the immune drivers with causal relevance remain poorly defined. Here, through large-scale Mendelian randomization integrating multi-omics data, we identified a consistent negative causal association between the proportion of CD4⁺ effector memory T cells re-expressing CD45RA (TEMRA) and IPF risk. Multi-platform validation-including single-cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and multiplex immunofluorescence-confirmed a significant reduction in CD4⁺ TEMRA frequency in both peripheral blood and lung tissues of IPF patients, establishing this subset as a clinically relevant biomarker. Spatial transcriptomics further revealed a negative correlation between TEMRA differentiation signatures and local fibrotic burden. Mechanistically, integrated single-cell analyses pinpointed metaplastic KRT5⁺ basal cells as a key epithelial population with the capacity to disrupt immune homeostasis. These aberrant epithelial cells upregulate Galectin-7 (LGALS7), which we demonstrate competes with IL-7 for receptor binding, suppresses STAT5 phosphorylation, and limits CD4⁺ TEMRA differentiation, thereby uncovering a previously unrecognized epithelial-immune crosstalk axis in IPF. Guided by these findings, virtual screening of 20,000 compounds identified neoeriocitrin as a Galectin-7 inhibitor that restores STAT5 phosphorylation in vitro and attenuates pulmonary fibrosis in vivo. This study positions Galectin-7 as a druggable target and establishes a novel framework linking epithelial dysfunction to immune dysregulation in IPF.

The volcano plots displayed the causal effects of immune traits on IPF in the discovery cohort ( b ) and validation cohort ( c ). d Flow cytometry detected the level of CD4 + TEMRA in the peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) of normal subjects and IPF patients. e The histogram compared CD4. + TEMRA abundance between IPF patients and normal subjects. papers.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing combined with artificial intelligence to uncover immunotherapy biomarkers and decipher drug resistance mechanisms in glioblastoma.
papers.authors: Fu T, Hu M, Wu X.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma represents the most aggressive primary malignant tumor of the central nervous system, characterized by extensive intratumoral heterogeneity, profound immunosuppression, therapeutic resistance, and poor clinical outcomes. Although immunotherapy has revolutionized cancer treatment, its clinical efficacy in GBM remains limited, largely due to the complexity of the tumor ecosystem and the lack of validated predictive biomarkers. Recent advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based computational approaches have provided unprecedented opportunities to decipher tumor heterogeneity and identify clinically actionable biomarkers. This mini-review integrates studies related to scRNA-seq and its combination technology, further elaborating on the tumor plasticity, immune suppression, and metabolic-epigenetic reprogramming mechanisms of GBM. The article systematically summarizes the complete analysis process of integrating single-cell multi-omics data by AI and highlights the application value of AI in validating biomarkers. The above research ideas are expected to overcome clinical resistance problems, optimize patient stratification schemes, and enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy, providing theoretical support for developing highly stable prognostic biomarkers and achieving individualized precise immunotherapy for glioblastoma.

papers.title: Single-Cell Multiplex Immune Biomarker Prediction from Histopathology Across Cancer Types and Clinical Endpoints
Single-Cell RNA Sequencing deciphers the imbalance of Microenvironment of the Maternal-Fetal Interface in Cesarean Scar Pregnancy.
papers.authors: Wang T, Wei J, Yan J, Yang H.
papers.abstract: Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) has posed a serious threat to women's reproductive health. The view on its mechanism remained controversial. Here, we performed a single-cell sequencing on villi and decidua from three normal and three cesarean scar pregnancies in patients with a history of cesarean delivery. Enrichment analysis was performed to elucidate the functional roles of various cell types. Pseudotime analysis was utilized to infer the differentiation of trajectory. SCENIC provided insights into transcription regulation. CellChat was employed to explore intercellular interactions. A single-cell atlas of the maternal-fetal interface microenvironment in patients with a history of cesarean delivery was conducted to elucidate aberrant activities associated with CSP. Significant alterations were observed in trophoblast differentiation and function, including changes in angiogenesis, migration, and interactions with the extracellular matrix (ECM). A marked reduction in decidual stroma cells was observed, accompanied by abnormal ECM remodeling. Neutrophils (Neu) emerged as the principal immune cells, with elevated numbers and activation. Inflammatory pathways such as NF-κB in Neu increased. Cellular interactions between stroma cells and trophoblasts were mainly COLLAGEN, FN1, and LAMININ, and between immune cells and trophoblasts were VISFATIN and CXCL. This comprehensive single-cell analysis has elucidated the cellular heterogeneity at the maternal-fetal interface in patients with a history of cesarean delivery and shed light on distinct cellular abnormalities associated with CSP.

papers.title: methylTFR: Computational quantification of transcription factor activity from DNA methylation
papers.authors: Gunduz, I. B.; Nitsch, R.; Murugan, S. K.; Mueller, F.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation modulates transcription factor (TF) binding, and plays an important role in regulating gene expression. We developed methylTFR, an R package for quantifying TF activity from DNA methylation across TF-binding sites, providing a low-dimensional and interpretable activity profile. Across 147 human immune cell methylomes, methylTFR identified cell-type-specific regulators, including CEBP and ETS family activity in myeloid cells. In CD4+ T cells, TF activity scores resolved the naive-to-memory trajectory and highlighted AP-1 factors as important memory regulators. We applied methylTFR to sparse single-cell methylome data, and we integrated derived activity scores with gene expression and accessibility into joint factor models yielding multimodal views of lineage regulators.

papers.title: Mesenchymal Stromal Cells Fuel Immunometabolic Reprogramming of Type 2 Conventional Dendritic Cells to Alleviate Systemic Sclerosis.
papers.authors: Wang Z, Liu S, Liu X, Ou Y, Zhang Y, Li H, Liu M, Hu Z, Wang D, Sun L.
papers.abstract: Objective This study aimed to investigate the clinical efficacy and underlying mechanisms of mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapy in systemic sclerosis (SSc). Methods We prospectively evaluated the efficacy of MSC therapy in patients with SSc. To elucidate the therapeutic mechanisms, we integrated paired multiomics data: proteomics (n = 7), metabolomics (n = 7), and both bulk (n = 6) and single-cell (n = 2) RNA sequencing. Baseline disease-associated signatures were mainly defined by publicly available data sets of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs; 21 SSc vs 6 healthy donors). Results MSC therapy significantly ameliorated skin fibrosis (median modified Rodnan Skin Score decreased 7.0 [interquartile range 3.8-9.3]; P adj ] adj adj Conclusion Our study underscores the MSC-mediated immunometabolic reprogramming to restore immune homeostasis by targeting upstream OXPHOS defects of cDC2s in SSc.

papers.title: Development and application of a mechanistic model for protein A resolution of a bispecific antibody for process characterization and optimization.
papers.authors: Wadsworth S, Reilly J, Mattila J, Cowan C, Bak H.
papers.abstract: Regeneron's bispecific technology, based on a fully human IgG antibody construct, consists of two distinct heavy chains and a common light chain co-expressed in a single cell. The co-expression of the two distinct heavy chains, one of which contains a dipeptide substitution that ablates Protein A binding, leads to the formation of three species with varying degrees of avidity to Protein A: the heterodimer bispecific and two parental homodimer impurities. The avidity difference between the three species can be leveraged for both bulk capture of the bispecific and resolution of the bispecific from the homodimer impurities via a ternary resolving Protein A chromatographic separation on commercially available resins amenable to large scale Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) production. This case study highlights the efficiency of a mechanistic modeling approach for the optimization and characterization of ternary resolving Protein A unit operations. A mechanistic model, comprised of a general rate transport model and colloidal particle adsorption (CPA) affinity isotherm, was developed to describe this ternary separation for a model bispecific. The model was calibrated and validated with 10 laboratory experiments and demonstrated an ability to predict bispecific yield within 3% and bispecific purity within 1% on average. The model was then used to optimize the process and characterize the design space, while providing mechanistic insight into the process.

papers.title: Targeting a Novel AREG + Dendritic Cell Alleviates Renal Fibrosis Induced by Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.authors: Luo X, Xiong L, Zhou Z, Zhang L, Peng Y, Zou X, Huang Y, Lin Y, Yang X, Zhan Z, Zhou F, Liu Y, Yu C, Ye B, Zhang Z.
papers.abstract: Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (RIRI) is a major cause of acute tubular damage and a key driver of maladaptive repair and fibrosis. However, the cellular initiators that connect early immune activation to tubular epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) during RIRI remain poorly defined. Here, we established a human RIRI model by modifying the surgical procedures in patients undergoing radical nephrectomy and confirmed successful injury induction by tubular dilation, severe mitochondrial swelling and increased apoptosis in renal tissues. Using single-cell RNA sequencing, we uncovered an underappreciated dendritic cell (DC) subset, CD11c + AREG + DCs, that expands after RIRI, coinciding with EMT activation in tubular epithelial cells at early stages. Notably, ligand-receptor inference revealed markedly enhanced communication between CD11c + AREG + DCs and tubular epithelial cells after RIRI, suggesting the AREG-EGFR as a dominant axis. Mechanistically, CD11c + AREG + DCs initiate and promote tubular EMT via AREG-dependent EGFR signalling, establishing a direct causal link between this DC population and injured tubular epithelial cells. Importantly, Areg knockdown or DC depletion significantly alleviated tubular damage and fibrosis and preserved kidney function in the IRI mouse model, which highlights these cells could be potential therapeutic targets for mitigating RIRI.

papers.title: PLA1A Inhibition Enhances Chemoimmunotherapy Efficacy by Blocking Immunosuppressive Macrophage Polarization in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.authors: Wang TT, Kong WS, Li JJ, Qiu YY, Huang RZ, Chen HJ, Duan XT, Chen P, Xie YC, Mo HY, Xuan Y, Han Y, Liao K, Zeng ZL, Wang FH, Li YH, Gao Q, Ju HQ.
papers.abstract: Clinical outcomes are often suboptimal in colorectal cancer (CRC) patients treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC). A key determinant of the response to NAC is the functional state of tumor-infiltrating immune cells. Understanding how NAC reshapes the immunological landscape will be essential for refining patient stratification and identifying effective combination treatment strategies. Here, we analyzed paired samples before and after NAC treatment by single-cell RNA sequencing, revealing that NAC treatment significantly reshaped the immune microenvironment. Tumors from NAC non-responders featured increased immunosuppressive M2-like macrophage infiltration, which correlated with elevated phosphatidylserine-specific phospholipase A1 (PLA1A). Mechanistically, PLA1A hydrolyzed phosphatidylserine (PS) exposed by chemotherapy to elevate lysophosphatidylserine (LysoPS), which activated the P2ry10 receptor and downstream signaling to promote M2-like macrophage polarization. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of PLA1A by cilengitide synergized with chemoimmunotherapy to suppress tumor progression in murine models. Clinically, high plasma PLA1A levels negatively correlated with responses to chemoimmunotherapy. Collectively, these findings reveal a chemotherapy-driven metabolic axis that induces an immunosuppressive milieu by increasing lysoPS release. This axis highlights PLA1A as a therapeutic target to mitigate immunosuppression and improve chemoimmunotherapy efficacy.

papers.title: Characterization of SPP1 + macrophages and their correlation with resistance to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in colorectal cancer liver metastasis.
papers.authors: Tang J, Hao W, He X, Qian X, Ruan L, Quan M, Zhou J, Tang J, Wang L, Guo Y, Zhao Y, Chang C, Zhou S.
papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) for colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) remains a major clinical challenge, with outcomes varying widely among patients, yet the mechanisms that drive therapeutic resistance remain incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated single‑cell RNA‑sequencing and spatial transcriptomics of patient tumor specimens to dissect the interplay between the hepatic tumor microenvironment and chemotherapy resistance. We identified a specific macrophage subpopulation marked by elevated expression of Secreted Phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1) that is significantly enriched in insufficient responders to NAC. Mechanistically, these SPP1 + macrophages exhibit a pro‑tumoral transcriptomic profile and directly suppress CD8 + T cell cytotoxic function through the SPP1‑CD44 signaling axis, as demonstrated by in vitro co‑culture assays, a large‑scale tissue microarray, and multiple syngeneic mouse models. Spatially, they are scattered throughout the tumour and form dense barriers that sequester CD8 + T cells and drive their exhaustion. Strikingly, this spatial configuration inversely correlates with cytotoxic activity and adaptive immune signatures and thereby reinforces a local immunosuppressive niche that sustains chemoresistance. These data provide the missing link: effective chemotherapy requires an immune‑active hepatic microenvironment, and SPP1 + macrophage infiltration actively disrupts this state, which in turn promotes clinical resistance. In a preclinical CRLM model, SPP1 blockade synergised with anti‑PD‑1, inducing significant tumour regression and restoring T‑cell function. Collectively, our findings position SPP1 + macrophages as central drivers of NAC resistance in CRLM and highlight the spatial immune barrier they create as a promising therapeutic target for overcoming chemoresistance and improving immunotherapy responses.

papers.title: Ferroptosis Profiling of Outcome-Associated Monocyte Subsets and the Potential Regulatory Role of LDHA in Early Sepsis.
papers.authors: Wang X, Liu D, Li S, Wang K.
papers.abstract: Objective Sepsis carries high morbidity and mortality, and early precise intervention is critical for improving outcomes. The heterogeneity of circulating immune cells, particularly at the monocyte subset level, remains a major barrier to early risk stratification. This study aimed to identify prognosis-associated monocyte subsets and their key regulators in early sepsis, providing potential clues for early prognostic assessment and targeted intervention. Methods We analyzed single-cell transcriptomic profiles of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from patients with early sepsis and healthy controls in the GSE167363 dataset to define myeloid subsets associated with clinical outcomes. Core regulatory molecules were prioritized by intersecting differentially expressed genes (DEGs) with cell death-related gene sets, and their expression patterns were examined in bulk transcriptomic cohorts. The lead candidate was further evaluated through in vitro functional experiments and in vivo survival studies using the cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) mouse model. Results A transitional monocyte subset defined by high CD14 and modest FCGR3A expression, positioned at the intermediate node of monocyte differentiation, was markedly depleted in sepsis non-survivors. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) revealed ferroptosis as the predominant cell death modality in this subset among non-survivors. Lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) was pinpointed as a core regulatory molecule, and its differential expression was validated in independent bulk transcriptomic cohorts. In vitro assays confirmed that LDHA inhibition attenuated ferroptosis in THP-1-derived macrophages. Consistently, both myeloid-specific Ldha conditional knockout (cKO) and pharmacological inhibition of LDHA markedly improved the 7-day survival of CLP-induced septic mice. Conclusion This study identifies an outcome-associated monocyte subset with a ferroptosis signature in early sepsis and suggests a potential regulatory role for LDHA in monocyte ferroptosis.

papers.title: From density to spatial function: spatial multi-omics, composite biomarker design, and therapeutic engineering of tertiary lymphoid structures in solid tumors.
papers.authors: Wang X, Lin L.
papers.abstract: Background Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) have emerged as clinically relevant immune niches associated with improved survival and enhanced response to immune checkpoint inhibitors across multiple solid tumors. However, translational evaluation remains dominated by density-based scoring, which inadequately captures the functional heterogeneity of histologically similar lymphoid aggregates. This review synthesizes recent advances in spatial biology that support a shift from counting TLSs to interpreting them as spatially organized immune microenvironmental units embedded within local tumor ecosystems. Main body Evidence from spatial transcriptomics, multiplexed imaging, single-cell profiling, computational pathology, and spatial-proteomic approaches converges on four coupled requirements for productive TLS function: stromal licensing through lymphotoxin-dependent chemokine circuits, vascular competence mediated by specialized high endothelial venules, helper T-cell programs that bridge follicular and cytotoxic immunity, and a permissive metabolic context that enables maturation. Spatial studies further show that regulatory infiltration, suppressive plasma-cell programs, and metabolic disruption can decouple structural presence from effective antitumor immunity. Across tumor types, these insights indicate that biomarker performance improves when TLS density is integrated with maturity, anatomical location, HEV coupling, immune composition, and treatment context rather than used as a standalone metric. We further discuss how spatial analyses reveal actionable pathways for inducing or reprogramming TLSs and outline a staged, module-matched composite biomarker workflow combining digital pathology, targeted multiplexed imaging, and focused molecular or metabolic augmentation. Conclusions TLSs should be regarded as spatially organized, functionally heterogeneous immune microenvironmental units rather than biologically equivalent lymphoid aggregates. A spatial-functional framework helps explain productive, arrested, and suppressive TLS states, provides a basis for next-generation composite biomarkers, and supports module-matched therapeutic strategies tailored to the stromal, vascular, helper-cell, or metabolic bottleneck limiting TLS function in individual tumors. The immediate next step is prospective validation of a minimal TLS panel across defined treatment contexts.

figure.caption: TLSs as spatially organized immune microenvironmental units. Panel (A) illustrates canonical TLS architecture as a compartmentalized immune niche containing a B-cell follicle with germinal center, adjacent T-cell zone, dendritic cells, high endothelial venule (HEV), stromal/fibroblastic reticular cell (FRC) network, extracellular matrix, and effector-cell compartment. Panel (B) contrasts density-only assessment with spatial-functional interpretation by integrating maturity, anatomical location, HEV coupling, immune composition, and metabolic context. Panel (C) compares productive, arrested/immature, and suppressive/dysfunctional TLS states according to organization, vascular competence, immune composition, metabolic support, and expected antitumor function. Cell, vascular, stromal, and matrix symbols are identified in the figure keys. The arrow in panel (B) indicates the shift from density-only assessment to spatial-functional interpretation. papers.title: AKNA serves as a prognostic biomarker and restrains endometrial cancer progression via STING activation and macrophage reprogramming.
papers.authors: Tu Y, Xu L, Tian C, Shi Y, Yu J, Gong C, Peng T, Yu H, Yuan R, Jiang P.
papers.abstract: Background AKNA, an AT-hook transcription factor, plays a critical role in cancer development. However, its prognostic value and biological function in endometrial cancer (EC) remain unclear. Methods To systematically investigate AKNA in EC, we integrated multi-omics data (The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx), and single-cell transcriptomics), dual independent clinical cohorts (TCGA-UCEC dataset and two institutional cohorts), and in vitro / in vivo experimental models. Immunohistochemistry, RT-qPCR and Western blotting were used for expression validation. Functional assays, including lentiviral-mediated AKNA knockdown/overexpression, CCK-8, scratch-wound, Transwell, flow cytometry, and colony formation assays were conducted to assess the effects of AKNA modulation on proliferation, migration, invasion, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, chemosensitivity and macrophage polarization. Mechanistically, chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) sequencing (ChIP-seq), ChIP-qPCR, and dual-luciferase reporter assays were employed to define the transcriptional regulation of stimulator of interferon genes (STING) by AKNA. A prognostic nomogram integrating AKNA expression with clinicopathological features was developed and externally validated in independent cohorts. Results AKNA was significantly downregulated in EC tissues compared with normal endometrium, which was associated with advanced International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage, aggressive histological subtypes, and poor prognosis. AKNA knockdown promoted EC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, while enhancing M2 macrophage polarization and reducing sensitivity to paclitaxel and potentially compromising anti-tumor innate immunity. Conversely, AKNA overexpression or STING activation by cyclic GMP-AMP reversed these malignant phenotypes. Mechanistically, AKNA directly bound to the STING promoter and transcriptionally activated STING, thereby inducing TANK-binding kinase 1 and interferon regulatory factor 3 phosphorylation. The nomogram combining AKNA with clinicopathological features demonstrated high accuracy in predicting EC recurrence and outperformed single-variable models in both training and validation cohorts. Conclusions AKNA deficiency promotes EC progression by transcriptionally suppressing STING and driving M2 macrophage polarization. AKNA serves as a robust prognostic biomarker and predictive indicator for chemotherapy and innate immune modulation, offering a promising therapeutic target for precision treatment of EC.

papers.title: IL18BP links antigen processing and presentation programs to a dendritic cell-enriched immunoregulatory state in colorectal cancer.
papers.authors: Zheng J, Guo G, Tian Y, Chen L, Xia H, Jiang Y, Lin D, Zhang H, Zhang N, Huang C.
papers.abstract: Background Antigen processing and presentation (APP) is required for tumor immune recognition, but its relationship with the immune landscape in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains incompletely defined. In this study, APP-related transcriptional programs were used as the starting point to identify immune-cell-associated biomarkers with prognostic and immunotherapeutic relevance in CRC. Methods Six public CRC bulk cohorts were analyzed to define APP-related molecular states. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis and four machine-learning frameworks, including Boruta, LassoLR, Pamr, and XGBoost, were applied to prioritize genes linked to APP activity. Single-cell analysis was performed with an atlas of 121 samples and 169,427 cells to identify the cellular origin of the candidate gene. Immune infiltration, cancer-immunity-cycle activity, immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) response, predicted drug response, somatic mutation patterns, and in vitro function were then evaluated. Results Two APP-associated patterns were identified and showed different survival outcomes and immune landscapes. Network- and machine-learning-based screening prioritized IL18BP as the main APP-associated candidate. Higher IL18BP expression was associated with longer survival and an immune-active phenotype, including stronger antigen-presentation signals, increased immune infiltration, checkpoint-related signatures, and cancer-immunity-cycle activation. Single-cell profiling showed that IL18BP was preferentially enriched in dendritic cells (DCs), linking the APP-derived bulk signature to a DC-centered immunoregulatory compartment. Across nine external ICB-treated cohorts, IL18BP showed response-classification performance. Drug-response prediction and somatic mutation analyses identified additional features associated with IL18BP-defined groups. In CRC cell lines, IL18BP knockdown increased proliferation, migration, and invasion. Conclusion These findings identify IL18BP as a DC-enriched, APP-associated biomarker in CRC. By connecting APP programs in bulk tumors with DC-level expression patterns at single-cell resolution, this study positions IL18BP as an APP-associated marker of a DC-enriched immune state. These findings support further evaluation of IL18BP for prognostic and immunotherapy stratification in colorectal cancer but do not establish a causal APP-DC-IL18BP pathway.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis reveals a membrane tension signature associated with tumor-stroma crosstalk in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.authors: Zhu P, Zhu P, Zhu Z, Bian G, Liu Y, Yang Q, Luo P.
papers.abstract: Background Dysregulated membrane tension (MT) drives tumor cell migration, invasion, and immune evasion, yet the prognostic value of MT-related genes (MTRGs) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains unclear. Methods We integrated transcriptomic and clinical data from TCGA, ICGC, and GEO. A three-gene MTRG prognostic signature was developed through univariate and LASSO-Cox regression, and validated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, time-dependent ROC curves, and calibration plots. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, tumor mutational burden, and immunotherapy response was predicted using the Tumor Immune Dysfunction and Exclusion (TIDE) algorithm. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics were used to investigate the mechanistic role of CFL1 in tumor-stroma crosstalk. Results The signature (CFL1, CRTC2, SRGAP2) stratified HCC patients into high- and low-risk groups with distinct overall survival (OS). High-risk tumors showed coordinated activation of MT and ECM-remodeling pathways alongside an immunosuppressive microenvironment. In silico analyses suggested that CFL1-high tumor cells may transmit MDK signals to fibroblasts (via SDC2, NCL, and ITGA4-ITGB1) and to T cells (via NCL). Spatial transcriptomics confirmed predominant CFL1 enrichment in stromal compartments. The signature was an independent prognostic factor, and the nomogram showed promising clinical utility. Conclusions This three-gene MTRG-associated signature is associated with predicted immunotherapy response based on computational analysis in HCC. Our results suggest a potential link between biophysical MT and tumor stroma co evolution and represent a potential therapeutic direction warranting further experimental validation.

papers.title: A MYC-LDHA-MCT4 expression program marks an SPP1/TREM2-centered macrophage state in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Ma Q, He H, Liu T, Li Y, Mao C, Shi C, Yao Q.
papers.abstract: Introduction Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) responds poorly to immune-checkpoint blockade, and the metabolic organization of its myeloid barrier is incompletely understood. Methods We integrated imaging mass cytometry from the phase II trial NCT04177810, three single-cell RNA-seq datasets, two spatial transcriptomic cohorts (12 sections), three survival cohorts, and in vitro siRNA perturbation of MYC, LDHA and SLC16A3 with conditioned-medium assays on THP-1-derived macrophage-like cells and primary human CD8+ T cells. Results CD8+ T-cell infiltration increased without objective responses while macrophages remained abundant. Patient-level epithelial MYC and glycolysis programs correlated with SLC16A3 (MCT4) and a macrophage lactate-reception program. Across 12 spatial sections, macrophage-receiver scores were higher around MCT4-high cores (ring 1: 12/12 positive; median difference 0.433; FDR = 0.010), with the strongest state-resolved signal for SPP1/TREM2 macrophages (median difference 0.613; FDR = 0.006); the composition-adjusted effect remained positive (10/12) but was non-significant (FDR = 0.071). Silencing MYC, LDHA or SLC16A3 reduced extracellular lactate and altered conditioned-medium effects, with partial rescue by lactate add-back. Survival associations were cohort-dependent with substantial heterogeneity. Discussion These results define an exploratory, expression-based spatial association between a tumor MYC-LDHA-MCT4 program and an SPP1/TREM2-centered macrophage state, constituting a testable hypothesis rather than evidence of lactate transfer.

papers.title: Human CD1c-autoreactive T-cells recognise Mycobacterium tuberculosis -infected antigen-presenting cells and display cytotoxic effector programmes.
papers.authors: Milton M, Farag SH, Garay-Baquero D, Gullick J, Niedobecka K, Burns D, Szoke-Kovacs R, Trimby-Smith P, Look A, Stopforth R, Lepore M, Cole DK, Denney L, White A, Sharpe S, Leslie A, Vallejo A, Tezera L, Elkington P, Mansour S.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains the leading cause of death from infection globally yet the contribution of non-classical T-cell pathways to human immunity remains poorly defined. CD1c-autoreactive T-cells, which recognise self-lipids presented by the antigen-presenting molecule CD1c, are frequent in human blood but their role during infection remains unclear. Here, we investigate how CD1c-expressing antigen-presenting cells (APCs) and Mtb infection shape CD1c-autoreactive T-cell responses using engineered human APC systems, complemented by single-cell transcriptomic profiling to define the ex vivo phenotypic landscape of these T-cells. CD1c is present within human TB granulomas, whereas Mtb down-modulates CD1c expression on infected APCs, consistent with an immune evasion strategy. CD1c-autoreactive T-cells respond more strongly to Mtb-infected CD1c + APCs than to uninfected cells, exhibiting enhanced activation, cytotoxicity, and diverse cytokine secretion via CD1c-dependent recognition. Under in vitro conditions, these T-cells reduce relative Mtb burden in infected phagocytes. Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals cytotoxic effector-memory programmes and expression of antimicrobial molecules, providing a mechanistic basis for these responses. Together, these findings define a human CD1c-restricted T-cell response to Mtb-infected APCs and identify autoreactive CD1c-restricted T-cells as a candidate cellular axis for lipid-directed immunity in TB.

papers.title: Necro-mosaic: a lesion-aware framework for testing programmed cell-death-associated mechanisms in tuberculosis.
papers.authors: Zhang Q, Chang.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) can progress despite substantial systemic immune activation, indicating that protection and immunopathology are shaped not only by the magnitude of host responses but also by their organization within individual lesions. TB granulomas are heterogeneous tissue ecosystems in which cellular composition, necrosis, vascular access, extracellular-matrix remodeling, metabolic stress, and local drug exposure vary across lesions and over time. Spatial and single-cell technologies now enable these features to be investigated at increasing resolution; however, spatial or molecular association alone does not establish mechanism, causality, or therapeutic relevance. Here, we propose the Necro-Mosaic framework as a hypothesis-generating, lesion-aware approach for investigating programmed cell death (PCD)-associated processes in TB. The framework is neither a mutually exclusive taxonomy nor a clinical classification system. It considers three non-exclusive, mechanistically framed axes: F-axis, involving ferroptosis-associated lipid-peroxidation injury and membrane damage; P-axis, involving coordinated inflammatory cell-death activity with PANoptosis-like features; and N-axis, involving neutrophil-associated extracellular activity, including NET-associated structures and effector processes. The anatomical distribution, co-occurrence, temporal sequence, and biological consequences of these axis-associated processes remain empirical questions. A single lesion may therefore exhibit one axis-associated pattern, several overlapping patterns, or no interpretable pattern. We distinguish pathway capacity, pathway engagement, and mechanism-specific execution and specify the measurements and controls required to support each level of inference in situ . The framework also defines evidence as established, emerging, or hypothesis-generating according to the strength, reproducibility, resolution, and causal support of the available data. We propose falsifiable predictions to determine whether F-, P-, or N-axis-associated processes act as drivers, amplifiers, or downstream correlates of destructive lesion evolution. Although lesion-resolved host-directed therapy (HDT) is an important long-term objective, current evidence does not support assigning lesion-level mechanistic profiles from blood alone or using these axes to select clinical treatment. Progress will require prospective longitudinal studies, lesion-anchored multimodal validation, perturbation and rescue experiments, spatial pharmacology, and explicit assessment of antimicrobial-preservation and safety risks. By prioritizing testable mechanisms over fixed spatial categories, Necro-Mosaic provides a structured framework for determining how PCD-associated processes may contribute to TB lesion heterogeneity and for identifying which observations are sufficiently validated to support future translational studies.

figure.label: Figure 1
figure.caption: Tuberculosis lesions occupy dynamic restrictive-to-permissive trajectories. TB lesions within the same host may differ in bacterial burden, tissue architecture, inflammatory organization, necrosis, cavitation, and local drug exposure. “Restrictive” and “permissive” are used as dynamic descriptors of lesion behavior rather than fixed histological categories. The figure illustrates candidate factors associated with lesion trajectory, including immune-cell organization, matrix remodeling, vascular access, metabolic context, and antimicrobial penetration. These features are not assumed to occur in a fixed anatomical order.

papers.title: Machine learning method for optimizing coding sequences in mammalian cells.
papers.authors: Theodorou E, Stadler M, Gustafsson C, Welch M.
papers.abstract: Mammalian cell lines are the preferred hosts for producing commercially relevant therapeutic proteins such as antibodies, antibody derivatives, and cytokine fusion proteins. Even though significant investment is made to optimize upstream and downstream processes, the optimal gene design parameters for heterologous recombinant protein expression remain poorly understood. We describe a generic approach to gene optimization in which design features are systematically sampled and iteratively modulated using machine learning (ML). Synthetic gene variants encoding the Dasher fluorescent protein, differing only in synonymous codons, were used to interrogate the gene-sequence preferences of transient antibody-expressing HEK293 cells. Synonymous codon variations influenced expression by more than 2 orders of magnitude. This variation in protein yield was used to build ML models relating gene design features, which were then employed to design further-improved genes. The ML models were shown to be expression system-specific. Messenger RNA levels and ribosome occupancy were highly correlated with protein levels, suggesting that mRNA lifetime is influenced by coding bias. Our results illustrate a novel, generally applicable method to improve gene expression via synonymous re-coding for any protein target or host cell.

The MEGA7 tree display indicates that each gene is equidistant from all other genes in the set as defined by global homology. (b) Codon usage correlation for the synthetic dasher sequences. papers.title: Identification of psoriasis-associated hub genes by integrated transcriptomics and machine learning.
papers.authors: Zhao Y, Liang X, Tang M, Qiao L, Bai W, Huang C, Li M, Zeng X, Leng X.
papers.abstract: This study aims to systematically identify key hub genes in psoriasis pathogenesis through the integration of bioinformatics, machine learning and experimental validation methods. Four psoriasis microarray datasets were retrieved from the GEO database, with differentially expressed genes identified through comparative analysis. A dual machine learning approach screened core hub genes, whose expression levels and diagnostic efficacy were validated in an independent cohort. CIBERSORT was employed for immune cell infiltration analysis, whilst a multi-database approach constructed an mRNA-miRNA-lncRNA regulatory network. Molecular docking technology assessed interactions between the environmental pollutant bisphenol A, predicted drugs, and hub genes. Finally, an in vitro psoriasis model was established by stimulating HaCaT cells with the M5 cytokine mixture, with hub gene expression validated via RT-qPCR. Results show that 77 co-differentially expressed genes were identified in psoriasis. Machine learning screened five key hub genes: CARHSP1, HPSE, PCLAF, SERPINB4, and SPRR2C. These were significantly upregulated in the validation cohort and demonstrated strong discriminative value for distinguishing psoriatic lesional skin from paired non-lesional skin, rather than serving as standalone diagnostic biomarkers for psoriasis. Immune cell infiltration analysis revealed extensive associations with immune subpopulations including T cells and macrophages. Molecular docking computationally predicted a potential binding interaction between the environmental pollutant BPA and the hub gene HPSE, which awaits future experimental validation. Concurrently, Genistein and HPSE were suggested a potential interaction that awaits functional validation. In vitro experiments confirmed significant upregulation of HPSE, PCLAF, and SPRR2C mRNA levels in M5-induced psoriasis cell models. HPSE emerged as a multifunctional core gene associated with immune dysregulation. Molecular docking additionally predicted a potential interaction between the environmental pollutant BPA and HPSE; however, this interaction remains a computational hypothesis requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: Antibody Discovery and Therapeutics in Spondyloarthritis: Recent Advances and Future Directions.
papers.authors: Chan KW, Koo GC, Lim CK.
papers.abstract: Spondyloarthritis is a multi-faceted condition housing a group of inter-related chronic inflammatory rheumatic diseases such as ankylosing spondylitis, IBD-associated arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and juvenile idiopathic arthritis. While decades of research and technological advancements have significantly improved our understanding of the disease, there remain many underlying genetic and physiological mechanisms which are unsolved but essential for the development of the right diagnosis and treatment. This mini-review examines our current foundational knowledge of spondyloarthritis, the main concepts related to the disease pathogenesis and the various lines of therapies developed thus far. We hope to provide a perspective on the current and potential antibody discovery platforms for the next decade as computational methods and artificial intelligence become increasingly mature and relevant in clinical research.

papers.title: Integrated proteomics and metabolomics for predicting cardiometabolic risk in pregnant women living with HIV: current evidence and future directions.
papers.authors: Eke AC, Eleje GU, Sani MU, Ezebialu IU, Dankishiya FS, Sodangi IS, Ibrahim IY, Wester CW, Aliyu MH, Graham DR.
papers.abstract: Introduction Pregnant women living with HIV (PWLWH) experience cardiometabolic risk across pregnancy and postpartum, including hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), dyslipidemia, obesity, and later metabolic disease. This heterogenous biology reflects gestational adaptation, HIV-associated immune adaptation, antiretroviral therapy (ART), placental function, and underlying cardiometabolic susceptibility. Integrated proteomic-metabolomic prediction studies in PWLWH remain scarce, positioning current evidence as a foundation for biomarker discovery and prospective validation. Areas covered This review evaluates molecular and biomarker evidence from PWLWH alongside broader pregnancy literature informing proteomic and metabolomic discovery. Approaches include mass-spectrometry-based proteomics and metabolomics, affinity-based platforms including Olink and SomaScan, nuclear magnetic resonance, targeted assays, and multi-omics integration using regression, network, machine learning, and latent-factor methods. Emphasis is placed on inflammatory, endothelial, angiogenic, lipid, amino-acid, mitochondrial, and immune-metabolic pathways relevant to HDP, GDM, dyslipidemia, and postpartum cardiometabolic risk. Expert opinion Integrated proteomics and metabolomics offer near-term value for mechanistic discovery and reproducible molecular risk signatures. Translation requires longitudinal cohorts, measured ART exposure, standardized pre-analytics, independent validation, and improvement beyond clinical risk factors. High burden settings additionally require resource-appropriate sampling, simplified targeted assays, local laboratory capacity, sustainable bioinformatics, demonstrable clinical utility, and scalable translational strategies.

papers.title: An integrative meningioma surfaceome atlas and a transferable framework for CAR-T target nomination.
papers.authors: Sanker V, Mahesh D, Liverani L, Abikenari MA, Li Z, Zhang Y, Theodros D, Medikonda R, Cavagnaro MJ, Banu MA, Desai A, Lim M.
papers.abstract: Meningioma is the most common primary intracranial tumor, yet recurrent and high-grade disease has few durable systemic options, and, unlike hematological malignancies, no systematically filtered cell-surface antigen resource exists to guide chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T development. We address this gap not by nominating a trial-ready target but by building two reusable resources: an integrative meningioma surfaceome atlas and a transferable, gate-based framework that separates transcriptomic discovery from CAR-T target nomination. Analyzing single-cell RNA sequencing from eight meningioma patients (GSE183655; 80,220 quality-controlled cells), patient-aware differential expression followed by a curated surfaceome filter (UniProt plasma-membrane localization; extracellular domain ≥20 aa; exclusion of ribosomal, nuclear, cytoplasmic, and secreted proteins) reduced 83 scored candidates to 13 bona fide plasma-membrane (Tier A) antigens, removing prominent false positives such as the nuclear proteins FOXC1 and MGMT, the cytoplasmic enzyme lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA), and the secreted protein PTGDS. Because expression ranking establishes discovery but not CAR-T suitability, we then applied explicit nomination gates: a systemic-safety score integrating whole-body GTEx transcriptomics with Human Protein Atlas protein-level evidence; a membrane-topology tractability gate distinguishing antibody-accessible single-pass and GPI-anchored ectodomains from multi-pass transporters and tail-anchored proteins; and a safety × coverage metric. Under stringent thresholds (combined safety ≥0.55, tumor-cell detection fraction ≥50%, safety × coverage ≥0.30), no Tier A antigen qualified. Ubiquitously expressed antigens were correctly demoted, including the tetraspanin CD9 (53.2% tumor-cell coverage but pan-tissue protein expression and high plasma abundance), and the highest-ranked transporter SLC7A2 was demoted by multi-pass topology (largest extracellular loop 38 aa) despite favorable transcriptomic safety. Leukemia inhibitory factor receptor (LIFR), a single-pass type I receptor with a contiguous 789-aa ectodomain, was the only antibody-tractable nominee for experimental follow-up yet remained liability laden (combined safety 0.41; safety × coverage 0.135) and is not a validated target. Cross-dataset expression overlap (93.3%) reflected mRNA reproducibility, not CAR-T validity or clinical validation, and generic-antibody docking was exploratory only. All findings are transcriptomic and require surface-level confirmation. This work contributes a reproducible meningioma surfaceome atlas and a transferable nomination framework and shows that rigorous gating leaves no single antigen with a favorable safety × coverage × tractability profile, motivating bispecific and logic-gated CAR-T strategies.

papers.title: An entosis-informed prognostic index for survival stratification and molecular characterization in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Liu Y, Zhao W, Mu S, Liang S, Wen Y, Li S, Zhan C, Cheng Y, Tang L, Wu Y, Lin Z, Fang H, Ding Y.
papers.abstract: Background Entosis is an actomyosin-dependent cell-in-cell process that may culminate in lysosome-mediated entotic cell death and is implicated in tumor evolution. Its clinical relevance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear. Methods To construct an Entosis-related Prognostic Prediction Index (EPPI), this study integrated TCGA-LUAD transcriptomic, clinical, and somatic mutation data. Three independent GEO cohorts provided external validation. The initial candidate gene set covered components driving cell-in-cell formation and the intracellular degradation of internalized cells. For subgroup comparison, the analytical approach incorporated survival analysis, functional enrichment, tumor microenvironment profiling, mutation analysis, immunotherapy assessment, and drug-sensitivity prediction. Tissue and cellular distributions of the EPPI genes were mapped using spatial transcriptomics and single-cell RNA sequencing. Molecular docking assessed predicted drug-target interactions. Finally, in vitro RAC1 knockdown experiments evaluated the cellular function of a representative EPPI gene. Results Comprising RND3, RAC1, KRAS, CTNNA1, AURKA, and ACTB, the final EPPI consistently stratified overall survival across all cohorts and showed moderate prognostic discrimination. The high-EPPI group had greater tumor purity and mutational burden, with enhanced cell-cycle, DNA-repair, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and NF-κB programs, whereas the low-EPPI group showed greater immune and stromal infiltration. TIDE and immunophenoscores also differed between subgroups. Drug-response models predicted greater sensitivity to cisplatin and paclitaxel in the high-EPPI group and to several targeted agents in the low-EPPI group. Molecular docking predicted RAC1-EHT-1864 and AURKA-alisertib interactions. Spatial and single-cell analyses showed heterogeneous EPPI-gene expression, with ACTB and RAC1 broadly distributed and AURKA restricted to selected populations. RAC1 depletion suppressed LUAD-cell proliferation, DNA synthesis, migration, and invasion. Conclusion The EPPI is an entosis-informed prognostic index for survival stratification in LUAD. Based on this index, patients can be separated into subgroups with distinct proliferative features, genomic alterations, tissue compositions, and predicted drug sensitivities. These findings associate entosis-related molecular features with distinct cellular and clinical characteristics of LUAD.
papers.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: Ferroptosis-associated candidate genes in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: evidence from human peripheral blood and mouse brain.
papers.authors: Li J, Wang C, Li H, Liu Y, Cheng C, Zhao Z, Jiang G, Cui X, Ng BCF, Zhao Y, Wu Z, Yang X.
papers.abstract: Background Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) has high morbidity and mortality. Ferroptosis may contribute to aSAH-related brain injury, but its peripheral and brain-associated signatures remain unclear. Methods Human peripheral-blood dataset GSE36791 (43 aSAH, 18 controls) was analyzed using limma, FerrDb intersection, WGCNA, GO/KEGG enrichment, and PPI-based prioritization. qPCR validation was performed in peripheral blood from 10 aSAH patients and 10 non-SAH controls; aSAH samples were collected within 24 h after rupture. Mean ages were 60.2 ± 7.7 and 63.6 ± 8.9 years, with 5 and 4 males, respectively. Brain-level validation used GSE79416 mouse cortex and OMIX006611 mouse SAH single-cell RNA-seq data. Male C57BL/6 J mice (8 weeks, 20-22 g) underwent cisterna magna autologous blood injection; brain tissues were collected 1 day after SAH (n = 6/group). Immune infiltration and molecular docking were also performed. Results Among 2,645 DEGs, 35 were ferroptosis-related. MAPK3, STAT3, G6PD, and PGD were prioritized as ferroptosis-associated candidate genes and were upregulated in human aSAH peripheral blood, mouse SAH cortex, and the clinical qPCR cohort. Single-cell analysis showed expression of the corresponding mouse genes across annotated brain cell types, especially immune/glial populations. In mouse SAH brain tissue, MAPK3/ERK1, STAT3, PGD, and G6PD protein levels increased, p-STAT3/STAT3 ratio was elevated, MDA content increased, and GPX4 activity decreased. Immune profiling showed increased neutrophils, mast cells, and activated dendritic cells. Ganoderic acid A was prioritized as a preliminary in silico candidate. Conclusion MAPK3, STAT3, G6PD, and PGD are ferroptosis-associated candidate genes in aSAH, supported by human peripheral-blood, mouse cortex, single-cell, and mouse brain validation. Ganoderic acid A remains an exploratory in silico candidate requiring further functional validation.

papers.title: Sequential and coordinated control of human plasma cell differentiation by IRF4 and BLIMP1 associated with a discriminating ISRE/EICE motif lexicon
papers.authors: Lau, L. C.; Lal, S.; Fan, J.; Pease, N.; Singh, H.
papers.abstract: The transcription factors IRF4 and BLIMP1 (PRDM1) promote plasma cell (PC) differentiation by repressing B cell identity genes while inducing the unfolded protein response, ER/Golgi biogenesis, and immunoglobulin secretion. How IRF4 and BLIMP1 partition and coordinate their genomic activities during plasma cell differentiation remains unresolved. Using naive human B cells and a stepwise in vitro differentiation system, we performed CRISPR/Cas9 perturbations of IRF4 or PRDM1 in plasma cell precursors followed by single-cell RNA sequencing. Despite their mutually reinforced expression and shared recognition of related IRF-family motifs (ISREs and EICEs), loss of IRF4, but not of BLIMP1, yielded a stunted intermediate with incomplete silencing of B cell identity genes and defective induction of the secretory program. Multiome profiling, base-pair-resolution motif modeling, CUT&RUN, and DNA-binding assays identified non-conserved nucleotides within ISRE/EICE motifs that discriminate IRF4 from BLIMP1 binding. These findings define an ISRE/EICE motif lexicon that predicts differential IRF4 and BLIMP1 occupancy and are consistent with a temporally ordered model, in which IRF4 first acts independently and then in concert with BLIMP1 to promote PC differentiation.

papers.title: A State-Resolved Single-Cell and Spatial Atlas Reveals IDH -Associated Differences in Malignant and Immune Architecture in Diffuse Glioma.
papers.authors: Zaman A, Holton E, Pandya M, Shillington G, Escher C, Sudhakar KK, Tuzesi A, Mehta A, Lam E, Zekanovic R, Sughrue M, Teo C, Yeung J, Muskovic W, Powell JE.
papers.abstract: Adult-type diffuse gliomas are defined by the isocitrate-dehydrogenase (IDH) axis, yet how this biology constrains malignant cell-state repertoires and their immune-modulatory potential remains unclear. We profiled 69 tumors using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), and spatial transcriptomics, and resolved seven recurrent malignant cell states: astrocyte-like progenitor cells (ALPC), hypoxia, cycling G1/S, cycling G2/M, oligo-lineage, neuro-oligo-lineage, and neuro-lineage. The IDH axis strongly biased state occupancy and malignant-immune composition, with IDH -mutant tumors dominated by differentiated lineage-like states and reduced immune infiltration, whereas glioblastoma (GBM) showed expansion of ALPC and hypoxia states alongside increased myeloid and lymphoid infiltration. Orthogonal analyses supported that ALPC-associated markers are expressed in situ and in patient-derived stem cell-permissive cultures, consistent with a stem-like, differentiation-competent malignant phenotype. State-resolved pathway analysis identified mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation programs enriched in GBM ALPC and extracellular matrix remodeling, and chemotaxis-associated programs enriched in GBM hypoxia. Composition-controlled, patient-level interaction modeling identified a greater malignant-myeloid signaling interface in GBM, driven by SPP1-CD44/integrin signaling and confirmed by differential expression; GBM networks also featured TGFB and NECTIN modules, whereas IDH -mutant networks were dominated by APP/APOE-TREM2/TYROBP and MIF modules. These data suggest that the IDH axis shapes glioma behavior by constraining malignant state repertoires and biasing the deployment of state-specific metabolic and immunomodulatory programs.
